papers.title: Geneva seven-colour synthetic photometry from Gaia DR3 spectrophotometry
papers.abstract: The well-established calibrations of astrophysical parameters derived from classical photometric systems (e.g. those of Johnson, Stromgren-Crawford, and Vilnius) are rarely applied at present. Instead, spectral energy distribution fitting techniques and the very broad Gaia photometric system are typically employed. However, these approaches have proven highly inaccurate for upper main-sequence stars. In this work, the Geneva seven-colour photometric system was synthesised from flux-calibrated low-resolution Gaia spectrophotometry (BP/RP spectra). The available ground-based observations have made it the most homogeneous dataset, offering a number of astrophysical calibrations and applications. The GaiaXPy Tool was used to synthesise the seven filters. The original Geneva U had to be exchanged with the SDSS u because it is found to be significantly blueward of the cut-off of the BP/RP spectra. The ground-based observations were used to correct for offsets and the known temperature dependence of the effective temperature in the ultraviolet region of the BP/RP spectra. The test using well-known effective temperature and metallicity calibrations on the synthetic photometry (with 21 080 stars) demonstrated the high accuracy of this approach. Further checks for possible correlations between the projected rotational velocity and binarity yielded negative results. As a direct application, the metallicity of 630 open clusters (and, thus, the radial Galactic metallicity gradient) was determined. Finally, we compiled a catalogue of 25 881 397 objects. This work demonstrates that alternatives exist to the widely used three-band Gaia photometric system. The Geneva seven-colour approach can help calibrate and analyse astrophysical parameters, especially those of upper main-sequence stars.

papers.title: Dirichlet does not imply Regularity for general elliptic operators in smooth domains
papers.abstract:
In the upper half-space $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$, $n\geq2$, we show that there exists a real, diagonal, strongly elliptic matrix $A$ of bounded measurable coefficients, smooth in the interior of $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$ and continuous on its closure, such that for the elliptic operator $L=-\operatorname{div}A\nabla$, the Dirichlet problem with data in $L^p$ is solvable, for every $p\in(1,\infty)$, but the Dirichlet-Regularity problem is not solvable for any $p\in(1,\infty)$. The counterexample has the following properties, in particular:
  1. $A$ equals the identity matrix at the boundary and their $L^\infty$ distance in $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$ can be made arbitrarily small.
  2. $A$ satisfies that $t|\partial_t A|^2$ is a Carleson measure.
  3. $A$ fails to satisfy the Dahlberg-Kenig-Pipher condition only slightly, in the sense that for every $q>2$, $t^q|\nabla A|^q\frac{dxdt}{t}$ is a vanishing Carleson measure, but $t|\nabla A|^2$ is not a Carleson measure.
  The counterexample resolves a long-standing question of C. Kenig.

authors.name: Andrea Merlo
authors.institution: Azienda Sanitaria Unità Locale di Reggio Emilia

papers.title: AI-generated support, worked examples, and script-based learning in undergraduate physics: A comparative study
papers.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used to support students during learning and problem solving, but its instructional value depends on how it is embedded in established learning approaches. Worked examples guide learners through the steps and reasoning of a solution; conversational AI may extend them by responding to individual questions. To isolate this added value, we compared a chatbot-delivered intelligent worked example with a matched static worked example and a lecture script. Nine recitation groups in an undergraduate electrodynamics course were cluster-randomized to the three conditions, and 86 students worked individually on a Gauss's law problem. Concept-test accuracy and self-efficacy increased significantly in all conditions, but changes did not differ significantly between groups (p=.07 for concept-test accuracy and p=.38 for self-efficacy). Four weeks later, in a reduced sample with selective participation and pre-existing group differences, students in the static worked-example condition scored higher than those in the script condition (p=.004, d=1.22), whereas the two worked-example conditions did not differ significantly. Usability, but not perceived educational value, was higher for the intelligent worked example than for the script (p=.011, d=0.88). In a subsequent homework assignment on Ampere's law with free choice of learning material (N=46), 62-71% of students in each condition reported using only the static worked example, at most 8% used exclusively the intelligent one, and 15-31% used neither. Thus, conversational delivery showed no clear additional learning benefit under the present conditions. More broadly, a learning format that is rated favorably need not be the one students voluntarily adopt.

papers.title: Collision of a sphere and a prolate spheroid settling in a quiescent ambient
papers.abstract: The collision rate of a prolate spheroid and a sphere settling through a quiescent fluid at small Reynolds number is computed for randomly oriented spheroids and for spheroids turned broadside by weak fluid inertia. Without hydrodynamic interactions, the collision cross-section is the projection of the spheroid enlarged by the radius of the sphere. The ideal kernel then follows in closed form for aligned spheroids and from a one-dimensional quadrature for isotropic ones. Alignment raises the ideal kernel by at most a factor of 4/{\pi}, but extinguishes it on the extinction locus, where an isolated broadside spheroid settles as fast as the sphere. Hydrodynamic interactions are computed from pair trajectories in a first-reflection slender-body model, in which the interaction velocity is proportional to the difference of the buoyant weights and only the flow of the sphere rotates the spheroid. A strongly aligned spheroid weathervanes, whereas a freely rotating one feathers and glides. Weathervaning lowers the collision efficiency, as does feathering far from the extinction locus, but gliding raises it near the locus. There, the collision rate of spheroids aligned at a finite rate lies far above both the strong-alignment result and the ideal isotropic kernel. Just above the extinction locus, where strongly aligned spheroids are blocked, collisions persist at all the finite alignment rates computed. A boundary-element solution shows that the model overestimates the rate at which the gap closes near contact. A lubrication film largely corrects this and reduces the collision efficiencies from their interception values. Simple fits for the ideal kernels, the efficiencies and the near-contact correction are provided for use in collision models.

authors.name: Arnab Choudhury
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences

papers.title: Structure Preservation of $2$-Wasserstein Barycenters on the Real Line with Applications to Log-Concave Distributions
papers.abstract: We study to what extent the $p$-Wasserstein barycenter ($p$-WB) of arbitrary, not only finite, collections of distributions preserves their structure, focusing on shape constraints on the densities, such as monotonicity, unimodality, or log-concavity. This preservation is a generalized convexity property in Wasserstein space, which we call $p$-WB convexity. We investigate $p$-WB convexity of the families of $\phi$-unimodal distributions: an absolutely continuous distribution $\mu$ is $\phi$-unimodal if composition with $\phi$ turns a density into a concave function on the interior of the convex support of $\mu$. This notion generalizes log-concavity and $s$-concave densities. We find a quantile representation of $\phi$-unimodality and then use a novel closed-form expression of the quantile density function of the $2$-WB to decide on $2$-WB convexity. In higher dimensions or for $p\neq2$, we give counterexamples ruling out the $p$-WB convexity of $\phi$-unimodal distributions. On $\mathbb{R}$ and for $p=2$, we characterize which $\phi$ generate $2$-WB convex families. The family of log-concave distributions is $2$-WB convex, as is the family of distributions with $s$-concave densities if and only if $s\geq-2$. General unimodality, corresponding to $s=-\infty$, is not preserved.

papers.title: A Characterized Softmax for Distributing Standing Across Multiple Affiliations
papers.abstract: Cooperative game theory answers canonical questions on payoff allocation (Shapley, Owen), interaction attribution (Grabisch-Roubens, Faith-Shap), and coalition formation and stability. None answers a fourth question that arises whenever players carry known, overlapping group tags fixed independently of the game: how should a player's standing be distributed across the groups it already belongs to? We call this membership attribution, formalize it, and give a complete characterization of its solution. The direct, ratio-based answer is provably invalid whenever a player's group-level signals have mixed sign --- a common, structurally unavoidable case. We propose a restricted-domain softmax construction instead, and prove that, for any player satisfying a precisely defined richness condition on the group structure, it is the unique such map, up to a temperature parameter, satisfying five requirements. A sixth requirement fixes the sign of this temperature; a seventh, shown independent of the rest via an explicit counterexample, forces one shared temperature across all eligible players. A worked example on an exact cooperative game confirms the applicable requirements numerically and shows the construction degrades gracefully, valid but uninformative, when a player's evidence fails to distinguish between its groups.

papers.title: DataRecycle: Trustworthy Distillation of Structured Data from Scattered Web Evidence
papers.abstract: The web contains vast amounts of scattered quantitative evidence that is difficult to organize into comparable and verifiable structures. Yet its unstructured, sparse, and sometimes conflicting nature makes a systematic distillation costly and error-prone. Existing approaches force users to make a trade-off: search engines return document lists that require labor-intensive extraction and reconciliation, while generative AI systems produce fluent summaries that obscure data provenance, introduce reporting bias, and hide inconsistencies. We present DataRecycle, an interactive system that helps transform scattered web evidence into structured tables of comparable numerical facts. Given a user's query or statement, DataRecycle decomposes it into entities and attributes, retrieves candidate evidence, and organizes scattered, potentially conflicting records in a table-based evidence view. To address key challenges in automated data distillation (i.e., incomplete retrieval, untraceable generation, sparse data distribution, and multi-source inconsistency), DataRecycle adopts an ontology-guided, top-down data acquisition strategy, visualizes the recorded lineage from retrieved snippets to extracted values, and aligns heterogeneous data across dimensions such as time, definition, and scale. We evaluate DataRecycle through module-level experiments, a usage scenario, and a user study, showing that the system helps users organize numerical web evidence into provenance-linked tables and inspect uncertainty and conflicting sources.

papers.title: Functionals commuting with reparametrizations
papers.abstract: Motivated by the study of tangent curve bundles of algebraic varieties, we consider the following simple-looking problem: given a space $E$ of functions, describe functionals from $E^n$ to $E$ which commutes with reparametrizations, i.e. with the right-composition with an element of $E$. Our main result is a complete description of the algebraic solutions of this problem when $E$ is the space of polynomials vanishing in $0$, which we denote by $\mathbb C[T]_0$. This description involves a simple operation, which we call semi-product, with interesting algebraic and geometric properties. The proof involves the study of polyharmonic functions on the positive discrete orthant $\mathbb Z^n_{>0}$, and a relation with the co-invariant algebra of type $A$. We also provide a generalization connected to colored permutations, and discuss the analogue problems where $E=\mathbb C[T]_0/(T^\ell)$ for some $\ell >0$, and where $E$ consists of infinitely differentiable functions. Finding a complete description of algebraic solutions in these settings is still open.

papers.title: Triage Accuracy of Jev and Open-Weight System One Decision Models and Their Use for Early Emergency Recognition in Symptom-Assessment Applications
papers.abstract: Laypeople increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for triage advice, but LLMs answer in variable free text, which makes it hard to evaluate them for use in medical devices. Decision models, which assign a probability to each predefined triage category, may be easier to evaluate. To test their triage accuracy, we evaluated 16 decision models (14 open-weight, 2 proprietary) on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, yielding 163,728 total assessments. The best models triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases correctly and agreed with an existing algorithm in 56.1% of real-world cases. They were more promising for recognising emergencies early: given only demographics, chief complaints, risk factors and red-flag answers, the best model reached an AUROC of 0.87. At a 5% error margin, it could decide for or against emergencies for about half of users. Decision models should therefore not replace triage engines but could shorten symptom assessments at setting-specific error margins.

papers.title: Planar Graphs Embed into Graphs with Treewidth $O(\log n /\epsilon)$
papers.abstract:
We construct a stochastic embedding of $n$-vertex planar graphs into graphs of treewidth $O(\log n/\epsilon)$ and expected distortion $1+\epsilon$ for any parameter $\epsilon \in (0,1)$. This result yields randomized polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTASes) for a broad class of connectivity problems on planar graphs, including the $k$-MST problem. The treewidth bound is asymptotically optimal and settles a conjecture of Chang, Cohen-Addad, Conroy, Le, Ma. Pilipczuk, and Mi. Pilipczuk (2025).
  The key idea is a new construction of a stochastic balanced cut of size $O(\log n/\epsilon)$ and expected distortion $1+\epsilon/\log n$ for every edge. We construct these cuts using the minimax principle, an approach that differs significantly from existing cut constructions based on a random clustering hierarchy.
  Our embedding extends to minor-free graphs using the Robertson-Seymour decomposition, giving the same treewidth bound. Using this decomposition, we obtain the first randomized PTASes for many connectivity problems in minor-free graphs, including the Steiner tree problem and its prize-collecting variant.

papers.title: Questions, Explanation and Synthesis in Service Mathematics: Course Design with Didactic Units and Hybrid Teaching
papers.abstract: Students may have access to a convincing mathematical explanation without being able to reconstruct or adapt it. A course must provide opportunities to develop that understanding while keeping the work sustainable for students and teachers. This article develops a methodology for service mathematics in which a question ledger guides both course authoring and classroom decisions. Course-relative didactic units organise explanatory purposes, prerequisites and connections, initially calibrated by a five-to-seven-minute expert account. Teaching combines preparation, student exposition and supported repair with substantial teacher exposition and synthesis. Their allocation changes with the topic, audience and conditions of teaching. Compression and recovery explain how developed constructions become reusable while their grounds remain accessible. Three analyses from mathematics for computing-full Sudoku encoding, grayscale projection and a software failure contract-show how contrasting cases guide explanation and revision. The practice-informed contribution connects coherent course design with adaptable teaching and manageable preparation, and identifies questions for evaluating learning, participation and sustained teacher effort.

papers.title: Scaling cores and dust-free layered sets
papers.abstract: We study Hausdorff-box dimension gaps in compact sets of finite positive Hausdorff measure. At each scale, the points of low local measure form a scaling core that carries all covering growth above the Hausdorff dimension. This gives gap criteria for both box and intermediate dimensions. We construct dust-free layered sets, in which every neighbourhood of every point has positive measure. Their dimensions are determined by the layer dimension and a product core formed from a horizontal limit set and a sequence of heights. Under a suitable approximation-rate condition, the volume remaining after subtraction of the product tube grows linearly with radius, with coefficient twice the total layer measure. Every compact null horizontal set admits such a construction. Cantor approximants, homogeneous cube constructions and Bedford-McMullen carpets illustrate the results.

papers.title: 5G NR Sensing of Robotic Arm Motion in Indoor Factory Environments
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the performance of monostatic Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems for tracking robotic arm kinematics in industrial factory (InF) environments. Building on a part-specific quasi-deterministic channel model previously derived from high-resolution robotic-arm measurements using our context-aware channel sounder and digital twin, we develop a framework for generating arbitrary articulated motion profiles through hierarchical kinematic transformations. By integrating this high-fidelity target model with the standardized 3GPP InF channel model, we employ 5G New Radio (NR) Positioning Reference Signals (PRS) as the sensing waveform to enable comprehensive system-level evaluation. Simulations are conducted for both sparse clutters (InF-SH) and dense clutters (InF-DH) scenarios using 3GPP-compliant antenna radiation patterns and analog beamforming, allowing us to assess the impact of industrial clutter on sensing performance. The results show that while high estimation accuracy is achievable under Line-of-Sight (LOS) conditions, dense clutter in InF-DH environments introduces severe blockage that significantly limits sensing reliability. In particular, the effective sensing coverage in InF-DH is drastically reduced, with detection probability dropping to approximately \(P_d \approx 10\,\%\) even when the robotic arm is located directly beneath the Transmission Reception Point (TRP). Furthermore, in InF-SH, achieving a high detection probability (e.g., \(P_d \geq 90\,\%\)) requires the target to remain in close proximity to the TRP, with an effective coverage radius of approximately 13 m.

authors.name: Jian Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Nada Golmie
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

papers.title: Profinite groups with coprime automorphisms whose orbits generate nilpotent subgroups
papers.abstract: Suppose that a profinite group $G$ admits a finite group of coprime automorphisms $A$ such that for any $\varphi\in A$ every subgroup $\langle x^{\langle\varphi\rangle}\rangle$ generated by the $\langle\varphi\rangle$-orbit of an element $x\in G$ is nilpotent. It is proved that $[G,A]$ is pronilpotent, and if $A$ is soluble and the fixed-point subgroup $C_G(A)$ is locally nilpotent, then $G$ is locally nilpotent.

papers.title: World Models and the Law
papers.abstract: Current AI may have a model of how we use human language, but this does not translate into a reliable representation of physical reality. World models promise to fill this gap by learning how an environment changes over time and predicting the consequences of an action, and they are already used to steer robots and generate explorable worlds. This article asks how AI regulation in three major legal contexts, the European Union, California, and China, copes with the distinctive challenges they raise. I propose a definition and a taxonomy of world models based on who or what acts on their predictions, and identify the risks of misplaced reliance on them. I argue that existing rules tend to cover world models but leave three questions open, i.e., action provenance, trajectory validity, and the weight of simulated evidence, and recommend ways to fill these gaps.

papers.title: Sierpi\'{n}ski Gaskets Julia set and Postcritically finite fractals
papers.abstract: Devaney's work on the Julia sets of the McMullen family, established these rational maps as central objects in holomorphic dynamics. For Misiurewicz parameters, that is when the orbits of the critical points are all strictly preperiodic to a repelling cycle, the topological point of view taken by Kameyama links the dynamics of such rational maps to that on the attractors of invertible self-similar iterated function system. Ero\u{g}lu, Rohde, and Solomyak showed that in favorable cases the topological conjugacy is in fact quasisymmetric. We survey the machinery underlying these results and propose directions for further research.

papers.title: Joint statistics on vexillary involutions via Fulton's essential set
papers.abstract: We jointly enumerate various statistics over vexillary involutions among which there are the number of descents and the number of peaks. As a by-product, we get an equidistribution result between vexillary involutions and 3412-avoiding involutions, which, notably, implies that, for every $n$ and $k$, the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $3412$ and having $k$ descents equals the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $2143$ and having $k$ ascents. The proof describes $2143$-avoiding involutions through Fulton's ranked essential set, translates the count into a weighted enumeration of walks in the quarter plane, and solves the latter explicitly. Finally, we show that arbitrary vexillary permutations are encoded by excursions of the same walk model.

papers.title: Molecular Pawns on a Surface Chessboard: Computational Investigation of Nanographenes with Atomistic Methods
papers.abstract: Atomically precise nanographenes combine tunable electronic topology with localized, coherent spin states, making them candidate platforms for molecular quantum technologies. This review examines the multiscale theoretical framework governing these systems: the hierarchy of computational methods for describing magnetic properties, the substrate-molecule interface, on-surface synthetic kinetics, and supramolecular self-assembly. We highlight how density functional theory, automated reaction-path discovery, and spin-aware machine-learned interatomic potentials connect static electronic structure to mesoscale dynamics, and how magnetic exchange, optical excitations, and spin transport can be predicted before synthesis.

authors.name: Jacopo Lupi
authors.institution: National Interuniversity Consortium of Materials Science and Technology

authors.name: Matteo Briganti
authors.institution: National Interuniversity Consortium of Materials Science and Technology

papers.title: Modeling extraordinary relativistic jets on the scale of the cosmic web
papers.abstract: Recent observations of supermassive black hole jets extending up to the typical sizes of cosmic web filaments challenge our current understanding. In particular, the overall jet size of J152932.16+601534.4 ("Porphyrion") reaches $\sim 7$ Mpc at redshift 0.896. Magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) models of relativistic jets have never been successfully applied to such extraordinary distances, requiring demanding jet-environment and flow stability conditions. By using state-of-the-art numerical simulations of 3D relativistic-MHD jets, we show that Porphyrion's observational properties can be successfully modelled in a realistic scenario, involving a jet kinetic power of $3.5 \times 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and an external medium of a low-density galaxy group. We find that the pair of jets expands to $\sim 9$ Mpc in about $20$ Myr, implying that the jet grows with relativistic speeds for most of its evolution. Comparing this case with other jets of similar power propagating in substantially denser cosmic structures, we find much slower outflows that can only reach a few Mpc, consistent with the bulk of the observed population of giant radio galaxies. Our results make a testable prediction, i.e. future detections of even larger-scale jets in upcoming surveys and database searches will be invaluable in studying the demographics and feedback of the poorly known population of powerful jets, particularly in under-dense regions of the cosmic web.

authors.name: Andrea Mignone
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Torino

papers.title: XRISM view of a featureless cluster Abell 1060: Revealing the advection of a diffuse radio source by ICM motions
papers.abstract: Abell 1060 is a nearby, dynamically relaxed galaxy cluster hosting the extended radio structure Flying Fox (FF) near its center. We used high-resolution XRISM/Resolve spectroscopy to measure intracluster medium (ICM) motions and velocity dispersion. Spatially resolved analysis reveals a velocity gradient of approximately 100 km/s along FF and enhanced velocity dispersion near the brightest cluster galaxy NGC 3311, suggesting turbulence generated by galaxy-ICM interactions. These results and the compact extent of FF favor fossil plasma supplied by past activity of the brightest cluster galaxy and transported by ICM motions. We also tested whether the measured turbulence could generate or maintain the nonthermal components of FF. For a velocity dispersion of $96.7^{+23.9}_{-24.6}$ km/s and an assumed turbulence scale of 50 kpc, comparable to the Resolve field of view and approximately half the cluster core radius, the turbulent energy flux is approximately $3.49 \times 10^{-28}$ erg cm$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$. Although this flux may weakly reenergize pre-existing relativistic electrons, the acceleration timescale of approximately 2.5 Gyr exceeds the synchrotron and inverse Compton cooling timescale of approximately 210 Myr. The present turbulence is therefore insufficient to accelerate electrons to high energies. In situ turbulent reacceleration is unlikely to dominate the generation of FF, although it may help maintain fossil electrons supplied by past AGN activity. These results link ICM dynamics to the origin of nonthermal emission and support a time-evolutionary picture of particle acceleration in galaxy clusters.

authors.name: Noriko Y. Yamasaki
authors.institution: Institute of Space and Astronautical Science

authors.name: Takayuki Tamura
authors.institution: Institute of Space and Astronautical Science

papers.title: Probing Invisible Actuation Shifts for Test-time Calibration of Visuomotor Policies
papers.abstract: Visuomotor policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world action models (WAMs) are increasingly deployed on robots whose cameras and controllers differ from those used to collect their training data. Such deployment introduces two kinds of shifts. Visual shifts, such as a moved camera, change the observed images; actuation shifts, such as a retuned controller, latency or an added payload, change only how commanded actions translate into robot motion. Invisible to the policy, actuation shifts sharply degrade its success, even under domain randomization. In this work, we propose PEA, a test-time calibration method that identifies actuation shifts through active probing before task execution. Specifically, before each episode, the robot executes a short probe that moves one arm axis at a time with known commands, so that gain, delay and drift leave separable traces. A closed-form identifier estimates them from the response, and PEA compensates every subsequent command so that the robot executes the motion the policy intends. The identifier requires no policy training and thus applies to any frozen visuomotor policy. Since visual shifts remain visible to the policy, PEA further adapts the frozen policy with a removable low-rank adapter, addressing coupled visual and actuation shifts. Experiments on LIBERO with a WAM and a VLA show that, without any policy training, the identifier of PEA recovers most of the success lost to actuation shifts and generalizes to shifts unseen during training (e.g., from 61.0% to 89.7% on LIBERO-Spatial with Cosmos-Policy).

authors.name: Jie Liu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Bivariant $K$-theory for bornological algebras
papers.abstract:
We construct a presentable, stable \(\infty\)-category \( KK\), and exhibit it as the target of the universal functor from the category of bornological algebras into cocomplete, stable \(\infty\)-categories, preserving filtered colimits, and satisfying smooth homotopy invariance, excision, and stabilisation with respect to Schatten-class or smooth compact operators. We also construct a bivariant \(K\)-theory \(
KK\) for suitably nuclear bornological algebras, and show that it is a right Bousfield localisation of \( KK\). The category \(
KK\) is symmetric monoidal and admits a bivariant Chern character to local cyclic homology. The categories \(
KK\) and \( KK\) corepresent Corti\~nas and Thom's diffeotopy \(K\)-theory. We use the Chern character to show that up to a suitable Schatten-class stabilisation, the complexified Chern character from the diffeotopy \(K\)-theory (resp. \(K\)-homology) of a smooth manifold to the compactly supported cohomology (resp. locally finite homology) of the manifold is an isomorphism.

authors.institution: Mathematical Institute of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

papers.title: VEGA: A Scalable Software-Hardware Co-design for Genome Alignment using RVV Extension
papers.abstract: Dynamic programming (DP)-based genome sequence analysis is fundamental to computational genomics, but it remains computationally intensive as genomic data volumes continue to outpace Moore's Law. Existing hardware accelerators often sacrifice programmability and scalability across diverse alignment algorithms. In this work, we present VEGA, a scalable software-hardware co-design that accelerates genome alignment using RISC-V Vector extensions. VEGA introduces specialized vector instructions and three key innovations: a Forefront Stationary dataflow that minimizes off-chip memory access, intersequence parallelism that maximizes SIMD lane utilization, and custom ISA extensions that accelerate core alignment operations. Evaluations show that VEGA achieves up to 15.1x and 9.7x speedups for Edit Distance and Smith-Waterman algorithms over the Ara2-RVV vector baseline, sustaining 10.2x and 6.7x gains for 10kbp sequences. Post-synthesis results indicate only 1.0% area overhead compared to a standard RISC-V core, with performance-per-area efficiency rivaling specialized ASICs. VEGA thus achieves a balanced advancement in efficiency, programmability, and scalability for genome sequence alignment.

papers.title: Projecting Beauty: Transferring Image Aesthetic Analysis onto 3D Heritage and Urban Scenes
papers.abstract: Judgments about the beauty of buildings and streets inform architectural design, urban planning, and heritage conservation, yet increasingly rely on scanned 3D models over material fabric. Automatic aesthetic assessment remains largely confined to 2D photographs. We ask what survives when image aesthetic assessment crosses this dimensional gap to produce dense, per-point aesthetic descriptions of heritage and urban point clouds. We examine three routes that sidestep costly, and sometimes ethically dubious, human labeling at scale: (1) lifting scalar scores from image aesthetic models (NIMA, SAAN) onto geometry; (2) training Aesthetic Visual Analysis (AVA) regression heads on frozen vision backbones (DINOv3, TIPS, SigLIP2, PE, RADSeg) or, in a 3D-native variant, a generalist point encoder on feed-forward AVA reconstructions; and (3) querying lifted vision-language features with a natural-language aesthetic label, taking similarity as a score. The two supervised routes transfer poorly: heads fitting AVA in-domain produce architectural class profiles that neither reproduce one another nor track other signals, while the 3D-native probe stays near chance due to reconstruction geometry quality. Text querying is markedly more coherent. Projecting out the class-text direction from point features raises mean cross-model agreement on architectural part profiles from +0.035 to +0.352, and from +0.113 to +0.293 per point; the four backbones passing a semantic sanity check correlate at 0.31-0.73, while the failing one remains an outlier. Since model agreement is not agreement with human aesthetic perception, we detail a part-aware rating protocol to clarify where human and automatic ratings disagree. We provide a reproducible transfer protocol, an account of which pseudo-labeling routes carry signal, and dense aesthetic pseudo-labels meant as hypotheses rather than ground truth.

papers.title: Vanishing Initialization Turns Diagonal Tensor Gradient Flow into Greedy Matching
papers.abstract: We study gradient-flow (GF) learning of tensors from vanishing initialization in canonical polyadic (CP) factorization models. For tensors of order $\nu\geq3$ whose targets are diagonal in mode-wise orthonormal bases, we prove that the limiting learning dynamics follows a simple greedy bipartite matching process. Each rank-one component of the model, called an atom, can potentially learn each rank-one component of the target, called a scalar sector. Every atom--sector pair has an initialization-dependent activation clock, representing the time at which the atom would grow to macroscopic size in that sector if the pair evolved in isolation. Processing these clocks in increasing order and selecting a pair whenever neither its atom nor its sector has been selected before determines the sequence of actual learning events. We prove that the GF trajectory converges to the corresponding staircase of learned target components. The task of learning modular addition by a CP model with complex weights falls exactly into this framework after Fourier diagonalization. Its activation clocks are independent and identically distributed, allowing us to combine the GF reduction with known random matching asymptotics and derive an explicit, distribution-free large-system loss curve after time reparametrization. We also obtain an asymptotic formula relating this curve to the original GF training time. For models with real weights, conjugate Fourier modes instead form two-dimensional blocks with richer internal structure. We characterize their rank and border-rank cascade and conjecture that the corresponding GF dynamics follows interleaved multi-stage learning processes.

authors.name: Yaroslav Gusev
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: $p$-Harmonic gauge and the regularity of spacetime isometries
papers.abstract: We show every Lorentzian metric of class $C^{k,\alpha}$, where $k\in\mathbf{N}_0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, admits local coordinates of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$ all of whose coordinate functions are temporal functions that are harmonic with respect to a nonlinear $p$-wave operator, where $p\in(-\infty,1)$. Unlike the classical wave operator, this operator is elliptic on temporal functions. As an application, we show that an isometry between Lorentzian metrics of class $C^{k,\alpha}$ is of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$.

papers.title: Accurate rank-controlled step-truncation methods for matrix differential equations
papers.abstract: A class of explicit time stepping schemes is introduced for the integration of matrix differential equations in low-rank format. These schemes combine explicit Runge-Kutta time stepping with rank-adaptive recompressions. For suitably chosen truncation thresholds, they converge at arbitrary order, while having close to optimal ranks, without any prior assumptions on the best approximation ranks. The ranks of the scheme also necessarily depend on the time step, as shown by counterexamples. A numerical experiment illustrates the advantages and performance of the proposed scheme.

papers.title: Stabilized Isogeometric Topology Optimization on Trimmed Geometries
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel stabilized isogeometric topology optimization method for complex design domains represented by trimmed geometries. Minimum compliance is taken as the model problem, where a generalized Cahn-Hilliard model, a time-dependent fourth-order partial differential equation, is solved and its steady-state solutions yield the optimized structures. This approach does not require sensitivity analysis and can naturally accommodate material constraints and complex topological changes. To impose Dirichlet boundary conditions and solve the instability issue caused by trimming, Nitsche's formulation with minimal stabilization is proposed for the high-order problem. Moreover, the immersed boundary-conformal method is extended to handle complex non-design domains, allowing material-void interfaces to be treated in a unified manner. Finally, a three-dimensional biharmonic problem and several two-dimensional topology optimization examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness, stability, and flexibility of the proposed method in dealing with complex design domains.

papers.title: Design of a Compact Cable-driven 4-DoF Salamander Robotic Limb with Large Range of Motion and High Load Capacity
papers.abstract: A compact yet agile and powerful limb is essential for amphibious legged robots that transition between spine-based swimming and leg-based terrestrial walking, as salamanders do. Salamander limbs combine large ranges of motion (ROM), multiple degrees of freedom (DoFs), and high load capacity. These features enable swinging and body-weight support during walking, as well as folding alongside the body during swimming. Their proximal kinematics can be represented by three rotational DoFs at the hip and one at the knee. Replicating these capabilities within a compact robotic limb is challenging with direct-drive architectures, because multiple joint-mounted actuators must be sufficiently spaced or placed distally to avoid self-collision, increasing limb size and rotational inertia. Here we present a cable-driven 4-DoF salamander robotic limb with a spatial cable-routing architecture that relocates actuators proximally while preserving large ROM and load capacity. Transmission-induced coupling is mitigated by mechanically compensating multi-segment cable paths, model-based feedforward decoupling, and output-side joint angle feedback. Compared with a direct-drive limb, the proposed design reduces mass by 20.4%, projected envelope area by 20.5%, and estimated effective yaw-axis inertia by 31.9%. Experiments verify independent, decoupled control over joint-angle ranges of 45 deg, 118 deg, 118 deg, and 135 deg for hip pitch, yaw, roll, and knee flexion/extension, respectively. During lifting tests, the limb supported an equivalent vertical load of at least 5.4 times its own weight. The proposed limb provides a compact, biologically representative platform for future studies of salamander locomotion and neural control.

papers.title: Modeling of reactive porosity waves as a fluid release process in a dehydrating slab
papers.abstract: Dehydration of subducting serpentinites releases aqueous fluids that must be efficiently extracted from the slab. We present a fully coupled two-dimensional hydro--mechanical--chemical model of reactive porosity waves in deforming and dehydrating serpentinite. Thermodynamic closure is provided by Gibbs free-energy minimization for the MgO--FeO--SiO$_2$--H$_2$O system, including dissolved SiO$_2$ in the aqueous phase. Natural multiscale compositional maps of serpentinites from the Mirdita ophiolite (Albania) are used to prescribe initial SiO$_2$ and FeO heterogeneities. The simulations show that these intrinsic chemical variations trigger spontaneous localization of porosity and fluid flow during dehydration, without prescribing channel geometry. Channelization results from the coupling of decompaction, fluid-pressure buildup, buoyancy-driven flow, and metasomatic reactions associated with infiltration of SiO$_2$-poor hydrous fluid and olivine formation. The resulting fluid-rich channels propagate upward and develop connected networks resembling natural vein systems. Our results demonstrate that reactive porosity waves in compositionally heterogeneous serpentinites provide a robust mechanism for focusing fluid flow and enhancing fluid extraction from dehydrating subducting slabs.

papers.title: WorldLatent: A Unified 4D Latent Space for World Perception and Generation
papers.abstract: Generative Pre-Training (GPT) represents a profound milestone in natural language processing, serving as the foundation for most of today's state-of-the-art large language models. By casting diverse understanding and generation problems into a shared token representation, GPT enables a single architecture and unified optimization loop to master heterogeneous tasks across massive corpora, giving rise to powerful foundation models for natural language. In contrast, 4D spatiotemporal vision lacks a common representational protocol: perception (such as depth and camera estimation) and generation are either handled by separate one-way pipelines or bolted together from unaligned single-modality spaces. In this work, we introduce WorldLatent, a framework that formulates a unified 4D latent space as a common protocol for both world perception and generation. Rather than relying on fragmented, task-specific models or stacked single-modality representations, our framework proposes a multimodal VAE architecture that compresses and fuses complex 4D visual appearance, geometry, and dynamics into a single structured latent representation. Within this formulation, perception and generation operate as complementary denoising processes over the same latent space, enabling one generative model to learn both capabilities simultaneously within a single training loop. Experiments across representative 4D benchmarks verify that our fused latent protocol achieves specialist-level zero-shot 4D perception, coherent 4D generation, and controllable editing from a single model. By demonstrating that diverse 4D tasks can be seamlessly unified under a shared representational protocol, our work provides a scalable foundation for general-purpose 4D spatial intelligence.

papers.title: Rate-Quality-Energy Convex Hull for High Dynamic Range Adaptive Video Streaming
papers.abstract: High Dynamic Range (HDR) video introduces substantially higher decoding complexity and energy consumption than Standard Dynamic Range (SDR), yet most adaptive streaming pipelines still rely on bitrate ladders optimized using SDR-oriented metrics such as VMAF. These ladders fail to capture HDR-specific perceptual behavior and ignore decoder-side energy, resulting in energetically inefficient operating points. This work proposes a rate-quality-energy convex-hull optimization framework that jointly considers bitrate, HDR-aware perceptual quality (HDRVMAF), and client-side processing energy, including decoding and upscaling. Experiments on twelve 4K HDR sequences from the LIVE HDR Video Quality Assessment Database evaluate 72 representations per clip and demonstrate that traditional VMAF-optimized ladders frequently select high-resolution encodes that become dominated once energy is accounted for. Compared to the Default HLS ladder, our HDR-aware method achieves substantial bitrate savings of up to 54.34% at equal HDRVMAF, while yielding relative client-side energy reductions of up to 43.10% under higher energy weighting. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework as a practical foundation for constructing HDR bitrate ladders that explicitly expose and control perceptual quality-energy trade-offs.

papers.title: The Effect of Security-Focused Prompts on Reported Findings: A Controlled Experiment on 400 AI-Generated Web Applications
papers.abstract: Agentic coding tools turn a specification into a running web application, so their defaults for authentication, sessions, input validation, and dependencies become its security posture. This study asks whether appending a fixed block of OWASP-aligned security requirements to the prompt changes what such tools produce, by how much, and with what side effects. Each of 100 frozen specifications was realized four times: two agentic tools (Claude Code, Codex CLI) crossed with two prompts sharing a byte-identical functional core, without (A) and with (B) the security block. A fixed static and dynamic pipeline scanned the 400 applications, yielding 6,721 triaged findings, analyzed with count and logistic mixed models and with a dependency diff. The block cut findings per application by a third (incidence-rate ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.60-0.71), equally through both tools, and roughly doubled the declared dependency surface, so variant-B applications carried more high-severity dependency advisories. Adjusted for that surface the advisory rate did not rise (flat per application, 18% lower in aggregate), while high-severity findings in first-party source fell by nearly half. Security-focused prompting is therefore an inexpensive and portable improvement, but it enlarges the dependency surface that has to be audited against it, an effect of library selection rather than of the security requirements themselves.

papers.title: A $C_2$-cofinite non-rational principal $W$-algebra of type $D_4$
papers.abstract: We show that a simple principal $W$-algebra can be $C_2$-cofinite and non-rational. For $\mathcal W=\mathcal W_{-38/7}(D_4,f_{\mathrm{reg}})$ of central charge $-50$, D. Xie predicted seventeen irreducible modules and a logarithmic module of lowest conformal weight $-2$. We determine the Zhu algebra $A(\mathcal W)$ and the Poisson algebra $R_{\mathcal W}=\mathcal W/C_2(\mathcal W)$. Both have dimension $18$, and $A(\mathcal W)\cong\mathbb{C}^{16}\times\mathbb{C}[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$. We construct all seventeen irreducible $\mathcal W$-modules using the realization of $\mathcal W$ as a diagonal coset in $L_{-14/3}(D_4)\otimes L_1(D_4)$ and our previous classification of irreducible $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-modules in the category $\mathcal O$. We also construct an indecomposable $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-module and use the coset realization to obtain an indecomposable logarithmic $\mathcal W$-module. Its lowest generalized $L(0)$-eigenspace is two-dimensional, and $L(0)$ acts on this space by a nontrivial Jordan block with eigenvalue $-2$.

papers.title: Elliptic curves with torsion Z/5: exact rank four over Q(k) and rank at least five infinitely often
papers.abstract: We give two elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(k)$ with torsion group $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank exactly $4$, with four explicit independent points. The upper bounds come from reducing the relevant elliptic surfaces modulo suitable primes and are unconditional. They match the known lower bound for the generic rank with this torsion, due to Eroshkin, and are not isomorphic to Eroshkin's curve or to each other: their parametrising maps to $X_1(5)$ have degree $8$ instead of $12$, the constructions are dihedral rather than biquadratic, and their branch loci differ. In each case, two of the points come from a ``doubling'' step in the spirit of Jaswal. Adding one further condition to the second curve, coming from a quadratic twist over an intermediate conic, gives a fifth independent point over a genus-one curve of rank two. Hence there are infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank at least $5$, improving the known bound $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 4$ to $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 5$.

papers.title: Dirichlet heat kernel estimates for Markov processes with jump kernels blowing up at the boundary
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a $C^{1, \eta}$ open set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathcal{B}: D\times D\to (0, \infty)$ a symmetric Borel function which blows up at the boundary of $D$. Let $\overline{X}$ be a conservative purely discontinuous Markov process on $\overline{D}$ with jump kernel $\mathcal{B}(x,y)|x-y|^{-d-\alpha}$, $0<\alpha<2$. In a recent paper, we obtained two-sided estimates on the transition density of $\overline{X}$. In this paper, we consider the process $X$ obtained by killing $\overline{X}$ upon approaching the boundary of $D$ or by a critical potential. We obtain sharp two-sided estimates on the transition density of $X$. The estimates capture the interplay between the blow-up rate of $\mathcal{B}$, the geometry of $D$, and killing.

papers.title: Universal thermodynamics and BKT transition of the planar Bose gas from weak to strong interactions
papers.abstract: We compute the universal thermodynamics of the dilute two-dimensional Bose gas at weak and strong coupling using the functional renormalization group (FRG). We employ an approximation that retains the full field dependence of the effective potential and spatial derivative terms, extending previous FRG calculations. We find that the equation of state is remarkably insensitive to the approximation scheme, with differences of only a few percent even at strong coupling. By contrast, the improved approximation substantially improves the description of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition, reproducing the universal jump of the superfluid density and the critical anomalous dimension to within a few percent. At weak coupling, our results agree very well with classical-field Monte Carlo simulations, while at stronger coupling we observe deviations from classical-field scaling, valid at weak coupling. Our approach thus provides a quantitative description of the thermodynamics and superfluid density across the BKT transition, including in the strong-coupling regime where classical-field methods are no longer reliable.

authors.name: Adam Rancon
authors.institution: Laboratoire de Physique des Lasers, Atomes et Molécules

papers.title: Tidal effects of bulk viscosity in neutron stars
papers.abstract: Bulk viscosity in neutron-star matter provides a temperature-dependent mechanism for tidal dissipation. In this study, we investigate the impact of bulk viscosity on the dissipative tidal response of neutron stars composed of neutrons, protons, and electrons. Employing cold equations of state derived through the momentum-dependent interaction model, we examine the bulk viscosity arising from the direct Urca process, which acts to restore chemical equilibrium. The temperature dependence is incorporated through the weak-interaction rate, allowing us to explore the behavior of bulk viscosity in the neutrino-transparent regime at temperatures up to a few MeV. To account for the spatial distribution of bulk viscosity within neutron stars, we introduce the effective bulk viscosity, a volume-averaged quantity over the region where direct Urca process operates, and establish a connection with the bulk viscosity. Specifically, we investigate its implications for tidal quantities, including the lag time and dissipative deformability, highlighting their dependence on temperature and stellar compactness. We find that the dissipative tidal effects become maximal at a temperature approximately coinciding with the one of maximum bulk viscosity on the onset of direct Urca. Additionally, these effects are more pronounced in intermediate neutron star masses compared to maximum ones. Finally, for both canonical $1.4\;M_\odot$ and maximum-mass neutron star configurations, we derive causality-based upper bounds on these quantities, providing theoretical benchmarks for assessing the potential observability of bulk-viscous effects in gravitational-wave signals from binary neutron star inspirals.

papers.title: Consecutive sums and Reconstructing Problems
papers.abstract: We study several problems concerning consecutive sums of integer sequences and their relationship with Sidon sets. We also provide new lower bounds for an extremal function related to sequences with distinct consecutive sums, and consider reconstruction problems from multisets of consecutive sums.

authors.name: Peter Pal Pach
authors.institution: HUN-REN Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics

papers.title: Morita equivalence classification for irrational noncommutative solenoids
papers.abstract: Given a prime integer $p$, we define a $p$-angle to be an element of the $p$-solenoid ${\mathcal S}_p$ or equivalently an element of $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{Q}_p$ modulo $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$. Noncommutative $p$-solenoids, or equivalently $p$-rotation algebras, are $C^*$-algebras defined by a $p$-angle in the same way as non-commutative tori or usual rotation algebras are defined by an angle. We give a complete classification, in terms of their $p$-angles and in the irrational case, of these $C^*$-algebras up to strong Morita equivalence, but also the associated groupoids up to Morita equivalence; more precisely, we obtain the following classification result: two irrational $p$-angles define strong Morita equivalent noncommutative solenoids if and only if they define isomorphic dimension groups if and only if they are congruent modulo $GL_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/p])$ if and only if they define Morita equivalent groupoids. This generalises, with a different proof, the classification up to isomorphism, previously obtained by Latr\'emoli\`ere and Packer. We also give a geometrical construction of projective $C^*$-modules in terms of proper $G$-spaces which exhaust the dimension group up to a shift and implement all relevant Morita equivalences by groupoid equivalences.

authors.name: Jean Renault
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: CNN-Based Locked Mode Detection and Prospects for Prediction Utilizing Density Fluctuation Signals
papers.abstract: The deceleration of Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) modes in tokamak plasmas is an observed behavior commonly associated with growing mode amplitude. As rotating MHD modes decelerate to a non-rotating state, they can form Locked Modes (LMs), which can degrade plasma confinement and cause disruptions. LMs therefore pose a serious threat to the sustained operation of otherwise-stable plasmas in Fusion Pilot Plants (FPPs). Identification of MHD modes and any subsequent locking is typically performed with an array of magnetic signals; these magnetic signals may not survive in the harsh reactor environment of an FPP and external magnetic measurements are delayed by magnetic diffusion through the tokamak shielding. This work uses the Radial Interferometer Polarimeter (RIP) as an alternative diagnostic to identify the slowing of rotating MHD modes into LMs. Because this fluctuation-based approach relies on observing prior mode rotation, detection and prediction are restricted to LMs with prior rotation and exclude born-locked modes. Labels were constructed to train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to distinguish MHD modes that lock from those that may appear to approach a locking state but ultimately do not lock. The trained CNN learned to identify low-frequency, descending MHD modes but struggled to distinguish modes that would continue toward locking from those that would not. A second-stage detection method significantly improved performance, detecting 88.5% of LMs with a precision of 83.7% by applying persistence and classification-margin filters to the CNN output. These results demonstrate the capability of an FPP-relevant, non-magnetic diagnostic for accurate LM detection while also identifying fundamental limitations in the achievable prediction time using a fluctuation-based approach.

papers.title: Decoding Frozen Vision Representations for Training-Free Few-Shot Pineapple Detection
papers.abstract: Few-shot object detection in agricultural imagery is hampered by dense vegetation, repeated patterns, and scarce annotations. We present a training-free detector that turns dense features from frozen visual foundation models directly into detections, without fine-tuning, a learned head, or external proposals: a whitened foreground-background direction estimated from annotated support images scores every query patch, and the score field is decoded with an adaptive threshold and support-derived geometry. We also test whether predicted relative depth can be fed directly to RGB-pretrained frozen encoders. On aerial pineapple imagery, the detector outperforms PET-DINO and GeCo2 at every evaluated support size; at K=40, predicted depth alone reaches 92% of the RGB performance with DINOv2, and RGB-depth fusion lowers counting error for both encoders. We release the Pineapple Plantation dataset (4,908 aerial frames, 1,995 annotated with 17,609 boxes, predicted depth, leakage-aware splits) and analyse transfer to two further agricultural datasets.

papers.title: Optimal Window Design for Intercarrier and Intersymbol Interference Power Minimization in w-OFDM
papers.abstract: Block transceivers are essential for modern communication systems, and they are vastly implemented in many day-to-day devices, especially the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) technique. The application of a pulseshaping technique in the OFDM generates the so-called windowed OFDM (w-OFDM). This letter proposes an optimization of the window shape, obtaining minimal intercarrier and intersymbol interference power, ICI, and ISI, respectively. A communication system is simulated by implementing the optimized w-OFDM, and its performance is compared with a non-optimized system using a raised-cosine window.

authors.name: Luiz Coelho
authors.institution: Hospital das Clínicas da Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais

authors.name: Paulo Sergio Ramirez Diniz
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained. Recognition, depth, and correspondence do not transfer reliably. Fine-tuning can improve the action readout even when other measurements move the other way, and no statistic is stable enough to replace a rollout before any deployment.

papers.title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? An Empirical Study of Decoupled Knowledge and Generation Trajectories in Clinical LLMs
papers.abstract: Continual pre-training (\textit{CPT}) is a standard route for domain adaptation, yet existing studies typically track pre-training loss or multiple-choice question answering (\textit{MCQA}) accuracy alone, offering only a narrow view of how adaptation unfolds. We jointly track factual knowledge via \textit{MCQA} and open-ended behavior via pairwise preference rankings across $18$ checkpoints for each of eight instruction-tuned \textit{Qwen} models ($0.5B$ to $8B$), adapted to German medicine with \textit{CPT} and \textit{SLERP} merging. The two axes converge at consistently different rates, with preference rankings reaching $90\%$ of their total gain after a median of $1.7B$ tokens versus $3.5B$ for \textit{MCQA}. A judge-free token-distribution measure reaches this threshold at $1.9B$ tokens. Per-aspect scores indicate that these early preference gains largely reflect surface alignment, meaning models can sound domain-appropriate before their factual knowledge catches up. Larger adapted models close more of the gap to unadapted next-tier generalists, whereas preference gain per FLOP falls by about an order of magnitude across our size range. We therefore argue that judge-based preference scores, which can plateau while \textit{MCQA} knowledge is still improving, should not be used alone to infer adaptation convergence or domain readiness.

papers.title: SARA: An Auditor-in-the-Loop LLM Recommender for Sustainability Reports
papers.abstract: Auditing corporate sustainability reports requires assurance professionals to map a company-specific checklist drawn from roughly 1,700 regulatory requirements onto the relevant passages of lengthy, repeatedly revised draft reports and to judge compliance. We present SARA (Sustainability Reporting Assistant), a human-in-the-loop recommender system delivered as a Microsoft Word add-in that recommends, for each requirement, the passages addressing it and predicts a compliance verdict while keeping the auditor in full control. SARA casts auditing as content-based recommendation over a fixed regulatory taxonomy and makes per-requirement large language model (LLM) matching cheaper, faster, and more accurate through topic-prediction filtering: on expert-annotated reports, it reduces matching cost about sixfold and runtime by 42% versus feeding the full report to the LLM. It is in production use across PwC Germany's sustainability-assurance practice.

papers.title: Unveiling the Eigenvector 1 Sequence in BZQ Blazars. I. Mg II and Ultraviolet Fe II Emission in the UV Main Sequence
papers.abstract: We investigate the location of flat-spectrum radio quasars confirmed as blazars (BZQ-C), Fanaroff-Riley type II radio-loud (RL) quasars (FRII-Q), and radio non-detected quasars within the ultraviolet (UV) Eigenvector 1 (E1) plane defined by the Mg II line width (FWHM Mg II) and the UV Fe II strength (RFeUV). This represents the first systematic comparison of BZQ blazars with their proposed parent population in the UV E1 framework. To minimize selection biases, we construct statistically representative control subsamples and perform matched-subsample analyses in redshift and Mg II luminosity. Population differences are assessed using one- and two-dimensional non-parametric tests, including the Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Anderson-Darling, Mann-Whitney U, and Fasano-Franceschini statistics. We find that the three AGN populations occupy statistically distinct regions of the UV E1 plane. The dominant separation is driven by FWHM Mg II, with BZQ blazars systematically exhibiting narrower line profiles than FRII-Q quasars, while radio non-detected quasars lie between both populations. In contrast, RFeUV provides only limited discrimination between the RL subclasses, although it separates radio-loud from radio non-detected quasars at the population level. The observed ordering demonstrates that the UV E1 plane preserves the physical sequence expected from RL AGN unification. Inclination-dependent projection provides a natural first-order explanation for the Mg II line-width ordering. Additional differences in intrinsic BLR structure or accretion properties may contribute to the observed distributions, although the present analysis does not allow these effects to be separated independently from orientation.

papers.title: Social sycophancy differs across access modes of large language models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can display sycophancy, a tendency to excessively praise, agree with, or validate a user. Existing studies have tested LLMs for sycophancy primarily through application programming interfaces (APIs) rather than the consumer user interfaces (UIs) through which the public commonly interacts with LLMs. Access mode (API vs. UI) may affect observed sycophancy rates. However, it remains unknown to what extent prominent models show API-UI differences in social sycophancy, which includes behaviors potentially more likely in UIs (e.g., softening warranted criticism). We tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek through both APIs and UIs on four dimensions of social sycophancy. Across models, UI access was generally associated with greater social sycophancy, with odds ratios up to 7.56 (95% CI [6.22, 9.20]). However, UI-API differences varied significantly across models for all sycophancy dimensions, including a pronounced reversal for DeepSeek moral sycophancy (43% UI vs. 82.3% API). Overall, our results suggest that API-based LLM evaluations may underestimate the prevalence of sycophancy in corresponding consumer-facing systems, making access conditions consequential for the external validity of LLM evaluation. To facilitate research on access-mode effects, we release 57,000 model responses and SycoUI, a browser-automation pipeline for standardized cross-interface LLM evaluation.

papers.title: Spectropolarimetric properties of fast radio bursts co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110
papers.abstract: We present spectropolarimetric analysis of twelve fast radio bursts (FRBs) co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110, eleven of which are apparently non-repeating. We obtain broadband spectral coverage (400-1530 MHz) for these FRBs and constrain propagation effects in their polarized spectra. We observe two notable spectral features: (i) in three FRBs, we find decreasing linear polarization fraction with increasing frequency and, (ii) in seven FRBs, we find that the linear polarization fraction decreases with decreasing frequency. The former spectral signature is commonly observed in radio pulsars and is suggestive of magnetospheric emission, where either the mixing of orthogonally polarized modes or incoherent summing of unresolved burst components may cause depolarization at high frequencies. The latter is consistent with depolarization due to multipath propagation. We report the first statistically significant correlation (3.5-3.9$\sigma$) between the extent of depolarization and amplitude of Faraday rotation arising from FRB host galaxies, implying that the two effects likely arise in the same turbulent, magnetoionic environments around FRB sources. The prevalence of depolarization in our sample suggests that turbulent environments that have, thus far, been predominantly associated with some repeating FRBs, may also be commonly present around a subset of apparently non-repeating FRBs. We highlight a systematic bias for detecting a disproportionately high fraction of constant polarization angle (PA) profiles in low-frequency FRB surveys due to amplified scatter broadening, which we also observe in two of our co-detected FRBs.

papers.title: Inverse design of polarization-analyzing gratings
papers.abstract: Metasurface polarization analyzing gratings have attracted increasing interest for polarization management and sensing in optical systems. Traditional strategies for the design of these gratings are based on a formalism combining the Jones calculus with Fourier optics. While this approach has achieved notable success in numerous applications, its validity is restricted to the paraxial regime. Here we introduce a differentiable topology optimization framework for these gratings which is free of this constraint. We show that this framework can yield designs which outperform the traditional approach, especially at high angles. Additionally, we provide preliminary experimental validation to corroborate these results.

papers.title: X-AQA: Unifying Action Quality Assessment with Multimodal Large Language Models and Multi-Domain Learning
papers.abstract: Action Quality Assessment (AQA) aims to evaluate the quality of human actions, yet existing methods are predominantly developed and evaluated on individual datasets with different task formulations and assessment criteria. We introduce X-AQA, the first unified training and evaluation framework for general-purpose AQA with multimodal large language models (MLLMs). We construct X-AQA-40K, a training corpus comprising 40,163 samples from 22 data sources across four domains: competitive sports, fitness exercises, rehabilitation, and general skills. We convert heterogeneous annotations into a unified question-answering format, incorporating dataset-specific annotation guidelines and official scoring rules when available. Using this corpus, we fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B to develop a single MLLM capable of handling diverse AQA tasks. We further establish X-AQA-Bench, which evaluates both in-distribution (ID) performance on datasets represented during training and out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization on four held-out datasets. The resulting model outperforms all evaluated open-source MLLMs on X-AQA-Bench and achieves competitive performance relative to proprietary MLLMs. Ablation studies further demonstrate that multi-domain joint training and explicitly providing assessment criteria in prompts both improve OOD generalization. X-AQA establishes a unified foundation for advancing general-purpose AQA across diverse real-world domains. Data and models are released at \hyperlink{https://huggingface.co/collections/Kelly0510/x-aqa}{here}.

papers.title: Survey of Compact Sources for Pulsars and Exotic Objects-II. Precision Timing of Millisecond Pulsar J1840+1102
papers.abstract: We present the timing analysis of the eclipsing millisecond pulsar PSR J1840+1102, discovered in the Survey of COmpact sources for Pulsars and Exotic objects (SCOPE) using the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT). PSR J1840+1102 has a short spin period of 1.60 ms and an orbital period of 1.68 days, with a dispersion measure (DM) of 98.8 pc cm$^{-3}$. We report timing analysis over a 2.7-year baseline, yielding a phase-connected solution with a post-fit residual RMS of 2.1 $\mu$s. Enabled by the timing solution, we report discovery of pulsed gamma-rays from PSR J1840+1102, with the gamma-ray peak aligned with that of the radio profile. PSR J1840+1102 also exhibits remarkably short eclipses, lasting only around $0.4\%$ of the total orbit at 650 MHz. Based on optical searches, the orbital parameters, short eclipses, and comparison with the known binary pulsar population, we infer a Helium white dwarf (He-WD) surrounded by plasma to be the most likely companion. Furthermore, using GMRT observations covering 300 to 750 MHz, we present a study of the interstellar medium properties towards PSR J1840+1102 including refractive scintillation, DM variations and scattering, and report a very low scattering index of $1.65\pm0.15$. The low timing residuals and lack of any prominent orbital parameters or DM variations support the overall suitability of PSR J1840+1102 for inclusion in the pulsar timing array campaigns.

papers.title: The MeerKAT absorption line survey: Galactic OH absorption at 18 cm
papers.abstract: We present a blind search for Galactic OH 18-cm absorption lines towards 19,130 radio sources brighter than 1mJy at 1.4GHz, using 390 pointings of the MeerKAT Absorption Line Survey (MALS). We apply an automated line search followed by Bayesian nested sampling to identify OH 1667MHz, 1665MHz and 1612MHz absorption features, using HI emission and absorption profiles as physically motivated priors. We identify 15 confident detections of OH 1667/1665 MHz absorption. The majority of detections are associated with a visual extinction ($A_{\rm V}$) excess and, within the same MALS pointings, with detected CO emission and a high incidence rate of HI absorption, consistent with OH tracing the H$_2$-bearing medium. We also identify 9 candidates of OH 1612MHz satellite line absorption, two of which coincide with OH main line detections and show integrated optical depth ratios well above the LTE expectation of 1:9. As in previous studies, $N(\rm OH)$ shows no dependence on $N$(HI). Accounting for the varying sensitivity across sight lines, we estimate the covering fraction of OH-bearing gas at $\log N(\rm OH) > 12$ to be $C = 0.051 \pm 0.008$, providing an independent and a more precise estimate than previous measurements of the diffuse molecular gas. We also find qualitative evidence for a decrease of the covering fraction with Galactic latitude. Stacking reveals a clear OH absorption signal that becomes increasingly prominent when sight lines are weighted by $A_{\rm V}$ excess, independently confirming the association of OH with diffuse molecular gas. Modeling of the physical conditions yields hydrogen number densities of 10-100 cm$^{-3}$, typical H$_2$ column densities $\log N(\rm H_2) > 21$, and UV-flux to number density ratios of 0.01-0.3 Mathis cm$^{3}$, typical of the CNM.

papers.title: Density of states for random Schr\"odinger operators with linearly correlated heavy-tailed disorder
papers.abstract: We study the density of states of random Schr\"odinger operators with linearly correlated heavy-tailed disorder. Using an integration-by-parts supersymmetric representation, we prove smoothness of the density of states and Wegner estimates in the strong-disorder regime. We are particularly interested in mixed-sign correlation kernels, which serve as a toy model for the hyperbolic structures arising in the analysis of averaged squared Green's functions. Our approach applies to a broad class of correlation kernels and disorder distributions, including $\alpha$-stable laws.
