papers.title: Quantitative Convergence of Hit-and-Run Beyond Log-Concavity via Variational Hypocoercivity
papers.abstract: We study the convergence to equilibrium of Hit-and-Run, a popular generalisation of the Gibbs sampler. To this end, we establish a novel connection between Hit-and-Run and the theory of variational hypocoercivity, an approach to establish convergence of continuous-time Markov processes. To bridge the gap between the discrete-time Hit-and-Run chain and hypocoercivity, we introduce Hit-and-Langevin, a continuous-time Markov process that approximates Hit-and-Run in an appropriate sense. Using the second-order lift and flow Poincar\'e inequality formulation of variational hypocoercivity, we show convergence of Hit-and-Langevin and deduce a lower bound on the spectral gap of Hit-and-Run. Notably, our analysis seamlessly extends beyond the extensively studied setting of log-concave target distributions, marking the first substantial departure from this setting beyond quasi-log-concave and uniform distributions. More broadly, this work demonstrates that discrete, non-local dynamics, such as Hit-and-Run, can be made amenable to powerful analytical methods, such as variational hypocoercivity.

papers.title: Hierarchical Multi-Timescale Deep Reinforcement Learning for QoS-Aware AI-RAN Configuration
papers.abstract: Configuring radio access networks (RANs) for heterogeneous services requires coordinating radio parameters whose effects on throughput, delay, and reliability are closely coupled and evolve over different timescales. This paper presents a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for joint, QoS-aware RAN configuration that aligns the learning structure with the real-time, near-real-time, and non-real-time control loops of O-RAN that are also adopted by AI-RAN. Three proximal policy optimization agents jointly select per-user modulation and coding schemes, user-to-bandwidth-part (BWP) assignments, per-BWP transmit power, numerology, and BWP bandwidth weights, at three timescales. The agents share a QoS-aware objective combining throughput demand satisfaction with delay and reliability penalties. We extend ns-3 5G-LENA and integrate it with Ray RLlib through ns3-ai to support the required radio controls, network observations, and hierarchical policy execution. We evaluate the agents' performance in a nine-cell downlink network with inter-cell interference, varying user populations, and mixed URLLC, gaming, conversational-video, and video-streaming traffic. Compared with the baseline 5G-NR RAN, our trained hierarchical DRL agents substantially reduce URLLC and conversational-video delays, lower the residual block error rate, and prevent the near-starvation of the weakest flows, trading off slightly lower throughput for high-rate video streaming under capacity-limited conditions.

papers.title: Optimizing Diameter of r-Gather under Connectivity Constraints from Convex to Connected
papers.abstract: The $r$-gather problem partitions the nodes of an edge-weighted graph into clusters of at least $r$ nodes each. The problem is NP-hard, and known approximation algorithms may return clusters whose induced subgraphs are disconnected. We therefore require each cluster to be connected, or even convex in the existential sense that some shortest path between any two of its members stays inside the cluster. We add a parameterized $\alpha$-ratio-convex variant that interpolates between the two by bounding the induced stretch by a factor $\alpha$. We measure the cost of a clustering by its diameter, the largest pairwise distance within a cluster, rather than by the radius as in the classical formulation. We show that the variants form a hierarchy, that they remain NP-hard in general, and that none of them admits a polynomial-time $(2-\varepsilon)$-approximation unless P=NP. Our main algorithmic result is a polynomial-time algorithm for convex $r$-gather on trees. This contrasts with connected $k$-diameter, which remains hard even on star-like connectivity graphs. On general weighted graphs, we give a $4$-approximation for connected $r$-gather. Extending the tree algorithm to tree decompositions, we obtain an exact algorithm for connected $r$-gather that is fixed-parameter tractable in the treewidth together with $d$ and $r$. Finally, we relate the $\alpha$-ratio-convex variant to $t$-spanners, which yields further approximation guarantees.

papers.title: Stress2Twin: Profile-Driven Network Digital Twins for Guarded Edge Computing Resource Management
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous edge systems require resource managers to determine how many application replicas to deploy, where to place them, and how to distribute incoming requests while satisfying service-level performance constraints. Acquiring the performance knowledge required for these decisions through exhaustive multi-node characterization is measurement-intensive and becomes increasingly difficult as the number of workers and configurations grows. Stress2Twin is a profile-driven Network Digital Twin (NDT) framework that profiles edge nodes independently and composes their measured behavior into a system-level resource-management model. Machine-level oracles characterize latency, throughput, loss, queueing, and power as functions of assigned request rate and replica count. A guarded optimizer derives operating regions and tests neighboring request-rate states before retaining a replica count, reserving capacity before measured nonlinear degradation. Independent profiling of our three-worker Kubernetes testbed requires 271 measured states, corresponding to approximately 4.5 hours, compared with an estimated 123 hours for exhaustive characterization of the considered cluster configuration space. In a single-run ramp evaluation, the selected policy records no latency or loss-threshold violations within the derived 1,650 requests per second (RPS) supported range and reduces estimated power by 27.84% relative to RPS100 Round Robin (RR) placement. An additional single-run evaluation under a non-monotonic workload records no latency violation and 19.67% lower estimated energy than a stabilized RPS50 RR policy. These results show that independently acquired machine profiles can support capacity-aware resource consolidation within a measured operating range. Power savings use an idealized active-worker accounting model.

papers.title: Mass-conservative and phase-consistent transport of phase-confined scalars in front tracking
papers.abstract: In front-tracking multiphase-flow simulations, the Lagrangian front defines the interface geometry and phase regions, while phase-confined scalars are transported independently on a fixed Eulerian mesh. This separation can make the scalar inconsistent with the tracked interface: even a conservative high-order scheme smears the scalar across the interface, leaks it into the other phase and distorts near-interface concentrations despite conserving total mass. We present a transport method that maintains consistency between the scalar and the tracked front while preserving global mass conservation. Instead of the cell-averaged concentration, the method transports the phase-averaged concentration, which is smooth across the interface. This concentration is obtained by dividing the cell-averaged concentration by the phase fraction, extended linearly across the interface and advected. The cell-averaged concentration is rebuilt by multiplying the transported concentration by the front's volume-preserving phase fraction. Because this rebuild can alter the total mass, a uniform shift of the phase-averaged concentration restores it. The method is compared with direct transport of the cell-averaged concentration by the same scheme in five three-dimensional cases: three drops (in translation, in a reversible vortex and with a localized source) and a rising bubble with and without dissolved surfactant. In the four cases without surfactant it reduces the error against the exact solution by more than a factor of ten at the finest resolution and converges faster for the drops. In the surfactant-laden bubble, direct transport leaks 5.5-24% of the surfactant into the wake, depending on resolution, whereas the proposed method keeps it in the bubble.

papers.title: Finding Integral Stable Matchings is PPAD-Complete: Unimodular Hypergraphs, Network $b$-Matchings, and Kernels in Perfect Graphs
papers.abstract: Polyhedral integrality guarantees integral stable solutions in several classical stability problems: stable matchings in normal hypergraphs, stable $b$-matchings in unimodular hypergraphs, and kernels in clique-acyclic orientations of perfect graphs. Whether they can be computed efficiently has been a long-standing open question; for kernels in perfect graphs it has been open since the existence theorem of Boros and Gurvich in 1996. We show that, unless $PPAD\subseteq FP$, they cannot. Finding a stable matching is $PPAD$-complete already in linear unimodular hypergraphs with hyperedges of size at most three and vertex degrees at most three. Consequently, finding a kernel in a clique-acyclic orientation of a perfect graph is $PPAD$-hard even if all cliques have at most three vertices, answering an open question of Pass-Lanneau, Igarashi and Meunier, and stable matchings are $PPAD$-hard to find in balanced and in normal hypergraphs. This contrasts with the polynomial algorithm of Chandrasekaran and Kalathur for network hypergraphs. With capacities, even network hypergraphs are hard: University Dual Admission is $PPAD$-complete with capacities at most nine, so stable $b$-matching is $PPAD$-complete on network hypergraphs with hyperedges of size three. This yields $PPAD$-completeness for a natural class of hospitals/residents markets with couples where stable matchings always exist, and $PPAD$-hardness of computing the near-feasible stable matchings, where capacities are flexible. Both reductions are from PURE CIRCUIT with constant-size gadgets. For unit capacities we use a dual-rail encoding, a symmetry-breaking gadget made of two coupled $2\times2$ stable marriage markets, and a parity criterion on the bipartite incidence graph that certifies total unimodularity. We expect these tools to be useful for further hardness results about problems with guaranteed integral solutions.

papers.title: Occamy: A Semi-Oblivious Reconfigurable Datacenter Network
papers.abstract:
Reconfigurable datacenter networks use fast circuit switches to provide high bandwidth at low cost, thereby emerging as a compelling alternative to packet switching. However, existing designs either react to fine-grained demand, requiring frequent optimization across the network, or remain completely demand-oblivious, requiring all-to-all connectivity that limits the cost benefits of circuit switching.
  We present Occamy, a semi-oblivious reconfigurable datacenter network that implements a tunable level of demand-fitting: it aggregates nodes into tunable-size clusters, and adapts a node-level circuit schedule to the coarse-grained demand between these clusters, thereby leveraging a demand-aware topology without frequent optimization overhead. Results on traditional cloud workloads and an AI training workload show that Occamy significantly improves the cost-performance tradeoff over state-of-the-art oblivious and demand-aware circuit-switched designs, while maintaining low overhead. We demonstrate the practicality of our approach using existing circuit-switched technology, implement an FPGA-based prototype, and evaluate failures.

papers.title: FlexGaze: Weakly Supervised Gaze Estimation at Scale
papers.abstract: Most gaze estimation models are trained on data collected using specialized equipment. The limited diversity of subjects, scenes, and head poses in these datasets hinders generalization to new conditions. We present FlexGaze, a family of 3D gaze estimators pretrained with weak supervision from gaze labels (pseudo-labels) automatically generated from in-the-wild images. We use off-the-shelf models to predict 2D gaze targets and scene depth, then combine these predictions to generate 3D gaze labels for approximately 3.24 million head instances. At inference, FlexGaze predicts gaze from a head crop alone and can handle profile and rear views without requiring face detection or head pose estimation. We use data augmentation during training to improve robustness to variations in crop position and scale. Pretrained using only these generated gaze labels, FlexGaze generalizes to unseen benchmarks. After supervised fine-tuning on public gaze datasets, we evaluate FlexGaze on eight benchmarks under a unified evaluation protocol. Our models match or outperform publicly available gaze estimators with several times as many parameters on most benchmarks. We release our dataset of generated gaze labels, all trained models, and code via https://github.com/ihp-lab/FlexGaze.

papers.title: Control Barrier Functions in Motion Control
papers.abstract: Projection-based controllers (PBCs) have significant engineering success in industrial high-precision motion systems by restricting their input-output behavior to performance-enhancing sector-sets thereby overcoming fundamental limitations of linear control. The projection results in continuous control signals, but their vector fields are discontinuous, potentially causing unwanted excitation of higher-order dynamics in the plant. Inspired by these projected controllers and the recent interest in control barrier functions (CBFs), we propose a new class of CBF-based motion controllers that (i) can mimic and exceed the performance benefits demonstrated by PBCs and (ii) have continuous dynamics thereby resulting in smooth control signals. We specialize our novel CBF-based control design to integrator dynamics, essentially connecting to a projected integrator, called Hybrid Integrator-Gain System (HIGS), thereby introducing CBF-HIGS. We analyze the CBF-HIGS's behavior using a describing function analysis, which reveals improved phase characteristics and a favorable trade-off in higher-order harmonic distortion compared to HIGS. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that CBF-HIGS enhances disturbance attenuation and reduces the excitation of higher-order harmonics compared to HIGS due to its continuous vector field, without compromising robustness properties. The paper provides the first use of CBFs for performance improvement of mechatronic motion systems.

papers.title: Competing climates of the present-day Earth: from Snowball to Hothouse
papers.abstract: Earth today has one climate, but it could have others. With the same continents, the same solar constant and the same pre-industrial CO2, our planet could settle into strikingly different ones. We explore this possibility with BIG-MITgcm, a model which couples atmosphere and ocean circulation with ice sheets and vegetation, and which can be integrated over many millennia. We find five different climates and describe them here. At one extreme is a Snowball, with ice from pole to pole. A Waterbelt also exists, in which sea ice reaches the tropics and only a thin equatorial ribbon of open ocean survives. There is a Cold world much like the Last Glacial Maximum, a Warm climate in which we live in today, and a Hot world in which the Atlantic overturning circulation has collapsed. Each state is held in place by its own balance of competing feedbacks. Ocean heat transport anchors each climate, holding the ice edge where that transport is weak. The familiar climate of the past 10 thousand years is perhaps just one of several possibilities. This has implications for glacial-interglacial transitions and the risk of crossing global tipping points in the future.

papers.title: Multi-Epoch Batch Least-Squares Positioning on the Lunar Surface Using LuGRE GPS L1 C/A Pseudorange Measurements
papers.abstract: The Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment (LuGRE) mission captured Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals in the lunar region, yielding position, velocity, and timing estimates. Analysis of onboard lunar-surface position estimates shows kilometer-level positioning errors due to the long propagation distances, limited measurements, and unfavorable GNSS geometry. This paper presents time-multiplexed positioning using publicly available LuGRE L1 C/A pseudorange measurements. The proposed approach accumulates measurements by exploiting the receiver's stationary position in the Lunar-Centered Lunar-Fixed frame after landing. The effects of the number of accumulated epochs, receiver altitude constraint using coarse a-priori information, straight-line tangential altitude threshold, and minimum number of measurements required per epoch are examined. Compared with single-epoch least-squares positioning, this approach substantially improves positioning performance using single-band, single-constellation signals. With selected combinations of these parameters, batches of epochs randomly selected from multiple operations yield 100-m-level accuracy at the 67th percentile.

papers.title: Lean Census: A Distributional Analysis of AI-Generated Lean Code
papers.abstract: We compare two human-written and four AI-generated Lean libraries with Mathlib through the distributions of simple statistics of their code. For each library we measure inline claims in proofs, proof length, how often each declaration is used, and design choices such as instances and private declarations, and we read each against the variation among Mathlib's own areas. The AI-generated libraries have more inline claims per theorem, longer proofs, fewer instances, and more private declarations than the human-written ones. We release the code for the analysis as a package, lean-census, at https://github.com/project-numina/lean-census.

authors.name: Pietro Pellegrino
authors.institution: Azienda Ospedaliera Citta' della Salute e della Scienza di Torino

papers.title: Separating physics from discrepancy: Orthogonalized kernels for physics-encoded system identification
papers.abstract: Physics-encoded identification combines a physical model with a data-driven correction, but the data alone do not determine how the input-output map is split between them: components representable by the physical model may be assigned to either part. In kernel-based model embedding, this allocation is governed by the kernel. As a consequence, the physical parameters lack a well-defined target. In this work, this ambiguity is resolved a priori by defining a canonical physical parameter as the parameter of the physical model that best approximates the noise-free map, in a weighted least-squares sense, over a user-defined operating domain, together with an orthogonal discrepancy. Specifically, an orthogonalized kernel is derived that restricts the correction to functions orthogonal to the physical model. The resulting estimator keeps the closed-form solution of model embedding, while the canonical parameter depends only on the prescribed geometry, not on the kernel or the data. As the inputs become dense and the noise vanishes, the set of parameters consistent with the data converges to the canonical parameter, a property that generally fails without orthogonalization. Under energy-bounded noise, suitable regularization attains optimal worst-case estimation accuracy. Numerical examples demonstrate consistent parameter estimates across different kernels and experiments.

authors.name: Martina Mammarella
authors.institution: Institute of Electronics, Computer and Telecommunication Engineering

papers.title: Parallel batch scheduling for optimizing hospital sterilization operations: arc-flow formulations, column generation and Lagrangian heuristics for flowtime minimization
papers.abstract: In a recent work by Schlembach et al., the problem of optimally managing sterilization operations in hospitals has been modeled as a machine scheduling problem with parallel batch processing and minimum flowtime objective, and heuristically solved by column generation. We draw upon this approach, developing arc-flow formulations and related column-generation procedures, using an exact dynamic programming algorithm to solve the pricing problems. We further derive Lagrangian relaxations based on minimum cost flows and shortest paths, with subgradient optimization and the volume algorithm guiding batch generation. A makespan bound for schedules minimizing total flow time provides a finite horizon when no operational limit is known. Computational experiments on literature benchmarks and more challenging generated instances demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches. The arc-flow model solves all literature benchmark instances to proven optimality within seconds, while the Lagrangian heuristics deliver high-quality schedules with substantially reduced computational effort.

papers.title: Probabilistic Timed Automata with Multiple Sure and Threshold Objectives
papers.abstract: Probabilistic timed automata extend the classical timed automata formalism with discrete probabilistic choice over edges. We consider the case of the verification of a combination of multiple objectives of probabilistic timed automata, where the objectives can be non-probabilistic (referring to sure satisfaction of all behaviors) and probabilistic (referring to a probability threshold), and refer to reachability or $\omega$-regular properties on executions expressed using parity conditions. We show that existing algorithms for multiple objectives for finite-state Markov decision processes can be applied, using the classical region-graph construction, to obtain algorithms for the corresponding objectives of probabilistic timed automata. In particular, the verification of a probabilistic timed automata against multiple probabilistic-threshold sink-reachability objectives subject to the almost-sure divergence of time is EXPTIME-complete, while verification against the combination of a sure property, including sure divergence of time, and a single probabilistic-threshold parity objective is in NEXPTIME $\cap$ coNEXPTIME.

papers.title: MobileNeTTT: a Lightweight DNN-based Time-To-Transit Estimator for Visual Navigation
papers.abstract: Time-to-Transit (TTT) is a perceptual cue, proxy for depth, that can be computed in the visual cortex, allowing animals to estimate the time remaining to move past features in the environment. We show how TTT can be estimated and used for bio-inspired navigation of a mobile robot equipped with a monocular camera. The paper describes a lightweight neural network estimation method, named MobileNeTTT, that (1) uses the full field of view and provides a rich array of visual feature TTT estimates; (2) is relatively insensitive to camera rotation; and (3) automatically adjusts to the geometry of the path and the presence of obstacles. Because TTT is a coarse visual cue, it is far simpler to use for robot navigation than current large visual depth foundation models. Our navigation model uses a 1.95M-parameter network that is two to three orders of magnitude smaller than well-known large vision foundation models, making it able to run in real time on edge hardware. Simulation and actual laboratory experiments validate the proposed approach in dynamic and spatially complex environments. Code, data, and video are available.

papers.title: Spatial dimensionality affects the convective thawing of permafrost
papers.abstract: Permafrost thaw is one of the major consequences of ongoing climate change, with potentially far-reaching implications for high-latitude and high-altitude environments. Because permafrost degradation is a subsurface phenomenon, its dynamics and future evolution are primarily investigated through numerical models. Yet, the role of groundwater convection in permafrost thawing is an underrepresented process. Here, we explore how the spatial dimensionality affects the simulation of permafrost thaw and heat transport within the thawed layer, known as the active layer. Using two- and three-dimensional (2D and 3D) simulations, with realistic parameter sets that enable convection, we show that permafrost thawing rate and heat transport are systematically slower in 2D than in 3D simulations. The ice-water interface develops spatial patterns that coincides with the underlying convective structures, with rising cold plumes and descending warm plumes shaping its morphology. These findings reveal a coupling between convective flow structures and the evolving geometry of the permafrost boundary, and highlight the importance of three-dimensional representations of subsurface heat transport for accurately capturing permafrost thaw dynamics in land-surface models.

papers.title: Boosting zero-shot learning through neuro-symbolic integration
papers.abstract: Zero-shot learning (ZSL) aims to train deep neural networks to recognize objects from unseen classes, starting from a semantic description of the concepts. Neuro-symbolic (NeSy) integration refers to a class of techniques that incorporate symbolic knowledge representation and reasoning with the learning capabilities of deep neural networks. However, to date, few studies have explored how to leverage NeSy techniques to inject prior knowledge during the training process to boost ZSL capabilities. Here, we present Fuzzy Logic Prototypical Network (FLPN) that formulates the classification task as prototype matching in a visual-semantic embedding space, which is trained by optimizing a NeSy loss. Specifically, FLPN exploits the Logic Tensor Network (LTN) framework to incorporate background knowledge in the form of logical axioms by grounding a first-order logic language as differentiable operations between real tensors. This prior knowledge includes class hierarchies (classes and macroclasses) along with robust high-level inductive biases. The latter allow, for instance, to handle exceptions in class-level attributes and to enforce similarity between images of the same class, preventing premature overfitting to seen classes and improving overall performance. % CHECK: original sentence had no verb ("Both class-level and attribute-level prototypes through an attention mechanism ...") FLPN learns both class-level and attribute-level prototypes, the latter through an attention mechanism specialized for either convolutional- or transformer-based backbones. FLPN achieves state-of-the-art performance on the GZSL benchmarks AWA2 and SUN, matching or exceeding the performance of competing algorithms with minimal computational overhead. The code is available at https://github.com/FrancescoManigrass/FLPN

papers.title: Beyond the Blueprint: The Continuing Evolution of Turing's Theory of Morphogenesis
papers.abstract: Turing's article ``The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis'' has profoundly influenced conceptual views on the emergence of biological form across scales and species. It has also served as a foundational framework to guide experimental investigations into the mechanisms that underlie pattern formation. In this article, we trace the historical development of Turing's ideas and examine their integration into contemporary research programs. We critically assess the broad and often overlapping concepts that have derived from Turing's work, both highlighting value in productive applications of the theory and suggesting that skepticism should remain in overly simplistic validations. By clarifying these concepts and their intrinsic limitations, we rethink contemporary approaches aimed at understanding the essential principles that govern biological pattern formation. We pose some important challenges that will require interdisciplinary expertise to overcome, and which will necessitate fundamentally new paradigms to understand the physical origin of Darwin's ``endless forms most beautiful''.

papers.title: Reflected Elastic Diffusions
papers.abstract: We study the reflected elastic diffusion (RED), the pathwise counterpart of Feller's elastic boundary condition for a one-dimensional diffusion on $[0,\infty)$ with time-homogeneous, continuous drift and diffusion coefficients. Given a diffusion $X$ reflecting at zero, we construct a Feller process $\widetilde X$ by killing $X$ at the first time its local time at zero exceeds an independent exponential random variable. We characterize the infinitesimal generator of $\widetilde X$ explicitly and prove that its domain satisfies a Robin boundary condition, thereby identifying $\widetilde X$ as a probabilistic representation of Feller's analytical characterization of the elastic boundary. A key analytical ingredient, of independent interest, is a pair of moment asymptotics, as $t\downarrow 0$, for the boundary local time of a reflected diffusion, extending known results for the unreflected case. Uniqueness in law of $\widetilde X$ among Feller REDs sharing the same interior dynamics is established through a resolvent/boundary-value-problem argument. The result extends the classical It\^o-McKean construction of elastic Brownian motion to time-homogeneous diffusions, closing the gap between analytic and probabilistic treatments of elastic killing used in recent applied models.

The companion probabilistic question — how to construct, path by path, a process whose generator satisfies a prescribed boundary condition — was answered by Itô and McKean in their complete treatment of Brownian motion on the half-line for arbitrary (κ,δ,β)(\kappa,\delta,\beta) [15, 16]. In recent years there has been a renewed interest in these two boundary behaviours. The literature on sticky boundaries has grown through a series of papers addressing the problem of representing sticky processes as solutions of SDEs: this question was revisited for the sticky Brownian motion in [8], and solved for the first time for sticky Bessel processes and sticky Feller diffusions in [23] and [20] respectively; both papers also provide a closed-form expression for the transition density function. The elastic boundary condition has likewise attracted renewed attention: [7] has extended the elastic Brownian motion to the case with (constant) drift, while [5] considered an elastic Brownian motion on a C2C^{2} domain which, instead of being killed at the boundary, restarts from a random position in the interior.

Beyond the classical Brownian setting, elastic killing has recently resurfaced in more general systems with non-constant coefficients, arising from applications rather than from an interest in the boundary behaviour itself. In particular, elastic processes have been used as a modelling device in the following papers (potentially among others): [14], whose focus is on the empirical measure of a system of interacting particles representing defaultable entities in a credit risk scenario, construct a system of correlated diffusions with space- and time-dependent drift and diffusion coefficients, each subject to elastic killing at a fixed rate κ\kappa; instead, [9] consider a related but more elaborate mechanism, motivated by a model for an epidemic advancing through a population, in which the killing rate is itself stochastic and the process reflects along a moving boundary. However, the applied papers above refer to such processes as elastic purely on the basis of an analogy with the elastic Brownian motion construction, without exploring the domain of the associated generator, and hence without relating their probabilistic construction to Feller’s analytic classification of boundary points. To the best of our knowledge, the only result in this direction is provided by [4]: starting from a Markov process killed upon reaching a (boundary) point aa, in Section 4 they construct an extension of it by piecing together the excursions from aa that return to aa, generated by a Poisson point process, and then joining the first excursion that either never returns to aa or ends in the cemetery state; the characteristic measure of the Poisson process carries an atom at the cemetery path, which accounts for the killing rate. They then study the L2L^{2}-infinitesimal generator of the resulting process, whose domain is determined by a flux condition at aa which, for Brownian motion on the half-line, is shown to coincide with the classical Robin condition. This construction is abstract and excursion-theoretic, and the boundary condition is explicitly identified as the Robin one only in the Brownian case.

papers.title: The Gamma-ray Luminosity Function of Fermi BL Lacertae Objects
papers.abstract: We have used the largest sample of gamma-ray-selected Fermi BL Lacertae objects (1035 BL Lacs) ever used to determine the luminosity function and its evolution through cosmic time. This sample has its survey biases and selection effects well studied and a robust calculation of its detection efficiency. It spans a large range in luminosity ($L_{\gamma,min}$ = $5.71\times10^{40}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and $L_{\gamma,max}$ = $1.76\times10^{48}$ erg s$^{-1}$) and redshift ($ 0 < z \lesssim 4 $). We find that the local luminosity function follows a double power law. The density evolution of BL Lacs depends on the luminosity of the objects, with low-luminosity objects showing negative evolution (i.e., they are less common in the past) and high-luminosity objects showing positive evolution (i.e., they are more common in the past). We confirm that gamma-ray selected BL Lacs and FSRQs evolve similarly depending on their luminosities.

papers.title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment. We propose a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model. This framework integrates the dynamics model into an on-policy reinforcement learning pipeline, letting the performance of the policy align with the empirical target dynamics. Experimental validations on bipedal locomotion tasks demonstrate competitive adaptability under extreme physical variations, including a payload reaching 80% of self-weight and an oil-lubricated low-friction surface.

papers.title: Multiorbital driving of quantum geometric nonlinear transport in oxide interfaces
papers.abstract: Quantum geometry plays a relevant role in determining the intrinsic non-linear transport properties of low-dimensional electron systems. Here, we theoretically investigate the quantum geometric contribution to the non-linear conductivity in $\text{SrTiO}_3$-based two-dimensional electron gases, comparing the prototypical (001) and (111) crystallographic interface orientations. Using a multi-orbital tight-binding approach, we uncover the crucial role of the multiband electronic structure in determining the quantum-geometric contribution to nonlinear transport. In particular, we show how the hybridization of $t_{2g}$ orbitals near avoided band crossings shapes the momentum-space distribution of the band-normalized quantum metric and the resulting nonlinear conductivity. Furthermore, we reveal a strong dependence on crystal orientation: while the (001) interface exhibits sharp peak-and-dip features confined around Lifshitz transitions, the trigonal symmetry of the (111) interface promotes strong orbital mixing. Our results highlight how the interplay between orbital hybridization and crystallographic orientation gives rise to distinct quantum-geometric nonlinear transport responses in oxide interfaces.

papers.title: Site-Conditioned Boundary Closure for Subsurface Seepage Forecasting and Relief Placement
papers.abstract: Truncating a large heterogeneous diffusion model around a localized, threshold-activated outlet saves degrees of freedom but severs exterior feedback that governs when the outlet opens and how much it discharges. By separating forcing-driven background head from local withdrawal drawdown, Site-Conditioned Boundary Closure (SCBC) maps local physical descriptors to positive exchange coefficients at the cut boundary. Supervised on unforced donor-domain withdrawal responses, these coefficients yield a passivity-preserving reduced operator that generalizes across unseen forcing histories without refitting. We evaluate SCBC on flood-driven subsurface seepage beneath levee foundations against full-grid reference simulations (MODFLOW~6). Across three held-out foundation panels, a single frozen SCBC tree estimator reduced peak-discharge log RMSE by 26.1%, 30.9% and 42.6% relative to identical local patches using a shared boundary coefficient. We then test whether better screening forecasts improve constrained placement, minimizing peak landside toe head subject to a discharge capacity limit and a budget of three sequential full-grid checks. On a separate 36-foundation test using a coarser 30-state ring operator, a neural SCBC estimator improved discharge forecasts across candidates yet selected four over-capacity placements before checks, compared with one for a shared-coefficient ring, which recovered all 144 reference optima after three checks.

papers.title: Adaptive Precision Incomplete Matrix Factorization
papers.abstract: Incomplete factorizations are widely used to precondition Krylov subspace methods for solving large sparse linear systems. Recent work has explored computing approximate factorizations in low precision, but using only one uniformly low precision limits the achievable accuracy and can degrade the quality of the preconditioner. We propose adaptive precision incomplete factorization algorithms in which we store each entry of the factors in a precision chosen according to its magnitude and a target accuracy. We present a rounding error analysis showing that the adaptive precision threshold-based incomplete LU and incomplete Cholesky factorizations achieve a backward error of the order of the target accuracy. We also discuss how to incorporate pivoting and scaling and how to perform the triangular solves with the adaptive precision factors. Finally, we explain how the approach applies to memory-limited incomplete Cholesky factorizations by using the magnitude of the largest dropped entry as the target accuracy. Numerical experiments on a wide range of matrices from the SuiteSparse collection show that adaptive precision can substantially reduce the storage required by the factors without degrading the quality of the preconditioner and improve the storage-weighted iteration count and overall storage required compared with uniform 64-, 32-, and 16-bit factorizations.

papers.title: Revisiting the role of reorthogonalisation in LSQR
papers.abstract: In this paper, we revisit the role of reorthogonalisation in the LSQR method for large-scale overdetermined linear least-squares problems. Motivated primarily by practical applications where matrix--vector products dominate the computational cost and only a limited number of iterations can be afforded because of time and/or memory restrictions, we investigate when reorthogonalisation can significantly accelerate convergence. Through synthetic test problems with controlled singular value distributions and experiments on practical sparse problems, we demonstrate that reorthogonalisation is particularly beneficial when the least-squares matrix has large outlying singular values. In such cases, loss of orthogonality can severely delay convergence. We explore the effectiveness of full (one-sided) reorthogonalisation when using LSQR, and present alternative reorthogonalisation strategies that can provide substantial acceleration compared to no reorthogonalisation and significant storage savings compared to full reorthogonalisation. The possibility of using low precision arithmetic for the reorthogonalisation is also investigated. We present bounds that demonstrate the quality of the solution depends on the level of orthogonality maintained by the selected reorthogonalisation strategy. Our results suggest that reorthogonalisation should be regarded as a practical tool for modern least-squares applications that can be employed instead of, or in addition to, preconditioning.

papers.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
papers.abstract: Agentic Robotics, in which foundation models act as coding agents to control robots through executable programs, has emerged as a compelling paradigm for embodied intelligence. Yet unlike software engineering, where massive executable environments power post-training, robotics remains constrained by small, manual benchmarks and in-distribution evaluation. To bridge this gap, we introduce RoboUniverse-10K, 10,807 interactive, resettable, and verifiable physics environments built from real-world videos via an automated Real2Sim and quality assurance pipeline. Each runs in an isolated, Harbor-compatible harness that hides privileged states and grading logic to mirror real-world sensing. From the same pipeline, we hold out 500 unseen tasks to establish RoboUniverse-Verified, an expert-verified zero-shot benchmark. Evaluating 11 closed- and open-source models reveals a huge gap: frontier models reach 85.8\% success, while open-source baselines lag at 2.6\% to 10.0\%, bottlenecked by low-level grasping, deformable-object manipulation, and post-contact physical control. Finally, we collect about 17K multi-turn trajectories totaling 0.79B tokens with GPT-6 Astra and perform full-parameter supervised fine-tuning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, yielding RoboUniverse-35B-A3B. Our model achieves substantial zero-shot gains on RoboUniverse-Verified, lifting the success rate from 0.8\% to 21.2\%, while achieving zero-shot task completions across LIBERO-MAX, RoboCasa, RoboTwin 2.0, and a real Franka arm. We open-source the RL-ready environments and model to lay the foundation for large-scale reinforcement learning in Agentic Robotics.

papers.title: Co-Defining Transparency for Clinical AI: A Replicable Participatory Methodology
papers.abstract: Transparency is the most invoked safeguard for clinical AI, yet frameworks (e.g. the EU AI Act, FUTURE-AI) are specified top-down by regulators and technical experts, not bottom-up by the frontline users whose trust and adoption they should calibrate. This disconnect exacerbates the central deployment failure of clinical AI, miscalibrated reliance and adoption (such as automation bias, deskilling, or disuse), which technical explanation alone does not resolve. We argue that "how much transparency, of what kind, and for whom" is an empirical, context-dependent question, and present a replicable participatory methodology to answer it, instantiated at a large European university hospital. A cumulative chain of six workshops engages an inter-professional panel (clinicians, patient and caregiver partners, students) in agnostic, open-ended elicitation: 274 stakeholder verbatims and external benchmarks (eCH-0272, EU AI Act, Stanford FMTI) yield 20 indicators (18 prioritised and 2 recovered at a later stage), rated across five clinical scenarios of graduated intervention before and after technical briefings, discussed with legal experts, and translated into concrete implementation features. As an existence proof, the use case yields decision-useful signals: human review of automated decisions is the single most critical transparency indicator (84% of participants), and required transparency for adoption rises monotonically with the perceived risk of intervention, corroborating WHO risk-proportionality. A short explainability briefing did not substantially shift participants' transparency requirements. Of 151 evaluated AI transparency solutions, 79 were accepted as-is, covering (at least partially) 17 out of the 20 selected indicators. We position the six-workshop protocol (not its single-site outcomes) as the transferable artefact and release all instruments to support replication.

papers.title: Real-time event-level zero-shot learning at 150 ns: towards a foundation model for particle physics experiment triggering
papers.abstract: The hardware-based Level-1 triggers of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments select collisions with algorithms designed for one signature each, acting on a coarse, low-latency view of every event. We present a learned event embedding for several trigger tasks and evaluate its transfer to processes absent from training. Using paired offline and Level-1 views of the same simulated collisions, we train an offline transformer with a supervised metric loss and distil it, event by event, into a quantised Level-1 transformer whose bit widths are learned under a fixed resource budget. Trained on 25 Standard Model processes, the embedding places 28 held-out processes next to their physical relatives. A nearest-neighbour selection against background collisions, which never enter encoder training, rejects 99% of them. It retains a median of 90% of seen and 96% of unseen Standard Model events and 88% of a set of 52 beyond-the-Standard-Model benchmark samples, the best-performing score across the three groups among the baselines evaluated on the same events. A second gate against the seen processes isolates high-mass dilepton signals into label-free clusters, and long-lived signals too when displaced-track information is available. With 7512 parameters and an FPGA latency of 147 ns, the encoder uses one event representation, learned once, to derive several selections, opening the door to a foundation model for the LHC's hardware-based triggers.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels---Part I: Stabilization in Polar Coordinates
papers.abstract: A surface vessel with surge force and yaw moment as inputs and no sway actuation cannot be stabilized at a fixed pose by continuous time-invariant feedback. We introduce a zero-sideslip point, a point whose position relative to the hull depends on the surge and sway speeds and whose velocity points along the vessel's heading at every instant, and show that it moves as a unicycle. This reduction allows the time-invariant, polar-coordinate steering laws of Todorovski et al. (2025) to be applied to the underactuated vessel without modification. With two steering laws, GloBa and BoLSA, we construct strict control Lyapunov functions and prove global asymptotic stability, first for a four-state model with surge speed and yaw rate as virtual inputs, and then, by one step of backstepping, for the full six-state model with surge force and yaw moment. The analysis extends to hulls with fore-aft asymmetric sway-yaw damping, excluded in prior work by the assumption of diagonal damping. Unlike prior time-varying designs, the time-invariant controller yields smooth, non-oscillatory trajectories, an important practical advantage for docking. The designs are validated in simulation on the Cybership I hull model.

papers.title: Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels---Part II: Underway Docking
papers.abstract: In underway directional docking, a second-order nonholonomic problem, six pairs of states of two vehicles have to be made to match by two inputs. The key challenge is to design time-invariant feedback of the relative states and the leader's measured motion only, which makes the follower's convergence in range outpaced, with no sway actuation whatsoever, by the bearing and heading convergence of the follower relative to the leader's path. We begin with nonmodular backstepping, choosing speed and commanded heading jointly to control range and bearing. Curvature compensation and normalization of angular errors by different powers of range remove the range singularity from the model. Our construction passes from unicycle kinematics to the ships' zero-sideslip points and through the sway dynamics to the physical hulls. The design extends to a leader with a different hull and to a docking point astern or abeam of the leader, where we show that, while the leader turns, a follower without sway actuation holds the point only with a heading that differs from the leader's. With strict control Lyapunov construction, we achieve global $\kappa$-exponential convergence, with a rate independent of the initial error.

papers.title: Floquet-Induced Valley Polarization and Topological Phases in Twisted Bilayer Graphene Heterostructures
papers.abstract: We theoretically investigate twisted bilayer graphene (tTBG) heterostructures subjected to circularly polarized light. Inversion symmetry is broken through the combined application of an out-of-plane electric field and the incorporation of insulating substrates, enabling precise control of the valley degrees of freedom and associated topological phases. We identify a regime in which the valley degeneracy is lifted: one valley retains a gapless, linear Dirac-like dispersion, whereas the other develops a finite band gap and becomes electronically inactive. The interplay between Floquet driving and inversion-symmetry breaking induces topological phase transitions characterized by Chern numbers C = -2, C = -1, and C = 0, together with the emergence of perfectly valley-polarized domain-wall channels. Furthermore, magnetic asymmetry arising from proximity to adjacent two-dimensional ferromagnetic contacts enables spin-valley filtering. These findings establish the potential of graphene-based heterostructures as highly tunable systems for controlling spin and valley degrees of freedom.

authors.institution: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

papers.title: Environmental dependence of the properties of H$\alpha$ emitters in the extremely massive galaxy protoclusters BOSS1244 and BOSS1542 at $z = 2.24$
papers.abstract: Protoclusters, the progenitors of galaxy clusters, provide ideal laboratories for studying how high-density environments influence galaxy formation and evolution at early cosmic epochs. It remains unclear whether environmental effects on galaxy properties over scales of $>30$ cMpc are already in place at $z > 2$ and how these effects depend on the evolutionary stage of large-scale structures. We investigate the physical properties of H$\alpha$ emitters (HAEs) in two extremely overdense protoclusters, BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, at $z = 2.24$, and explore the environmental dependence of galaxy properties at this redshift. In BOSS1244, we find a clear color-density and stellar mass-density relation. HAEs in higher-density regions are significantly redder in $z_{\rm s}-K_{\rm s}$ and more massive than those in lower-density regions. In contrast, BOSS1542 shows weak or no such correlations. Red HAEs $(z_{\rm s}-K_{\rm s}>2.5)$ in both fields are preferentially located in the densest cores, have high stellar masses $(>10^{11}\,M_{\odot})$, high SFRs, and are $4-7$ times more abundant than in general fields. The irregular morphologies observed in some red HAEs are consistent with ongoing mass assembly and may be associated with dust-obscured star formation or galaxy interactions. Both protoclusters broadly follow the star-forming main sequence, but BOSS1542 exhibits a steeper slope, indicating more active star formation in massive galaxies. Our results demonstrate that environmental effects on galaxy properties operate over scales of $\sim39$\,cMpc at $z=2.24$, but their manifestation is strongly dependent on the evolutionary state of the large-scale structure. BOSS1244 appears more evolved, with ongoing galaxy merging and possible quenching, while BOSS1542 remains in an early, filamentary, gas-rich phase.

authors.name: Dongdong Shi
authors.institution: Anhui University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Various Kinds of Defining Sets over $\mathbb{Z}_2^\alpha\mathbb{Z}_4^\beta$ and their $Lee$-Weight Distributions
papers.abstract: Recently, a particular type of defining set is being used to get $Lee$-weight distribution over a particular type of ring. However, little work has been done on mixed alphabets. Therefore, in Section 3, we investigate the $Lee$-weight distributions associated with various kinds of defining sets, labelled A to J, for code constructions over the mixed-alphabet ring $R=Z^{\alpha}_2 Z^{\beta}_4$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are positive finite integers. Using Parseval's identity, we determine the cardinalities of the defining sets A to J. We further establish several new results concerning 2-$Lee$-weight and 3-$Lee$-weight distributions.

papers.title: $\mu$- and $q$-extension of special functions in quantum field theory
papers.abstract: Analytic calculations up to single-scale quantities in perturbative quantum field theory result into special numbers and functions, which are generalizations as iterative integrals over special alphabets. In this way one obtains polylogarithms, Nielsen integrals, the iterated integrals over linear denominator terms, cyclotomic letters, letters induced by quadratic forms, and square-root valued letters. The inverse Mellin transform relates special nested sums to these quantities, which are harmonic sums, generalized harmonic sums, nested sums implied by quadratic forms, cyclotomic harmonic sums, and nested sums containing central binomials. We construct the $\mu$- and $q$-extensions of all these special functions. They are expected to occur in loop calculations within $\mu$- and $q$-extended quantum field theories via modified (anti)commutation relations. The $\mu$-extended special functions are quite different form the corresponding $q$-extended functions. While in the former case one observes class-preservation characterized by the polynomial $\mu$-parameter, except for the case of root-valued letters. In the latter case new higher transcendental functions are obtained.

papers.title: Two Rounds Are Already Hard for Loop-Free Updates of Routing Trees
papers.abstract: Updating a routing tree can create loops even when the old and new trees lead to the same destination. A controller chooses which routers update in each round, but their updates may finish in any order. Strong loop freedom therefore requires every partial completion to be acyclic. We show that deciding whether two rounds suffice is NP-complete, even when a safe three-round schedule is supplied. The proof is a linear-size reduction from 3-SAT with one old clause spine and four routers per variable. Three types of mixed cycles enforce consistent literal choices and clause satisfaction. For every nonempty input formula, the constructed instance needs exactly two rounds if the formula is satisfiable and exactly three otherwise.

papers.title: Bridging Continuous-Time MAPF and Industrial AGV Fleet Coordination with Lazy Priority-Based Search
papers.abstract: Continuous-time multi-agent path finding on roadmaps (MAPF$_R$) offers a principled way to coordinate robot fleets with geometric collision avoidance, yet its deployment on industrial automated guided vehicle (AGV) infrastructures remains challenging, as highly connected and redundant roadmaps amplify both safe-interval reasoning and multi-agent interaction handling. To bridge this gap, we formalize AGV-MAPF$_R$-CTC, a configuration-space variant of MAPF$_R$ with precomputed continuous-time conflicts that enables the reuse of MAPF$_R$ solvers for AGV fleet coordination with minimal changes. We then revisit continuous-time priority-based search (CPBS), identifying the boundary conditions required by its safe interval path planning (SIPP) low-level planner under priority-induced constraints and enabling earlier solution detection. As a central contribution, we analyze the structure of the priority search space, clarifying which agents are affected by each priority refinement and when replanning can be avoided. Building on this analysis, we introduce a novel algorithm, Lazy-CPBS, which materializes high-level nodes lazily: a child's plans are computed only when it is expanded, so siblings that are never expanded cost no low-level search. Experiments on standard MAPF benchmarks and on industrial AGV roadmaps imported from a proprietary digital-twin simulator show that CPBS-based solvers remain effective well beyond the agent counts reachable by optimal MAPF$_R$ solvers, while Lazy-CPBS substantially reduces CPBS overhead and offers the most consistent robustness/runtime trade-off across industrial layouts.

authors.name: Roberto Olmi
authors.institution: Nello Carrara Institute of Applied Physics

papers.title: CHARMS250V1: A Cryogenic Front-End ASIC for Low-Noise Readout of Charge or Light Signals in Noble Liquid Detectors
papers.abstract: This work presents the design and measurement results of CHARMS250V1, a next-generation cryogenic front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed using a 65 nm CMOS process. It is designed for low-noise readout of charge or light signals generated in noble liquid detectors. CHARMS250V1 is a single channel prototype whose design in the future will be integrated within a 16-channel ASIC. It comprises pre-amplification and pulse shaping stages that provide programmable charge gain between 4.3 mV/fC and 25 mV/fC, peaking time programmable between 250 ns and 2 us, and programmable baseline of either 200 mV or 900 mV for processing of unipolar and bipolar signals, respectively.

authors.name: Niccolo' Gallice
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Giovanni Pinaroli
authors.institution: Laboratoire d’Annecy de Physique des Particules

papers.title: Evaluating the Participation of Proactive Scouting Agents in Real-time Human Team Meetings
papers.abstract: An open research question is whether the addition of conversational AI agents to real-time discussions among human teams enhances group performance. This study tested the value of adding proactive scouting agents to teams engaged in collaborative forecasting tasks. These agents were designed to (i) monitor the groupwise discussion in real-time, (ii) identify critical information gaps in the group deliberation, (iii) autonomously find and retrieve relevant information, and (iv) express the acquired content into the conversation using emulated groupwise human etiquette. In a controlled set of trials, small human teams of 4 or 5 members were tasked with collaboratively predicting the outcome of 34 Major League Baseball (MLB) games, either by forecasting the winning team or by predicting the total number of runs scored. In half the trials, the groups were assisted by proactive scouting agents. The other half were human-only deliberations. When tasked with predicting the winning team, the addition of proactive scouting agents to the group discussion significantly increased forecasting accuracy, reducing the predictive mean-absolute error by 25% (p=0.006) and improving raw predictive accuracy from 60.0% to 76.4% (p=0.050). When predicting the total number of runs scored across both teams, the addition of proactive scouting agents yielded no statistical change in group performance. It should be noted that the human participants in this study were significantly worse at predicting the number of runs scored. This may have led to random outcomes in those forecasting trials. Still, the results of this study demonstrate that deploying proactive scouting agents can significantly boost forecasting accuracy during real-time team deliberations when participants possess baseline forecasting skill.

papers.title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
papers.abstract: Understanding a system that can be run but not inspected is a core engineering skill: one designs experiments, forms hypotheses about hidden state and timing, discards those that observations refute, and finally builds a replacement that works and is efficient. To evaluate this capability of LLM agents in the hardware domain, we present ChiProgramBench, 18 tasks derived from open-source processors, accelerators, codecs, transforms, interconnects, and control circuits. Agents can only drive and read the pins of a hidden, stateful simulated reference, then submit a gate-level netlist made of public library cells. Agents work in two settings: black-box discovery gives only anonymized functional pins and the interfaces of fixed memories, while function-guided reconstruction adds the circuit's purpose and each pin's role. Hidden test cases compare outputs with the reference cycle by cycle; power, delay, and area earn credit relative to the reference only when every case passes. Across 432 trials of 6 LLM agent configurations, successful agents recover algorithms and numerical conventions, yet only 12.0% of black-box and 14.8% of function-guided trials pass every case. Function-guided reconstruction raises the mean functional score, the cycle-weighted share of passed cases, from 24.6% to 30.9%. Of the 58 fully passing designs, only three improve on the reference's combined power, area, and delay, so behavioral recovery and efficient implementation remain distinct challenges.

authors.name: Kuan Li
authors.institution: Anhui University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Mean First Passage Times for Loop-Erased Random Walks and Erased-Loop Size Distributions on Graphs
papers.abstract: Loop-erased random walks provide a natural way to extract self-avoiding trajectories from ordinary random walks by chronologically removing loops. They are deeply connected with uniform spanning trees: the loop-erased path between two vertices has the same distribution law as the unique path connecting these vertices in a random spanning tree. In this work, we use this connection as a computational framework for finite graphs. First, using the classical transfer-current theorem, we obtain an explicit formula for the mean first passage time of loop-erased random walks. The resulting expression returns the expected length of the loop-erased path as a weighted sum over simple paths, where the weights are exact determinantal probabilities obtained from the spanning-tree kernel. Second, we express the distribution of erased loop sizes in the same framework. This distribution measures the scale of the redundant excursions removed during loop erasure and provides information that is complementary to effective path length. The approach is applied to arbitrary finite graphs and then specialized to complete graphs, cycle graphs, and motif-based networks, where explicit formulas and asymptotic behaviors are obtained. Numerical experiments show strong agreement between the theoretical predictions and Monte Carlo simulations. The results provide a unified method for quantifying both the effective paths kept by loop erasure and the loops removed during random exploration of networks.

papers.title: Analytical modelling of compliance dynamics under fiscal feedback: tipping thresholds, intervention costs and hysteresis
papers.abstract: Compliance with taxes and other collective obligations is often enforced with resources that come from those who comply, so that non-compliance erodes its own deterrent. We develop an exactly solvable dynamical model of compliance under this fiscal feedback. Individuals choose between paying and evading by imitating those who do better, and the budget against evasion is a share of the revenue, split between enforcement and education. The model yields closed-form expressions for the equilibria, the tipping thresholds and their bifurcations, the budgets needed to maintain compliance and to restore it after a collapse, and the recovery time near the threshold. Fiscal feedback alone does not produce tipping points: hysteresis appears only when an instrument that changes individual incentives, such as fines or education, is funded by the tax base. Stronger sanctions reduce both the maintenance and the rescue budget, but beyond a critical level they make the system bistable, so that the choice of sanction is a trade-off between efficiency and resilience, which we quantify with a resilience indicator and a resilience-constrained design problem. The cheapest allocation of the budget between enforcement and education is also obtained in closed form. A sensitivity analysis identifies the parameters that control prevention and recovery costs, and stochastic simulations of individual agents and a slow budget cycle confirm the analytical predictions. The framework provides quantitative guidelines for allocating scarce intervention resources in tax compliance and in other enforcement problems with similar feedbacks.

authors.name: Francisco J. Munoz
authors.institution: Center for the Development of Nanoscience and Nanotechnology

papers.title: Complex band-limited maximum likelihood: estimating the wave behind detected quanta
papers.abstract: Detected photons and electrons land at positions drawn from $|\psi|^2$, yet it is $\psi$, phase included, that a wave equation propagates, and the state that produced the particles is often known only in part. A density estimator can recover $|\psi|^2$ directly from the positions, without any wave equation, but it discards the phase, and with it the state. We introduce complex band-limited maximum likelihood (complex BLML), which estimates $\psi$ itself by maximising the likelihood of the detected positions over exactly the intensities the physics allows: squared moduli of complex functions whose spectrum lies in a given set, such as a band, the shape of the aperture, or several modes for a partially coherent source. A single eigenvalue can certify a global maximum. On simulated two-slit far fields we measure what each prior is worth: a band reaches a given accuracy with seven times fewer photons than a kernel density estimate and already gives the fringe contrast and the relative phase, and the shape of the aperture adds the slit geometry. Some quantities need a prior at any number of photons: for slits of one profile the intensity fixes only the contrast $2\rho V/(1+\rho^2)$, and on a line two different apertures can produce the same particles. Cutting a pattern to a few fringes, as published records are, removes the slit width. On four public single-particle double-slit records it predicts held-out particles best among the methods we tested, kernel estimators and two-slit optical models included, and it recovers the fringe contrast without a model of the optics. On fluorescent beads it finds the resolution limit of the microscope, $2\mathrm{NA}/\lambda$, from the photons alone.

papers.title: Exact superdiffusion exponents and hull exploration of chiral random walkers on critical percolation clusters
papers.abstract: Generalizing de Gennes' ant-in-the-labyrinth concept, we consider a chiral random walker on a percolation cluster at criticality. The fully chiral ant clings to obstacle boundaries and traces the fractal hulls of the cluster, spreading with the exact walk dimension $7/4$ until its orbit closes. Because the cluster contains holes on all scales, the ensemble spreads superdiffusively, $\langle r^2\rangle\sim t^{89/84}$, carried by a diminishing fraction of walkers whose orbits are still open. Both exponents follow from percolation geometry alone, and agree well with large-scale numerical simulations. When the walker turns chirally only with probability $\chi<1$, superdiffusion gives way to the subdiffusion of the ant at a crossover time set by both exponents, with a diffusion coefficient enhanced by $(1-\chi)^{-2/d_w}$. The relation between crossover time and diffusion coefficient does not depend on how chirality is realized, offering a direct test for chiral tracers in disordered media.

papers.title: ApexID: Hierarchical Learning for Multi-Species Animal Re-Identification
papers.abstract: Animal re-identification (Re-ID) must distinguish individuals across species and capture conditions. We introduce ApexID, a hierarchical SphereFace2-based loss that integrates global identity discrimination with balanced animal-category supervision. Using 132,533 images curated from 19 public datasets, we evaluate three model families and four objectives on four external datasets with observation-aware retrieval protocols. ApexID achieves a dataset-averaged Rank-1 accuracy of 64.89% with ConvNeXt-Small and an mAP of 32.54% with MIEW-ID, outperforming their pretrained reference models. On elephants, a category absent from animal Re-ID training, our ConvNeXt-Small variant achieves the highest retrieval performance among the fourteen evaluated configurations. Scores vary by backbone and dataset, and open-set evaluation reveals remaining discovery challenges. These findings support hierarchical category-identity learning to improve transfer to unseen datasets and species.

papers.title: DREAM: Dual-Memory Reasoning for Anticipatory 3D Perception in Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Autonomous driving systems must not only interpret the current scene but also anticipate perceptual challenges such as occlusions, sparse observations, and recurring failure patterns. However, most existing LiDAR semantic segmentation methods operate in a frame-centric manner, processing each scan independently and discarding past contextual experience, which limits robustness under dynamic scene changes. We propose DREAM, a Dual-memory REAsoning framework for continual LiDAR seMantic segmentation that reframes perception as an experience-driven and anticipatory process. DREAM maintains two complementary memory banks in a strictly online setting: a latent memory that stores compact semantic abstractions of previously observed scenes, and an error memory that records representations associated with uncertain predictions. At each timestep, relevant memory entries are retrieved via cosine similarity and integrated into the feature space through a lightweight modulation mechanism, enabling the model to reinforce consistent semantic patterns while suppressing recurring failure modes. The backbone remains frozen and no past scans are replayed, ensuring computational efficiency and bounded memory growth. Extensive experiments on multiple large-scale LiDAR benchmarks demonstrate that DREAM achieves state-of-the-art performance, with consistent improvements on dynamic and small-scale objects, highlighting the effectiveness of persistent and error-aware memory for robust long-horizon perception.

authors.name: Athira Nambiar
authors.institution: SRM Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
papers.abstract: Animating arbitrary 3D assets from instructions requires both structural inference and motion control, yet existing motion benchmarks mostly cover conventional human or animal skeletons with simple instructions. We introduce DivDynBench, which evaluates rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories, with instructions requiring multi-phase part coordination and explicit timing, angle, repetition, and trajectory constraints. With large language models, we systematically compare three common paradigms: specialized motion generation, video generation followed by motion recovery, and direct agent-driven generation. We analyze their control capabilities, cross-morphology adaptability, and generation costs. Guided by this comparison, we propose an Agentic Motion Framework in which an agent writes compact parametric skeleton and motion programs, and a deterministic executor performs rigging, kinematic solving, and geometric correction. Compact parameter control reduces generation overhead and improves rigging reliability and motion-control accuracy, providing practical guidance for deploying complex 3D motion generation.

papers.title: Exact edge cover by strict and non-strict temporal walks
papers.abstract: Exact edge cover asks whether the edges of a temporal graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges can be partitioned into time-respecting walks with a prescribed number of walks starting at each vertex and, in the fixed-end variant, ending at each vertex. For non-strict walks, we prove that the problem is polynomially solvable by a new approach based on M-convexity, which also closes a gap in the proof sketch of an earlier static reduction. An orientation of the edges is realizable by walks exactly when walk counters stay non-negative and every snapshot component contains a walk, and only components with all degrees and counters even can violate the latter condition. Once a dead state is removed, the states of each such component form an M-convex set. This yields an augmenting path algorithm that returns walks or an infeasibility certificate, using at most $m/2$ augmentations and $O(n+nm^2)$ arithmetic operations with path-reversing re-orientation. The implementation was validated on small instances. For strict walks, we prove that the problem is NP-complete, already with six time labels for prescribed ends and two for free ends.

papers.title: Ballistic propagation-mediated super-resolution light-element imaging: in-situ tracking dynamic hydrogen migration
papers.abstract: Transmission electrons - with few-picometer wavelengths - can theoretically resolve all atoms in solids. However, constrained by factors such as lens aberrations, Z-contrast dependence and poor temporal resolution, the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) fails to tackle the long-standing challenge of hydrogen dynamics on atomic scale. Here, our experiment-guided simulations reveal that unlike heavy-atom imaging - governed by wave-based imaging process - ballistic propagation of particle-like electrons in Cs-corrected TEM enables super-resolution imaging (SRI) of light atoms, achieving a resolution down to 14 pm and a robust hydrogen contrast of ~24%. Our in-situ SRI study not only uncovers polymetric hydrogen aggregation in TiHx and H-LaAlO3, but also inter-site migration, rotational displacement of hydrogen species and collective hydrogen tunneling-induced polarization surge in the oxide. By exploiting the novel electron-matter interactions, our findings offer an unparalleled approach to probe hydrogen dynamics and establish accurate structure-property relationships in diverse functional materials.

authors.name: Zhiyao Liang
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Chemistry for Energy Materials

authors.name: Hua Bing Tao
