papers.title: Eigenvector geometry and spectra of doubly stochastic matrices
papers.abstract: Let $U_N$ be the union of the convex hulls of the $k$th roots of unity for $1\le k\le N$. We prove that, for $N\ge10^{213}$, every convex combination of two permutation matrices of order $N$ has spectrum in $U_N$. The ordered pairs of columns selected in the rows form directed cycles. The proof uses the winding about the origin and the Fourier coefficients of the eigenvector coordinates along one cycle. For arbitrary doubly stochastic matrices, we form a polygon by assigning distinct columns to selected eigenvector coordinates. Near a root of unity of exact order $q\le N$, the full eigenvalue region agrees locally with the regular $q\lfloor N/q\rfloor$-gon. For $N\ge256$, suppose an eigenvalue lies outside $U_N$. In every associated eigenvector $v$ normalised by $\max_i|v_i|=1$, some coordinate $v_j$ lies strictly inside the convex hull of the coordinates and satisfies $|v_j|^2>1-100/N$.

papers.title: How Far Can Linear Go? BiPert, a Unified Framework for Single-Cell Perturbation Modelling
papers.abstract: Understanding how genetic perturbations affect cellular behaviour is essential for studying gene function and regulatory mechanisms. Large-scale CRISPR screens measure these effects across thousands of genes, but cover relatively few cellular contexts. Predicting perturbation responses in unseen cell types and identifying perturbed genes from their transcriptional effects therefore remain challenging. Here, we show that both tasks can be addressed through a common linear decomposition of transcriptional responses into shared and perturbation-specific components. Building on this principle, we introduce BiPert, a simple linear framework for both forward perturbation prediction and inverse identification. For forward prediction, BiPert outperforms existing methods that use no external biological knowledge when predicting gene expression changes in unseen cell lines. Its few-shot extension, BiPert-FS, adapts to new cell lines using as few as ten measured perturbations. For inverse identification, BiPert-ID identifies perturbed genes from single-cell expression profiles, outperforming deep-learning methods in unseen cell lines and donors. We further show that perturbations whose effects transfer more consistently across cellular contexts are also easier to identify, even after controlling for perturbation effect size. Together, these results establish a connection between perturbation transfer and identification, and demonstrate that simple linear models provide strong, interpretable baselines for both tasks.

papers.title: The EX~Lupi Asymmetric Micro-jet Revealed with Spectro-astrometry
papers.abstract: EXor variables are a class of young pre-main-sequence stars that show repeated brightenings,likely caused by sudden increases in accretion. Studying their outflow properties, especially during periods of increased activity offers a unique perspective on the accretion-ejection connection in young stars. The aim is to detect and characterise the jet from the prototype EXor variable EX Lupi. Evidence of an outflow driven by EX Lupi has existed for some time but prior to this work, but the jet properties were unknown. This YSO has been monitored for over 100 years and during this time it has undergone increases in magnitude of between 1 and 5 mags which have been connected to increases in the mass accretion rate onto the star. A further aim of this work is to investigate if the jet can be connected to specific accretion events. Spectro-astrometry was applied to UVES spectra collected in 2021 and 2022. HIRES spectra with a similar wavelength range, taken in 2003, 2008 and 2010 were obtained from the Keck Observatory Archive and also analysed with spectro-astrometry. The spatial and kinematic properties of the EX Lupi optical bipolar jet are revealed for the first time. In 2022 the blue-shifted jet is compact.In the same year the red-shifted jet extends to approx 60 au. This finding is significant as it identifies a source that can be used to study the impact of episodes of intense accretion on jet launching. The strongest detection of the jet is in 2010, between the 2008 outburst and the 2022 burst, which points to a new ejection event triggered by the 2008 outburst. Evidence of enhanced ejection connected to a 2002 burst is also presented. No change in the jet is observed during the 2022 burst. However, we are hindered here by the limitations of the technique.

papers.title: Sharp $s$-nice recurrence without the van der Corput property
papers.abstract:
For every real $s>2$, we construct a set $R_s\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ which is a set of $t$-nice measurable recurrence exactly for $t\ge s$ and is not a van der Corput set. The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--R\"odl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure $\sigma_s$ which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass $(s-2)/(2s-2)$. A Gaussian tail argument proves both sharpness of the recurrence exponent and the fact that this atom is the largest possible for any $s$-nice recurrent set. The result sharpens the recurrence separations of Bourgain and Mountakis, answers a question of Mountakis about the maximal mass of an atom at zero, and answers a question of Forrest about separating the various degrees of nice recurrence.
  In the appendix we give a self-contained proof of the Density Frankl-R\"odl theorem.

papers.title: Some results on the isotropy groups of non-invertible simple derivations
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $2\le i<n$, and let $d_i$ be a $k$-derivation of $k[x_1,\dots,x_i]$. We study the $k$-derivation of $k[x_1,\dots, x_n]$ of the form $d_n=d_i+\sum_{j=i}^{n-1}\bigl(a_jx_{j+1}+g_j(x_j)\bigr)\partial_{x_{j+1}}$ where $a_j\in k$ and $g_j\in k[x_j]\setminus k$. Under suitable conditions on $d_i$, we show that the isotropy group of $d_n$ consists of translations and is either trivial or isomorphic to $(k,+)$.

papers.title: Estimating Extrapolation Factors in Time-Resolved Crystallography
papers.abstract: Time-resolved crystallography (TRX) captures macromolecules in action, but a triggered crystal contains a mixture of triggered proteins in an unknown state and untriggered proteins in the reference state. Separating these is necessary to isolate the dynamics of interest and is an underdetermined data-analysis task. For the simplest case, with one triggered state and one reference state, a range of methods exists, but their assumptions, accuracy, and domains of applicability have not been systematically investigated. Here, we deconstruct and review the methods in current use, employing a unified notation. We make their assumptions explicit and benchmark each on a simulated dataset. A key point is that many of these methods do not estimate the fraction of all triggered molecules in the crystal, but instead estimate a latent parameter we call the extrapolation factor, which is related to but distinct from the so-called "occupancy". As our simulations make apparent, current methods do not always yield accurate results, in particular with noisy data and when the fraction of triggered protein is low. Inspired by previous work, we introduce Vacuum Level Matching, a method that grounds the estimate in the physical constraint that electron density is a nonnegative quantity: it cannot fall below a vacuum level. Operating voxel by voxel, Vacuum Level Matching replaces the manual choices of previous methods with a data-driven procedure and reports quality-control metrics that flag data unable to support a confident prediction. On the same simulated data, it outperforms state-of-the-art methods, and on two experimental datasets, rsEGFP2 and a multi-time-point photolyase series, it recovers known structural changes while flagging issues where the data are weak. Finally, we report an implementation of Vacuum Level Matching in the form of a small, reusable Python package.

papers.title: FGPA-based advanced muon trigger algorithms for long-lived particle detection at the High-Luminosity LHC
papers.abstract: The CMS Level-1 trigger must reconstruct muons in real time under stringent latency and hardware resource constraints. Conventional algorithms lose efficiency for high-energy muons undergoing radiative energy losses and can be suboptimal for displaced trajectories, limiting sensitivity to exotic signatures such as long-lived particles (LLPs). The Phase-2 upgrade introduces advanced FPGAs that enable more sophisticated reconstruction algorithms. This work presents two complementary developments addressing these challenges. In the barrel region, a dedicated algorithm detects showers from Drift Tube hit patterns at the first processing stage. At the subsequent filtering stage, shower primitives are correlated with conventional trigger primitives, currently targeting radiatively showering high-momentum muons, with LLP signatures as a broader objective. Simulation studies yield approximately $80\%$ shower-classification accuracy and an estimated matching efficiency above $80\%$ for radiating muons. Firmware prototypes demonstrate a shower-detection latency of approximately $20\,\mathrm{ns}$ and sub-bunch-crossing latency for preliminary matching logic. In parallel, a hardware-oriented optimization methodology is investigated for future graph neural network based displaced-muon reconstruction in the barrel--endcap overlap region. Using a GraphSAGE proxy on a benchmark dataset, a workflow combining integer quantization, power-of-two scaling, and data-driven bit-width optimization achieves $(75.0 \pm 1.1)\%$ accuracy and a deterministic latency of $19$ cycles ($52.8\,\mathrm{ns}$ at $360\,\mathrm{MHz}$), with only $20\%$ digital signal processor utilization. These results establish a basis for implementation studies using CMS muon data.

papers.title: Two-Component Model for the Unidentified Extended Fermi-LAT Source 4FGL J1908.6+0915e / FL16Y J1908.6+0915e in the SGR 1900+14--W49A Sky Region
papers.abstract: Galactic PeVatrons are expected to be powerful sources of non-thermal high-energy (HE, $E>100$ MeV) and very-high-energy (VHE, $E>100$ GeV) $\gamma$-ray emission as a manifestation of acceleration processes in supernova remnants (SNRs), star formation regions (SFRs), and pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe). In the sky region containing the magnetar SGR 1900+14 and the young massive star cluster (YMSC) W49A, there is one recently identified point-like source FL16Y J1910.2+0903, and there are three unidentified gamma-ray sources: the Fermi-LAT extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e, the HAWC extended source 4HWC J1908+0845, and the LHAASO point-like source LHAASO J1907+0913. We investigate the possibility of explaining the HE and VHE $\gamma$-ray emission from the SGR 1900+14--W49A sky region using a model of the Fermi-LAT extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e as superposition of two extended sources -- a potential SNR/PWN associated with the magnetar SGR 1900+14 and the stellar-wind superbubble adjacent to the YMSC W49A complex. To this end, we simulate the observed $\gamma$-ray emission in hadronic and leptonic models using the open NAIMA code and show that it consists of two extended regions: the stellar wind superbubble in W49A region -- an analog of the Westerlund 1 superbubble -- powered by the YMSC W49A (the southern part of the extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e); and the SGR 1900+14 region, powered by a potential SNR/PWN associated with the magnetar (the northern part of the extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e). However, due to the considerable distance to the magnetar ($d=12.5$ kpc), the required cosmic-ray energy budget in both hadronic and leptonic scenarios corresponds to a hypernova explosion and/or a powerful magnetar wind nebula created by a newly born millisecond magnetar with a rotational energy of the order of $10^{52}$ erg.

papers.title: Electric Field Assisted Charge Transfer Mediated Electronic Coupling in Ferromagnetic/Multiferroic Hetero-structure
papers.abstract: The strongly coupled ferromagnet-multiferroic material could be a better alternative to complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) based data storage device or rather lone multiferroic oxide materials because it offers the electric field controlled conductivity and large magnetisation at the interfaces, but choosing a proper system is still very much challenging. In the present scenario, an interionic charge transfer from Co ion to Fe ion via oxygen is observed at the interfacial region of LaCoO3 (LCO)/BiFeO3 (BFO) grown on SrTiO3 substrate, leading to induce multivalency in Co, Fe ion and also induces exchange biasing in the system. The charge transferring between Co and Fe ions gets further enhanced by electric biasing across the bilayer in the low temperature region, which affects the polarisation behaviour of BFO layer. This confirms the electronic coupling between the ferromagnetic LCO and the multiferroic BFO layers, useful for the making of voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) systems.

papers.title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models
papers.abstract: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy. Pretrained video world models natively generate high-fidelity dynamics, yet represent them densely, entangled across all layers. Viewing the world model as a LAM, we show that these dynamics can be extracted with minimal changes to the model. Native LAM operates one pretrained video diffusion transformer as both IDM and FDM, with learnable dynamics registers as the only causal bridge between the two, and trains on counterfactual temporal pairs that differ in motion alone, so that the registers distill a video's dynamics into a compact native latent action. We further propose a pretraining paradigm for vision-language-action (VLA) policies, Pretraining Actions from World models (PAWlicy), in which Native LAM serves as a dynamics teacher on large-scale video; unlike world action models, it never generates video. Native latent actions outperform existing LAMs on the LARY benchmark in both action classification and control regression, and replay the same motion on new robots, in new scenes, and from human hands to robots, although no transfer objective is used in training. With a 3.8B model, PAWlicy reaches a 93.6% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 trained with domain-randomized demonstrations, the highest among VLAs. On RoboDojo, it is competitive on every dimension we evaluate, and its Precision, evaluated by us, is on par with the leading leaderboard entries. On real robots, it improves over the pi_0.5 baseline on both tasks. Both stages use only public data and a publicly released world model.

papers.title: A response-based self-energy from equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory and its reduction to GW, GW+SOSEX, and GF2
papers.abstract: We construct a frequency-dependent one-particle correlation self-energy by coupling a reference Green's function to the neutral excitation response obtained from equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory with singles and doubles (EOM-CCSD). Direct, mixed direct-antisymmetrized, and fully antisymmetrized choices of the external interaction vertices define three approximations, all admitting an explicit spectral representation without numerical frequency integration. In the bare-state limit, the mixed and fully antisymmetrized forms recover second-order Green's-function theory (GF2), whereas the direct form retains only its ring contribution. With a direct random-phase approximation (RPA) response, the direct and mixed forms reduce to $G_0W_0$ and $G_0W_0$ plus second-order screened exchange (SOSEX), respectively. For molecular ionization potentials, replacing the RPA response by EOM-CCSD generally lowers the ionization energies, whereas introducing exchange at one external vertex raises them. These substantial opposing effects partially compensate, although the mixed approximation does not systematically improve upon conventional $G_0W_0$, either against IP-EOM-CCSD or QUESTDB reference energies (aug-cc-pVDZ mean absolute errors relative to the QUESTDB theoretical best estimates: 0.45 vs 0.36~eV). A third-order perturbative analysis reveals that the three approximations retain different contributions and weights of particle-hole diagrams while omitting explicit particle-particle and hole-hole ladder contributions and the static self-energy. In particular, the fully antisymmetrized form recovers GF2 at second order but assigns incorrect weights to its retained third-order diagrams. These findings highlight the importance of a balanced treatment of screening and vertex corrections in constructing accurate self-energy approximations.

papers.title: Epidemic random model under vaccination regime and non-permanent immunity driven by time-changed Levy noise
papers.abstract: A random version of the Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Vaccinated (SIRV) epidemic model with non-permanent immunity and a population of non-constant size is studied. The compartments satisfy a system of differential equations in which the contact rate is a random coefficient, and the contact rate itself is driven by a stochastic differential equation with time-changed Levy noise. This noise is constructed from a conditional Brownian motion and a doubly stochastic Poisson random field, both governed by a stochastic clock. When the clock is independent of the Brownian and Poisson components, the two parts of the noise are a time-changed Brownian motion and a time-changed Poisson random measure. The equation for the contact rate decouples from the compartment equations and enters them as a random parameter, which allows the compartments to be treated pathwise. The existence, uniqueness, and positivity of the global solution are proven, and the basic reproduction number of the model is shown to be random. Furthermore, sufficient conditions for extinction and persistence in mean of the disease are derived. The conditions are expressed in terms of the parameters of the model and two long-run characteristics.

papers.title: Introduced cases, spread of infection in a community and travel control measures
papers.abstract: Travel restrictions, border screening and quarantine were widely used during the COVID-19 pandemic to prevent or delay the spatial spread of SARS-CoV-2, yet their effectiveness varied greatly across jurisdictions. To investigate how the timing and combination of border control measures interact with pathogen introductions and local transmission, we formulate a coupled Exporter--Importer epidemic model in both deterministic (ordinary differential equations) and stochastic (continuous-time Markov chain and multitype branching process approximation) frameworks. The model distinguishes latently infected, detected infectious and undetected infectious individuals, and explicitly separates recently arrived travellers in an introduction layer from the destination community. We derive analytical expressions for the control and basic reproduction numbers, final epidemic sizes and probabilities of outbreak extinction, and complement them with stochastic simulations. We show that pre-departure screening in the Exporter alone cannot prevent outbreaks in an Importer community with reproduction number larger than unity because latently infected travellers cross borders undetected. Post-arrival quarantine and screening in the introduction layer, as well as travel interruptions, can substantially reduce the attack rate in the Importer, but only when implemented with high stringency and triggered early. Triggering border interventions based on local detections in the Importer almost always acts too late because silent introductions precede local case detection, whereas triggers informed by surveillance in the Exporter provide a wider window of action. Effective protection of the Importer ultimately requires combining proactive, Exporter-informed border measures with local public health interventions that keep the community reproduction number near or below one.

papers.title: Disclosure Bias in AI Reviewers
papers.abstract: AI models increasingly help to review papers, and many conferences and journals now require authors to state how they used AI. Does this AI-use statement change how an AI reviewer rates a paper, and could it change which papers are accepted? In a preliminary study, we varied only the AI-use statement of 150 ICLR 2027 submissions, in up to nine versions adapted from real statements: from no AI, through writing help and coding, to an AI research agent and an AI author. Six AI reviewers rated the versions: the decision model Jev and the language models Claude Haiku 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemini 4 Argon. Across 23,652 reviews, we find that every reviewer rates papers lower on average when the statement says AI did all the work than under a statement of no AI use. The AI research agent statement lowers the rating significantly for Jev, Sonnet and Argon. We find no evidence of a disclosure bias for AI assistance: for writing help, coding and research help, no reviewer's rating differs significantly from its rating under a statement of no AI use. Whether the observed penalty changes which papers are accepted depends on more than the size of the penalty: on how finely and how consistently the reviewer separates the papers near the acceptance boundary, on whether the penalty is spread over all papers or concentrated on a few, and possibly on how many other papers disclose AI use.

papers.title: Quantizing Diffusion LLMs under Parallel Decoding: Commitment Risk and the Parallelism Tax
papers.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) are served with accelerated decoders that cache context and commit, in one step, every masked position whose confidence clears a threshold. Yet post-training quantization of dLLMs has so far been calibrated and evaluated under fixed-step samplers without caching. We study W4A4 quantization under the deployed decoder and find that the decoder determines both where quantization harms accuracy and what it costs. Irreversible errors enter chiefly through forced commitments, made when no position clears the threshold: they are a minority of commitments but carry most quantization-induced flips. Quantization also levies a parallelism tax, extra forward passes per response: by compressing top logit gaps, it pushes positions below the threshold while leaving predictions largely intact. We propose DECAL, which reweights layer-wise calibration by a commitment-risk prior measured on the deployed decoder, and an argmax-preserving commit temperature that recovers the tax. On LLaDA and Dream, DECAL attains the best average accuracy among W4A4 methods, with lower run-to-run variance than the closest existing calibration method.

authors.name: Tao Chen
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Classes de Steinitz d'extensions galoisiennes non ramifi\'ees
papers.abstract:
Let $K$ be a number field and $Cl_{K}$ its class group. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group. We denote by $ R_{nr}(K,\Gamma)$ the subset of $Cl_{K}$ formed by the classes which are realizable as Steinitz classes of Galois extensions of $K$, unramified at the finite places of $K$ and having a Galois group isomorphic to $\Gamma$. If $\Gamma$ is abelian and the narrow class number of $K$ is prime to the order of $\Gamma$, then $R_{nr}(K,\Gamma)=\emptyset$. In the present article, for any $\Gamma$ we consider the set
  $R'_{nr}(K,\Gamma):=\lbrace 1 \rbrace \cup R_{nr}(K,\Gamma)$.
  We prove that $R'_{nr}(K, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$ is a subgroup of $Cl_{K,2}:=\lbrace c\in Cl_{K}\vert c^{2}=1\rbrace$ ; furthermore, it is equal to $Cl_{K,2}$ under a certain assumption on $K$. Using this result we show that $R'_{nr}(K,\Gamma)$ is a subgroup of $R'_{nr}(K, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$ if $\Gamma$ either has odd order, or has a noncyclic $2$-Sylow subgroup (for instance $\Gamma$ a nonabelian $2$-group, $\Gamma=S_n$ or $A_n$, with $n\geq 4$), or has a normal cyclic $2$-Sylow subgroup
  (for instance $\Gamma$ nilpotent having even order).

papers.title: Dual-Side Uncertainty Estimation: Calibrating Data and Model Uncertainty into a Shared Probability Space
papers.abstract: Multimodal user intention analysis infers latent goals from heterogeneous behavioral observations but faces cross-modal input mismatch and output semantic errors. Existing uncertainty estimators focus on input reliability or output confidence and often reduce token uncertainty to simple statistics, overlooking structured dependencies. We propose DUE (Dual-Side Uncertainty Estimation), which jointly estimates input-side aleatoric and sentence-level epistemic uncertainty. From a single generation, Dirichlet perturbations of cross-layer representations produce an ordered token uncertainty sequence. A sequence-aware Normal-Inverse-Gamma estimator uses this sequence to quantify epistemic uncertainty and confidence in its estimate. Evidential multimodal alignment captures aleatoric uncertainty from noisy, incomplete, or inconsistent inputs. DUE calibrates both heterogeneous scores into a shared error-probability space and sequentially fuses them to estimate overall generation risk. Experiments demonstrate strong performance in input-mismatch detection, output semantic-error detection, and overall reliability estimation without repeated generation.

authors.name: Yang Hu
authors.institution: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung

papers.title: Rank-unimodality of one-descent composition ideals
papers.abstract: The principal ideal of a composition consists of its distinct generalized subwords, ranked by the sum of their parts. We prove rank-unimodality for every composition with at most one descent and for every bitonic composition. Both the part sizes and the number of parts are unrestricted. The main ingredient is a coupling for a monotone host. If a subword is chosen uniformly among those of weight at most n, its length and its unused weight can be made to increase weakly when n increases by one. A decreasing threshold on the next available part then compares the positive difference of two ordinary rank coefficients with an earlier cumulative ratio. This supplies the coefficient inequality in the hereditary reduction at a strict peak.

papers.title: Stackelberg Games with Convex Risk Measures
papers.abstract: Stackelberg games have important real-world applications in which reliable commitments require accounting for multiple sources of uncertainty. We study finite Stackelberg games in which environmental uncertainty makes each mixed strategy profile induce a random reward, and each player evaluates that reward with a convex monetary risk criterion. In reward form, it is a concave, monotone, translation-equivariant utility and also represented as penalized expected reward over distributions of environmental outcomes. We provide two conditions under which the follower has a unique continuous mixed response, which leads to inducible optimistic equilibrium. We show that even approximate equilibrium computation is NP Hard. We then derive an exact mathematical program with equilibrium constraints for the problem. We also develop an action entropy smoothed implicit-gradient method and prove an end-to-end additive approximation guarantee under the assumption that the gradient method reaches global optimality. We validate our scalability and other results with experiments on synthetic and real data.

authors.name: Arunesh Sinha
authors.institution: Rutgers Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

papers.title: On the Complexity of Orientable Domination
papers.abstract: The orientable domination number of an undirected graph $G$ is the maximum over all orientations $D$ of $G$ of the minimum size of a dominating set of $D$. In this paper, we look at the problem to decide if the orientable domination number of a given undirected graph $G$ is at least a given integer $\ell$. We show that this problem is complete for the class $\Sigma_2^P$, is fixed-parameter tractable by treewidth, and has a polynomial kernel parameterized by vertex cover number.

authors.name: Yuto Okada
authors.institution: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science London

papers.title: Symplectizing stable generalized complex four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We explicitly describe a surgery that turns a stable generalized complex four-manifold into a symplectic four-manifold. As a consequence, we show that for $n\geq 2$, the almost complex manifold $(n^2+n+1)S^1\times S^3\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ admits no stable generalized complex structures or constant type generalized complex structures. We also prove an irreducibility result for stable generalized complex four-manifolds and we show that the moduli space of generalized complex structures on an elliptic surface has infinitely many components.

papers.title: SAEPO: Sparse-Autoencoder-Guided Credit Assignment for Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has demonstrated strong performance in improving large language model (LLM) reasoning, yet its credit-assignment signal remains coarse. Outcome verifiers provide scalable supervision by judging whether a completed response is correct, but they do not directly indicate which intermediate reasoning tokens contribute to success or failure. As a result, policy optimization can be inefficient, especially when training base models directly from sparse outcome feedback. In this paper, we introduce SAEPO, a Sparse AutoEncoder-guided token-level credit assignment method for outcome-supervised Policy Optimization. Rather than treating correctness only as a rollout-level (sequence-level) signal, SAEPO uses a pretrained sparse autoencoder (SAE) to build token-level semantic representations within reasoning trajectories; it scores each token based on the SAE concepts (e.g., penalizing wrong "final-answer" tokens but rewarding correct "reasoning-process" tokens), learned in an unsupervised manner, to achieve fine-grained credit assignment. SAEPO is a plug-in advantage-shaping module compatible with various policy optimization algorithms. We instantiate SAEPO with both GRPO and GSPO, covering token-ratio and sequence-ratio policy-gradient objectives, and evaluate SAEPO across three LLM backbones on six math and two code benchmarks. Empirical results show that SAEPO improves both the math and code benchmark averages over the matched baselines, with gains of up to 6.63% and 5.57%, respectively. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, training curves also show faster early accuracy growth. Feature and token-level analyses suggest that the SAE-derived signal favors question-relevant concepts and reasoning tokens.

authors.name: Yusong Zhao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

authors.name: Zihao Zhao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Tunyu Zhang
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

authors.name: Chengzhi Mao
authors.institution: Rutgers Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

papers.title: Growing Knot Embeddings into Spherical Graphs
papers.abstract: Knotted structures occur throughout soft matter and biology, where topological constraints can shape relaxation and spatial organization. Here, we introduce a computational construction that maps a specific 3D knot embedding to a graph embedded on the sphere through growth and interfacial-energy relaxation. For standard 3D embeddings of prime knots with at most seven crossings, we obtain a family of growth-based graphs that generally differ from the corresponding Tait graphs. We further identify an empirical growth-graph reconstruction rule based on polygonal regions with alternating crossing structure in a knot diagram. Non-minimal diagrams demonstrate that these graphs are not knot invariants, while selected connected sums suggest that graph features associated with their prime factors can remain recognizable. Determining how these graphs transform under isotopy may reveal invariant features, which we leave for future study.

papers.title: Automatic Occupational Coding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Annually 1.9 million deaths and 89.7 million disability-adjusted life years are caused by exposure to agents during work (e.g., welding fumes, silica dust, and noise pollution). To improve worker health, high-quality exposure assessments are crucial. Therefore, free-text job descriptions from large-scale occupational cohorts are manually standardized through occupational classifications and linked to hazardous exposures using Job Exposure Matrices (JEM). However, manual coding is slow, unreliable (i.e., 44-89% inter-coder reliability), and costly, due to i) short, ambiguous free-text job descriptions, ii) classifications containing hundreds to thousands of categories, and iii) the absence of gold standards. With 46%-79% accuracy, state-of-the-art automatic occupational coding tools achieve classification performance on human level. However, their performance drops to 17-26% on out-of-distribution datasets. Furthermore, their supervised architectures limit them to occupational classifications present in the training set. Consequently, JEM using other classifications are incompatible, leaving vital exposure-response associations unexplored. Our Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework, OPERAG, enables classification into any occupational classification without expert-labelled databases. It retrieves coding index information and combines this with Large Language Model-based classification. Validated on AsiaLymph's 36,062 real-world job descriptions, OPERAG achieved 42.6% occupational classification accuracy on the 4th coding level, substantially outperforming existing tools and approaching human coders' 51-56% inter-coder reliability. Using two JEM named ALOHA+ and SHOCK, 89.9-98.6% accuracy was achieved on exposure assessment. OPERAG approaches human-level, universal occupational classification, enabling efficient and effective large-scale exposure assessment to improve worker health.

authors.name: Lukas P. A. Arts
authors.institution: Amsterdam UMC Location University of Amsterdam

papers.title: DKnown-Jev-2: Article-Level Answer-Evidence Classification and Efficient Inference with a Pre-trained Language Model
papers.abstract: Evidence selection in normative knowledge question answering requires determining whether a candidate article contains content that directly supports an answer under the applicable conditions of the question. We present DKnown-Jev-2, an article-level answer evidence classifier designed for evidence integration across multiple paragraphs. The model jointly encodes question conditions, article metadata, and paragraph content, and uses a pointer-style classification head to predict Answer Evidence (AE) and Non-answer Evidence (NE) in a single forward pass. Ona manually annotated test set of 972 evaluation instances, DKnown-Jev-2 achieves 91.77% accuracy and 91.28% macro-F1, outperforming Jev by 2.16 and 2.37 percentage points, respectively, while reducing both evidence misses and non-evidence false positives. The test set contains 317 multi-paragraph instances, with a maximum body length of 9,322 characters. Shared article encoding and non-autoregressive classification support low-latency inference. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for article-level evidence selection in normative knowledge question answering.

papers.title: Visual-RFT++: Extending Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning to Multimodal Tool Use
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) has recently become a central paradigm for advancing Large Reasoning Models (LRMs), as demonstrated by systems such as OpenAI's o3 and the R1 series. Despite significant progress in LLMs, how to leverage RFT to unify visual perception, step-by-step reasoning, and agentic tool use into one coherent training paradigm remains an open challenge. In this work, we present Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning++ (Visual-RFT++), a unified framework that extends RFT to both visual perception tasks and multimodal agentic workflows, enabling LVLMs to reason with images, act upon images, and evaluate their own outputs using verifiable reward. With Visual-RFT++, open-source LVLMs not only show significant gains on diverse visual perception tasks, but also acquire agentic abilities such as web searching for real-time information and code-based image manipulation (e.g., cropping, rotation, and analysis). Across visual perception tasks, including fine-grained classification, few-shot detection, reasoning grounding, and open-vocabulary detection, Visual-RFT++ delivers strong gains over SFT, including a +24.3 percentage points improvement in one-shot fine-grained classification and +21.0 percentage points on COCO's 4-shot setting and +15.4 percentage points on LVIS with around several hundred samples. To evaluate agentic behaviors, we introduce the Multimodal Agentic Tool Bench (MAT) with MAT-Search and MAT-Coding. Visual-RFT++ surpasses its baseline by +18.6 F1 / +13.0 EM percentage points on MAT-Coding and +10.3 F1 / +8.7 EM percentage points on MAT-Search. It also shows gains of 29.3 F1 and 25.9 EM percentage points on multi-hop QA benchmarks such as 2Wiki and HotpotQA, demonstrating strong cross-modal generalization. Visual-RFT++ introduces a data-efficient and reward-driven framework that strengthens both visual reasoning and agentic adaptability.

authors.name: Jiaqi Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yuhang Zang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Leveraging Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) for the Exchange of Wearable Inertial Sensor Data: Design and Development Study
papers.abstract: Continuous monitoring with wearables can support the assessment of frailty, functional decline, and movement disorders, but raw inertial measurement unit (IMU) recordings are typically stored in proprietary files that electronic health records cannot exchange or interpret. HL7 Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) standardizes health data exchange, yet existing FHIR profiles for personal health devices target spot measurements and short waveforms, not long multichannel motion recordings with their recording context and activity labels. We present WHIR (Wearable Health Interoperable Recordings), a FHIR R5-based information model and implementation guide for wearable IMU recordings. Metadata requirements were derived from a review of 23 published human activity recognition datasets and formalized in a FHIR-independent information model, which was then mapped to FHIR R5 and authored in FHIR Shorthand. Raw signals are kept in files referenced through DocumentReference resources, so that FHIR holds the metadata and activity labels. Terminology reuses SNOMED CT, LOINC, and ISO/IEEE 11073 concepts wherever available. The implementation guide defines 9 profiles, 4 extensions, 10 code systems, and 15 value sets; all artifacts and 67 example instances passed the conformance checks of the HL7 FHIR IG Publisher without errors. Two use cases, machine learning training data and automated home-based geriatric assessment, were implemented as conformant example instances, and we compare the model with the HL7 Personal Health Device Implementation Guide. WHIR provides a FHIR R5-conformant representation of wearable IMU recordings together with device metadata, sensor placement, and time-aligned activity labels, covering concepts that the Personal Health Device Implementation Guide does not address. The implementation guide and its sources are openly available for reuse and extension.

papers.title: Totally geodesic sets and Caratheodory geometry in the polydisk
papers.abstract:
A subset $V$ of the polydisk ${\mathbb D}^N$ is called totally geodesic if every pair of points in $V$ lie on a
  Kobayashi geodesic of ${\mathbb D}^N$ that lies entirely in $V$. It is called a Caratheodory set if its intrinsic Caratheodory metric agrees with the Caratheodory metric inherited from ${\mathbb D}^N$.
  We prove that for algebraic subvarieties of the polydisk these two notions coincide, and we obtain a complete geometric classification of such sets. The invariant metric geometry of the polydisk is unexpectedly rigid: every such set is, up to automorphism, built from only two basic geometric objects: disks and a distinguished family of two-dimensional algebraic surfaces that we call Roman surfaces.
  Roman surfaces arise independently in the study of the three-point interpolation problem in the polydisk.

papers.title: A corank one Lipschitz normally embedded surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with non-trivial link
papers.abstract: We show that the knot-triviality theorem for Lipschitz normally embedded (LNE) corank one surface singularities in $\mathbb{R}^4$ proved by Birbrair, Mendes and Nu\~no-Ballesteros (2018) does not generalize unrestrictedly. More precisely, we exhibit a polynomial map germ $F:(\mathbb{R}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{R}^4,0)$ of corank one at the origin, with isolated singularity and $2$-jet $(x,0,0,0)$, whose image $X=F(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is LNE at the origin, yet its link is the granny knot $T\#T$, and hence non-trivial. The example is obtained via a general uniform-degree homogenization procedure applied to a known polynomial parametrization of the trefoil knot. We also give a finitely $\mathcal A$-determined polynomial realization with the same LNE and knot properties.

papers.title: On the performance of the randomized Euler scheme for nonlinear ODEs under inexact information
papers.abstract: We analyze the randomized explicit Euler scheme for nonlinear ordinary differential equations under a local one-sided Lipschitz condition, local H\"older regularity in the space variable, and H\"older regularity in the time variable. We allow for noisy evaluations of the right-hand side. For the resulting approximation, we derive an error bound in which the contribution associated with the H\"older regularity in the time variable exhibits the characteristic 1/2-order gain of randomized methods. While existing results cover deterministic schemes under the one-sided Lipschitz condition and randomized schemes under the classical Lipschitz condition, our results combine randomized approximation and one-sided Lipschitz regularity.

papers.title: Rotationa Chaos in the Driven Pendulum
papers.abstract: Building on recent developments in the topological theory of surface dynamics, we develop readily applicable criteria for computer-assisted proofs of the existence of rotational horseshoes and apply them to the Driven Pendulum. These tools also allow us to localize the resulting instability region, and to compute a lower bound for the length of their rotation sets. This, in turn, implies the existence of periodic points realizing a wide range of rational rotation numbers. The obtained results correspond to physically meaningful parameter values of the Driven Pendulum. The method also applies to periodically forced Hamiltonian systems whenever the stated conditions are satisfied.

authors.name: Sofia Llavayol
authors.institution: Universidad de la República de Uruguay

authors.name: Alejandro Passeggi
authors.institution: Universidad de la República de Uruguay

papers.title: Shadow economy as a null set. Measure-theoretic approach to shadow economy
papers.abstract: In this paper we asked if the shadow economy can be defined as a system of null sets for institutional measures or sensors that measure economic transactions. As an answer a measure-theoretic testable framework to redefine and quantify the shadow economy was designed. Traditional economic definitions frequently conflate the actual shadow economy with the observational limitations of state institutions. To resolve this, we model the shadow economy as a null set relative to institutional measures and analyze three complementary economic regimes. We explore in this context how standard mathematical tools can be given economic meaning. First, in the low-resolution regime, we apply Banach Lattices and Lebesgue decomposition of a measure to address transaction underreporting by aggregating incomplete institutional registries using a supremum fusion operator. Second, for hidden economic dimensions, we utilize Copula theory and Kullback-Leibler divergence optimization to reconstruct unobserved financial flows from technological and physical indicators. Third, we address audit scalability by modeling the shadow economy as a sparse vector, applying Compressed Sensing to detect high-volume sparse evasion networks through random, incoherent, and privacy-preserving sampling.

papers.title: One UWB Radar, Many Views: Comparing and Fusing Signal Representations for Human Activity Recognition
papers.abstract: IEEE 802.15.4z-compliant impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) transceivers are increasingly built into consumer devices, enabling contactless, privacy-preserving human activity recognition (HAR) in healthcare. Before activity classification, the signal is typically converted into range-time, range-Doppler, or time-Doppler maps, each exposing different spatial and motion cues. Existing comparisons often apply shared processing across representations, leaving it unclear whether their rankings hold after independent tuning. It is also unknown whether rankings and fusion gains generalize across environments and activities, and at what computational cost. Consequently, practitioners lack guidance on which representation and processing suit a given HAR deployment. We release an open dataset of raw IR-UWB measurements collected by a ceiling-mounted radar from 44 participants during scripted activity sequences in 12 layouts across two bedrooms. Using a statistically guided, staged search, we independently tune each representation across five processing and deployment settings. We then compare individual and fused performance under layout and room shifts and quantify computational cost. Across over 1{,}000 cross-validated models, independent tuning proves essential, as optimal processing differs per representation and processing choices shift macro-F1 by up to 26 points, four times the gap between representations. Once tuned, the range-Doppler map leads for unseen layouts (85.1\% macro-F1), while time-Doppler map does for unseen rooms (72.7\%). Fusing all three maps raises these scores to 89.1\% and 80.0\%, respectively. Lower sampling rates and narrower Doppler bands reduce latency by 38--51\% with at most a 1.5-point macro-F1 loss. The best representation for UWB HAR is therefore a deployment decision, not a fixed property.

authors.name: Jelle De Moerloose
authors.institution: HOGENT University of Applied Sciences and Arts

authors.name: Anton Lambrecht
authors.institution: HOGENT University of Applied Sciences and Arts

papers.title: Wavelet-CFM for the extragalactic millimeter-wave sky
papers.abstract: We develop a Wavelet-factorized Conditional Flow Matching (Wavelet-CFM) framework to generate fast, accurate simulations of correlated astrophysical fields including gravitational lensing convergence ($\kappa$), the kinetic and thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ and tSZ) effects, and cosmic infrared background (CIB) emission. Together these make up every bright extragalactic component of the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) sky apart from radio sources. Our approach combines multi-scale wavelet decomposition with conditional flow matching models, trained on $\sim$9$\times$9 deg$^2$ patches at 1-arcminute resolution. The four fields are generated jointly, including their cross couplings, and the model has a tractable likelihood, which to our knowledge has not previously been achieved for this set of components. The power spectra, one-point distributions and Minkowski functionals of the generated maps match a validation set to a few percent. These results show promise for enabling field-level cosmological analyses of mm-wave data.

papers.title: Linear and non-linear integro-differential equations with variable coefficients and Sonin kernels
papers.abstract: We study linear and non-linear integro-differential equations, with Sonin and absolutely continuous kernels, and with variable coefficients which are either integrable or continuous functions. In the linear case, for all cases, the unique solution is given explicitly by a convergent infinite series involving compositions of convolutions of the kernels and the variable coefficients. Many examples are provided. For the non-linear case, the existence and uniqueness are established under a suitable condition in the non-linear term. The analytic solution is given by the limit of the iterative sequence found from the method of successive approximations. The exact analytical expressions for several problems are found by computing the iterative sequences that approximate the solution.

authors.name: Sebastian Nunez
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: Accuracy Is Not Evidence: Measuring and Training Evidence Dependence in Video Temporal Grounding
papers.abstract: In video temporal grounding, a correct interval can come from finding the event, answering blind or fitting one annotation style, and Recall at IoU scores them alike. We measure evidence dependence, how much the answer rests on the event's frames. Our fixed-answer audit edits either the frames inside the annotated interval or, as a placebo, as many frames elsewhere in the same video, and compares the two drops in the annotated answer's likelihood. Supervised fine-tuning and three public checkpoints trained with IoU-reward reinforcement learning raise the accuracy of Qwen2.5-VL-7B by 9 to 20 points, partly by answering blind and by fitting one annotation. Yet their answers rest on the event no more than the base model's, and the same holds for IoU-reward training on our data at the audit's frame rate. This comparison is a difference of the model's own likelihoods, so we can train on it. A placebo contrast and a bound on the placebo drop rule out learning to react to any edit. With them, evidence dependence rises in all five base models we train, and the weight on clean supervision controls how much. Added to IoU-reward training, the objective raises evidence dependence while keeping the accuracy gain. Masking the event's frames makes the trained models decline or miss the event more often than their base; masking as many other frames does not. The dependence moves to another event when the query names it, and holds on a second dataset and under patch scrambling, an edit never used in training.

papers.title: Learning Global Probabilistic Explanations
papers.abstract:
Interpreting the predictions of complex black-box classifiers remains a central challenge in explainable artificial intelligence.
  While local explanations clarify individual predictions, there is a significant need for global probabilistic explanations that capture a model's overall behavior across the input distribution.
  Such an explanation is a small subset $K$ of features, whose relevance is measured by the expected probability, over a random input $\mathbf x$, that the classifier assigns the same label to $\mathbf x$ and to a random input agreeing with $\mathbf x$ on $K$.
  In this study, we investigate the task of identifying maximally relevant global explanations under a cardinality constraint, focusing on product distributions with full support on discrete feature spaces.
  We introduce a spectral explainer that leverages membership queries to the black-box classifier and employs Fourier-analytic, junta-learning methods to produce probably approximately correct (PAC) explanations.
  Our algorithm is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the explanation size limit, maximum feature cardinality, and desired accuracy.
  Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets confirm the theoretical guarantees and show that the spectral explainer outperforms a greedy baseline as the explanation size increases.

papers.title: A Reactive Cross-Layer QoS Adaptation Framework for SDN-Enabled DDS Communications in IoD
papers.abstract: The Internet of Drones (IoD) is a subset of the Internet of Things (IoT) where drones operate as networked smart objects communicating with entities across terrestrial, aerial, and spatial domains. The increasing deployment of drones has accelerated the adoption of IoD in both mainstream and emerging applications. Increasingly, IoD systems rely on the standardized Data Distribution Service (DDS) as their communication middleware, thanks to its rich Quality of Service (QoS) policies, which enable meeting the demanding constraints of IoD applications. However, QoS policies, particularly reliability modes, are often statically configured, which limits their effectiveness in IoD environments that are characterized by high mobility, frequent network impairments, and dynamic topology changes. In this paper, we propose a reactive QoS adaptation framework for DDS-based IoD systems. The framework leverages Software Defined Networking (SDN) to capture global network conditions and incorporates device energy levels and topic popularity to dynamically adapt reliability modes to changing operating environments. By jointly considering network-level, device-level, and topic-level inputs, the proposed approach enhances middleware adaptability, reliability, and efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework compared to static QoS configurations.

authors.name: Hicham Lakhlef
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Multimarginal Optimal Transport (MOT) suffers from exponential computational and memory costs in the number of marginals, as transport plans are represented by high-dimensional tensors. We introduce Low-Rank Multimarginal Optimal Transport (LRMOT), which restricts transport plans to tensors with bounded multilinear rank, providing a compact and structured representation of multimarginal couplings. This structure enables efficient algorithms with a low memory footprint. We establish approximation bounds for the resulting low-rank formulations and demonstrate experimentally that the proposed algorithms substantially reduce computational time while achieving solutions with low transport cost.

authors.name: Johann Clement-Cottuz
authors.institution: Laboratoire d'Informatique, du Traitement de l'Information et des Systèmes

authors.name: Gilles Gasso
authors.institution: Laboratoire de mathématiques appliquées de Compiègne

authors.name: Maxime Berar
authors.institution: Laboratoire d'Informatique, du Traitement de l'Information et des Systèmes

papers.title: Decoding Transformer Dynamics via Koopman Subspaces
papers.abstract: We apply Koopman operator theory and Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) to characterise how large language models (LLMs) process different input topics. Treating the layer-to-layer evolution of hidden states as a dynamical system, we fit a linear Koopman operator and take the subspace spanned by its dominant modes as a per-topic spectral fingerprint. Four findings emerge. First, the depth map is near-linear: a single linear operator predicts each next-layer state to within approx. 18% relative error (interior variance explained approx. 0.99). Second, over the 57 MMLU subjects the fingerprint is topic-discriminative, matching the MMLU taxonomy at 0.72 nearest-neighbour purity and each subject's semantic neighbourhood at 0.75 any-hit@3. Third, it is a reproducible signature (split-half self-retrieval approx. 0.97$). Finally, these findings are consistent across seven base models (Qwen2.5 0.5-7B, Llama-3 1-8B), with a suggestive trend of alignment rising with MMLU accuracy. The spectral fingerprint thus provides a probe of how transformers process different topics across depth. Code is available at https://github.com/DeepK/koopman-llm-eacl27.

papers.title: Neighbourhood flood damage amplifies mortgage default cascades
papers.abstract: Floods threaten mortgage repayment by damaging homes, disrupting incomes, and worsening conditions in surrounding neighbourhoods. However, it remains unclear how these neighbourhood effects turn local damage into systemic mortgage distress, as Europe's housing crisis leaves households that lose their homes with few affordable alternatives. Using an agent-based model calibrated to Limburg, the Netherlands, we show that damage to surrounding properties can trigger mortgage defaults among households that can still afford to pay, including those whose own homes remain undamaged. In the most severe flood scenario, the annual foreclosure rate more than doubles. As each foreclosure lowers the value of nearby homes, it triggers a cascade. Floods make such large foreclosure cascades more frequent, with the share of foreclosures that belong to these cascades rising from 31% to 45%. They also shift foreclosures towards younger mortgages, when more debt is still outstanding. These findings show how neighbourhood damage extends mortgage risk beyond directly flooded homes and causes foreclosures to arrive in concentrated waves earlier in repayment.

papers.title: MTL-MHOL: Predicting Online Conversions under Delayed Feedback and Data Sparsity
papers.abstract: This paper proposes the model-agnostic Multi-Task Learning Multi-Head Online Learning (MTL-MHOL) framework for conversion rate (CVR) prediction. Existing approaches typically address key challenges in CVR prediction, such as delayed feedback and data sparsity, in isolation or lack flexibility and practical applicability. MTL-MHOL adopts a time bucketing approach to account for delayed feedback and combines it with multi-task learning of an auxiliary task to mitigate data sparsity. We evaluate the framework on proprietary datasets from a private company and on a public dataset from Criteo. MTL-MHOL matches or outperforms all benchmark models in terms of Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) and Relative Cross Entropy (RCE), and it correctly captures temporal trends in the data using an MLP backbone, while maintaining strong performance with a DeepFM backbone. In particular, MTL-MHOL matches the performance of the advanced delayed-feedback method FSIW, outperforms the entire-space approach ESMM by 21.5% in RCE, and achieves up to 81% lift in RCE compared to the best-performing classical benchmark.

papers.title: A local-in-time quadratic functional for scalar conservation laws
papers.abstract: We construct a Glimm-type functional for scalar conservation laws, which is quadratic (w.r.t. the total variation of the initial datum), it controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions, and, differently than functionals with similar properties already present in the literature, it is purely local in time, meaning that it depends only on the present profile of the (approximate) solution (and not on its past or future evolution).

papers.title: The cost functional for hyperbolic systems of conservation laws
papers.abstract: For hyperbolic systems of conservation laws (without any genuine nonlinearity of linear degeneracy assumption on the flux) we construct a quadratic interaction functional, which controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions and it is local in time. This extends the analysis of [3] from scalar conservation laws to $n \times n$ systems.

papers.title: $C^{m,\alpha}$-rectifiability in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: In an arbitrary Carnot group $\mathbb{G}$ of homogeneous dimension $Q$, we characterize rectifiability of sets of finite Hausdorff measure by $\mathbf C_{\mathbb{G}}^{m,\alpha}$-regular surfaces with complemented vertical tangent subgroups, for every $m\ge1$ and $\alpha\in[0,1]$. The criterion combines positive lower density with approximation in measure by tubes around such surfaces. At almost every point, one tube radius $\lambda r^{m+\alpha}$ suffices for $\alpha>0$, whereas the estimate must hold for every $\lambda r^m$, $\lambda>0$, for $\alpha=0$. Tubular approximation upgrades $\mathbf C^1_{\mathbb{G}}$-rectifiability to class $(m,\alpha)$ without an additional density assumption. The proof combines ambient normal-form polynomial jets, a Remez-type norming inequality, and Whitney extension. In topological dimension at least two, quantitative volume approximation by noncharacteristic sublevel sets yields higher-order rectifiability of reduced boundaries. In particular, for weak solutions of the horizontal Poisson equation with $L^q_{\mathrm{loc}}$ forcing ($q>\max\{Q,2\}$ finite), almost every sublevel set has second-order rectifiable reduced boundary.

papers.title: Phase-Conditioned Action Contracts for Auditable Microsurgical Control
papers.abstract: Staged robotic procedures may reuse a fixed-dimensional policy output even though the admissible motions and physical meanings of its coordinates change across phases. We call this action-semantic shift. To address it, we propose a phase-conditioned executable policy that separates learned action proposal from deterministic command formation. Phase-specific heads generate proposals, while an action contract removes inadmissible components, enforces state-dependent bounds, and decodes the remaining action into phase-dependent task-space commands. We further introduce failure-focused local repair and a read-only provenance trace for exact command replay and rule-level auditing. Across three held-out retinal-injection evaluation blocks, our method achieves $94.27\pm0.64\%$ procedural completion and $64.40\pm2.43\%$ success within $35\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, with no hard violations. Applying the contract and decoder to the same frozen Correction network raises completion from $12.27\%$ to $90.47\%$. The trace exactly reconstructs 96,350 commands, and all 1,996 binding interventions follow their declared effects. These results show the importance of explicit executable action semantics for auditable staged microsurgical control.

papers.title: CoSel: Cooperation as Selection for End-to-End Driving
papers.abstract: Cooperative driving can extend a vehicle's awareness beyond its own sensors, but existing cooperative end-to-end methods inject shared information into the planner and rely on cooperative driving demonstrations to learn how to use it. The moments in which shared information should change a driving decision are rare in such data, providing limited supervision for learning this behavior. We argue that cooperation need not be learned by the planner. Instead, reacting to shared information requires predicting how surrounding agents will move and selecting a response from the candidate trajectories of an ego planner. We introduce CoSel, a cooperation-as-selection framework that leaves the planner and its ego-only input unchanged. A separately trained cooperative predictor uses observations from the ego vehicle, roadside units, and connected automated vehicles to predict surrounding agents and their future motion. CoSel evaluates the planner's candidate trajectories against these predictions, preserves the planner's choice when it remains safe, and selects the closest safe alternative when shared information reveals additional risk. Each safety intervention is traceable to the shared evidence that triggers it. In closed-loop evaluation, CoSel achieves a driving score of 70.7 on V2Xverse, outperforming the best compared cooperative method by 7.5 points, and the highest average driving score of 85.8 on MDrive. Under missing ego detections, the collision count of CoSel increases only from 17 to 19 in 72 scenarios, compared with 19 to 32 for an existing cooperative end-to-end model.

papers.title: A Homotopic Kuratowski Theorem
papers.abstract: We prove that if a map from a graph G to a compact orientable surface, possibly with boundary, cannot be deformed so as to remove all crossings, then neither can its restriction to some subgraph of G with at most 72 vertices of degree other than two. On the sphere, this is Kuratowski's theorem; in contrast, minimal obstructions to embeddability in a surface grow with its genus. Our proof reduces the problem to planarity in a disk with order constraints, and identifies a condition under which this problem has small obstructions. Our main tool is a homotopic version of depth-first search trees, which underlie classical planarity tests and the extraction of Kuratowski subgraphs.

papers.title: Exploring Attention-Driven Deep Learning for Accurate Lung Nodule Segmentation
papers.abstract: This study explores the application of various deep learning models for the segmentation of lung nodules using LIDC-IDRI. Unlike traditional approaches that utilize the full dataset, our work emphasizes the efficacy of training models on a filtered subset of 356 samples. Novel configurations, including attention mechanisms and advanced preprocessing strategies, were employed to optimize segmentation accuracy. Among the models evaluated, the DPL nkNet50 with a Channel Attention Bridge and ResNet backbone demonstrated the highest performance with a Dice score of 0.86, significantly outperforming conventional architectures. This work underscores the potential of leveraging data efficiency and tailored architectures in achieving robust segmentation performance, paving the way for improved computer-aided diagnosis in clinical settings.

papers.title: The XRISM view of the front and rear ejecta dynamics in Tycho's SNR
papers.abstract: We present a line-of-sight dynamics study of Tycho's supernova remnant (SNR) with XRISM/Resolve, based on five pointings obtained during the first two years of the mission. Thanks to a spectral resolution better than 5 eV, the spectra reveal a clear Doppler splitting of the Si, S, Ar, Ca and Fe emission lines towards the center of the remnant, allowing us to study the front and back sides of the shocked ejecta independently for the first time. Using a phenomenological Gaussian line model and a Bayesian fitting method, we analyze the broadband spectra of each pointing and of 149 individual pixels. We derive the dynamics and flux of the front and back sides for each element, as well as a global line broadening. The dynamics of Tycho's SNR are asymmetric, with the back side expanding faster than the front side for Si, S and Fe. We reveal a line-of-sight stratification of the elements, with Fe at lower velocities than Si and S. Si shows a strong front/back flux asymmetry, the front side being up to twice as bright as the back side in the northeastern part of the remnant. A similar but weaker asymmetry is found for S. For Fe, the flux ratio varies spatially, with either side dominating. These measurements allow us to reassess the average line-of-sight kinematics obtained at CCD resolution, which is affected by the flux asymmetry between the front and back sides and not only by a velocity asymmetry. Combining our line-of-sight velocities with Chandra proper motions, we reconstruct the three-dimensional dynamics of Tycho's SNR. Finally, we discuss the constraints these results set on the explosion model and the progenitor system.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: A. Decourchelle
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Model-Assisted Probability of Detection Studies for Image-Based Human Inspection
papers.abstract: Establishing a probability of detection (POD) curve is important for assessing the reliability of components in aging systems. Traditional POD studies rely on physical specimens containing representative flaws and human inspectors who record detection results, making such studies costly. This paper demonstrates how appropriately validated physics-based simulation can substantially reduce, and in suitable applications potentially replace, physical POD experiments. We use XRSIM, an X-ray radiographic simulator, to generate weld images containing cracks of varying size, morphology, and location. Flaw characteristics, locations, and the number of flaws per image were randomized, with images containing zero to three flaws. Each simulated flaw is treated as an observational unit contributing flaw-level hit-miss responses. To capture human inspection variability, the images were presented in random order to five inspectors, each of whom inspected the images twice. The resulting data were analyzed using a repeated-measures binary-regression model accounting for flaw-to-flaw, inspector-to-inspector, flaw/inspector-combination, and inspection-to-inspection variability. Bayesian inference was used to estimate the population-mean POD curve, inspector-specific POD curves, and associated statistical uncertainty. Results show that flaw-to-flaw variability dominates, with appreciable differences among inspectors. The study provides a framework for combining physics-based image simulation with controlled human inspection to estimate POD while reducing the experimental burden of physical specimen fabrication.

papers.title: Pixel as the Common Language: Unified Multimodal Embedding via Visual Rendering
papers.abstract: Multimodal embedding models map heterogeneous inputs into a shared representation space, yet text-only, image-only, and composed inputs are still presented in distinct formats and follow different routes through the model. This fragmentation prevents heterogeneous tasks from jointly optimizing the same end-to-end encoding process, limiting supervision transfer across input configurations. To address this issue, we propose unification before encoding and instantiate this paradigm in RenderEmbed. The framework uses Visual Substrate Rendering to convert heterogeneous inputs into a common visual substrate for encoding with a VLM. From the resulting visual tokens, Progressive Hierarchical Anchor Encoding produces compact retrieval representations by interleaving learnable anchors and fusing their states across layers, retaining broad context and fine-grained cues. Interventional Rendering Learning trains these representations to remain sensitive to content changes and stable across rendering variations through complementary semantic and rendering interventions. Extensive experiments on MMEB and ViDoRe v2, spanning diverse retrieval tasks, show that RenderEmbed outperforms prior state-of-the-art models at the same scale and exhibits strong out-of-domain generalization. Compared with MetaEmbed, RenderEmbed improves MMEB Overall Precision@1 by 1.7 points, with a larger 2.1-point gain on out-of-domain tasks. Transfer and scaling analyses further show that a shared visual pathway enables more effective learning from heterogeneous supervision.

papers.title: Physics-Constrained Neural ODEs for Learning Traffic Dynamics and Trajectories from Road Entry/Exit Times
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of learning microscopic traffic dynamics and reconstructing vehicle trajectories from section entry/exit timestamps (EET) recorded by cameras and from the positions of a probe vehicle leading the platoon. The dynamics are difficult to recover as each vehicle's position is measured only at two points, and its trajectory between them is unknown. By combining Neural ODEs with a local density approximation, we learn a follow-the-leader model whose speed--density relation is a neural network. With such sparse data, an unconstrained network may learn physically unrealistic relations, such as negative speeds or non-zero speeds on a fully congested road. We therefore introduce a normalization that, applied to a monotone neural network with a learned regime change, enforces the endpoint conditions, guaranteeing an admissible speed--density relation while provably retaining the ability to approximate any admissible one. We validate the method on first- and second-order simulations, recovering the speed--density relation of the first-order model and reconstructing the trajectories of both models, with mean maximum position errors of 2.50~m and 2.51~m, respectively, on a 125~m road segment. On real-world ring-road data, the proposed model still yields an admissible relation, whereas both baselines violate the constraints; the large spread in the data, however, highlights the limitations of a first-order model with homogeneous driver behaviors.

papers.title: Power-Swing Blocking and Out-of-Step Tripping Scheme Using the Swing Center Voltage in Systems With Inverter-Based Resources
papers.abstract: Misoperation of power-swing blocking (PSB) and out-of-step tripping (OST) schemes in distance relays is a critical concern in power systems with increasing penetration levels of inverter-based resources (IBRs). Recently, several papers have studied the impact of IBRs on conventional dual-blinder PSB/OST schemes. They highlight interoperability issues concerning fast power swings and unconventional impedance trajectories, and propose revised relay settings in attempts to deal with the problems. However, the blinder-based PSB methodology suffers from being dependent on the speed of the apparent impedance just as it crosses between the blinders. It is therefore important to consider alternative methods. This paper thoroughly analyzes the characteristics of the swing center voltage (SCV) and the impacts of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) inverters on its local estimation. Then, an SCV-based PSB/OST scheme is proposed, where the main PSB criterion can be tuned from simple system parameters. This is made possible by a separate PSB activation function. The OST scheme uses only one setting and is motivated from the analytical analysis of the SCV with IBRs. Extensive PSCAD/EMTDC simulations verify the performance of the proposed SCV-based PSB/OST scheme and how it overcomes limitations of blinder-based schemes with GFM and GFL inverters.

authors.name: Qianli Xing
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: When AI Performance Is Not Enough: Statistical Guardrails for Clinical Development
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are reshaping the operational and inferential landscape of clinical development, yet their adoption frequently outpaces the statistical scrutiny these methods demand. This commentary offers first-principles perspectives across four application domains: anomaly detection in clinical trial data, real-time monitoring and adaptive trial designs, biomarker-based enrichment, and virtual and digital twins. For each domain, we articulate the underlying inferential problem, the contribution of AI and ML relative to established statistical methods, and the risks that statisticians, data scientists, and clinical developers must actively manage. Across these domains, a unifying theme emerges: AI and ML methods may succeed locally while failing to satisfy the broader statistical assumptions required for valid clinical and regulatory decisions. These risks include false-positive signals, compromised Type I error control in adaptive designs, conflation of prognostic with predictive biomarkers, and causal claims not supported by data and assumptions. We argue that a clearly defined context of use, relevant statistical assumptions, and consequences of the intended decision should guide the evaluation. For treatment-effect questions, the ICH E9(R1) estimand framework provides a useful organizing principle. Responsible use of AI in clinical development requires not restraint, but rigor: the inferential discipline necessary to make these technologies reproducible, interpretable, and defensible in the service of patients.

authors.name: Siddhesh Kulkarni
authors.institution: Khalifa University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Failure Modes and Data-Efficient Remedies for Transformer-Based Prediction of Viscoplastic Flows
papers.abstract: Fast and accurate prediction of viscoplastic flows remains a challenge in computational rheology due to yield surfaces, discontinuous gradients, and strongly nonlinear transitions between yielded and unyielded regions. Transformer-based neural operators such as RheOFormer have recently shown strong potential for surrogate modeling of non-Newtonian flows. However, their applicability to viscoplastic systems and their efficacy in recovering realistic flows remain poorly understood. In this work, we present the first systematic investigation of RheOFormer applied to steady Bingham channel flow. By isolating the problem to a simple geometry and constitutive model, we examine how dataset structure, numerical value range, and input representation govern the model's ability to interpolate and extrapolate within the parameter space. The data regimes in which RheOFormer remains accurate and those in which errors emerge are identified, particularly for plug-dominated flows and for conditions outside the velocity scales or flow structures represented during training. Upon identifying these failure modes, targeted enhancements to the input representation and loss formulation are introduced to better predict low-gradient plug regions. Logarithmic velocity representations and gradient-aware loss formulations substantially improve accuracy in challenging regimes where the baseline formulation fails. In addition, extrapolation errors are reduced by augmenting the training set with only a few strategically selected cases spanning the missing physical regimes. Finally, a single partially developed snapshot suffices for an accurate steady-state prediction, and the model outperforms simply copying its input throughout flow development. These results highlight the importance of appropriate field representation and parameter-space coverage for data-efficient neural-operator prediction of viscoplastic flows.

papers.title: PROSPER: LLMs as Sparse Retrievers for First-Stage Product Search
papers.abstract: Product search is a crucial component of large-scale e-commerce platforms, where first-stage retrieval should achieve high recall while ensuring efficient online deployment. Sparse retrieval remains attractive for this setting due to its interpretability and deployability, yet it suffers from severe vocabulary mismatch challenges, especially for short queries and product titles. Large language models (LLMs) offer strong semantic capabilities, but directly applying them to sparse retrieval in product search introduces new challenges: (i) semantic expansion may distort critical literal signals such as brand names and model identifiers; and (ii) learning meaningful sparse representations is difficult in the high-dimensional vocabulary space induced by LLMs.To address these challenges, we propose PROSPER, a framework that uses LLMs as sparse retrievers for product search while explicitly preserving lexical fidelity.
