papers.title: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
papers.abstract:
Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[
  |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$. The proof's key idea is to run the prime-field Stepanov method in reverse, constructing an auxiliary polynomial whose specialization vanishes identically instead of requiring it to be nonzero.

papers.title: QUISA: A Compact, Flexible and Unified Instruction-Set Coprocessor for QR-UOV Signature
papers.abstract: QR-UOV is a Quotient Ring Unbalanced Oil and Vinegar (UOV) multivariate quadratic (MQ) signature scheme that has progressed to round-3 of the post-quantum cryptography (PQC) additional signatures call by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Until now, for architectural efficiency and performance trade-offs, QR-UOV has been evaluated only on software platforms and has never been considered on hardware, such as field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). To address this, we are the first to provide a complete QR-UOV hardware implementation through a flexible and unified QUISA coprocessor design, which supports instruction-driven execution for key generation, signing, and verification across all three NIST security levels (SL-I, SL-III, SL-V). The proposed architecture features extensive throughput optimizations by parallelizing key QR-UOV module operations, such as the pseudorandom byte generator, hashing, and rejection sampling. To minimize hardware resources, we propose a modular arithmetic unit with finite-field reduction based on the shift-add folding method. The design introduces a linear system solver for QUISA based on LU decomposition with partial pivoting and a sample solution module, operating over the prime field Fq (q = 127). We comprehensively evaluate QUISA on an Artix-7 FPGA at 80 MHz up to the post-place-and-route stage, utilizing 11,144 slices and 35,248 look-up tables. For higher SL-V security levels, it completes key generation, signing, and verification in 30.4M, 3.8M, and 2.8M clock cycles, respectively.

papers.title: TamperCert: A Benchmark for Detecting Text Tampering in Degree Certificates
papers.abstract: Degree certificates play a critical role in high-stakes decisions such as university admission, immigration, and hiring. The issuing institution vouches for the holder, so a forged certificate may let its bearer pass these checks. Degree certificate forgery is increasingly prevalent. Yet, many assume that it is easy to spot. Reported cases show otherwise: in 2024, the business school of the University of Hong Kong found that about 30 master's students had enrolled with forged academic credentials. Few studies have looked at how to detect forged degree certificates, partly because public benchmarks are scarce. We present TamperCert, a benchmark built from 400 real degree certificates issued by 38 universities. Each certificate was subjected to 11 publicly available tampering methods to alter the holder's name and further processed with four additional post-processing techniques, resulting in over 20,000 forged images. We evaluate 13 detectors, a commercial multimodal large language model (MLLM), and detectors trained on TamperCert.Our findings reveal that no detector is reliable for every tampering method. Consequently, a determined forger may still evade detection. Moreover, the commercial MLLM misses most forgeries made by general-purpose generative models, and post-processing, such as resizing an image or photographing it with a camera, severely degrades detection.

authors.name: Youqian Zhang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

authors.name: Yongjian Wu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
papers.abstract: Physics simulation outputs increasingly come from solvers that no expert inspects, such as third-party packages in automated pipelines, programs written by large language models (LLMs), and learned surrogates. In earlier work on cardiac pulsed field ablation, we proposed that solvers return a certificate with their answers. The certificate consists of an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current, and a small independent checker turns it into guaranteed error bounds against a written specification of the physics. Here, the same checker verifies the outputs of other solvers on the same problem. Specifically, FEniCSx computes both fields and receives the same bounds as our own solver. Five plausible bugs in a correct solver, one of them about 0.2% from the true impedance, all converge and pass a grid convergence study, yet the certificate rejects or refutes all five. Of three solvers written by LLMs, one is correct and certified to 0.1%, and one never solves the equation but converges. Neural networks that predict the coefficients of a reduced basis emit admissible fields and receive valid per-prediction bounds, at most 0.0021% wide inside their training range and 0.3-25% wide outside it, where 90% conformal intervals cover none of 14 tests. Untuned Fourier neural operators with free nodal outputs receive valid but uninformative bounds. On a uniform grid, interpolation onto the certificate grid limits them, and on the certificate grid, thin cells turn small nodal errors into large energy errors. Energy-norm training narrows the certified interval tenfold, and projecting the nodal-loss outputs onto the reduced basis narrows it by two to four orders of magnitude, still uninformative. The guarantee concerns the stated model and holds for any output, wherever its input lies. It is informative only when the output is accurate in energy on a grid that resolves the problem.

papers.title: The Seifert--van Kampen Theorem
papers.abstract: The Seifert--van Kampen theorem computes the fundamental group of a space from an open cover by two path-connected subspaces, provided their intersection is path-connected. This article gives a self-contained account of the theorem, explains its universal-property formulation as a pushout in the category of groups, and derives several standard computations. Particular attention is paid to base points, the role of path-connectedness, and the passage from a topological decomposition to a group presentation. The purpose is expository: the results are classical, and no claim of a new theorem is made.

papers.title: Parity-safe digraphs with countably many ends are kernel-perfect
papers.abstract:
A kernel of a digraph is an independent set that every other vertex points into, and a digraph is kernel-perfect if every induced subgraph has a kernel. A digraph without odd cycles in which no ray contains infinitely many vertices that each send an infinite fan of disjoint paths to that ray is safe. The conjecture that every safe digraph is kernel-perfect was proved earlier for digraphs with finitely many ends.
  We prove a stronger statement for at most countably many ends. Number the vertices of a ray, and let the type of a path that ends on the ray be the parity of the sum of its length and the number of its last vertex. A fan is mixed if it has infinitely many paths of each type, and a digraph is parity-safe if it has no odd cycle and no ray containing infinitely many vertices with a mixed fan to it. Yablo's graph (omega,<) is not parity-safe. Its variant with edges only between vertices of different parity has a kernel - it is parity-safe but not safe. Our main result is that a parity-safe digraph with at most countably many ends is kernel-perfect, and the claim for safe digraphs follows since safety implies parity-safety. The digraph may have any cardinality, and nothing is assumed about the structure of the ends, but the case of uncountably many ends remains open.

authors.name: Sjur Dyrkolbotn
authors.institution: Western Norway University of Applied Sciences

papers.title: Toward a Classification of Differentially $3$-Uniform Power Mappings over $\F_{p^2}$ and $\F_{p^3}$
papers.abstract: We study the classification, up to the CCZ-equivalence, of differentially $3$-uniform power mappings over quadratic and cubic extensions of prime fields. Over $\F_{p^2}$ exhaustive searches for primes $3<p<300$ found only the known families E1 and E4 for $p>23$. Over $\F_{p^3}$, the previously unexplained exponents for $7<p<200$ belong to a single family. We give an elementary proof that this family has differential uniformity at most $3$ for primes $p\equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and prove that the bound is attained for $p>1444$.

papers.title: Local Pressure Induced Quantum Dot to Ring Transition and Aharonov Bohm Effect in Reconfigurable MoTe2 Bilayers
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that local pressure provides an effective means of engineering reconfigurable quantum confinement in MoTe2 homobilayers. By applying a smooth, spatially varying pressure profile, we show that the confinement geometry can be continuously tuned from a conventional quantum dot to a quantum ring, with the emergence of annular confinement being a distinctive feature of AB-stacked bilayers. This crossover originates from the pressure-induced spatial modulation in the electronic parameters, which produces an off-center minimum in the effective confinement potential, thereby redistributing the ground-state probability density away from the center and giving rise to an annular confinement geometry. In the quantum-ring regime, a perpendicular magnetic field gives rise to a flux-periodic energy spectrum and persistent currents, providing characteristic signatures of the Aharonov-Bohm effect. By coupling the pressure-induced quantum ring to source and drain leads, we further demonstrate pronounced Aharonov-Bohm conductance oscillations, accompanied by real-space current patterns exhibiting constructive and destructive interference at integer and half-integer magnetic flux quanta, respectively. These findings establish locally pressurized MoTe2 bilayers as a lithography-free platform for reconfigurable quantum confinement and realizing pressure-tunable Aharonov-Bohm interferometry in two dimensional materials.

authors.name: Hocine Bahlouli
authors.institution: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

authors.name: Udo Schwingenschlogl
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Green ACO: An Energy-Aware Ant Colony Optimisation for the MAX-SAT Problem with EI/J Scheduling and Thompson Sampling
papers.abstract: NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems demand heavy computation, and this raises real environmental concerns, especially in regions with carbon-intensive power grids. This paper presents Green ACO, an energy-aware Ant Colony Optimisation algorithm for the MAXIMUM SATISFIABILITY (MAX-SAT) problem. At its core is an Expected Improvement per Joule (EI/J) scheduler. At every iteration, it picks the operator that best balances expected quality gain against expected energy cost. Three operators feed the scheduler: WalkSAT, Focused Variable Neighbourhood Search, and Clause-Restart Greedy, ranging from cheap and surgical to aggressive and costly. An offline dual-regime profiling phase calibrates these operators before the search even begins, and, combined with Thompson sampling, this reduces uninformed early operator choices; online call-count warm-up still occurs. A pre-dispatch guard rejects calls when their estimated energy cost, with a safety multiplier, exceeds the remaining budget. Sparse pheromone updates, pheromone caching across budgets, and stagnation-based early stopping trim energy use further, without hurting solution quality. The framework also incorporates a budget predictor that estimates the energy budget required for unseen instances. On four hard MAX-SAT reference instances, Green ACO reaches an average quality of 98.44%. This beats the standard ACO baselines by close to 3 points, while using only 986 J against 4,171 to 6,610 J for the strongest competitors, a six-and-a-half-fold gain in quality per joule. Under the Algerian grid's carbon intensity, this cuts CO$_2$e emissions by approximately 85% compared with the most energy-hungry baseline.

papers.title: TOGO: Take One Image Editor, Get One Video Editor for Free
papers.abstract: Instruction-based image editors are trained on millions of edit pairs and follow instructions far more reliably than current video editors. We show that this ability can be transferred to video editing without any training. Our key observation is that a growing number of image editors and video generators share the same latent space. Their velocity fields can therefore be combined at sampling time: the difference between the editor's velocity under the instruction and under a neutral prompt, which we call the \emph{edit velocity}, can be added to the sampler of a video model. Added naively, however, it blurs the video, alters the background and flickers. An analysis of the edit velocity explains why. It is small and reliable only at coarse scales and high noise levels, not concentrated on the edited object, and uncorrelated across frames. From these properties, we derive a simple guidance operator that amplifies the edit velocity and restricts it in noise level, space, and time. The video model then turns the incoherent per-frame signal into a temporally coherent edit. Our method, TOGO, combines Qwen-Image-Edit with the Wan2.1 video model without training or fine-tuning. On FiVE-Bench, it raises the edit success rate from 47.0\% (the same video model without the editor) to 65.6\%, above the best published method (59.2\%). At the same time, it maintains the background PSNR and obtains the best LPIPS and SSIM of all methods. Because the video editor is assembled at inference time, it can be upgraded to any newer image editor that shares the latent space with no cost.

authors.name: Yixuan Luo
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Zunyi Medical College

authors.name: Yanjing Li
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Degree 2 foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ with only saddle-node and nilpotent singularities
papers.abstract: We classify all foliations of degree $2$ on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ having only saddle-node or nilpotent singularities up to projective equivalence. To do so, we use the bijection between such foliations and their polar configurations stated by Campillo and Olivares~\cite{CO}. We also show that three families of the found foliations admit no algebraic invariant curve.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation via Mutual Information Maximization
papers.abstract: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress a large dataset into a small synthetic one that remains effective for training neural networks. Despite its success in supervised learning, DD remains underexplored in self-supervised learning (SSL), where distilled data must preserve the information needed to learn representations that remain consistent across augmentations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mutual Information Prototype Alignment (MIPA), an efficient SSL dataset distillation approach that optimizes synthetic images to preserve augmentation-invariant information. Specifically, MIPA treats synthetic images as learnable prototypes and uses a frozen encoder to assign real samples to them based on feature similarity. A synthetic dataset that preserves such augmentation invariance should yield stable prototype assignments across multiple augmented views of the same real image. MIPA encourages this by maximizing mutual information between cross-view assignments while avoiding trivial solutions in which all real samples are assigned to only a few synthetic prototypes. Evaluations on image classification benchmarks show that synthetic data generated by MIPA yield higher-quality representations than existing distillation approaches while reducing time and storage demands during distillation.

authors.name: Jiale Cai
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: MRI-Driven Dual-Energy CT Synthesis via Conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models for MRI-only Radiotherapy and Protontherapy
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides excellent soft-tissue contrast without ionizing radiation but lacks the electron-density information needed for radiotherapy dose calculation. Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) improves tissue characterization and stopping-power ratio (SPR) estimation for proton therapy, but requires additional radiation exposure. We developed a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) to synthesize high- and low-energy CT (sHECT and sLECT) simultaneously from a single MRI scan. Retrospective paired MRI-DECT data from patients receiving head-and-neck proton therapy were used to train and evaluate a multi-decoder DDPM with SwinViT or ResUNet denoisers. Performance was compared with Pix2PixGAN and CycleGAN using image-quality metrics, Hounsfield unit (HU) errors, anatomical profiles, and SPR maps and uncertainties. The DDPM outperformed both generative adversarial network baselines in visual fidelity and quantitative image quality. For sHECT and sLECT, respectively, mean absolute errors were 36.29 +/- 5.25 and 43.72 +/- 6.77 HU; peak signal-to-noise ratios were 27.44 +/- 1.06 and 26.26 +/- 0.98 dB; structural similarity indices were 0.89 +/- 0.02 and 0.87 +/- 0.03; and normalized cross-correlations were 0.95 +/- 0.01 and 0.94 +/- 0.01. The synthesized images preserved anatomical boundaries, while uncertainties in derived SPR maps remained within the expected acceptable range. MRI-based DECT synthesis using DDPM may provide tissue-specific information for proton therapy planning while reducing the need for radiation-based DECT acquisition.

authors.name: Xiaofeng Yang
authors.institution: The Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering

papers.title: BIRD-Persona: A Persona-Aware Benchmark for SQL and pandas Analytics Code Generation
papers.abstract: Production text-to-code systems use large language models to turn natural-language analytics requests into executable SQL and pandas code. Existing benchmarks cover both tasks but do not isolate when performance diverges between them. We introduce BIRD-Persona, a persona-stratified extension of BIRD-Python that adds novice and expert rewrites to tasks with matched SQL and pandas ground truth, along with schema variants and task-structure annotations. Across 1,534 tasks, nine models, and 245,592 evaluations, SQL outperforms pandas for eight of nine systems. The gap varies by condition: expert, schema-explicit prompts improve both paradigms but help SQL more; schema representations have mixed, model-dependent effects; and selected-column burden widens the gap while subqueries do not. By making user phrasing a controlled benchmark dimension, BIRD-Persona supports persona-aware and paradigm-aware evaluation of natural-language analytics systems. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/optum-cognition-lab/BIRD-Persona.

papers.title: Formation of Multiple BGK-like Structures in the Time-asymptotic State of Collisionless Vlasov-Poisson Plasmas
papers.abstract: The time-asymptotic state of a finite-amplitude perturbation in a collisionless and Maxwellian plasma is typically represented as a steady state of two non-linearly superposed, counter-propagating Bernstein-Greene-Kruskal (BGK) modes. Using high-resolution Vlasov-Poisson simulations, we show that the plasma evolves self-consistently into a time-asymptotic state of multiple vortex-like structures that gradually fill the phase-space and reduce filamentation. This occurs without the need for external forcing or the presence of an energetic plasma population. This finding suggests that the time-asymptotic regime of the plasma is rather akin to a non-linear superposition of multiple BGK-like modes associated with nearly constant phase-speed waves. The electric field and the space-averaged particle distribution function exhibit a power-law broad spectrum, which is consistent with an energy cascade towards smaller scales in both position and velocity spaces.

papers.title: Identification multiplicity across study designs
papers.abstract: The answer to a causal question often admits several translations in terms of observed data. These may differ in adjustment sets, comparison groups, instruments, mediators, cutoffs, eligibility occasions, or data sources. We describe the resulting collection of analyses by three structures: the causal target that each analysis identifies under its assumptions, the assumptions that the analyses share, and the sampling dependence among their estimates. A single decomposition separates identification discrepancies from differences in causal targets, and we make both terms explicit in fourteen examples spanning adjustment, comparative panels, proxies, mediators, instruments, discontinuities, staggered adoption, sequential trials, and source combination. Comparisons within a collection can reveal differential violations of assumptions but not a bias common to all analyses; agreement is therefore evidence about the assumptions that differ, not about those that are shared. Averaging retains a causal interpretation in three ways: efficient combination of analyses that identify one target, a projection of a causal curve with a declared approximating family and weighting measure, and inference under weaker premises such as validity of at least one analysis or a known sign of its bias. Precision weights, regression-implied weights, and hierarchical models do not supply these interpretations by themselves. We relate this account to triangulation, overidentification, marginal treatment effects, transportability, and recent methods for inference under model uncertainty, and distinguish identification multiplicity from multiple testing.

papers.title: Hard to Translate, Harder to Detect: Human Analysis Remains Essential in AI Meme Translation
papers.abstract: We present a dataset and evaluation setup for a problem in creative machine translation: translating culturally loaded passages that carry much of a text's meaning and humor that may depend on subtle or implicit discourse. We study Soviet comedy quotations that function as memes in Russian-language communication. Off-the-shelf difficulty estimators do not find these passages; current models searching the web find most but not all of them, but their own analyses of the difficulty do not help translation as well as a human-validated one. Given a brief human-validated analysis of why each passage is difficult, older models improve modestly; the strongest current translators (GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5) improve more, and in human evaluation GPT-6 Sol comes close to the approved references on most films. Newer models have thus become much better at using such an analysis while still not reliably producing it themselves. We release (1) a dataset of five films' Russian subtitles with their audience-selected culturally salient passages, human-validated analyses, and reference translations (into English, Galician, and Spanish), together with every full-film LLM translation and evaluation produced in this study; and (2) an item-level MQM-style evaluation protocol that measures translator and evaluator noise to set the number of runs the evaluation needs, and whose automatic version tracks human judgment of these passages, which reference-free neural metrics do not, whether they score the whole text or the passages alone.

authors.name: Carla Martinez
authors.institution: Hospital Universitario Puerta de Hierro Majadahonda

papers.title: Compactness-like properties in Alexandroff paratopological groups
papers.abstract: We study compactness-like and covering properties in non-compact Alexandroff paratopological groups. Several properties are characterized in terms of the order structure associated with the Alexandroff topology and the number of connected components. We establish equivalences among $2$-pseudocompactness, countable $o$-compactness, Baire, and an intersection property for increasing chains. We also obtain a common characterization of $\sigma$-local compactness, $\sigma$-compactness, the Lindel\"of property, and left $\omega$-precompactness in terms of the existence of a countable cofinal subset. Moreover, we characterize pseudocompactness, $H$-compactness, star-compactness, the countable chain condition, and the weakly Lindel\"of property by means of the number of connected components. Finally, we determine further implications among the properties considered and provide examples and counterexamples.

papers.title: Gaudin's determinantal norm formula and Hall--Littlewood polynomials
papers.abstract: The Hall--Littlewood polynomials are orthogonal with respect to a discrete measure stemming from a discretization of the Lieb--Liniger model that describes $q$-bosons on the circle. This note establishes a previously conjectured Gaudin-type determinantal formula for their quadratic norms.

papers.title: Norm-attaining operators on renormings of $c_0$
papers.abstract: We study norm-attaining operators on three renormings of $c_0$: Read's space $\Read$, its smooth renorming $\sRead$, and Mart\'in's space $\X$. We prove that, for every Banach space $F$ and every $Z\in\{\Read,\sRead\}$, norm-attaining finite-rank operators are dense in $\K(Z,F)$. Consequently, $\NA(Z,F)$ is dense in $\Lin(Z,F)$ whenever $F$ is reflexive. More generally, we establish that the compact Hilbertian smoothing construction of Debs, Godefroy and Saint-Raymond \cite{DGS} preserves the density of norm-attaining operators for all finite-dimensional ranges. We also extend a second-order criterion of Kadets, L\'opez-P\'erez, Mart\'in and Werner \cite{KLMWfr} from rank two to arbitrary ranks $k\geq 2$ for operators into $\ell_2^k$, and prove that the same smoothing preserves the existence and non-existence of such operators. We further investigate the possibilities and limitations of renorming techniques for excluding rank-two norm-attaining operators through analytical and geometrical approaches, including constructions that preserve the set of norm-attaining functionals. For Mart\'in's space $\X$, we prove that, for every Banach space $F$ and every integer $1\leq k\leq\dim F$, there exists a rank $k$ norm-attaining operator from $\X$ into $F$, answering a question of Mart\'in \cite{Mar}. We also show that, for every nonzero Banach space $F$, $\K(\X,F)$ contains a norm-dense linear subspace whose nonzero elements fail to attain their norms.

papers.title: Who Speaks for the Water? Simulating Discursive Closure and Power Asymmetries in Hydrosocial Governance
papers.abstract: Water governance conflicts stem not only from material scarcity, but from power asymmetries, institutional distrust, and the discursive frameworks through which actors assign meaning to water, infrastructure, and legitimate authority. Conventional simulation tools represent these dynamics via numerical opinion variables, missing the argumentative and narrative dimensions structuring real deliberation in hydrosocial territories. We present the Hydrosocial Agent-Based Model with Large Language Models (HSABM-LLM), a hybrid framework enabling heterogeneous agents to generate, evaluate, and adapt natural language arguments conditioned on institutional roles, interaction histories, and territorial context. Grounded in semi-structured interviews, a water-user survey, and 456 press and official documents from the Longav\'i River sub-basin (Maule Region, Chile), the model simulates deliberation over a contested large-scale reservoir proposal across four experimental scenarios. Opinion convergence toward unanimous opposition emerged within 7-14 months, operating through discursive closure driven by distributive equity and water security framings rather than argumentative dominance. Governance actors accelerated convergence by activating pre-existing institutional distrust rather than direct persuasion, while peer-based smallholder interactions drove 77-79% of all opinion changes. The formal authority of state institutions proved structurally decoupled from deliberative influence, revealing a legitimacy deficit that formal inclusion alone cannot resolve. These findings suggest participatory governance design must attend to the discursive conditions under which institutional actors enter deliberative spaces, rather than assuming inclusion is inherently consensus-building. HSABM-LLM offers a novel platform for integrating political ecology insights into computational social science.

papers.title: Fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces revisited
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to revisit our work [J. Funct. Anal. 277 (2019), 333--367], where fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces were introduced and their behavior as the fractional parameter $s\uparrow1$ was studied, and to redo it without assuming the $\Delta_2$ condition on the Young function $G$ or on its complementary function. Since that paper appeared, the theory of these spaces has been considerably developed, and the tools available today allow for a cleaner treatment in full generality. We prove a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type formula as $s\uparrow1$, a compactness and lower semicontinuity result for sequences with bounded energy, a Poincar\'e inequality uniform in $s$, and the $\Gamma$-convergence of the fractional modulars to a local modular on arbitrary open sets. As an application we study the asymptotic behavior of minimizers and of solutions of Dirichlet problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian as $s\uparrow1$. This version also corrects some errors in the original paper, and it is intended to serve as a more complete and reliable reference for these results.

authors.name: Julian Fernandez Bonder
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: Checking the Cumulative Exposure Model: Cumulative Chi-Squared Goodness-of-Fit Tests for Interval-Monitored Step-Stress Life Tests
papers.abstract: In an interval-monitored step-stress life test the data are the numbers of devices that fail between consecutive inspections. These cells are ordered in time, but the usual goodness-of-fit check, Pearson's statistic, ignores the order. We propose goodness-of-fit tests based on the cumulative residuals, the differences between the empirical and the fitted distribution functions at the inspection times, with the parameters estimated by the minimum density power divergence estimator. The two statistics are Taguchi's cumulative chi-squared statistic and its version with constant weights, the classical members of a family of cumulative divergences for ordered categories, with the null probabilities replaced by those of the fitted model. For the exponential cumulative exposure model with a log-linear link we prove the existence, uniqueness and consistency of the estimator under explicit conditions, and we derive the limit distribution of the statistics under the null hypothesis and under contiguous alternatives: a weighted chi-square distribution with $L-s$ terms, where $L$ is the number of inspection times and $s$ the number of parameters. The critical values are obtained by plugging the estimated weights into Imhof's formula, and the procedure has asymptotic size $\alpha$. A local-power analysis and a simulation study show that the cumulative statistics are more powerful than Pearson's statistic against a wrong lifetime distribution, and that the limit distribution is accurate already with $50$ devices. An application to light bulbs tested under step voltage illustrates the method.

papers.title: Support functions of sections of $p$-minimal tubes
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact $p$-minimal hypersurface in ${\mathbb R}^{n+1}$ with boundary in two parallel hyperplanes. We study the convex hulls $\Omega(\tau)$ of its horizontal sections through their support function $H(\tau,\cdot)$, without any assumption on the topology of $M$. We prove that $H$ is a viscosity subsolution of a degenerate elliptic inequality. For $n=2$ it is of Monge--Amp\`ere type, and its equality case for minimal surfaces with circular sections is Riemann's system. A posteriori, $H$ is locally semiconvex and every hull is a smooth convex body; the inequality then also holds in the sense of measures, with the edges of the hulls appearing as atoms of Alexandrov's area functions. Averaging over directions gives a catenary-type inequality for the mean width of the hulls. It yields lifetime bounds for $p$-minimal tubes when $n>p$. For minimal surfaces in ${\mathbb R}^3$ it gives a sharp bound for the distance between the planes in terms of the perimeters of the hulls of the boundary curves, with equality only for a catenoid. For one convex curve in each plane this recovers, by a different method, the nonexistence and rigidity theorem of Bernstein and Breiner. The bound extends to non-convex curves and to boundaries with several components. Finally, we show that the Meeks annulus conjecture is equivalent to the absence of atoms in the area functions of the hulls of all intermediate sections.

papers.title: Reproducible by Seed? Not on GPUs: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models
papers.abstract: In text to image AI models, fixing the prompt and the random seed is widely assumed to fix the image. We show that it does not on GPUs. We evaluate six text-to-image models (diffusion and autoregressive) under four numerical precisions and quantizations on three GPU types (RTX A6000, RTX 6000 Ada, and H100 NVL), across up to 100 prompts per set for all six models. For each configuration we compare, with the prompt and seed fixed, the image generated alone with the image generated inside a batch, and we also compare across GPUs. Every replay control reported here is bit-exact, so the variation is not random noise: the execution setting, mainly the batch composition and the GPU, decides the output. The effect is large and model dependent. Structural similarity between the single-image and the batched output falls to 0.580 for an autoregressive model in bf16 and to 0.551 with int8. For a second autoregressive model in bf16 it falls to 0.261 with sampled decoding and to 0.229 with greedy decoding, and for an fp8 diffusion model to 0.68. A diffusion model in bf16 stays close to the batch-1 output (0.96-0.98) but changes every image. In most cases the batched image is a different but equally valid image; in some, such as prompts with digits and counters, it is visibly worse. Cross-GPU differences are of the same order as the batch effect: for one autoregressive model in bf16 compared across two GPU architectures (RTX 6000 Ada versus RTX A6000), no image is bit-identical and the cross-GPU LPIPS (0.355 to 0.383) matches the batch effect within one GPU (0.347 to 0.381). The consequences are direct: seeds do not make results reproducible, benchmarks and image-quality comparisons that mix batch sizes or hardware can be biased, and safety audits and A/B tests on generated images need the serving setup reported.

authors.name: Javier Conde
authors.institution: Instituto de Investigación Sanitaria de Santiago

authors.name: Xiuyuan Qi
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Femtosecond laser-controlled production of functional titanium niobate layers from TiO$_{2}$/Nb$_{2}$O$_{5}$ powders
papers.abstract: Conventional synthesis methods of titanium niobates (TNO) require prolongated high-temperature treatments. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we have developed a confined powder-bed femtosecond (fs) laser-based technique to sinter TNO films starting from a mixture of TiO$_{2}$ and Nb$_{2}$O$_{5}$ powders, avoiding furnace-based approaches. The influence of laser-processing conditions on film formation, phase composition, and microstructure is systematically investigated, demonstrating that different TNO phases and morphologies can be obtained by controlling the laser pulse energy. A comprehensive characterization of the processed films has been performed, providing insights into the mechanisms governing their formation, which appear to share key features with laser-induced backward transfer (LIBT) processes. Our findings establish the relationship between laser-processing conditions and TNO film formation, highlighting the potential of confined powder-bed fs-laser processing as an alternative route for manufacturing functional oxide layers. Tentative applications of these layers are finally discussed.

papers.title: All-in-one Spintronic Sensory Neurons for Magnetic Edge Intelligence
papers.abstract: Magnetic fields enable non-contact sensing through nonmagnetic materials, offering opportunities for magnetic edge intelligence in autonomous recognition, navigation, and control. However, directly converting magnetic stimuli into neural spikes for local neuromorphic processing remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate an all-in-one spintronic sensory neuron (SSN) based on spin-transfer-torque magnetic tunnel junctions (STT-MTJs) fabricated using a 40-nm magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) process. By exploiting magnetic-field-modulated stochastic switching, the SSN enables probability-based sensing with an electrically tunable sensitive field window, allowing adaptive operation across different magnetic-field ranges without structural modification. This tunability alleviates the fixed sensitivity-range constraint of conventional tunneling magnetoresistance sensing, providing an accessible sensing range of +/-40 mT with an average probability sensitivity of 2.91%/mT. Importantly, the same stochastic switching process directly transduces magnetic stimuli into binary spike trains, integrating magnetic sensing, nonlinear rate encoding, and spike generation within a single nanoscale device. The resulting sigmoidal spike-rate response enables magnetic-field encoding, experimentally validated using the Neural Engineering Framework. Using experimentally characterized device responses, a simulated 10 x 10 SSN array achieves 90.7% accuracy in contactless magnetic-trajectory recognition with optimized encoding, approaching the software baseline. These results establish a scalable, MRAM-compatible approach to unifying programmable magnetic sensing and neural encoding for sensor-native edge intelligence.

authors.name: Tao Huang
authors.institution: Henan University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jian Fu Zhang
authors.institution: China Iron and Steel Research Institute Group

papers.title: Surfaces of constant sectional curvature in Minkowski space with a canonical semi-symmetric connection
papers.abstract: We study surfaces in Minkowski space $\mathbb{R}^3_1$ with constant intrinsic sectional curvature with respect to canonical semi-symmetric connections, metric or non-metric, determined by a parallel vector field $\mathcal{V}$. We compute the ambient sectional curvature and obtain a formula for the intrinsic sectional curvature of nondegenerate surfaces in terms of their Gauss and mean curvatures. We provide a complete classification of cylindrical surfaces with constant intrinsic sectional curvature, covering all causal characters of $\mathcal{V}$ and of the rulings. For rotational surfaces whose axes are parallel to $\mathcal{V}$, we reduce the constant-curvature condition to an ordinary differential equation. Explicit solutions are obtained for null axes and, in the metric case, for surfaces with zero intrinsic sectional curvature.

papers.title: A Comparison of Uncertainty in AI and Dynamical Climate Ensembles
papers.abstract: Climate model ensembles and their uncertainty estimates are essential for evaluating risk and designing climate policy. Yet, in the assessment of newly developed AI climate models, evaluating uncertainty is often secondary to diagnosing mean-state climate biases and trends. In this work, we conduct the first systematic comparison of uncertainty representation in ensembles of state-of-the-art AI and dynamical atmospheric climate models. Examining 2-meter temperature, 500 hPa geopotential height, and precipitable water, we find that the AI ensemble exhibits reduced internal variability and model uncertainty across variables relative to the dynamical ensemble. We show that this dampened variability causes the AI ensemble to produce more limited climate extremes and yields underdispersion relative to ERA5. Under a uniform warming scenario, the AI ensemble shows increased model uncertainty. Dynamical models grapple with their own challenges, exhibiting stronger miscalibration (overdispersion) relative to ERA5 and larger climate biases than the AI models. As AI and dynamical climate models are mutually integrated into operational climate prediction, careful consideration of their differences in uncertainty representations is crucial for grounded assessment of climate risk.

papers.title: MemVanta: Memory-Efficient CPU Inference for Quantized GGUF Language Models
papers.abstract: Deploying large language models on commodity CPUs is often constrained not only by computational throughput but also by the resident memory required to execute quantized models within fixed system budgets. We present MemVanta, an experimental C++20 inference runtime for quantized GGUF language models that treats memory residency as a first-class systems objective. MemVanta combines memory-mapped model access, bounded tensor caching, quantized execution paths, paged key-value state, and explicit memory-pressure validation. We evaluate MemVanta against a pinned llama.cpp baseline using the same OpenLLaMA 7B v2 Q4_0 GGUF under CPU-only execution. Across five measured runs following warm-up, MemVanta records a peak resident set size of 3,983,412 KiB compared with 7,586,960 KiB for llama.cpp, corresponding to a 47.50 percent reduction in peak RSS. This memory reduction involves a substantial throughput trade-off: MemVanta achieves 3.15 +/- 0.04 tokens/s for prompt processing and 1.52 +/- 0.02 tokens/s for token generation, compared with 45.82 +/- 0.96 and 7.76 +/- 0.09 tokens/s, respectively, for llama.cpp. In a separate Linux cgroup-v2 experiment with swap disabled, MemVanta completes execution at a tested 3584 MiB memory ceiling, while llama.cpp is OOM-killed at that ceiling and first succeeds at the tested 3840 MiB level. These results position MemVanta as a memory-efficiency research prototype rather than a throughput competitor. We analyze the architectural mechanisms underlying this trade-off and discuss reproducibility, correctness, limitations, and opportunities for memory-constrained CPU and edge inference.

authors.name: Advik Gupta
authors.institution: Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi

papers.title: CART: Clustering-based Analysis of Recurring narratives for Taxonomy construction
papers.abstract: We present CART, a computational pipeline for extracting political narratives from parliamentary discourse and organizing them into a data-driven taxonomy without relying on predefined narrative categories. It encodes parliamentary discourse using semantic representations, filters relevant and reliable content through unsupervised confidence estimation, extracts narrative statements using LLMs, and uses narrative clustering and cluster analysis to construct a narrative taxonomy. Applied to Greek Parliament proceedings surrounding the 2023 Tempi train crash, it identifies ten recurring narrative families concerning responsibility attribution, institutional failure, railway safety, accountability, privatization, and the political interpretation of the tragedy. Our results demonstrate how combining unsupervised learning with LLM narrative extraction enables large parliamentary corpora to be transformed into interpretable, data-driven taxonomies of political narratives.

authors.name: Aggelos Semoglou
authors.institution: Athena Research and Innovation Center In Information Communication & Knowledge Technologies

authors.name: John Pavlopoulos
authors.institution: Athena Research and Innovation Center In Information Communication & Knowledge Technologies

papers.title: Tearing stability of pulsar equatorial current sheets
papers.abstract: Harris-type current sheets have been studied extensively with particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. These local configurations generally contain no systematic magnetic-field component normal to the current sheet. Such a component develops naturally in a global pulsar magnetosphere because reconnecting field lines connect the northern and southern magnetic hemispheres. We investigate how the normal field component affects the tearing stability and dissipation of the pulsar equatorial current sheet, and we examine the consequences for the global magnetospheric configuration. We combine the tearing-stability condition for a current sheet threaded by a normal field with the electromagnetic relations imposed by the surrounding ideal force-free magnetosphere. We also formulate a dissipative equatorial boundary condition and incorporate it into a global force-free model solved with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). For realistic Lundquist numbers the normal magnetic field can suppress the tearing instability. Preliminary solutions indicate two distinct magnetospheric configurations: a nearly ideal CKF-like state with negligible equatorial dissipation, and a strongly dissipative state resembling the solutions of Contopoulos et al. (2014) and Cerutti et al. (2015). The reconnection rate in the pulsar equatorial current sheet cannot be inferred from local Harris-type current sheet calculations because it depends on the global magnetic topology. Present global 3D PIC simulations operate at effective Lundquist numbers far below astrophysical values, and may therefore exhibit tearing that in a real pulsar magnetosphere would be strongly suppressed.

papers.title: Safety-Tiered ISAC Scheduling with History-Aware Value of Information for V2X Networks
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) assisted vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks prioritize safety-critical radar sensing over communication. However, existing scheduling methods overlook the varying criticality of vehicles, long-term fairness in service quality, and information staleness. Considering this, we propose a low-complexity sensing-prioritized allocation for radar and communication (SPARC-V) to maximize the value of information (VoI) in V2X networks. SPARC-V addresses these challenges with a two-stage hierarchical resource scheduling framework. For sensing, vehicles are first categorized into safety tiers based on a risk metric. Safety-critical vehicles receive orthogonal resources, while others can reuse resources under specific constraints. Sensing resources are allocated based on a sensing priority metric that balances safety significance and long-term fairness. In the next stage, communication resources are allocated to vehicles with the most outdated information. Performance is measured using a unified VoI metric that considers sensing quality, safety relevance, and information freshness. Monte Carlo simulations show that SPARC-V achieves the highest network VoI of 26.5 among all baselines, with its advantage over baselines widening as vehicle density increases.

papers.title: Economic cap coverings for log-concave measures
papers.abstract: Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Write $q_\mu$ for its half-space depth, $W_t=\{q_\mu \leqslant t\}$ for its wet part, and $w_\mu(t)=\mu(W_t)$. For sufficiently small $t$, we construct a cover of $W_t$ by half-spaces of measure at most $A_nt$, with cardinality bounded by $$D_n\frac{w_\mu(t)-w_\mu(a_nt)}{t},$$ where the constants depend only on $n$. For each $0<\varepsilon\leqslant 1$ we also construct a cover by half-spaces of measure at most $(1+\varepsilon)t$, with cardinality bounded by $$B_n\varepsilon^{-(n-1)/2}\frac{w_\mu(t)-w_\mu(a_nt)}{t}.$$ The exponent $(n-1)/2$ is optimal for $n\geqslant 2$, as shown by the Gaussian example. We further establish containment coverings for half-spaces in every dimension: there is a family of $O_n(w_\mu(t)/t)$ Borel covering sets, each of $\mu$-measure $O_n(t)$, such that every half-space of measure at most $t$ is contained in one covering set. We also obtain a relative wet-part estimate with sharp exponent $2/(n+1)$ and a reverse doubling inequality.

authors.name: Minas Pafis
authors.institution: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

papers.title: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Discover, Repair, and Migrate at the Edge
papers.abstract: Most LLM agent frameworks build a crew that runs a task and exits. Physical environments (e.g., homes, labs, factory floors) need agents that stay up for months, survive their own bugs, and run on whatever hardware is already next to the sensors. We present Wactorz, an open-source runtime in which LLM-generated agents are long-lived, supervised actors: a planner turns a chat request into Python, compiles it into a new actor at runtime, and a supervisor restarts that actor alone, with its state intact, when it crashes. All coordination rides on MQTT, so agents can be spawned on, and live-migrated between, edge nodes such as a Raspberry Pi, and every internal event is a topic external systems can subscribe to. The recorded demo builds a camera-to-lamp automation from one chat request, adds a second agent that is auto-wired to the first by topic and carries a deliberate division-by-zero, watches that agent repair its own code without losing its count, then deploys a fresh Raspberry Pi node and live-migrates the agent onto it, in under four minutes of wall-clock time and \$0.13 of model usage. This extended version adds what the two-page demonstration paper could not: the Wiring view of the topic graph, Wactorz as a library for hand-written agents, how trained models are stored, sent to nodes and replaced, the security model, and the system's limitations.

papers.title: Learning-Augmented QUBO for Time-Expanded Multi-Commodity Flow
papers.abstract: We study energy-aware multi-commodity flow on time-expanded graphs, a problem that captures dynamic routing in layered networks and is NP-hard in general. We formulate the problem as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problem, give an explicit penalty coefficient that provably guarantees feasibility, and show that it is smaller than the standard bound by a factor of roughly the number of active links. The layered structure of the time-expanded graph yields three structural results: a treewidth bound that gives a fixed-parameter tractable exact algorithm in the bag size, a matrix-product-operator representation of small bond dimension, and a proof that the annealing gap of the associated Ising Hamiltonian is strictly positive for every instance with a unique optimum, uniformly over bounded windows. For learning-augmented routing, we bound the Hamming distance between a predicted and an optimal flow by the flow error, and prove a consistency guarantee: a hybrid algorithm that keeps the better of the prediction and the solver output returns a flow whose cost exceeds the optimum by a factor that grows linearly with the prediction error. The results are exact statements about the QUBO and its associated Ising Hamiltonian, and they hold for any physical implementation.

papers.title: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
papers.abstract: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the generality of interface problems under consideration. To our knowledge, this careful analysis has not appeared in (nor does it follow easily from) literature published so far. Our explicit formulae directly lend themselves to explorations of solutions' qualitative properties such as regularity, asymptotic behavior and well-posedness. This work has also been of utility in the investigation of nonlinear counterparts as well as in the study of phase-transition phenomena, moving-interface and diffuse-interface problems. Such results for RAD and high-order PDEs will soon appear in a series of separate papers.

authors.name: Andreas Chatziafratis
authors.institution: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

authors.name: Georgia Karali
authors.institution: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

papers.title: Faculty Experience with Generative AI Integration into the Teaching and Learning Process
papers.abstract: This study was conducted to enhance our knowledge and understanding of the lived experiences of faculty regarding generative artificial intelligence (AI) in teaching and learning within the English and Communication Program at the American University of Armenia. This phenomenological qualitative research study used face-to-face, in-depth, open-ended interviews with five faculty members from the program. Faculty expressed different levels of conflict, voicing both positive and negative issues and concerns regarding their experiences with generative AI in the teaching and learning process. Five categories and 11 themes emerged from the analysis of these interviews, including concerns about academic integrity and student learning, as well as a lack of faculty AI training, understanding, and experience. Emergent themes indicated that faculty need additional support, including training and leadership guidance, in order to better understand the importance and benefits of effective AI utilization and AI literacy development. Faculty lacked sufficient experience with and understanding of generative AI capabilities and ongoing developments. Overall, faculty perceptions and attitudes toward generative AI within teaching and learning can be characterized as a mix of reservation and optimism.

papers.title: Cache the Knowledge, Not Just the Prompt: Dynamic Datalog as the Action Language for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: An LLM agent that answers questions about a knowledge graph writes a program per question, and its tools evaluate each from scratch. We give the agent a Datalog REPL, a session over a dynamic Datalog engine, in which rules are inserted and retracted like facts while derived facts stay current. Prompt caching reuses the model's processing of what a session shares, and the Datalog REPL reuses the evaluation of it. On chains of questions over three knowledge graphs, agents reuse a relation that the REPL keeps in 179 of 180 cases, with two models, and write fewer output tokens: SQL and Python agents write 23 to 82% more. With SQL tables or a Python namespace, Claude Haiku 5.5 stores almost nothing for later questions, and a chain of seven questions at 13 million facts takes it a median of 48 and 56 s, against 31 s with the REPL. Claude Opus 5.5 matches the REPL by storing tables in SQL, and when the data changes it stores views, which are evaluated again at every read. A relation that the REPL keeps is read like a table and stays current like a view. Datalog is a niche language beside SQL and Python, and with thinking enabled the models answer as accurately with it.

authors.name: Bruno Rucy Carneiro Alves de Lima

papers.title: Gorenstein and Ding injectivity over coherent rings
papers.abstract: For a commutative Ding--Chen ring $B$, we prove that Gorenstein and Ding injectivity coincide over $R=B[x,y]/(x,y)^2$ if and only if injective $B$-modules generate the unbounded derived category of $B$. We construct a commutative von Neumann regular ring $B$ whose unbounded derived category is not generated by its pure injective objects. For this $B$, the coherent ring $R$ admits a strongly Gorenstein injective module $G$ which is not Ding injective. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $G_{\mathfrak p}$ has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. The ring $R$ can be chosen to have cardinality $\aleph_\omega$, the least possible among coherent rings over which Gorenstein and Ding injectivity differ.

papers.title: Composing Independently Distilled Memory and Retrieval Policies for Long-Term Agents
papers.abstract: Long-lived Web assistants require effective memory and retrieval mechanisms to access information from past user interactions. While these capabilities can be learned through specialized policies, it remains unclear whether specialists trained independently in different environments can be effectively composed without joint optimization. This paper investigates compositional transfer through policy distillation. Memory-writing and sequential retrieval policies are independently distilled from frontier-model action trajectories into 3B models and combined with a fixed answer generator without downstream training. On a LongMemEval-based benchmark, the distilled composition achieves 73.1% accuracy, compared with 36.2% for a composition of existing RL-trained specialists, and also outperforms the evaluated RL-trained compositions on PersonaMem-v2. Component ablations reveal that improvements in individual policies depend on their composition, highlighting the importance of cross-specialist compatibility. Further task-specific adaptation improves accuracy to 75.2% on LongMemEval through RL and 48.9% on PersonaMem-v2 through supervised distillation. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of independent specialist distillation for modular multi-agent systems. Source code and datasets of teacher-generated memory-editing and retrieval trajectories are released to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
