papers.title: Defect Engineering of the Water-Carbon Interface: Insights from First-Principles Calculations
papers.abstract: Interactions at solid-liquid interfaces are fundamental to hydrovoltaic and catalytic technologies. While carbon nanomaterials have been extensively studied, the role of abundant defects in amorphous carbon remains poorly understood. Here, using first-principles calculations, we systematically investigate how various defects (topological, point, line, edge, and doping defects) modulate water-carbon interactions. We find that armchair-edge defects with dangling bonds reduce the energy barrier for water dissociation by up to 30 times compared with pristine carbon, while di-vacancies exhibit a near-zero Gibbs free energy for hydrogen evolution, enabling potential hydrogen evolution reaction activity on a purely carbon-based interface. Moreover, mono-vacancy defects, characterized by reduced electronic localization, enhance charge transfer to evaporating water molecules by up to 12.4 times, a key factor in evaporation-induced electricity generation. Crucially, we demonstrate that coupling distinct defects produces synergistic effects that outperform individual defects, revealing a promising strategy for designing multifunctional interfaces. These insights establish a defect-engineering framework for the rational design of high-efficiency hydrovoltaic and catalytic devices.

authors.name: Zhuhua Zhang
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Mechanical Structure Mechanics and Control

papers.title: Acoustic bound states in the continuum in a labyrinthine meta-atom
papers.abstract: In this Letter, we theoretically and experimentally study acoustic bound states in the continuum (BICs) emerging in labyrinth meta-atom embedded in an acoustic waveguide. A symmetry-protected BIC is supported in the lossless limit when the meta-atom is positioned on the waveguide axis. Breaking the symmetry by shifting the meta-atom away from the center of the waveguide transforms the BIC into a radiative quasi-BIC, manifested by the emergence of a narrow resonant feature in the transmittance spectrum. The proposed concept is experimentally tested using a 3D-printed labyrinthine meta-atom placed inside an impedance tube. The measured transmittance spectra are consistent with numerical simulations and support the BIC-to-quasi-BIC transition induced by symmetry breaking in the presence of thermoviscous losses. The resonance frequency, contrast, and linewidth can be controlled by varying the meta-atom position. The observed behavior is interpreted within a two-mode temporal coupled-mode theory (TCMT), providing an analytical description of the resonant response. The ability to tune radiative leakage in the presence of absorption makes the proposed acoustic BIC platform promising for the development of tunable absorbers, sensors, and modulators.

authors.name: Yunmeng Wang
authors.institution: Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University

papers.title: Kinetic inductance of two-dimensional viscous electron fluid
papers.abstract: Modern high-mobility two-dimensional electron systems are pure enough to manifest hydrodynamic regime of electron transport similar to dynamics of classical fluids. With the bulk scattering controlled by momentum-conserving electron-electron collisions, these novel hydrodynamic materials demonstrate systematic violation of conventional metallic behavior due to the Drude model in stationary electric transport. In this letter, we study the linear reactive AC response of 2D electron fluid in a narrow channel geometry and show that the essentially non-local viscous dissipation induces non-trivial size effect in it. In particular, kinetic inductance, which represents collective inertia of the entire electron fluid, is enhanced by non-uniform flow profile and, in contrast to diffusive transport, dominates the electrical impedance already in collisional regime by virtue of viscous skin effect. The onset of reactive behavior falls within the microwave frequency domain in the state-of-the-art 2D hydrodynamic conductors which makes them promising material system for applications in high-frequency electronics at elevated temperatures.

papers.title: Light Shining Through the Moon: A Lunar-Occultation Helioscope for Solar Axions
papers.abstract: We propose a lunar-occultation helioscope in which the Moon suppresses the direct solar x-ray beam before solar axions enter the terrestrial magnetosphere, where they may reconvert into keV photons. We evaluate the conversion with a geomagnetic model combining the IGRF-14 internal contribution and the Tsyganenko T89 external magnetospheric contribution, retaining the two signed transverse components in the oscillation amplitude. As an explicit realizability test, we propagate a circular near-600-km polar orbit through the 12 August 2026 occultation. A $4'$-radius region around the solar center remains lunar occulted for about $470$ s while the sunward line of sight stays clear of the Earth; the coherent magnetic lever arm spans $69.1$--$96.4~\mathrm{T\,m}$ with $\mathcal I_{B,\mathrm{rms}}=76.9~\mathrm{T\,m}$. A B16-AGSS09 Primakoff calculation shows that this aperture contains $97.4\%$ of the 3--15 keV axion flux. For an explicitly specified NuSTAR-like detector benchmark, the propagated single-event exposure gives an expected low-mass 95\% C.L. sensitivity of $g_{a \gamma}=1.31\times10^{-10}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. The proposal therefore establishes the plausibility of a distinct experimental channel for solar-axion searches, characterized by a lunar-defined spatial and temporal window and by a predictable geomagnetic modulation. A future detection would additionally provide directional access to the axion-emitting solar core, opening a complementary probe of the solar interior.

papers.title: Development of an Effective Federated Learning-Based Defense System Against Phishing Attacks on Mobile Platforms
papers.abstract: Phishing remains one of the most pervasive and damaging cyber threats, exploiting both technical flaws and human behavior to compromise sensitive data. We present a privacy-preserving, real-time defense that analyzes full webpage source code on mobile platforms. Our system combines a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for end-to-end feature extraction with a Federated Learning (FL) framework that updates models collaboratively on user devices without transferring raw data-supporting regulatory compliance and personalization. Evaluated on a large and diverse dataset, the model attains 86.02\% accuracy, 90.35\% precision, 80.64\% recall, and 92.78\% ROC-AUC. While some centralized, classical approaches may report higher accuracy, our design emphasizes a practical balance among accuracy, user privacy, and real-time performance on resource-constrained devices. We further demonstrate an end-to-end integration within the open-source Lightning Android browser, achieving real-time detection with low computational overhead. This work shows that privacy-first, AI-driven phishing detection is both feasible and scalable across mobile and IoT settings, delivering robust protection while keeping user data on-device.

papers.title: Spectral-Leakage-Guided Phase-Noise Compensation for Sub-THz OFDM
papers.abstract: Oscillator phase noise is a key impairment in sub-THz OFDM, where it spreads energy across subcarriers and generates inter-carrier interference (ICI). Since the resulting leakage depends on both the oscillator phase noise spectrum and OFDM numerology, the useful compensation dimension varies with the operating configuration. This letter develops a leakage-guided receiver framework that relates these characteristics to the retained dimension of dominant-component Least Squares (LS) compensation and its clustered-pilot support. At 130 GHz with 64-QAM, the minimum tested order achieving BER <= 10^-6 decreases from 9 at 240 kHz to 3 at 960-1920 kHz for Hexa-X Model 2, while the first 3GPP crossing at 1920 kHz occurs with Np = 13 at 38 dB. Order adaptation reduces Stage-2 arithmetic by 66%, while four-cluster pilots improve 32-dB goodput by 35% over comb allocation.

papers.title: An Algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay
papers.abstract: A 4-dimensional algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay over an arbitrary field is constructed. Furthermore, it is shown that every three-dimensional graded ASL domain is Cohen--Macaulay.

papers.title: Comparable Overrings of Marot Rings II
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a Marot ring. We study comparable overrings of $R$ that are integral over $R$, generalizing results of Ayache for integral domains. We show that such an overring has at most two regular maximal ideals. When $R$ has a unique regular maximal ideal, we study the three possible types and give characterizations of comparability and minimality in the first two cases. In the case of two regular maximal ideals, we describe the integral closure of $R$ as an intersection of two valuation overrings. We also obtain comparability criteria using normal pairs and finite chain conditions. Finally, we construct counterexamples giving negative answers to two conjectures posed by Ayache.

papers.title: Sharp constant off-diagonal extrapolation for Muckenhoupt bases
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a sharp constant version of off-diagonal extrapolation for matrix weights, improving the result we proved in an earlier paper. In an appendix, we give a new and simpler proof of this result in the scalar case.

papers.title: StutterStigma-TR: A Novel Turkish Dataset and Target-Aware BERT Framework for Stuttering-Related Stigma Detection
papers.abstract: Computational research on disability-related ableist harm remains limited, and condition specific resources for stuttering-related stigma are particularly scarce. This study introduces StutterStigma-TR, a Turkish dataset of 6,019 public X/Twitter posts annotated as Stigmatizing, Non-stigmatizing/contextual, or Supportive using a speech and language therapy-informed protocol with independent lived-experience evaluation. We also propose StutterStigma-BERT, a BERTurk-based target-aware framework that combines explicit target marking, target-span representation, target-conditioned context, character-level and handcrafted orthographic information, and gated discourse cues. The framework is evaluated in complementary three-class and binary settings using controlled three-seed ablation analyses and final 20-seed robustness evaluations. Under the common training protocol, Gated Discourse-OrthoTarget trained with cross-entropy is selected as the final configuration for both tasks based on internal-validation Macro-F1. Across 20 random seeds, the final three-class model achieves a mean Macro-F1 of 73.54%, while the final binary model achieves 85.17% using validation-selected decision thresholds. Task adapted harmful-language comparators are additionally evaluated under the common training protocol, and the proposed model obtains the highest mean Macro-F1 among them. For the primary three-class task, matched backbone analyses show higher internal validation Macro-F1 with BERTurk than with TurkishBERTweet or Turkish Mamba, while substantial train-validation separation persists across all three backbones. Separate direct-transfer and zero-shot experiments examine performance without StutterStigma-TR supervision. Across the task-adapted, direct-transfer, and zero-shot comparisons, the condition-specific supervised systems retain the strongest aggregate performance.

papers.title: Synthetic Twins: Closing the Gap Between TTS Test Sets and Real Recordings in Turkish ASR Evaluation
papers.abstract: Speech synthesized by text-to-speech engines is a low-cost substitute for recorded test sets in automatic speech recognition, yet an off-the-shelf synthetic test set is worth only a few dozen real recordings for estimating the real error rate of a recognizer. This paper examines which properties of real recordings are missing from synthetic speech and how much of the gap can be closed. For 507 Turkish Common Voice recordings, synthetic twins are built: a ladder of synthetic copies that adds, one factor at a time, the pitch of the speaker, a clone of the same speaker, the real recording channel and the speaking rate. At each step, the agreement between ASR behaviour on the copy and on the real recording is measured. Across three zero-shot cloning engines and panels of six and 19 recognizers, the speaker clone is the step that improves agreement on which sentences are hard, raising the Spearman correlation from .41 to .55 for Chatterbox. Matching the channel or adding generic noise corrects the error level when the synthetic speech is easier than real speech. The twin with the highest worth is equivalent to 70 to 122 real recordings, depending on the recognizer panel, compared with about 9 for a stock voice. The findings replicate on VoxForge, a second corpus in which speaker identity is known rather than inferred: the clone raises sentence agreement from .31 to .50 and the worth from 8 to about 50 recordings. Agreement on which sentences are hard is distinct from agreement on how hard they are. The paper concludes with a practical recipe and a reporting checklist for synthetic ASR test sets.

papers.title: The Privacy Cost of Writing an Audit Receipt Before Its Context Is Known
papers.abstract: An audit recorder must permit exact recovery with a small private index before it knows which questions a future reader will ask. A recursion on question partitions generates the decision trees, their eventwise costs and the price equations. A common-optimal-tree criterion explains when reduction to a fractional cover preserves the result. On uniform binary linear event spaces with four private roles, if every quartet is split evenly by some bit, optimal identification probability at expected follow-up budget $b$ is $(1+b)/2$. Otherwise it is $\min(1/2+b/3,3/4)$. We characterize all priors attaining the latter curve in its rising regime and derive a closed-form compiler for three binary fields. For a population tilted by one pairwise parity we obtain the full budget curve and a single recorder attaining it. On eight negotiated TLS suites the aligned populations allow a 60 percent follow-up rate at a 70 percent identification ceiling. A pairwise correlation with unchanged marginal field frequencies reduces that maximum to 40 percent. Across 960 local TLS sessions, the recorder recovered every negotiated suite using two private bits per session.

papers.title: Understanding Membership Inference Attacks on EEG Models
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals contain sensitive, subject-specific information, making models trained on them potential targets for membership inference attacks (MIAs). Although MIAs have been studied extensively in other domains, their applications to EEG models are relatively scarce, and the factors driving the vulnerability of EEG models to MIAs are not adequately understood. In this paper, we present a systematic empirical analysis of MIAs on EEG models using three datasets, seven model architectures, four attack methods, and two metrics. Results show that poor model generalization (large train-test loss and accuracy gap) is the strongest indicator of MIA vulnerability. Longer training and larger models also increase vulnerability. Moreover, no particular scalp region, frequency band, inter-channel correlation pattern, or temporal versus spectral representation of EEG data consistently explains MIA vulnerability across datasets. Finally, subject identification and leave-one-subject-out experiments indicate that models relying more heavily on subject-specific representations are more vulnerable to MIAs. Overall, our findings identify the key drivers of membership leakage in EEG models and can provide guidance for developing MIA-resilient EEG systems.

papers.title: TesseraFlow: Scalable Video Diffusion for Dynamic Medical Imaging Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Generative priors are state-of-the-art for modeling medical images in image reconstruction tasks, but reconstruction with video priors takes tens of seconds to minutes per frame. Latent priors inherit the errors of their autoencoder, the memory of pixel-space whole-frame priors grows with the frame size, and pixel-space patch priors are slow for two reasons. First, their deep networks process every frame at full resolution at every sampling step, even though early steps resolve only low frequencies. Second, their samplers spend many network evaluations per sampling step on overlapping windows, multiple re-noising rounds, or backpropagation through the prior. We introduce TesseraFlow, a complex-valued pixel-space flow prior that reduces the first cost. A global encoder reads a low-resolution view of every frame once per sampling step. A single shallow decoder operates on this view during early steps and on full-resolution space-time tiles during later steps, so no network processes a whole frame at full resolution. Our sampler, ReTile, addresses the second reason. We use randomized grid shifting at every sampling step along with re-noising, which acts as a stochastic gradient instead of computing overlapping tiles, so a single network pass per sampling step suffices. On its own, ReTile speeds up an existing global-context patch prior by 6-9x, and our prior adds a further 3-5x speedup. TesseraFlow reconstructs about one 256x256 frame per second, 20-367x faster than patch and latent video priors, and can match or exceed the best generative baseline on cardiac, brain, and abdominal MRI and lung CT, at a fraction of its GPU time.

papers.title: Integrated Study of NGC 1662, NGC 1778, NGC 2422, and NGC 2437 Open Clusters: from Stellar Parameters to Orbital Trajectories Utilizing Gaia DR3 Archive
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive photometric, astrometric, and dynamical study of four Galactic open clusters, NGC 1662, NGC 1778, NGC 2422, and NGC 2437, using Gaia DR3 data. Probable cluster members were identified through astrometric and photometric criteria. Radial density profiles were modelled with a King-type surface-density distribution to derive structural parameters. Mean parallaxes and proper motions yielded astrometric distances of 410 +/- 12 pc (NGC 1662), 1761 +/- 335 pc (NGC 1778), 477 +/- 18 pc (NGC 2422), and 1681 +/- 172 pc (NGC 2437). Fundamental astrophysical parameters were estimated through Bayesian isochrone fitting using PARSEC evolutionary models within an MCMC framework. The resulting ages (log(t/yr)) are 8.91 (-0.33/+0.24), 8.20 (-0.11/+0.18), 7.80 (-0.11/+0.06), and 8.56 (-0.34/+0.27), respectively. Luminosity functions were transformed into present-day mass functions using an isochrone-based mass-luminosity relation. The derived mass-function slopes are broadly consistent, within uncertainties, with the classical Salpeter form. Mean systemic radial velocities from Gaia DR3 and complementary spectroscopic surveys enabled the determination of Galactic space velocities (U, V, W) in the Local Standard of Rest frame. Backward orbital integrations over 3 Gyr were performed using galpy with the MWPotential2014 Galactic potential. The resulting orbits are nearly circular (e <= 0.106), with limited vertical excursions (Z_max < 0.3 kpc), consistent with thin-disc kinematics. Inferred birth radii suggest possible outward radial displacement for NGC 2422, NGC 2437, and NGC 1778, and inward displacement for NGC 1662. Overall, all four clusters appear to have evolved within relatively stable Galactic disc orbits.

papers.title: BiLight: A Fast Method for Estimating Counts of 6-Vertex Bipartite Motifs in Large Graphs
papers.abstract:
Motifs, or small subgraphs, are fundamental building blocks of complex networks. Analyzing their frequency distribution provides deep insights into the local structure of graphs, with applications in social network analysis, bioinformatics, and web mining. However, exact enumeration of motifs becomes computationally expensive as the size of the motif and the network increases. This challenge is particularly acute for bipartite motifs, which are ubiquitous in modeling relationships like user-item, author-paper, and actor-movie interactions.
  In this work, we present BiLight (Bipartite Lightweight motif estimation), a scalable framework for estimating the frequencies of all 17 non-isomorphic 6-vertex bipartite motifs. Specifically, we focus on estimating the non-induced counts of these motifs, which is a common requirement in many graph mining tasks.
  Our approach relies on a randomized path sampling of paths on four vertices. We use an efficient, weighted strategy by counting the ways that each sampled path can be extended to one of the 17 motifs. This framework yields unbiased estimates of the global motif counts. We conduct extensive experiments on networks of various sizes.
  Our experiments demonstrate that BiLight converges rapidly to the ground truth with high accuracy, even on massive networks where exact counting is infeasible.
  The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/celikmustaa/BiLight.

papers.title: Weakly Nonlinear Whitham Modulation and Dispersive Shock Waves in the Modified Gardner Equation
papers.abstract: We investigate weakly nonlinear Whitham modulation and dispersive shock waves (DSWs) in a modified Gardner equation. A three-equation modulation system is derived through a Stokes expansion and averaged conservation laws. Perturbative analysis of its characteristic structure provides explicit conditions for hyperbolicity and genuine nonlinearity, and identifies a wavenumber-dependent transition between real and complex characteristic splitting. The dispersive resolution of compressive Riemann data is examined using DSW fitting, yielding analytical predictions for the harmonic- and solitary-wave edge velocities. The solitary-wave prediction is further supported by a traveling-wave energy analysis. Numerical continuation of the modulation characteristics identifies the limitations of the weakly nonlinear approximation, while direct numerical simulations using a Fourier pseudospectral method confirm close agreement with the predicted leading-edge velocity and the leading solitary-wave amplitude for the resolved cases. These results clarify the weakly nonlinear characteristic structure and the edge dynamics of dispersive shocks for the modified Gardner equation.

papers.title: CineAct: Interaction-State Agents for Playable, Branching Film Generation
papers.abstract: Open video generators such as MiniMax-H3 produce short clips of only several to a dozen seconds per run. To synthesize longer sequences, existing methods either rely on agentic systems following preset scripts, or roll out autoregressively from the previous clip's last frame, losing off-screen states and accumulating hallucinations across turns. Consequently, users still cannot take an explicit goal, choose how to accomplish it, and see that choice persist across subsequent clips. We study goal-grounded interactive video generation, where one goal admits multiple valid approaches, the user's chosen approach must be executed on screen, and its consequences must persist across clips. To this end, we propose CineAct, a state-first agentic framework in which language-model agents handle reasoning while frozen image and video generators serve purely as renderers. Before interaction, the Architect initializes the world as a spatial layout with cameras, an asset library, and a scene graph; at each turn, the system deduces the planned state change, generates a target end frame with an image generator and rigorously verifies it, and synthesizes intermediate motion with an FL2V model. We further introduce a multi-space benchmark covering two suites: long-horizon step execution and open-intent branching admissibility. Experiments show that explicit world-state modeling boosts multi-step rollout consistency over the pixel-only baseline (+11.4 automated, +23.1 human points) and raises paired branching success toward a shared goal by +30.8 points.

authors.name: Hanxin Zhu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Shuai Li
authors.institution: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland

papers.title: A No-Code Toolchain for Validating Wearable Motion Sensing Systems
papers.abstract: Designing e-textiles for human motion sensing often demands engineering expertise for sensor data processing, typically relying on advanced machine learning methods. In addition, validating designs---collecting sensor measurements and ground-truth motion data, training and testing machine learning models, and iterating on sensor layouts---can be labour- and time-intensive. To address this, we present a no-code toolchain that enables non-technical users to validate system designs efficiently. The tool provides three key capabilities: (1) deriving ground-truth joint-angle measurements from webcam recordings; (2) training and testing machine learning models using collected sensor data; and (3) visualising and analysing motion sensing performance and sensor layout choices. Our tool requires a simple, low-cost setup and produces test reports within minutes. A user study was conducted to validate the usability of this toolchain. This toolchain is open source and available at https://github.com/yaozhang182/etextile-validation-gui.

papers.title: Quantity-Level FDIA in SDR-Based P2P Energy Trading: Cyber-Economic Impact and Pre-Clearing Detection
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the cyber-economic impact and pre-clearing detectability of false data injection attacks (FDIAs) in peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading among interconnected microgrids. In the proposed cyber-economic framework, load and photovoltaic profiles drive a sequential 15-minute market with deterministic double-sided proportional (pro-rata) allocation and supply-to-demand-ratio (SDR) pricing, while true physical injections are separated from communicated market quantities. The framework is evaluated through a multi-microgrid case study over 69,904 market-aligned states, for which all AC power-flow solutions converged and voltages remained within 0.98999-1.04369 per unit. Healthy local exchange reached 1,159.66 MWh and generated USD 92,772.62 of community benefit. Bias, scaling, and ramp attacks modify only one microgrid's communicated quantity, altering the settlement price, P2P allocation, scheduled residual-grid exchange, participant financial outcomes, and benefit fairness, while true feeder injections remain unchanged. Role-specific random forest, statistical threshold, and score-fusion detectors are compared using only information available before clearing. Pooled sample-level detection rates range from 7.82% to 12.14%, with false-alarm rates from 4.69% to 7.70% and role dependence. In the investigated case study, measurable downstream economic distortion and low pre-clearing detectability coexist under bounded quantity manipulation.

papers.title: Enabling Verifiable Output Lineage for Virtualized ML Workload Execution
papers.abstract:
Machine learning (ML) property attestation lets a model provider demonstrate properties of their models and datasets to verifiers, and trusted execution environments (TEEs) have emerged as its most practical mechanism. However, existing TEE-based systems attest only a static snapshot of the TEE's initial configuration, leaving run-time behavior unauditable. Proof of execution (PoX) architectures close this gap by requiring the prover's root of trust to also demonstrate that (1) the attested operation actually executed and (2) the claimed outputs were affected only by that operation. Existing PoX designs, though, target microcontrollers and rely on hardware features unavailable in server-grade TEEs, so they cannot be applied directly to ML workloads.
  We present EVOLVE, a software-based PoX framework for server-grade TEEs. EVOLVE mediates an operation's writes and control flow to track whether a requested ML operation executes without violation. It binds the execution status to measurements of the operation's inputs and outputs, enabling verifiers to assess run-time behavior through ML property attestation. We implement EVOLVE on Intel TDX as a Rust module within its virtual firmware, with policy checks built on primitives formally verified in F*. Our evaluation shows that EVOLVE is versatile across diverse ML applications on unmodified hardware, provides formal guarantees for its policy checks. EVOLVE incurs per-request run-time overhead on average ranging from 1.07$\times$ (for decision trees) to 2.13$\times$ (for multi-layer perceptrons).

papers.title: Quantum Hall Effect in a 3D Cross-Dimensional Quantum Anomalous Hall System
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate cross-dimensional transport and the resulting quantum Hall effect in 3D quantum anomalous Hall effect systems, which are constructed by coupling two Weyl-semimetal Hamiltonians. Our study unveils that the system hosts highly anisotropic surface states and chiral modes, leading to rich quantum Hall responses. Crucially, we clarify how magnetic fields applied along three high-symmetry directions dictate the evolution of the Chern numbers, chiral modes, and Hall responses. We discover that chiral modes along different directions can originate from distinct mechanisms, giving rise to various magnetic modulation characteristics. Furthermore, we unveil the breakdown of the conventional Chern-number-based bulk-boundary correspondence under magnetic fields, where the Chern numbers alone fail to fully characterize the evolution of the chiral states. This anomalous behavior is attributed to the unique momentum-space distributions of surface bands. These insights are further validated numerically through multi-terminal Hall transport simulations. Our findings expand the understanding of magnetic-field-driven mechanisms in 3D topological systems and provide deeper insights into the interplay between quantized Hall effects and Chern numbers in 3D systems.

papers.title: OCCA-Seg: Object and Channel Context Aggregation for Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images
papers.abstract: Semantic segmentation, which assigns a class label to each pixel, is a key task in computer vision. However, semantic segmentation of remote sensing images (RSIs) remains challenging because of complex scenes and objects at multiple scales, which limits segmentation accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose a context aggregation scheme called object and channel context aggregation (OCCA), consisting of three components: object contextual attention module (OCAM), channel contextual attention module (CCAM), and aggregation module (AM). Firstly, motivated by the observation that each pixel shares the class label of the object to which it belongs, object-level context represents each pixel through aggregating context from its corresponding object class. Secondly, because feature channels are correlated with object categories, channel-wise context models channel-wise contextual dependencies conditioned on object categories. Finally, the context information from OCAM and CCAM are fed into AM and used to weight and modulate the object context, enhancing the discriminative ability of the segmentation model. The experiments on several public remote sensing datasets including LoveDA, UAVid, ISPRS Potsdam, and Vaihingen datasets demonstrate competitive improvements over existing methods.

papers.title: CGSpec: Consistency-Guided Speculative Decoding with Overlap-Aware Verification Scheduling for Edge-Cloud Inference
papers.abstract: Collaborative speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by enabling edge clients to draft tokens locally and a shared cloud model to verify them. However, draft target disagreement wastes communication and verification resources, while heterogeneous client return times complicate shared verifier scheduling. We propose CGSpec, a consistency guided framework for multi client edge-cloud speculative decoding. CGSpec uses draft target distribution divergence to adapt the speculative budget and introduces a nomination and competition mechanism to construct candidate trees through global growth control and local token selection. An overlap-aware scheduler further estimates remaining verification work and client return times to prioritize requests and improve verifier utilization. We evaluate CGSpec using four model pairs and three datasets under heterogeneous network conditions. Across 24 configurations with 8 and 16 clients, CGSpec achieves the highest mean system and client throughput among the evaluated methods. Compared with current SOTA methods, it improves system throughput by 12.2\% and 10.2\%, and mean client throughput by 14.0\% and 33.0\%, respectively.

papers.title: Interpolation of nonlocal Sobolev spaces for general gradients
papers.abstract: We study the interpolation structure of nonlocal Sobolev spaces associated with general radial gradients. For compactly supported kernels satisfying suitable regularity and two-sided growth assumptions of fractional order, we characterize the spaces $H^{\rho,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $1<p<\infty$, by the Gustavsson--Peetre interpolation method between $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The function parameter is determined, up to equivalence, by the behavior of the kernel near the origin. We also establish a complex interpolation formula between spaces associated with different kernels and integrability exponents, in which the interpolated kernel is their geometric mean. For the corresponding nonlocal Gagliardo spaces $W^{\rho,p}(\R^n)$, defined through an integral seminorm of first differences, we prove an identification with generalized Besov spaces and a real interpolation characterization involving the same function parameter. These results extend the classical relation between Bessel potential and Gagliardo spaces beyond power-type kernels, yielding continuous embeddings between the two families and their coincidence in the Hilbertian case. We further discuss logarithmic kernels and restriction spaces on Lipschitz domains, and obtain extension and compact embedding results for the Gagliardo spaces under weaker assumptions on the kernel.

papers.title: Growth versus boundedness for viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations with a forcing term: a Fujita-type dichotomy
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t=\Delta u+|\nabla u|^q+a(t)w(x)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, where $q>1$ and the integrable forcing has positive total mass. Unlike classical Fujita problems, regular solutions exist globally, so the relevant dichotomy concerns boundedness versus grow-up. We identify the critical exponent $q_c=N/(N-1)$ for $N\geq 2$, with $q_c=\infty$ for $N=1$. For stationary forcing, every solution grows at least linearly on a fixed ball when $1<q\leq q_c$. In two dimensions, solutions tend to infinity locally uniformly for every $q>1$, with an explicit logarithmic lower bound. For $q=2$, the Cole--Hopf transformation relates the exact growth rate to the spectrum of $-\Delta-w$. Conversely, when $N\geq 3$ and $q>q_c$, bounded solutions exist for sufficiently small nonnegative data and forcing. We also establish growth criteria for time-dependent forcing, including decaying profiles.

papers.title: Existence and nonexistence of global solutions to a semilinear parabolic equation with variable reaction on sub-Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t-\Delta_{\mathcal{M}}u=h(t)[f(u)]^{p(x)}$ on $\mathcal{M}\times(0,T)$, with $u(\cdot,0)=u_0\in L^q(\mathcal{M})$, where $\mathcal{M}$ is a complete sub-Riemannian manifold endowed with a smooth volume measure and $\Delta_{\mathcal{M}}$ denotes the associated sub-Laplacian. The function $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty))$, $f$ is nonnegative and continuous, and $p$ is a bounded measurable function on $\mathcal{M}$. We establish sharp criteria for the existence and nonexistence of nonnegative global solutions. In particular, our framework applies to connected unimodular Lie groups, yielding global existence, nonexistence, and Fujita-type results. Our approach allows for nonlinearities $f$ beyond the convex setting, thereby broadening the scope of earlier nonexistence results in the Euclidean framework. Furthermore, our results generalize those of Ruzhansky and Yessirkegenov, whose analysis relies on polynomial-type bounds of the form $K_1u^p\le f(u)\le K_2u^p$ with fixed constants $K_1,K_2>0$ and $p>1$.

papers.title: Group Buying through Bankruptcy Rules: Cost Sharing and Endogenous Pricing
papers.abstract: Group buying allows independent buyers to pool their demand and benefit from quantity discounts that would not be available to them individually. While collective purchasing reduces total procurement costs, it raises a fundamental allocation question: how should the resulting savings be distributed among heterogeneous buyers? We address this question by integrating cost-allocation and bankruptcy approaches into a unified group-buying framework. Starting from a continuous quantity discount function, we examine cost-gap-based allocation mechanisms and develop an endogenous pricing representation in which each buyer's effective discount may depend on the demand profile of the entire group. We then establish a connection between group buying and bankruptcy theory by interpreting the aggregate savings from cooperation as the estate and each buyer's potential savings as its claim. This formulation allows us to derive cost-allocation mechanisms based on the proportional, constrained equal awards, constrained equal losses, and Talmud rules. For each rule, we obtain the corresponding buyer-specific price function and characterize the associated variable discount factor. We further examine the relationships between bankruptcy-based and cost-gap-based allocation mechanisms and use a numerical example with simulated data to compare their implications. The proposed framework links alternative fairness principles for allocating cooperative savings to economically interpretable pricing mechanisms, providing a unified basis for analyzing how group purchasing gains are distributed among heterogeneous buyers.

authors.name: A. Meca
authors.institution: The University of Texas at San Antonio

papers.title: LaTSEC: Lattice-Based Threshold Signatures with Native Non-Interactive Identifiable Abort and Compact Per-Party Storage
papers.abstract: We present $\mathsf{LaTSEC}$, a three-round lattice-based threshold signature scheme with native non-interactive identifiable abort. Each party holds one small-norm signing share and is associated with one public abort key, against which its partial signature is verified directly, without zero-knowledge proofs or an additional interactive protocol. Prior lattice-based threshold signatures that identify misbehaving parties rely on one of three mechanisms: zero-knowledge proofs, an additional interactive protocol, or an everywhere-short secret sharing scheme in which each party holds multiple signing shares, each with its own public abort key. Compared with schemes that use the third mechanism, $\mathsf{LaTSEC}$ substantially reduces per-party storage. The construction uses $\mathsf{SEC}$, a recent ramp everywhere-short secret sharing scheme based on lossless expanders that gives each party a single short share. We prove correctness, identifiable-abort security, and threshold unforgeability under the standard $\mathsf{MLWE}$ and $\mathsf{MSIS}$ assumptions. The unforgeability proof introduces the Repeated-$\boldsymbol{A}$ Matrix Hint-MLWE problem, a new variant of $\mathsf{MLWE}$ with hints that captures the complete tuple of correlated public abort keys. We rigorously prove that this new variant admits a reduction from the standard $\mathsf{MLWE}$ problem. For 60 parties at 128-bit security, $\mathsf{LaTSEC}$ tolerates up to 6 corrupted parties, and, empirically, a randomly chosen set of at least 46 parties can sign with probability at least 0.99. Each party holds one signing share of about 14.3 KiB and is associated with one 24-KiB public abort key.

papers.title: Global Stability Analysis of an Excitable Infinite-Dimensional System
papers.abstract: Motivated by the study of excitable control of infinite-dimensional linear systems, we investigate the global stability properties of a closed-loop system consisting of a stable linear infinite-dimensional plant and a non-monotone controller. The controller has piecewise-linear dynamics that resemble the FitzHugh-Nagumo model of neural behaviour. As our main result, we derive a checkable condition for the global exponential stability of the closed-loop system using the circle criterion. Finally we illustrate the stability result for a one-dimensional heat equation.

papers.title: Gorenstein homological algebra over comma categories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories with enough projective objects. In this paper, we characterize those functors $F:\mathcal{A}\to \mathcal{B}$ for which the Gorenstein projective objects in the comma category $(F\downarrow \mathcal{B})$ admit an explicit description in terms of the Gorenstein projective objects of $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$. As a main application, we obtain estimates for the global Gorenstein projective dimension of $(F\downarrow \mathcal{B})$ in terms of those of $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ and the functor $F$, and derive exact formulas in several important cases. Our categorical approach also yields dual results concerning Gorenstein injective objects and dimension. Special attention is devoted to the module category over a triangular matrix ring $ \begin{pmatrix} A & 0\\ U & B \end{pmatrix}$, the product category $\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{B}$, and the $n$-morphism category $Mor_n(\mathcal{C})$ associated with an abelian category $\mathcal{C}$ and an integer $n\geq 2$.

papers.title: On the stress-bienergy tensor of conformal immersions and hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study the stress-bienergy tensor $\bar S_2$ of a conformal immersion $\phi:(M^m,\bar g)\to(N^n,h)$ with conformal factor $\lambda$, and we compute it, together with its trace and its divergence, in terms of $\lambda$ and of the second fundamental form of the associated isometric immersion. This gives a characterization of biconservative conformal immersions and, for hypersurfaces, we prove that $\mathrm{div}\,\bar S_2=0$ if and only if the tangent part of the bitension field vanishes. We introduce conformally biconservative hypersurfaces and show that a totally umbilical hypersurface of a space form is conformally biconservative with a non-constant conformal factor if and only if this factor is an isoparametric function satisfying an explicit ordinary differential equation. We illustrate this result with several examples, in which dimension four plays a special role. Finally, we study the equation $\bar S_2=0$: on a compact manifold of dimension $m\neq 4$, it forces the associated isometric immersion to be harmonic.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Dynamics of R-loop Formation in the CRISPR-Cas9 System
papers.abstract: The binding specificity of CRISPR-Cas9 is governed by the stepwise formation of an R-loop, in which the sgRNA displaces the nontarget DNA strand and hybridizes with the target strand in discrete base pair steps. Here we develop a nonequilibrium dynamics framework that models R-loop formation as a continuous-time Markov birth-death process over twenty base pairs. Each transition rate is derived from Eyring transition-state theory and the Bell model, and combines three physical contributions, i.e., the torsional strain generated by the B-form to A-form helical conversion at the unwinding front, a base stacking correction that couples neighboring base pairs, and the allosteric work supplied by Cas9 conformational changes. We further derive the entropy production of the process, which is decomposed into activation, stacking, torsional, and allosteric terms. The resulting prediction model uses no external thermodynamic database and reaches Spearman correlations of 0.84 and 0.82 in two independent libraries of dCas9-sgRNA mismatch variants measured in vivo. The mismatch-type dependence is carried by one twist deviation and one pairing weight per type. Our model recovers the seed region sensitivity, the PAM-proximal activity gradient, and the moderate cost of dDrG mismatches, while isolating the high-activity double mismatch tail as the regime in which the present free-energy mapping is inadequate. The framework gives quantitative predictions on how DNA supercoiling and sequence context modulate binding affinity, and provides a mechanistic basis for sgRNA design.

papers.title: Integrating a one-dimensional convolutional neural network with nonlinear model predictive control for slug flow modeling and control
papers.abstract: Severe slugging in pipeline--riser systems degrades production efficiency and threatens equipment integrity, motivating the development of accurate yet deployable control models. This paper presents a lightweight, data-driven modeling and control framework specifically designed for slug flow. First, we revisit a commonly used low-order mechanistic model and introduce two changes that improve physical plausibility and numerical robustness: (i) an explicit zero-outflow boundary during the starvation period at the riser top, and (ii) a reformulated expression for the liquid volume fraction at the riser top that enforces admissible bounds. Synthetic input--output trajectories generated by this model are then used to train a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN) that parameterizes a neural ODE with an affine-in-control. Training employs an 8-step free-roll objective on standardized data; a differential sensitivity check confirms an explicit control channel. The learned model is embedded in a shooting-based nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) scheme with bounded and rate-smoothed actuation. In closed-loop simulations at {\Delta}t = 0.1 second, the controller drives the output to a constant setpoint within approximately 15--18 seconds while maintaining smooth, bounded inputs and non-oscillatory transients. The results indicate that a simple 1D CNN, coupled with NMPC, can capture the characteristic oscillations and regime transitions of slug flow and deliver effective regulation with modest computational cost. Although training is conducted offline to ensure reproducibility, the architecture and identification procedure are designed for extension to online learning, providing a practical path toward adaptive slug-flow mitigation.

papers.title: Spin-controlled thermophase and noise-optimized thermometry in multiorbital quantum dots
papers.abstract: Converting temperature differences into electrical signals underlies both thermoelectric energy conversion and thermometry, which is essential for managing heat in cryogenic quantum technologies. Superconducting circuits typically show a weak thermoelectric response, since their quasiparticle spectrum is nearly particle-hole symmetric. In a Josephson junction, a temperature difference can instead be converted into a superconducting phase difference in an open circuit. We investigate this thermophase effect in a setup where the junction consists of a two-orbital quantum dot with Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and Zeeman splitting. A second orbital near the superconducting coherence peaks supports quasiparticle transport over a broad gate range. Zeeman splitting can enhance the thermophase by suppressing pair transport, while spin-orbit hybridization shifts the orbital resonances and can reverse the sign of the response. We assess the junction as a phase-based thermometer using a noise budget that includes readout and current noise together with fluctuations of the orbital energies and the magnetic field. The optimal operating points do not maximize the thermophase but balance a large quasiparticle response against sensitivity to parameter fluctuations. Under experimentally motivated noise assumptions, we obtain projected noise-equivalent temperatures of order $10\,\mu\mathrm{K}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ and determine the range over which a linear calibration remains accurate. Gate-tunable quantum-dot junctions thus offer a phase-based route to sensing temperature differences in superconducting circuits at sub-kelvin temperatures.

papers.title: Refined, Reliable and Reproducible: Algorithmic Analysis and Reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder
papers.abstract: Cosmic voids are vast underdense regions of the Universe that encode valuable information about its large-scale structure and evolution. By extending spherical voids into overlapping sphere structures, the Popcorn Void Finder demonstrated an improved statistical characterization of cosmic void populations. However, its origin as a research prototype progressively hindered its maintainability and extensibility. Moreover, post-publication algorithmic modifications have not been systematically evaluated, leaving their statistical and computational consequences insufficiently characterized. In this work, we present a comprehensive reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder, prioritizing algorithmic transparency, maintainability, and reproducibility. We document the complete identification procedure, revisit the original algorithmic choices, and evaluate their statistical and computational consequences. Comparisons between implementations revealed a significant change in the behavior of the Void Size Function, which is now characterized by a power-law regime transitioning to a Schechter-like distribution. These changes not only provide a better characterization of void sizes, but enable a new and more robust method to the determination of the shot-noise dominated regime, without implicit dependencies on internal finder parameters present in previous works. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a 1.62x speedup in spherical void identification and a substantial improvement in overlap-removal throughput. We determined the Popcorn algorithm to be negatively affected by load imbalance, and found a speedup of 63x in a tested configuration with a newly introduced early growth termination criterion. These results establish a more maintainable and reproducible foundation for popcorn void identification, while clarifying the statistical and computational trade-offs that govern its performance.

papers.title: Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Operators: Strict Monotonicity and Asymptotic Behavior
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the properties of the generalized principal eigenvalue for a coupled local/nonlocal operator. First, we establish sufficient conditions to guarantee strict monotonicity properties, obtaining weaker hypotheses than those currently available in the literature for nonlocal operators. Next, we establish several results concerning the asymptotic behavior of this generalized eigenvalue, along with the convergence of the corresponding eigenfunctions. These results are very useful for the study of nonlinear problems. Our findings reveal novel phenomena that are not present in purely local or purely nonlocal cases. The main mathematical difficulty lies in the fact that the generalized eigenvalue does not always admit an eigenfunction, in addition to the inherent technicalities of the considered coupling.

papers.title: Finite simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes
papers.abstract: A theorem by Guralnick classifying finite simple groups with subgroups of prime power index implies that $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ is the unique finite non-abelian simple group whose maximal subgroups all have prime power index. Motivated by this result and appealing to Li and Li's classification of primitive permutation groups of degree $p^a q^b$, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes, we classify all finite non-abelian simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes, proving that they are precisely $A_5$, $A_6$, $A_7$, $A_8$, ${\rm PSL}(2,7)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,8)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,11)$, ${\rm PSp}(4,3)$, ${\rm PSU}(3,3)$, and ${\rm PSU}(3,4)$.

authors.name: Changguo Shao
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Updated View on Titan's Habitability: Interior and Surface Aqueous Environments
papers.abstract: Saturn's moon Titan is the only world beyond Earth where abundant organic molecules and liquid water are expected to interact. Crucially, these interactions yield prebiotic molecules central to terrestrial biochemistry. Characterizing this prebiotic chemistry is one of the main science goals of NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission. Here we synthesize the current state of knowledge on the habitability and prebiotic potential of Titan's three aqueous settings: its interior hydrosphere, its putative cryovolcanic flows, and its impact-melt pools. For each setting, we identify the enabling factors and the principal bottlenecks that limit prebiotic complexification. Titan's interior is likely pervaded by liquid water in contact with organic material delivered from the surface and released from the core, though the longevity of its liquid water has recently been called into question. Cryovolcanic regions transiently expose surface organics to ammonia-bearing aqueous melts but are constrained by short freezing timescales. Impact-melt pools, by contrast, are warm and long-lived environments whose prebiotic chemistry is limited by the scarcity of ammonia. Dragonfly will return ground-truth data not only for Titan's habitability, but also for organic-rich aqueous environments across the Solar System and beyond. The years before its arrival are the last in which predictive work can still shape Dragonfly's investigations.

authors.name: Diogo Goncalves
authors.institution: Institute of Mechanical Engineering and Industrial Mangement

papers.title: Lincege.jl: LINked Cluster Expansions on a GEneral GEometry
papers.abstract: The numerical linked-cluster expansion (NLCE) is a powerful tool for studying properties of quantum lattice models directly in the thermodynamic limit. Here, we introduce Lincege.jl, a versatile, efficient, and easy-to-use package for generating the clusters needed to perform the NLCE on a general finite or infinite lattice. Lincege.jl takes as input only the Bravais lattice vectors, the basis information, and the expansion unit and uses a depth-first search to efficiently generate clusters, their lattice constants, and the sub-cluster information. It outputs final coefficients of the series, expressed in terms of the extensive properties of the clusters, in different orders. The package also contains tools for visualizing the lattice and the generated clusters as well as a classical Ising model solver that can be used as a template for interfacing Lincege.jl with solvers of other lattice models. This package can be installed using the Julia package manager and utilized with example scripts from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/rightleftspin/Lincege.jl. The online documentation, including examples, can be found at https://rightleftspin.github.io/Lincege.jl/stable/.

papers.title: Path Integrals on Functional Lattices
papers.abstract: Path integrals in quantum field theory are commonly approached through finite-dimensional approximations, but existence and regulator independence of the infinite-dimensional limit require separate analysis. We introduce a scheme in which spacetime remains continuous and the field is expanded in a discrete complete family of localized functions, called a functional lattice. Truncation to finite-dimensional functional subspaces yields ordinary finite-dimensional integrals while leaving the continuum differential operator unchanged. For the massive free Euclidean scalar field, we prove convergence of the finite-dimensional covariance operators and normalized generating functionals by a Galerkin argument. The limit is independent of the compatible functional lattice: any sequence of finite-dimensional subspaces dense in the quadratic-form domain converges to the same continuum covariance and generating functional. A direct Minkowski construction is obtained at fixed Feynman regulator $i\epsilon$, followed by the distributional limit $\epsilon\downarrow0$. For interacting theories, each truncation gives an ordinary non-Gaussian integral. At fixed perturbative order, convergence follows when the finite-resolution graph integrands converge pointwise and admit an integrable majorant independent of the functional resolution. Numerical results for one-dimensional $\phi^4$ theory approach the known first- and second-order mass-gap coefficients, while four-dimensional calculations exhibit the expected mass divergence and logarithmic wave-function renormalization. Thus functional lattices provide a continuum-space approach to path integrals with mathematically controlled limits in the cases considered here.

authors.name: Alexey A. Kryukov
authors.institution: All-Russian Research Institute of Agricultural Microbiology

papers.title: Bayesian Optimization for Inhomogeneous Functions via Locally Adaptive Kernels
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful and general framework for sample-efficient global optimization. Most BO methods rely on stationary Gaussian processes, implicitly assuming that an objective black-box function exhibits homogeneous smoothness across the input space. However, many complex real-world functions have highly inhomogeneous regularity, exhibiting both smooth and rough behavior. This fundamental mismatch between the model and the black-box function severely degrades both sample efficiency and surrogate accuracy of BO. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Inhomogeneous Bayesian optimization framework. We develop a partitioned modeling strategy that dynamically subdivides the search space into subdomains, capturing spatially varying smoothness through locally adaptive kernels. To dynamically adjust the spatial resolution of the surrogate model, this approach utilizes a recursive splitting criterion. Furthermore, we develop a sampling allocation theory, establishing that driving the regional acquisition suprema below a common target level is achieved by polynomially denser sampling in rougher subdomains. Numerical experiments across homogeneous functions, synthetic inhomogeneous functions, and a real-world 8-dimensional LASSO hyperparameter tuning task demonstrate that our approach improves optimization efficiency on synthetic inhomogeneous functions, while performing comparably to Classic BO on homogeneous functions and on the LASSO task. This demonstrates the robustness of the adaptive partitioning mechanism.

papers.title: Inverse problems for ZS operators and their isomorphisms, II
papers.abstract: We study isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators on the unit interval with generic boundary conditions. A unitary gauge transformation reduces these problems to the corresponding problems with basic boundary conditions, with an explicit shift of the spectral parameter. Using previous results for canonical boundary conditions and four-spectra data mapping we describe isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators. Moreover, study other inverse problems including replacing mappings and canonical relations.

papers.title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
papers.abstract: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.

papers.title: R2WM: Recursive Reasoning Wireless Model for Long-Horizon mmWave Beam Prediction
papers.abstract: Long-horizon beam prediction aims to extend beam-training intervals while supporting beam alignment in mobile millimeter-wave systems. Although pretrained large models can improve prediction over compact recurrent baselines, their large backbones impose substantial storage and computing requirements. To address this limitation, we propose a recursive reasoning wireless model (R2WM). Given a fixed history of beam indices and angles of departure (AoDs), R2WM repeatedly updates coupled latent and prediction states using a shared causal-attention backbone before jointly decoding the future beam indices. Backbone reuse increases computational depth at fixed parameter count. In the standard 10-step DeepMIMO setting, R2WM achieves an average normalized beamforming gain of 0.9597, compared with 0.8629 for the prompt-as-prefix large language model, with 99.1% fewer parameters and 59.1% fewer counted floating-point operations. Transfer experiments show that R2WM retains normalized gain under the tested carrier-frequency and antenna-count changes, while its beam-index-only variant retains gain under the tested base-station change. Component ablations show higher gains with historical AoD conditioning and causal attention. Recursion analysis reveals a gain-computation trade-off across separately trained configurations with the same parameter count. An additional comparison with a nonrecursive Transformer of similar parameter count shows higher gain for R2WM at greater computational cost. These results support accurate long-horizon beam prediction without a large pretrained backbone.

papers.title: Uniguided and unicoupled resonances in an asymmetric acoustic metasurface
papers.abstract: We theoretically study an acoustic metasurface that exhibits ultimate asymmetry in absorption under oblique incidence. This behavior arises from a counter-propagating pair of uniguided (UGR) and unicoupled (UCR) resonances. The UGR radiates to only one side, while the UCR radiates to both sides but can be excited from only one. In the lossless regime, the transmission phase winds by $2\pi$ across both UCR and UGR while the transmittance remains flat at any prescribed nonzero level. Thermoviscous losses introduce resonant intensity modulation and enable critical coupling, yielding perfect sound absorption exclusively for incidence through the channel that excites the UCR. Therefore, asymmetric metasurfaces with UCR and UGR offer a route to full phase control and perfect sound absorption.

authors.name: Mingzhao Song
authors.institution: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

papers.title: CoHABIT: Complementary Evaluation of Furniture Layouts through Spatial Rules and Household Routines
papers.abstract: We introduce CoHABIT, a framework for evaluating furniture layouts through complementary spatial rules and household routines. Static assessment captures geometric validity, ergonomic access, functional organization, and configurable design preferences, including Feng Shui. Dynamic assessment uses learned resident policies to simulate everyday activities, resource sharing, coordination, and individual burdens in multi-agent households. Controlled comparisons show how spatial criteria and household behavior reveal distinct aspects of layout quality, while resident profiles and scheduling influence furnishing rankings. Independent verification of household needs grounds dynamic comparisons in observed outcomes, enabling interpretable assessments of how furnished environments serve different households.

authors.name: Ewsey Obzherin
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: $w_0$ Is All You Need: Field-Level Matching of General Dark Energy Models to $w_0$CDM Simulations
papers.abstract: We show that clustering in general dynamical dark energy models $w(z)$ can be predicted with constant dark energy $w_0\text{CDM}$ models at the field level via spectral equivalence. The prescription of this method requires equating comoving distances to the last scattering surface between predictor and target models, which is equivalent to requiring equal recent background expansion history averages. Dark energy models with the same distance thus form approximate equivalence classes, with nearly identical matter fields. To test the precision of spectral equivalence beyond the CPL parametrization, we run $N$-body simulations with various dynamical dark energy models, including spline-based $w(z)$, all matched to a single $w_0\text{CDM}$ run. Our measurements show that the power spectra of all matched dark energies agree with the predictor within $0.2\%$ up to $k = 0.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and within $0.6\%$ up to $k = 1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. We also compare the non-Gaussian information contained in the simulated fields. Bispectra differ by at most $0.26\%$ across all runs up to $k = 0.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and $1.75\%$ up to $k = 1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, while wavelet scattering transform coefficients are all within $0.05\%$. The decorrelation, $1 - r^2$, between each matched field and the predictor stays below $0.006\%$ up to $k = 1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. We run a toy power spectrum analysis in the CPL parametrization demonstrating that a $w_0$-only emulator could produce the same posterior without any knowledge of the full $w_0w_a$ model. This matching prescription thus offers a new tool to constrain dynamical dark energy models with arbitrary equations of state at the field level, without running additional simulation suites.

authors.name: Peter L. Taylor
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

papers.title: The Boundary Conjecture for Smoothable Alexandrov Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that in a noncollapsed limit of complete Riemannian manifolds with $\sec\ge\kappa$, each boundary component of a compact full-dimensional convex body, equipped with its intrinsic length metric, has Alexandrov curvature at least $\kappa$. We also consider such a body in the limit of a noncollapsed sequence of Alexandrov spaces with curvature at least $\kappa$. If $\kappa>0$ or the boundary of the body is strongly convex, we show that the body can be approximated by convex bodies in the given sequence.

papers.title: RadioWorld: Transferring World Models to Radio-Frequency Radiance Fields
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in the physical world constitutes a Radio-Frequency (RF) radiance field, providing rich information for 6G communication and sensing. However, existing neural RF field methods suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) they predominantly rely on per-scene optimization and cannot generalize to unseen scenes; (2) they require costly reference RF measurements in each target scene; and (3) they degrade severely when extrapolating beyond the vicinity of reference measurements. To overcome these limitations, we present RadioWorld, a general framework that adapts a world model to synthesize RF radiance fields directly from physical scene geometry and transceiver locations, without requiring any reference RF measurements at inference. Specifically, RadioWorld couples two specialized modules within a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture: a Scene-Understanding Transformer that encodes 3D scene geometry and transceiver locations to extract environment-aware global EM propagation features, and a Field-Generation Transformer that attends to these features to synthesize the RF radiance field with the local query conditions. We also establish UrbanRF-Bench, a large-scale ray-traced benchmark spanning 657 urban scenes and 32,850 RF radiance fields across seven global cities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RadioWorld significantly outperforms specialized baselines and accurately synthesizes RF fields at arbitrary locations in unseen cities. Code, datasets, and checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.

authors.name: Jiazhou Zhou
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: High-Throughput Screening of Phononic Bandgap in Experimentally Realized Materials
papers.abstract: Materials with a phonon band gap offer a unique mechanism to restrict phonon scattering, making them promising candidates for developing functional materials for targeted thermal applications. Unlocking this mechanism across broad material classes requires systematic exploration, but first-principles methods and experiments are too expensive. Here, we used the universal machine-learning interatomic potential to quantify phonons and thermodynamic properties. We validated the accuracy of machine-learning-calculated results by comparing them with density-functional theory. We screened 154,879 materials and performed phonon calculations for 42,347 thermodynamically stable and experimentally observed compounds. We then performed phonon band gap analysis for dynamically stable materials and identified 11,176 materials with a phononic gap, including 10,960 materials with optical-optical gaps and 270 with acoustic-optical gaps. We also analyzed the lattice thermal conductivity of materials with phonon band gaps to identify candidates with acoustic-optical gaps and low thermal conductivity. Finally, by solving the linearized phonon Boltzmann equation from first principles, we demonstrate low room-temperature lattice thermal conductivities in three Li-metal binaries.

papers.title: Hodge cycles of Klein hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study the space of Hodge cycles on Klein varieties. Relating it to the Hodge characters in a covering Fermat variety, we decompose the space of Hodge characters into a part generated by classes of rational subvarieties, and a non-trivial part which we call exceptional. Using Dirichlet characters we show that the exceptional part is always finite. Furthermore, we give sufficient conditions under which there are no exceptional characters, providing infinitely many new cases of the Hodge conjecture for Klein varieties. Finally, we describe the set of exceptional characters of Klein varieties for small dimensions.

papers.title: Reverse Schensted bumping, inverse reduction map and concatenation in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection
papers.abstract: Provided the explicit formula for the inverse reduction map, arXiv:2606.24840, we exhibit for symplectic bumped intervals and for symplectic bumped columns disjoint for the action of the parity involution, the feasibility of the concatenation operation to return a semi-standard tableau in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection

papers.title: Complying with Cybersecurity Legislation: NIS2 Challenges and Industry Case Study
papers.abstract: Given the ever-increasing dependency on interconnected digital systems, cybersecurity has become a major concern. To protect markets and societies, governmental entities are developing legislation to enhance cyber resilience across sectors, introducing new technical and legal requirements. The NIS2 Directive, a revised version of the European-wide cybersecurity legislation, entered into force on 16 January 2023. Member States were required to adopt and publish transposing measures by 17 October 2024 and apply them from 18 October 2024. Specific obligations for essential and important entities are set out in national legislation. At the same time, other organizations, while not legally bound, seek to improve their cybersecurity maturity in alignment with EU-wide advances, for which NIS2 serves as a key reference. This paper presents the work conducted within a large European enterprise to align itself with the NIS2 Directive, focusing on how organizations can analyze and interpret its provisions to drive concrete technical and organizational improvements. A systematic methodology is applied to frame the company within the NIS2 context, identify relevant requirements, and derive actionable measures. Beyond outlining the technical steps taken, the work highlights the challenges of translating legislative requirements into practical implementations, emphasizing the use of existing IT resources while accounting for key legal aspects. The paper concludes with a discussion and reusable artifacts addressing critical areas such as Supply Chains and Third Parties and Zero-Trust Principles, illustrating how legislative instruments such as NIS2 can be translated into practical mechanisms to strengthen cybersecurity strategies.

papers.title: Regularity of invariant measures of solutions for fractional stochastic partial differential equations with memory and nonlinear noise
papers.abstract: We are concerned with stochastic fractional partial differential equations involving memory and nonlinear multiplicative noise. Based on the well-known Dafermos method, a suitable variable defined by the integrated past history is introduced. This transformation not only overcomes the non-Markovianity of the original problem which prevents us from analyzing invariant measures for the associated Markov semigroup, but also facilitates the analysis of the well-posedness together with the Faedo-Galerkin approximations and Minty's technique. Moreover, we prove the existence of invariant measures by the classical Krylov-Bogoliubov approach, and further establish the regularity of invariant measures by virtue of a control argument.

papers.title: The dimensions of curly and dipolar Besicovitch-Kakeya sets
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we establish sharp Hausdorff dimension and box-counting dimension bounds for sets containing meridian circles and for sets whose difference sets contain a sphere.
  Fix two antipodal points N, S on S^{n-1}, n\ge 3, and consider the family of great circles passing through them. Assuming the Besicovitch-Kakeya overlapping conjecture in R^{n-1}, we prove that every bounded set K\subset R^n containing a translated and dilated copy of each circle in this family satisfies \dim_H K\ge n-1. In particular, the same conclusion holds for bounded sets containing a circle in every orientation. This bound is sharp, as shown by the unit sphere. We also prove unconditionally that every bounded set K\subset R^n, n\ge2, satisfying S^{n-1}\subset K-K has lower box counting dimension greater than or equal to n(n-1)/(2n-1), and the bound is also sharp.

papers.title: Algorithms for Detecting Shape Defects in Concentrated Solar Power Plant Components
papers.abstract: Concentrated solar power (CSP) technology offers a dispatchable renewable energy solution, capable of bridging the gap between intermittent generation and grid demand through high-capacity thermal energy storage. However, the overall thermodynamic efficiency and cost-effectiveness of CSP plants depend crucially on the optical quality and precise geometric alignment of thousands of reflective surfaces spread across vast solar fields. Shape defect detection algorithms have become essential tools for automating mirror profilometry, tracking the flow spot and diagnosing alignment issues. This paper presents a novel framework for geometric shape detection techniques tailored to CSP applications. It introduces the notion of \emph{parabolicity}, which motivates a class of optimisation problems in this setting and suggests a possible direction for further work in computational geometry. Both exact and approximate algorithms are proposed, together with an experimental study on synthetic datasets generated via simulation.

papers.title: Total curvature and area growth of entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space
papers.abstract: We prove that entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space $\mathrm{Nil}_3(\tau)$ have infinite total curvature. Since their Gauss curvature is negative, this means that their intrinsic area growth is not quadratic, as conjectured by P\'erez, Rodr\'iguez and the author. It follows that vertical planes are the only orientable complete stable surfaces with constant mean curvature and quadratic area growth in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(\tau)$, and this classification is extended to surfaces with critical and supercritical constant mean curvature in the homogeneous spaces $\mathbb{E}(\kappa,\tau)$. We also prove that the height of an entire minimal graph in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(\tau)$ grows at most quadratically, as conjectured by Nelli and the author, whence the extrinsic and cylindrical area growths of such a graph are exactly cubic. Our arguments rely on the conformal Calabi-Lee duality between minimal graphs in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(\tau)$ and spacelike graphs with constant mean curvature $\tau$ in the Lorentz-Minkowski space $\mathbb{L}^3$, for which we also get sharp gradient estimates.

papers.title: Can Open LLMs Clear Sanctions-Screening Alerts? A Pre-registered Test on Public Sanctions Lists with Turkish Name Variants
papers.abstract: Sanctions screening raises name-based alerts that are mostly false positives, and level-1 analysts clear them by checking the customer's date of birth and name against a written policy. We test whether open-weight language models that a bank can run on its own premises can perform this level-1 disposition. From the UK and EU sanctions lists (7,103 natural persons) we built 12,200 synthetic customers: listed persons under six name conditions, including Turkish spellings of Arabic-origin names and Turkish romanisations of Cyrillic names, and two date-of-birth conditions, plus namesakes, near-name customers and a general population. A deterministic fuzzy and embedding screen raised 7,383 alerts, which three open models served on domestic infrastructure and three rule baselines dispositioned under the same policy. The models sent far fewer innocent customers to level 2 than a rule that applies the policy's date clause: 0.6 to 16.9 per 1,000 screened customers against 24.4, and they stated the date-of-birth status correctly in 98.3% to 98.5% of alerts. They also failed to escalate 1.5% to 2.2% of the listed persons. The pre-registered non-inferiority test against the rule was met, but only because of a construction error we found after the analysis: 21 customers in the "minor discrepancy" condition had dates that conflict under the policy. Without them the rule misses no listed person and no model meets the margin. The misses had model-specific causes: one model read minor date discrepancies as conflicts, one declared word-order and typing variants to be different names, and one discounted alerts that its own rationale said to escalate. Fuzzy matching found 69% of the Turkish spellings of Arabic-origin names; adding embeddings raised this to 74%. Open LLMs can cut level-1 workload, but on this evidence only behind a deterministic date check and with every name doubt escalated.
