papers.abstract: A tool router retrieves a few candidate tools per request and lets a language model choose. Methods that share experience across organizations add past requests about each tool to what the router retrieves. StableToolBench calls some of its test groups tests on "unseen" tools, yet the ToolBench instruction pool, which retrievers and experience-sharing methods learn from, contains every test query and labels every gold tool of the two single-tool groups among them. We release STUN-Bench (StableToolBench, Truly UNseen), a split whose experience pool has no item that labels or names 172 held-out tools. Unseen here means absent from shared experience and retriever training data, not from pretraining. On the split we find crowding: experience pooled from five simulated clients, added to an index of tool descriptions, outranks the descriptions of tools no client has used, which then often drop out of the candidate list. Under the Jina-v2 retriever, routing accuracy on held-out tools falls from 0.534 to 0.278. Retrievers trained for tool retrieval lose much less, and keeping experience in a separate index recovers most of the loss under Jina-v2. The split also reverses a conclusion: with every test tool labeled in the pool and our default leak filter applied, shared experience beats descriptions alone; on STUN-Bench it falls below them. The split, leak filter and evaluation harness are available at https://github.com/<org>/STUN-Bench.

authors.name: Abhijit Chakraborty
authors.institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

papers.title: PruneNAS: Constraint Aware Neural Architecture Search based Pruning
papers.abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has achieved state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks, but its high computational cost remains a major barrier. We introduce PruneNAS, a novel framework that integrates structured pruning into NAS to efficiently explore high-performing architectures while leveraging pretrained models. Unlike conventional NAS methods that train each candidate from scratch, PruneNAS generates a candidate pool by pruning pretrained networks at multiple granularity levels and formulates the selection as a global optimization problem using training-free importance metrics. This approach enables rapid evaluation of candidate architectures under strict resource constraints, dramatically reducing search time from hundreds of GPU hours to mere minutes. Experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that PruneNAS discovers compact, high-accuracy architectures that nearly halve the computational cost (MACs) of prior methods on ResNet-50, while also showing strong generalization on object detection tasks with YOLO. Our method bridges structured pruning and NAS, offering a practical solution for resource-constrained model deployment.

authors.name: Honnesh Rohmetra
authors.institution: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

authors.name: Andy Li
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Self-Refining VLA Sampling
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models typically use flow-based generative modeling to learn a rich, often multimodal, distribution of robot actions. Generating samples from flow-based methods involves iteratively updating random noise, and distinct noise samples from the same state can result in distinct trajectories and task outcomes. Existing test-time scaling methods improve action chunk generation via selection, aggregation, or correction, but commonly require the generation of large ensembles of candidates or the training of an external corrector. We adapt Predict-and-Perturb (P&P), a self-refinement procedure for flow-based models originally used for mode-seeking in video generation, to the robotics domain. We find that applying P&P to VLA models requires modifications to the refinement process used in video generation due to differences in the underlying structure of the data. Across 400 episodes of LIBERO evaluated using SmolVLA, P&P improves upon the stock baseline by 5.3 percentage points. Further, episode-level P\&P uncertainty correlates strongly with task failure (AUC 0.851).

papers.title: The first Fu\v{c}\'ik curve of the $p$-Laplacian on compact quantum graphs: slopes at the diagonal and nonresonance
papers.abstract: We study the Fu\v{c}\'{\i}k spectrum of the $p$-Laplacian, $1<p<\infty$, on a compact connected quantum graph, with Dirichlet conditions on a possibly empty set $V_D$ of vertices whose removal does not disconnect the graph and Kirchhoff conditions at the others. We construct the first nontrivial curve $\mathfrak C$ of the spectrum by a mountain pass argument and show that it is Lipschitz and strictly decreasing. As the parameter tends to infinity, $\mathfrak C$ tends to the first eigenvalue if $V_D\neq\emptyset$, and otherwise to the smallest first eigenvalue obtained by a Dirichlet condition at a single point. If the second eigenvalue is simple, we compute the two one-sided slopes of $\mathfrak C$ at the diagonal. The curve is differentiable there if and only if the positive and negative parts of the second eigenfunction have the same $L^p$ norm. On three-edge stars these norms differ for suitable edge lengths and every $p$, so the Lipschitz regularity is optimal. For $p=2$ the simplicity assumption can be dropped, and for a simple eigenvalue the corner is the crossing of the two smooth branches of the spectrum through the diagonal point. Finally, we prove a nonresonance result in which, for $V_D=\emptyset$, the ratio $f(x,s)/|s|^{p-2}s$ may be arbitrarily large at $+\infty$, provided it stays below the threshold at $-\infty$.

authors.name: Divya Goel
authors.institution: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar State Institute of Medical Sciences

papers.title: IP-GNO: An Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator for Automated Distribution System State Estimation
papers.abstract: Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE) is a crucial tool for real-time monitoring, operation, and control of the new-age distribution systems (DSs) due to intensified voltage fluctuations and operational uncertainties introduced by volatile power injection at the nodes. Existing GNN-based approaches generally exhibit limited generalization across networks with different sizes and topologies, making zero-shot cross-grid transfer to unseen DSs a significant challenge. To overcome the aforementioned challenges, this article proposes an Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator (IP-GNO) for scalable and transferable DSSE. The proposed framework frames complex bus voltage estimation as an operator-learning problem inspired by the Neumann series expansion of the inverse bus admittance matrix. An admittance-parameterized kernel, incorporating a self-admittance gate in the zeroth-order term and a persistent source-injection skip connection across network layers, captures the underlying electrical dependencies. Additionally, a Physics-Embedded Tree Encoding (PETE) scheme introduces five grid-size-invariant positional features derived from path impedance and a DC-linearized phase-angle prior. A sine-cosine output formulation is further employed to address phase-angle periodicity and ensure stable training. The proposed IP-GNO module is evaluated on two small (IEEE 33- and 69-bus), two medium (IEEE 123- and 136-bus), and one large (2522-bus) sized DSs. Particularly, its zero-shot cross-grid generalization capability is investigated by training the model exclusively on the IEEE 33-bus system and directly evaluating it on four unseen distribution networks of different sizes without retraining or fine-tuning. A detailed comparative analysis with the existing state-of-the-art DSSE tools proves the superiority of IP-GNO, enabling scalable DSSE across heterogeneous DSs.

papers.title: Ultrahigh Thermal Conductivity and Mirror-Parity Constraints in a Corrugated Two-Dimensional Oxide
papers.abstract: Contrary to the expectation of poor heat transport in oxides, first-principles calculations predict an ultrahigh lattice thermal conductivity of 756 $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ at 300 K in corrugated two-dimensional B$_2$O$_2$. Acoustic phonons dominate heat transport, with the flexural acoustic (ZA) branch contributing 40.62$\%$. Triplet resolved analysis including acoustic and optical partners finds that mirror forbidden three phonon scattering is negligible within numerical precision for sampled ZA modes. These results highlight horizontal mirror symmetry as a constraint on phonon scattering in corrugated oxides.

authors.name: Babu Ram
authors.institution: Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research

authors.name: Geunsik Lee
authors.institution: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: MERIT: Experience-Guided Memory for Long-Horizon Persona-Specific Persuasive Dialogue
papers.abstract: Effective long-horizon persuasion in recurring goal-oriented settings requires more than factual memory: it must track how a user's trust, negotiation behavior, and strategic receptiveness evolve across interactions. Existing persuasive dialogue systems are largely single-session, static, and unimodal, while cross-session memory systems, though temporally aware, retain only factual content and overlook persuasion-specific dynamics. We propose MERIT (Memory-augmented Experience-Rationale for Iterative Temporal persuasion), which pairs a graph-based memory of four persuasion-specific memory types with a per-persona experience rationale library that records which strategies succeed for each user and why. Together they enable adaptive persuasion through prompt composition alone, with no parameter updates. To support this setting, we introduce PERSIST (PERSona-driven InSurance Interactions over Time), a dataset of 60 curated personas spanning 10+ years of motor insurance renewal interactions, with probabilistic life events that shift negotiation behavior and receptiveness across sessions, verified through strict human-in-the-loop annotation. MERIT surpasses memory and experience-based baselines on every metric across two policy backbones, reaching persuasive-appeal scores of 4.10 and 4.74 (out of 5).

authors.name: Akash Ghosh
authors.institution: Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research

papers.title: Two-dimensional Thyristor
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer a viable platform for next-generation electronics beyond sub-3 nm nodes, yet essential nonlinear circuit elements, such as thyristors, remain unexplored on atomically thin platforms. Here, we report an atomically thin reconfigurable electro-optical thyristor based on a lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure, directly grown via sequential edge epitaxy. Unlike single-junction 2D diodes, this multijunction architecture exhibits thyristor-like nonlinear switching, including forward blocking, abrupt snapback, bistability, and electrical latching. The device exhibits a forward-blocking voltage of 183 V, corresponding to a critical electric field of 1 MV/cm. Under open-gate conditions, avalanche-assisted carrier multiplication and regenerative feedback are associated with a sharp forward-voltage drop of 175 V, a pronounced current surge, and an ultralow holding voltage. Gate-pulse modulation and temperature-dependent measurements indicate avalanche-assisted thyristor operation and latching behavior. This 2D lateral heterostructure enables a new route to nonlinear and bistable switching, latching, ultralow standby power, and adaptive logic, opening the way for reconfigurable 2D electronics and photonic integrated circuits.

papers.title: Wirsing type approximation over totally real and totally $p$-adic extensions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish Wirsing-type bounds for approximation of real and $p$-adic transcendental numbers by totally real and totally $p$-adic algebraic numbers, respectively. More precisely, for every $n\ge 1$, we show that every transcendental $\xi\in\mathbb{Q}_p$ admits infinitely many totally $p$-adic algebraic approximants $\alpha$ of degree at most $n$ satisfying $0<|\xi-\alpha|_p\ll H(\alpha)^{-1-\lceil n/2\rceil}$. We improve this bound for even $n\ge 4$. For each $n\geq 2$, we also show that every real number $\xi$ that is not algebraic of degree at most $n$ admits totally real approximants of degree at most $n$ with a bound stronger than Wirsing's. In both cases, we can also restrict the approximants to be totally $\ell$-adic for every prime $\ell$ in a fixed finite set.

papers.title: Big Tree Viewer: A high-performance browser-based phylogenetic tree viewer with agentic AI integration
papers.abstract: Phylogenetic trees represent evolutionary history visually, and the ability to display and explore them is a key function in research across biological disciplines. Very large gene and species trees are becoming common with the increasing availability of low cost DNA sequencing, creating performance and informativeness challenges for display software originally designed for phylogenies with a few hundred to a few thousand tips. We discuss these limitations and introduce a browser-based Big Tree Viewer (BTV) highly optimized for fast display and biologically informative exploration of phylogenetic trees containing even a million tips. BTV can automatically map binomial species names to the NCBI or Catalogue of Life taxonomies and display colored ribbons to indicate taxonomic groups for enhanced exploration. Even without taxonomic mapping, BTV automatically labels groups of neighboring tips that share the first word of their names, such as a genus or gene family name, providing readable large-scale landmarks when individual tip labels are too dense to read. BTV supports metadata display, visual customization, tanglegram-like tree comparisons, statistics, figure export, and multiple tree layouts, including a new spiral form to display enormously large trees. BTV is also designed to integrate with common agentic AI tools, allowing agents to display, style, annotate, and inspect trees at the user's request. The BTV web app is freely available at https://BigTreeViewer.net and runs entirely in the user's browser, with no data uploads to any central server. Desktop versions of the BTV app for macOS, Windows, and Linux are also provided for download.

authors.name: Sudhir Kumar
authors.institution: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University

papers.title: Algorithms for Collaborative Truck-Multi-Drone Delivery in the En-Route Model
papers.abstract: We study collaborative truck--multi-drone delivery in the en-route model, in which a truck moves continuously along a fixed straight-line path while drones serve $n$ off-route deliveries. For maximum coverage with $k$ drones, we prove that Sequential Greedy achieves an approximation guarantee of $1-(k/(k+1))^k$, which approaches $1-e^{-1}$. For $k=2$, our analysis is tight, with a matching $5/9$ instance. We refute the claimed exchange property for proper instances. For a new class of swap-monotone instances with distinct $x$-coordinates, we give an exact $O(n^2)$-time dynamic program for single-drone maximum coverage. For minimum fleet size, we prove NP-hardness and give an $O(1+\log(n/k^\ast))$-approximation using an integer residual bound, where $k^\ast$ is the optimum fleet size.

authors.name: Kelin Luo
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

papers.title: Is the learner or the summary the limit? Auditing machine-learning energy reconstruction for air-shower arrays on KASCADE and GRAPES-3
papers.abstract: Machine-learning energy estimators for cosmic-ray arrays are usually trained on a few fitted shower parameters, not station signals. When their resolution stops improving, standard diagnostics cannot say whether a better model would help or the summary has run out of information. We use a five-step audit that compares trained models with a learner-independent estimate of the lowest error the summary allows (its squared-loss Bayes risk, or floor), tests which inputs add information and flags inputs merely computed from the fit. We apply it to public KASCADE simulations with three hadronic-interaction models (QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC and SIBYLL-2.3d), to 13,848,509 measured KASCADE events and to simulated GRAPES-3 events. Within known energy decades below 10^16 eV, gradient boosting on nine reconstructed features is within 2.2% of the estimated floor under every estimator setting, so more capacity is not expected to gain more than about 2%. The floor is an estimate, accurate to about 1% in a semi-synthetic benchmark with intervals that under-cover, and not a bound on the true Bayes risk. Replacing reconstructed by true particle numbers removes 70 to 72% of the error variance below 10^15 eV and 24 to 26% between 10^16 and 10^17 eV on all three models, yet simulated station signals close about a tenth of that gap. On GRAPES-3, networks given images rendered from the fit do no better than the fit. In measured data, the mean muon size at fixed electron size lies within every model's proton-to-iron bracket and a label-free probe finds the muon channel used as in simulation; neither fixes the energy scale. Energy-labelled results are simulated.

papers.title: Separating Protocol Effects from Spatio-Temporal Evidence in Person Re-Identification Re-Ranking
papers.abstract: Spatio-temporal priors re-rank person re-identification matches using the camera pair and the time gap, and are reported to add large gains on Market-1501. We ask how much of such a gain encodes the evaluation protocol rather than learned spatio-temporal evidence. Starting from a course-project re-ranker that adds log camera-transition and log time-gap terms to cosine similarity, we train a strong ResNet-50 baseline (Rank-1 94.3 %, mAP 86.2 % over three seeds), choose the fusion weights on an identity-disjoint validation split and evaluate on the official test set with control priors. The repository form adds 2.30 mAP points, but a one-parameter penalty on same-camera pairs alone adds 2.19: the protocol never places a true match in the query's camera, so the penalty removes distractors for free. The time term of that form is almost unused; a pair-level diagnostic traces this to its modelling the time gap given a match without dividing by the gap distribution of all candidate pairs. A likelihood-ratio prior adds 4.04 points without the penalty and 5.62 with it; shuffling the time stamps removes the extra gain, so about 3.43 points are tied to identity. The prior fixes the first-ranked match of 4.2 % of the queries and breaks it for 0.1 %. The gain shrinks as the visual baseline improves (11.9 to 5.62 points between a 70.5 % and a 86.2 % mAP model) and concentrates on queries whose true matches share the query's video sequence. The study covers one dataset, one backbone and three seeds.

authors.name: Doan Pham Thao Nhu
authors.institution: Ho Chi Minh City University of Economics and Finance

papers.title: Dhaani: A Data-Flow-Driven Tool for Greenfield Construction and Brownfield Modernisation
papers.abstract: Large language models can generate plausible code quickly, but an end-to-end prompt leaves developers with little control over decomposition, interfaces, or the assumptions that must survive later revisions. We present Dhaani, a free desktop application for greenfield program construction and brownfield repository modernisation. It makes an annotated data-flow diagram (ADFD) the inspectable contract between intent and implementation. In the greenfield workflow, Build, a user turns natural-language requirements into a typed graph, reviews process specifications and pre/post-conditions, ratifies generated modules, and proceeds in dependency order for Python or .NET (C#). In the brownfield workflow, Migrate uses source inference to recover an ADFD from a Fortran repository, performs target generation in bounded dependency groups, and exposes source-target alignment, generated code, errors, time, token use, and cost. The tool keeps code and artifacts on the user's machine and supports cloud or locally hosted models. Two scientific synthesis case studies produced executable systems where matched low/no-code baselines failed or were substantially less accurate. On 50 open-source Fortran repositories, the migration workflow made all 382 fixed source-oracle probes runnable and passed 327 (85.6%); two direct translation baselines each passed 83 (21.7% of planned probes). Pre-built installers and usage instructions are freely available. Tool and usage guide: https://shraddhasurana.github.io/dhaani/. Video: https://youtu.be/SShWwOMgJ9c.

authors.name: Shraddha Surana
authors.institution: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

authors.name: Ashwin Srinivasan
authors.institution: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

papers.title: A ROS2 based Human-In-The-Loop Framework for UAV Search and Rescue Operations
papers.abstract: Existing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) autonomy frameworks lack human contextual awareness, limiting real-time adaptability in unstructured Search and Rescue (SAR) environments. To address data availability, we propose a Robot Operating System (ROS2)-based human-in-the-loop (HITL) framework that translates human directional gestures (left/right) into UAV navigation commands using RGB-Depth (RGB-D) sensing and YOLOv11 (You Only Look Once). The deprecation of ROS1 necessitates migrating to ROS2, prioritising real-time communication, scalability, and long-term maintainability. Unlike approaches optimised for peak accuracy under ideal conditions, the proposed system prioritises robustness and real-time deployment in degraded SAR environments. Our system achieves 89% confidence in depth estimation under occlusion and varying environmental conditions in Gazebo-PX4 simulations. In foggy conditions, RGB-D fusion consistently provides more informative cues than RGB alone, with an average improvement of 46.7% across all scenarios and distances. The framework demonstrates superior occlusion handling (+15%), adaptive RGB-D fusion, temporal consistency modelling, and real-time deployment via a ROS2 data distribution service (DDS), with end-to-end latency below 50 ms. We evaluate the modified YOLOv11 and the depth-weighted pose estimation on a held-out simulated test set and on real people from the public UAV-GESTURE dataset, in clear air and in Koschmieder fog. Without retraining, the framework reads the gestures of real people with 80% accuracy, depth keeps 77% at a visibility of 10 m where RGB drops to 24%, and the modified YOLOv11 reaches 91% in simulation and 99% on held-out real people when trained on real data. The open-source ROS2 implementation eases the transition of SAR-UAV platforms from ROS1, enabling UAVs to act directly on operator gestures without complex path planning.

authors.name: Harshit Nagpal
authors.institution: Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies

authors.name: Aditya Agarwal
authors.institution: SRM Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Tejasvi Alladi
authors.institution: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

papers.title: Flow-induced vibration of an array of circular cylinders in a square enclosure due to thermal buoyancy
papers.abstract: Flow-induced oscillations of heated cylinder arrays in a square enclosure driven solely by natural convection are investigated in the current study at Prandtl number of 7 and Raleigh number of $10^7$ (based on side of square enclosure). This is accomplished by a coupled thermal-fluid-structure-interaction formulation based on body-fitted arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian framework, implemented using variational finite element methodology. Study on stationary array shows asymmetry in the $3\times 3$ configuration, along with a non-dimensional wall-gap plume oscillation frequency of 0.183 on the left column cylinders. When elastically mounted, these cylinders synchronize and lock-in with the frequency at reduced velocity of 15.7. The remaining cylinders undergo broadband buffeting that grows monotonically with reduced velocity and exceeds the synchronized response. The $4\times 4$ array shows symmetric behavior with no synchronization. The response is observed to be forced buffeting for all the cylinders, and dominated by the slow plume forcing for the inner column cylinders. The motion of the cylinders also influence the heat transfer characteristics. The $3\times 3$ array shows negligible change in heat transfer for the whole array, while measurable enhancement is observed for $4\times 4$ array.

authors.name: Vaibhav Joshi
authors.institution: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

papers.title: Where Compositionality Hides: Shared-Content Interference in Vision-Language Retrieval
papers.abstract: Paired compositional benchmarks such as Winoground ask each image to prefer its matching caption and each caption to prefer its matching image. A failed Group decision can come from a wrong caption preference or from the cross-image comparison alone, and Group Score merges the two. Choosing between retraining the encoder and changing the scoring rule therefore requires separating them. We study mean-erasure, which projects each frozen image embedding away from the mean of the two normalized candidate captions. We prove that the projection preserves every within-image caption ranking and makes Group Score equal baseline Text Score. On Winoground, mean-erasure raises CLIP ViT-B/32 Group Score from 9% to 31%, and five CLIP and SigLIP checkpoints gain 21 to 27 percentage points. ColorSwap shows a similar gain for color-object binding. A score decomposition shows that about 60% of Image failures already score the correct joint assignment above the swapped one and fail only on an offset between the two images. Fixed corrections and a learned bilinear scorer gain under one point. A direction estimated from retrieved captions gains about five points with two captions and falls below baseline with sixteen. Before retraining an encoder for paired retrieval, measure the Group loss that mean-erasure recovers: gains beyond baseline Text Score require changing the caption decisions themselves.

authors.name: Chimata Anudeep
authors.institution: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

authors.name: Harsh Vardhan Poddar
authors.institution: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

papers.title: Urban State Representation for Autonomous Mobility: A Survey of Multimodal Perception, Architectures, Datasets, and Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Cities are sensed by many platforms at once: on-board cameras, LiDAR and radar on autonomous vehicles, roadside units at intersections, drones and satellites overhead, and the GNSS traces of millions of trips. Yet most learned representations are built for one platform, one city, and one task. We survey this fragmented landscape through a single lens, the Urban State Representation (USR): a georeferenced, layered, time-varying, uncertainty-aware state that any sensing platform can write to and any downstream task can read from. We (i) formalize USR and five desiderata for it, and relate it to bird's-eye-view (BEV) features, occupancy, vectorized maps, neural fields and 3D Gaussians, scene graphs, road-network graphs, language tokens, and world-model latents; (ii) organize sensing platforms, cross-view (ground-aerial) matching, fusion operators, 3D geometric foundation models, end-to-end and vision-language-action models, and generative world models and data engines in one taxonomy that spans sensors to decisions; (iii) compile 26 urban datasets and simulators across ego, cooperative (V2X), aerial, trajectory, and language settings, with a metric glossary, a cross-benchmark results snapshot, a trend analysis, and a platform-coverage gap analysis; and (iv) review applications and propose, as an outlook, USR-5, a five-test protocol with explicit references and one aggregate score for measuring whether a state is shared, together with a research agenda of six open problems covering cross-city and cross-sensor transfer, uncertainty, efficiency, sim-to-real evaluation, and governance. This survey is an entry point for computer vision, autonomous driving, transportation, and urban computing researchers; the paper list, datasets, and USR-5 code are at https://github.com/binayksingh/Awesome-Urban-State-Representation.

authors.name: Binay Kumar Singh
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research

papers.title: Optimization of a Solar-Grid Water Supply System with Hydraulic Energy Storage: A Case Study
papers.abstract: Given the high cost of grid-scale batteries, other energy storage approaches are needed for developing and low-income regions. Elevated volumes of water are often more economically feasible energy storage options than batteries in these contexts. This paper presents a dual-framework modeling approach for one such energy storage setup: a solar-grid hybrid water supply system in the arid Afar region of Ethiopia. By utilizing an elevated 1,900 m3 water reservoir as a "hydraulic battery," the system replaces traditional electrochemical storage, significantly reducing capital expenditures. Using Python for high-resolution technical simulation and Xendee for economic optimization, the study shows a 55.1% solar fraction and a 10% Internal Rate of Return (IRR). The results confirm that hybrid systems with hydraulic storage offer a financially viable and reliable solution for water access in energy-constrained regions.

papers.title: Ultrasound Watermark: Real-time Acoustic Watermarking against Voice Scams on Smartphones
papers.abstract: Recent advances in text-to-speech (TTS), voice conversion (VC), and AI-driven speech synthesis enable adversaries to convincingly impersonate trusted individuals during phone calls. Existing defenses often rely on offline analysis, degrade under telephony distortions, or remain vulnerable to adaptive attacks. To address these limitations, we present Ultrasound Watermark, a real-time, smartphone-native framework that protects live calls by binding speech to the caller's physical articulatory motion through acoustic watermarking. During a call, the smartphone emits ultrasonic signals and captures reflections from facial articulatory movements using only its built-in speaker and microphone. Ultrasound Watermark extracts motion features from these reflections and fuses them with outgoing speech to generate a dynamic watermark. Because the ultrasonic measurements are physically and temporally coupled with speech production, they are difficult to spoof without the underlying articulatory motion. A synchronized generator-detector architecture enforces cross-modal speech-motion consistency against replay, synthesized speech, and articulation-mimicking attacks. Ultrasound Watermark operates continuously with less than 200 ms latency overhead and requires no additional hardware. We implement Ultrasound Watermark on iOS and Android and evaluate it using over 2.5 hours of synchronized speech-ultrasound recordings from 22 speakers across eight smartphones and four real-world environments. Results demonstrate robustness to diverse attacks and telephony distortions while preserving perceptual audio quality.

authors.name: Rishav Gupta
authors.institution: Pandit Bhagwat Dayal Sharma Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences

papers.title: On the Planar Optimal Transport Problem
papers.abstract: We develop a complex analytic framework based on rotation of gradient graphs for the study of quadratic cost planar optimal transport with uniform densities. Using this framework we carry out the construction, characterization, and approximation of non-degenerate optimal transport maps up to the boundary. We also identify obstructions for continuous optimal transport and construct discontinuous optimal transport maps with prescribed analytic singular sets.

papers.title: Quadratic unitary Cayley graphs over finite commutative rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with identity, and let $T_R=Q_R\cup(-Q_R)$, where $Q_R=\{u^2:u\in R^\times\}$. In this paper, we investigate the spectral properties of quadratic unitary Cayley graphs $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$, over finite commutative rings with identity. We determine all the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ when $R$ has odd characteristic. Our results extend the previously known spectral formulas for this family of graphs. We also obtain all the eigenvalues when the characteristic of $R$ is $2$. Furthermore, for rings of odd characteristic, we give a complete characterization of when $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ is a strongly regular Cayley graph.

papers.title: From Head to Tail: LLM-Augmented Sequential Recommendation and Trade-off Optimization
papers.abstract: Recommender systems exhibit popularity bias, often under-serving long-tail and cold-start items with sparse interaction data. We propose a group-specific data augmentation approach that leverages LLMs to generate synthetic interactions, formulated as a constrained optimization problem, maximizing group-specific NDCG@20 and coverage while bounding overall NDCG@20 degradation within an acceptable threshold. Items are partitioned by interaction frequency to find the optimal augmentation strategy for each group. We further study combining the augmentation across groups simultaneously and find that while individual optimal strategies navigate the multi-group augmentation design, they are not simply additive. We further ablate on the LLM-based augmentation itself, comparing LLM scales, augmentation configuration under token constraints, finding that augmentation quality scales with contextual richness, albeit at a proportionally higher cost. Experiments with SASRec demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving over 100% and 60% improvement in group-specific NDCG@20 for extreme and regular long-tail items, respectively, on our industrial dataset, and 40%, 25% for MovieLens-32M, while increasing their coverage without significant overall degradation.

authors.name: Shaghayegh Agah
authors.institution: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

papers.title: Numerical approximation of the Hilfer fractional derivative using orthogonal Quasi-Polynomials
papers.abstract: A numerical approach based on a composite Gaussian quadrature for the Hilfer fractional derivative is presented. This approach employs quasi-polynomials that are orthogonal with respect to the weight function on the interval $(0,1)$. As special cases, the Riemann--Liouville and Caputo fractional derivatives are obtained. Error bounds for the approximation are derived. To confirm the convergence rates as well as the high efficiency of the new approach, numerical examples are provided.

authors.name: Rabab Beirkdar
authors.institution: SRM Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Transient coupling of Marangoni spreading and interfacial waves
papers.abstract: How does an initially non-uniform distribution of surfactant generate waves on a de- formable interface, and how do those waves then govern the redistribution of the surfactant? We answer this question for the linear Cauchy-Poisson problem of an axisymmetric interface between two viscous fluids, released from rest with independently prescribed distributions of surfactant and of interface displacement, by Hankel and Laplace transforms. In Stokes flow the pressure and the viscous normal stress of the Marangoni flow cancel in the nor- mal traction on the interface, for any viscosity ratio, so that the surfactant relaxes without displacing the interface: the coupling between surfactant redistribution and interface de- formation is inertial. With inertia, the Marangoni flow initiates a capillary-gravity wave whose polarity, at leading order for thin boundary layers, is set by the sign of $\rho_l \mu_l - \rho_u \mu_u $, and the surfactant is then carried by the wave, so that its concentration performs weakly damped oscillations at the wave frequency after the Marangoni relaxation of a flat surface has ended. The amplitude of these oscillations is given in closed form at small viscosity; its maximum does not coincide with that of the familiar resonant damping, and the surfactant and the interface shape decouple exactly only when the two fluids have equal densities and viscosities. A localized displacement radiates a wave packet that the surfactant damps, and a localized surfactant redistribution initiates a wave on an initially flat interface. Direct numerical simulations with sharp geometric surfactant transport verify these predictions.

papers.title: Diagnosing Verbalized Confidence in a Medical Vision-Language Model for Selective Prediction on Colorectal Histopathology Patches
papers.abstract: Flagging uncertain histopathology patches for specialist review needs a confidence that is higher when the model is right. We test whether an open medical vision-language model emits one. MedGemma-27b-it and its base Gemma-3-27b-it were run zero-shot under one prompt on 10,004 PathMNIST validation patches and 7,180 patches of a patient-disjoint external cohort. Both are too inaccurate to deploy (40.6% and 35.5%); the object of study is the confidence. MedGemma's verbalized confidence puts 96% of patches at one value; its confidence-correctness AUROC is 0.499 and 0.528, and routing by it moves selective-accuracy AUC by -0.004 and +0.037. Gemma-3 spreads its confidence over nine values, reaches AUROC 0.70, and gains +0.114 and +0.115. MedGemma's label-token probabilities do not rescue it: their validation advantage reverses where the top-20 alternatives include every class. On 1,800-patch subsets of each cohort, stratified on correctness and reweighted to the full splits, agreement across five prompt variants beats random by +0.123 and +0.106, and wording-only paraphrases give +0.100 and, externally and in direction only, +0.054; agreement's external margins over confidence do not survive slide-level clustering. Under one restructured prompt variant, MedGemma's stated confidence routes (+0.112, +0.141), so the failure is tied to a prompt chosen for macro F1.

papers.title: Refine, Don't Reinvent: RASA-Bench for Source-Grounded Hindi Prose Refinement
papers.abstract: For a producer of Hindi creative prose, drafting is cheap and editing is not: a machine-written episode, story, or essay reads as under-written and flat, laced with translationese, and it sometimes quietly alters what the source says. RASA-Bench targets that editing task across three Hindi prose forms, measuring how well a model refines an under-written AI draft, a task distinct from writing from scratch. Across 2,050 drafts and eight refiners (16,400 rewrites), a four-layer protocol credits a rewrite only after it passes a faithfulness check against its own source, then ranks the survivors by holistic editorial preference through per-form Bradley-Terry fits whose centered coefficients are standardized before equal-weight averaging. Staying faithful proves to be a decisive test that behaves differently by form: gate-failure rates range from 9.1% on short stories to 29.5% on audio fiction, and the drift that disqualifies a rewrite shifts from events and identity in narrative to claims and evidence in essays. A 600-case human audit puts gate agreement at 0.925 (0.91 to 0.94 across forms), whereas subjective preference is form-sensitive and least settled for essays, among human readers no less than the model judge. The benchmark, evaluation protocol, and Hindi prose diagnostics are available at https://abdur75648.github.io/rasa-bench.

papers.title: SWIFT: A Handcrafted, Arithmetic-Minimal FPGA Engine for Real-Time Audio Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Generative voice cloning threatens voice-based authentication, yet current deepfake detectors rely on power-hungry, high-precision models unsuited to edge hardware. We present SWIFT (Streaming Whiten-Integer Forensic Trust-Engine), a handcrafted detector that works in the high-frequency noise domain where synthesis artifacts concentrate. A first-order integer high-pass residual drives nine families of fixed-point descriptors, among them integer lifting-wavelet cepstral quantiles, Mahalanobis anomaly distances, Poincar\'e phase-space geometry, and phase jitter, fused by calibrated gradient-boosted trees and a sparse L1-regularised meta-learner. Under leakage-controlled nested cross-validation, with one shared preprocessing chain for real and fake audio, this reference model reaches accuracy of up to 99.86% and an Equal Error Rate (EER) as low as 0.03% across eight benchmarks. Its integer front-end and a fixed-point linear classifier run on the programmable logic of a PYNQ-Z2 (Zynq-7020) board, with a 7.85 microseconds per-frame datapath latency (127.4k frames/s) at 1.734 W and 11.2% LUT utilisation. Integer-only audio deepfake feature extraction is thus feasible at the edge without pretrained neural models or floating-point units.

authors.name: Soumita Chatterjee
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur

authors.name: Hafizur Rahaman
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur

papers.title: Two Primes Suffice for Definable Graph Canonisation
papers.abstract: We study inflationary fixed-point logic on finite simple graphs with unordered vertices and an ordered number sort. For a prime $r$, the quantifier $M_r$ tests whether the number of relations satisfying a formula is nonzero modulo $r$. For any distinct primes $p$ and $q$, the logic with $M_p$ and $M_q$ defines the adjacency matrix of a canonical copy on the number sort. On labelled inputs this matrix is computable in deterministic polynomial time with an oracle that tests whether the number of satisfying assignments of a Boolean circuit is nonzero modulo $p$. For each prime $p$, the logic with $M_p$ alone cannot define a canonical copy on all graphs. The primes also differ on Boolean queries. There is a single first-order formula $\beta(S)$ on vertex sets such that $M_q S \beta(S)$ is undefinable with $M_p$ alone whenever $p \ne q$. For a positive integer-valued function $g$, consider the class of all graphs $G$ with at most $g(|V(G)|)$ automorphisms. For each fixed prime $p$, the logic with $M_p$ canonises this class exactly when $g$ is bounded.

papers.title: Lightweight Spectral Subspace Filtering for Trojan-Resilient AI Inference Engines
papers.abstract: Backdoor attacks pose a significant security threat to deep neural networks (DNNs) deployed on AI inference engines and hardware accelerators. By embedding hidden triggers during training, these attacks induce malicious behavior while maintaining high accuracy on benign inputs. Multi-trigger backdoor attacks are particularly challenging to detect and mitigate because of the distributed and stealthy nature of their effects. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a training-free Spectral Subspace Filtering framework that detects and suppresses backdoor-induced activations by analyzing latent feature representations. Exploiting the geometric separation between benign and malicious feature distributions, the framework employs Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to identify the dominant malicious subspace and performs inference-time spectral scrubbing through activation projection. This approach suppresses backdoor effects without model retraining, requiring only a small set of triggered samples collected offline. Experimental evaluation across CNN and transformer architectures, including AlexNet, ResNet18, VGG16, MobileNetV2, and Vision Transformer (ViT), demonstrates that the proposed method reduces the attack success rate (ASR) from 94.2-99.8% to an average of 2.07%, while preserving clean accuracy of up to 98.54% with low inference overhead. The framework also demonstrates robustness across varying poisoning rates and multiple concurrent triggers, highlighting its potential as a lightweight runtime defense for enhancing the security and reliability of AI inference engines against backdoor attacks.

authors.name: Soumita Chatterjee
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur

authors.name: Hafizur Rahaman
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur

papers.title: Sondheimer oscillations in Weyl semimetal films
papers.abstract: In conducting films subject to an out-of-plane magnetic field, electron motion between the surfaces gives rise to conductance oscillations periodic in magnetic field, known as Sondheimer oscillations. While this size effect has been investigated in conventional metals, its dependence on the Berry curvature of topological materials remains less explored. In this work, we extend the semiclassical Boltzmann description of Sondheimer oscillations to type-I Weyl semimetal films. We account for the Berry curvature, the orbital magnetic moment and the effect of the Zeeman coupling on the Fermi wavevector and the electronic group velocity. The Berry curvature and the orbital magnetic moment generate a beating pattern and chirping in the Sondheimer oscillations. In the thick-film and thin-film regimes, we provide analytical expressions for the longitudinal conductivity, which highlight the interplay between electronic band topology and boundary-scattering in magnetotransport.

authors.name: Ion Garate
authors.institution: Regroupement Québécois sur les Matériaux de Pointe

papers.title: Click and Count: Multimodal Prototype Adaptation for Class-Agnostic Object Counting
papers.abstract: We propose a multimodal, class-agnostic, density-based object counting framework that specifies the object of interest through visual exemplars, a text description, or both, within a single iterative refinement pipeline. Existing counters typically fall into two groups: methods that fuse two modalities, a hand-drawn bounding box and a text description, to specify the target object, and single-modality methods that rely on either a box exemplar or text alone. A few recent methods replace the box with a point or click. We expand a single click into a precise object mask via a frozen visual-prompt segmentation model, feeding an iterative prototype-refinement process that also fuses a text description at every refinement step. We make two contributions: first, a click-derived exemplar extraction module that removes the bounding-box requirement of prior exemplar-based counters; second, a per-step text-fusion mechanism that combines visual and textual prompts throughout refinement. Combined with text guidance, our model achieves state-of-the-art counting accuracy, outperforming prior click-based counting methods across all metrics and surpassing the box-exemplar base architecture in mean absolute error. The code is available at github.com/ameniifi/Click-and-Count.

papers.title: Statistical inference under response-adaptive experimental designs: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Response-adaptive designs, including bandit-based approaches, update treatment allocation using accrued outcomes. In this paper, we systematically reviewed how studies in health and biostatistics conducted and evaluated inference under these designs. We searched six databases for studies published from January 2010 through October 2025. Of 774 records identified, 36 studies met the inclusion criteria. We summarized them using study-level counts and structured narrative comparisons, with reporting guided by PRISMA 2020. Most studies focused on methods or designs. Evidence supporting inference came mainly from theory and simulation. Among studies for which each metric was relevant, 26 of 32 numerically evaluated power, 23 of 32 type I error, eight of 35 estimator bias, and five of 12 interval coverage. These findings suggest that studies more often quantified power and type I error than estimator bias or interval coverage. Evaluations of adaptive allocation should also examine estimation and interval performance when these are relevant to the study objective.

papers.title: Reconfigurable Microwave Photonic All-Pass Filters based on Optical Kerr Microcombs
papers.abstract: Microwave photonic (MWP) all pass filters (APFs), which enable phase manipulation without altering signal amplitudes, are essential for phase engineering in high bandwidth microwave signal processing. However, achieving a high degree of reconfigurability in the filter order and characteristic parameters of APFs remains challenging for conventional methods. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a new strategy for realizing MWP APFs based on a microcomb driven transversal filter system, enabling high reconfigurability, sharp phase transitions with high group delays, and low loss. We experimentally demonstrate both 1st and 2nd order APFs, achieving a maximum amplitude variation (MAV) of 1.95 dB and a maximum group delay (MGD) of 580 ps for the former, and a MAV of 2.01 dB and an MGD of 1740 ps for the latter. In addition, both independent and joint tuning of APF characteristic parameters are demonstrated by simply programming the tap coefficients without changing any hardware, enabling highly reconfigurable filter response for diverse phase engineering functionalities. These results highlight the potential of our approach for implementing MWP APFs with both high performance and reconfigurability for practical applications requiring dynamic and versatile phase control.

authors.name: David J. Moss
authors.institution: Institut National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: 2D MXene integrated optical polarizers based on TiO2 with high performance
papers.abstract: Polarization control is essential for modern optical systems. Recently, two dimensional (2D) materials featuring highly anisotropic absorption across broad wavelength regions have emerged as a promising solution for realizing optical polarizers with operation bandwidths far exceeding those achievable using bulk materials. Despite this, existing 2D material based optical polarizers face critical limitations in simultaneously delivering high polarizer figures of merit (FOMs), robust power endurance, and scalable fabrication, hindering their practical deployment beyond laboratory. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by demonstrating optical polarizers through integrating 2D MXene films onto silicon photonic devices and subsequently converting them in situ into 2D titanium dioxide (TiO2). The 2D TiO2 exhibits significantly improved anisotropic absorption and thermal / chemical stability compared with MXene, enabling the hybrid polarizers to achieve a record high polarizer FOM of 17.5 (among 2D material-coated devices) and excellent power tolerance (stable under > 2 W coupled average power), together with a broad operation bandwidth (> 140 nm) and a high fabrication yield ( 98%). We also demonstrate microring resonator polarizers achieving high polarization extinction ratios up to 12 dB. With outstanding overall performance and strong capability for large-scale manufacturing, these polarizers represent a solid step towards industry ready implementations of 2D material based optical polarizers.

authors.name: David J. Moss
authors.institution: Institut National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Interactions with hidden traits induce diversification and conceal its origin
papers.abstract: Adaptive diversification is often inferred from a small number of measurable traits, even though evolutionary dynamics arise from many interacting phenotypic dimensions. Unmeasured traits may therefore do more than bias inference: through their interactions, they may determine whether diversification occurs at all. Here we develop a theory of the onset and attribution of adaptive diversification by partitioning phenotype space into focal and hidden sectors. Eliminating the hidden sector yields an exact effective operator. Coupling to hidden traits that are stabilizing in isolation can destabilize an otherwise stable phenotype and generate a diversifying composite mode: the interaction creates diversification rather than merely strengthening it. Conversely, when the hidden sector is itself diversifying, the focal traits diversify as a correlated response to a hidden-driven process: no effective description in the focal traits, not even the exact one obtained by eliminating the hidden sector, predicts the variation they display, and stabilizing the focal traits reduces it without removing it. These effects become strongest near the hidden sector's own threshold, so a weakly stabilized hidden trait can have a large effect even with modest coupling to the focal traits, and they can generate correlations between focal traits that have no direct interaction. Onset and observability are distinct: systems with the same leading eigenvalue can project very differently onto the measured traits, so the theory tracks both the full operator and the focal-hidden partition. Individual-based simulations recover the predicted threshold and variance law, coupling-induced trait splitting, and the reversal of induced correlations. Interactions with unmeasured traits can both create adaptive diversification and determine whether the diversification seen in measured phenotypes can be attributed to them.

authors.name: Vikas Kumar Jha
authors.institution: Foundation for Research in Health Systems

papers.title: Coupled Altermagnetic and Valley Physics in Monolayer VBiSe$_3$
papers.abstract: The interplay of compensated magnetism, spin--orbit coupling (SOC), and valley degrees of freedom provides a promising route toward spin--valley control without conventional ferromagnetism. Here, using first-principles calculations combined with Wannier-based analysis, we reveal coupled altermagnetic and valley physics in monolayer VBiSe$_3$. In the absence of SOC, the compensated N\'eel antiferromagnetic state, whose opposite-spin V sublattices are related only by mirror operations, exhibits momentum-dependent spin splitting with a characteristic $i$-wave altermagnetic texture. Upon inclusion of SOC, the conduction-band states develop anisotropic Rashba-like spin splitting together with a sizable $K/K'$ valley splitting of about $112.2$~meV. Orbital analysis and an effective SOC Hamiltonian identify the hybridization between SOC-active Se-$p_{x,y}$ states and predominantly V-$d_{z^2}$ conduction-band states as an important microscopic origin of the valley splitting. The two valleys carry Berry curvature of the same sign but different magnitude, unlike the opposite-sign pattern of conventional valley Hall systems, so the large valley splitting, rather than a valley Hall effect, offers a possible route to valley-selective carrier occupation by gating. Moreover, a modest $-1\%$ biaxial compressive strain drives the system into a quasi-half-valley-metallic state with valley-polarized electrons and non-valley-polarized holes. These results establish monolayer VBiSe$_3$ as a promising platform for coupled altermagnetic, spin--orbit, and valley phenomena with strain-tunable electronic states.

papers.title: Empirical Limits of Risk-Averse Reinforcement Learning versus Gas-Aware Routing in Deterministic DeFi Execution
papers.abstract: The migration of order execution to Automated Market Makers (AMMs) introduces two deterministic frictions absent from classical microstructure: closed-form constant-product slippage and Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) sandwich attacks gated by gas costs. We construct an end-to-end execution environment calibrated to live Uniswap V2 reserves, an EIP-1559 AR(1) gas process, and real Swap events, utilising stress-volatility gas shocks to make the MEV trigger informative. A Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) agent with a Rockafellar-Uryasev Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) penalty and a dual-head Chow-Ghavamzadeh critic is trained for one million steps across five risk-aversion levels and seeds, benchmarked against a myopic gas-aware oracle. We document a reproducible specification-gaming pathology: prior to a patch, a forced terminal liquidation routed through a no-MEV code path artificially inflated returns threefold and was preferentially exploited by higher-$\lambda$ runs. On the corrected environment, the strongest PPO variant captures 79\% of the myopic gas-aware oracle (46,542 $\pm$ 673 vs 58,786 $\pm$ 616 USDC), and extending the observation with three blocks of gas history fails to close the gap. We find no empirical evidence that the tested model-free MLP policies dominate this myopic gas-aware oracle, which can be evaluated in $\mathcal{O}(\log \epsilon^{-1})$ time per block. This result is robust to a $\sim$16x trunk-capacity expansion and a variance-controlled gas-history ablation. Code and reproducibility materials are available upon request.

papers.title: Grammar-as-a-Draft: More Tokens per Speculative Decoding Step on Grammar-Constrained Structured Outputs
papers.abstract:
Under structured outputs (JSON schemas, regexes, tool calls), speculative drafters do not see the grammar constraint and repeatedly propose invalid keys, delimiters, and indentation, while the grammar engine already knows which tokens must come next.
  We present Grammar-as-a-Draft (GaaD), which treats the grammar as a second drafter. Before each verify step, the scheduler merges the drafter's proposal with grammar-forced tokens into one draft row: matching tokens stay as GRAMMAR, the proposal is cut where it leaves the forced path, and forced tokens fill the rest of a row wider than the drafter's proposal. The verify step accepts GRAMMAR drafts without computing their logits, composing with any drafter with no new kernels or compilation on the critical path. Because grammars fix text rather than tokens, committing canonical forced tokens changes the output distribution relative to grammar-masked target decoding.
  We implement GaaD in vllm-torchtpu and an independent Rust serving runtime, evaluating on TPU v7x with MTP, DFlash, and n-gram drafters on a JSON character-profile benchmark. GaaD raises average acceptance length from 2.06 to 5.43 (MTP, Qwen3.5-0.8B), 1.99 to 5.31 (MTP, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B), 1.57 to 4.13 (DFlash, Qwen3-4B), and 1.30 to 3.64 (n-gram, Qwen3-4B), decoding 2.66-2.81x faster at batch size 1 and 1.14-1.70x at batch size 64. In Rust, MTP+GaaD is 2.23x faster on Qwen3.5-0.8B, 2.02x on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, and 1.22x at 128 concurrent requests. Under mixed traffic (25-50% structured), GaaD finishes the workload 1.03-1.23x sooner (structured requests 2.2-3.2x sooner) while plain-text TPOT rises 7-42%. We also show grammar-masked greedy decoding can pick non-canonical tokenizations, so GaaD can yield different valid outputs that an fp32 reference finds equally likely.

authors.name: John Zhang
authors.institution: Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center Shreveport

authors.name: Silky Arora
authors.institution: All India Institute of Medical Sciences

papers.title: Censored Regression Models with Endogeneity: A Survey
papers.abstract: This survey article provides a comprehensive overview of methodologies developed to handle endogeneity in censored regression models. We emphasize their theoretical basis, and estimating methodologies. The paper summarizes the benefits and drawbacks of each technique and addresses expansions to nonlinear, panel, and high-dimensional settings, offering researchers practical assistance and identifying options for future methodological improvement in censored models with endogenous regressors.

authors.name: Swati Shukla
authors.institution: All India Institute of Medical Sciences

papers.title: Learning How a Body Moves: Few-Shot Body Inference for Visual World Models of Animated Characters
papers.abstract: Two visually identical animated characters can respond differently to the same action command because their body dynamics differ. For example, a stiff blob and its bouncy twin reach different heights when both receive the jump command. Given only the first frame and the action command, a visual world model has no information to distinguish these twins, because their initial appearances are identical. We therefore propose an in-context world model that encodes clips of a character's other actions into a body representation, using a contrastive loss to separate look-alike characters. We introduce ToonTwins, a benchmark of 144 2D cartoon characters that run, jump, fall, turn and crouch. Its characters form look-alike groups of four that differ only in their dynamics profile, and we also evaluate the model on 32 animated animals from DeformingThings4D. Even with a body code from these clips, the latent pixel world model we tested recovered at most 25 percent of the twins' jump height difference. On new shapes, our model identified the correct twin in 85.9 percent of cases, compared with 76.7 percent for a transformer baseline that reads the same clips without a body summary, and in a controlled ablation the contrastive loss gave more than half of this gain. On the animated animals, it reduced the mean path prediction error by 8.5 percent against a model without body information.

authors.name: Amarnath R
authors.institution: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

papers.title: Differential Proteomics to XAI Rules: A SHAP-FOL-ILP Modeling for Lung Adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract:
Background: We developed an interpretable workflow linking paired differential proteomics, sparse logistic regression, SHAP attribution, and first-order logic (FOL) rule learning in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD).
  Methods: We analysed 213 CPTAC-LUAD tissue samples (111 tumour, 102 adjacent-normal) from 111 patients, including 102 matched pairs. Protein effect estimation and testing used the same complete pairs, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Sparse logistic regression used five-fold stratified patient-grouped nested cross-validation. Preprocessing and model selection were confined to training data, with feature selection repeated within inner folds. A separate five-fold patient-grouped evaluation tested SHAP-guided inductive logic programming (FOL/ILP) using training-derived evidence and discretisation.
  Results: Quality control retained 9,518 proteins. At FDR below 0.05 and an absolute mean paired log-ratio difference of at least 1, 378 were differentially abundant (40 increased, 338 decreased). The sparse classifier yielded ROC-AUC 0.9997, average precision 0.9998, accuracy 0.9906, and balanced accuracy 0.9906. FOL/ILP yielded held-out accuracy 0.9765, balanced accuracy 0.9767, precision 0.9818, recall 0.9730, and F1 0.9774. HSPA12B, PALM2-AKAP2, STARD13, and PPM1F had non-zero coefficients in all five classifier folds. The most frequent Horn clause occurred in two of five folds. All others occurred once.
  Conclusions: The workflow connects proteomic classification, attribution, and symbolic rules. Performance reflects tumour-versus-adjacent-normal discrimination within one cohort. Biomarker and clinical claims require independent validation, repeated assessment of rule stability, and further biological annotation.

papers.title: Operator-Valued Q-Learning: Compositional Bellman Recursions for Order-Sensitive Decision Making
papers.abstract: In quantum pulse sequences, spacecraft attitude control and in-hand reorientation, actions act on a hidden physical state as non-commuting operators, so the outcome of a plan depends on the order of its actions. We let the value function carry this structure: each Q(s,a) is an N x N operator, and the Bellman backup applies the action's dual map to the continuation value, Q(s,a) = K_a^*(R(s,a) + gamma E V(s')). Unrolled along a plan, the recursion builds the ordered product of the actions' operators, and the value at any latent state is a linear trace readout. It is exact for policies that do not observe the latent, the backup contracts for unitary and orthogonal dynamics, and an asynchronous operator TD scheme learns it with almost-sure convergence. Classical values live in a lattice, so a maximum over actions exists; self-adjoint operators form an anti-lattice (Kadison) and have none. An operator log-sum-exp still gives one operator per state-action pair whose readout upper-bounds the value of every policy at every latent state. The sampled update converges to it for a finite horizon, and it reduces to soft Q-learning and the QMDP bound when actions commute. We prove that scalar values on observations that ignore action order must confuse swapped histories, that exact history tables grow exponentially for free action groups but polynomially for nilpotent ones, and give a Hankel-rank lower bound on the operator dimension. In experiments the learned policy matches 1000-simulation tree search on SO(3) pointing for horizons up to 20 at ~10^4 times lower decision cost, transfers zero-shot to unseen initial states, and acts exactly on its belief mean when the initial state is hidden, where plugging the mean into a DQN does not. A planner with the same model knowledge is more sample-efficient at short horizons, and a DQN given the operators matches or exceeds OpQ.

papers.title: A High-Resolution UAV Benchmark Dataset and Baseline Evaluation for Teak Crown Segmentation in Western Ghats Tropical Forests
papers.abstract: Accurate teak-tree segmentation from high-resolution drone imagery is critical for sustainable plantation management, yet lacks dedicated benchmarks. We introduce TeakTreeNet, a comprehensive dataset and evaluation protocol for binary teak-tree segmentation at native 2cm resolution. Four state-of-the-art architectures: U-Net, PSPNet, DeepLabV3, and SegFormer were rigorously benchmarked across scratch and ImageNet-pretrained settings with three-seed reproducibility. SegFormer establishes new SOTA performance with F1 0.938 +/- 0.002 (Teak), IoU 0.968 +/- 0.001 (Teak), and Accuracy 0.986 +/- 0.001, outperforming all pretrained CNNs. Domain-adaptive training suffices, as the scratch SegFormer outperforms ImageNet pretrained baselines, avoiding large-scale pretraining overhead. Comprehensive analysis reveals Transformer's superior boundary delineation for dense plantation scenarios. TeakTreeNet provides researchers with 6391 expertly annotated drone patches (224x224) and establishes reproducible evaluation protocols, enabling direct comparison of future methods. Our benchmark demonstrates SegFormer's optimal balance of accuracy, efficiency, and deployability for operational forestry monitoring of teak plantations for India's western tropical forests.

papers.title: CAST: A Deployed Speech-to-Text Cascade for Closed Captioning of Entertainment Television
papers.abstract: Despite rapid progress in automatic speech recognition (ASR), caption generation for long-form entertainment video remains challenging for content dense in music and effects, rich in accents, crosstalk, and noise. The transcript quality depends on segmentation and surrounding modules as much as the acoustic model. A single pass voice activity detection (VAD) can miss faint, low-energy voice while forwarding near-silent segments that induce hallucination and repetition in an autoregressive decoder. These competing errors motivate a hierarchical VAD that revisits rejected segments under semantic and acoustic retention checks. We present Captioning ASR Stack for Television (CAST), an integrated speech-to-text pipeline for closed captioning (CC) combining frozen Whisper large-v3 with segmentation, language identification, lyrics routing, and targeted hallucination detection and repair on a single NVIDIA L4 GPU. On 100 in-house assets spanning 60.46 hours, CAST reduces normalized WER from 6.99% to 5.36% and subtitle edit rate from 254.2 to 221.9 min/hour against the WhisperX pipeline, and improves deletion rate by 11% on public datasets. We also present the behavior of each stage in the pipeline. CAST entered the production speech-to-text (STT) stage of our CC pipeline in late August 2026; we report the evaluation evidence and path to full-scale operation.

papers.title: On $k$-very ample line bundles on blowups of surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article we study the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow ups of some smooth surfaces. We begin by investigating the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow-ups of smooth surfaces with Picard number $1$, extending the previously known cases of uniform line bundles to arbitrary line bundles, under certain restrictions. We then show that for blowups of smooth surfaces with trivial canonical divisor, $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles implies the $k$-very ampleness of arbitrary line bundles. In view of the above, we study $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles on blow ups of certain $K3$-surfaces $(K_X \cong \mathcal{O}_X)$. Finally, we provide a result concerning the $k$ very ampleness of certain uniform line bundles on the general blow up of product of curves $(K_X \not\cong \mathcal{O}_X)$.

authors.name: Suratno Basu
authors.institution: Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research

papers.title: DiscernBench: Evaluating Cooperative Discernment of LLM Agents in Institutional Settings
papers.abstract: The deployment of large language models in operational settings demands evaluation of judgment under institutional constraint. We introduce DiscernBench, a benchmark for evaluating cooperative discernment: the ability of an agent to determine whether to comply with, refuse, or escalate a request in an institutional setting. DiscernBench comprises scenarios derived from real-world incident reports across domains such as aviation, law enforcement, and emergency management. We evaluate eight LLMs across three decision-making configurations and analyze both final decisions and the intermediate judgments produced during multi-agent deliberation. Under disagreement, Final Responders exhibit model- and role-dependent aggregation patterns in which a lone specialist recommendation can disproportionately influence the collective decision, a phenomenon we term Minority-Signal Override. Role-specialized multi-agent deliberation raises average over-escalation from 3.79% under direct single-agent judgment to 28.27%, with the direction and magnitude of minority-signal influence varying substantially across models and specialist roles. These results reveal distinct collective decision behaviors that are not captured by final-answer accuracy alone. Trustworthy multi-agent systems therefore require evaluating not only individual specialist reasoning, but also how conflicting judgments are transformed into collective decisions. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Disha1001/DiscernBench.

papers.title: Elicitation format changes zero-shot classification accuracy in a medical vision-language model: a two-center evaluation on colorectal histopathology
papers.abstract: Background. Verbalized confidence from a hosted medical vision-language model is usually treated as packaging around an unchanged prediction. Methods. We held a nine-class colorectal histopathology prompt fixed except for the requested response format and evaluated MedGemma-27b-it on 10,004 validation and 7,180 external-center PathMNIST patches, with preregistered endpoints, randomized ties, and random floors recomputed for each patch set. Results. Requesting probabilities over all nine classes instead of a ranked top-3 reduced accuracy by 14.8 points on validation, -0.1475 [-0.1594, -0.1353], and 13.4 at the external center, -0.1341 [-0.1484, -0.1196], against chance accuracy of 0.1111. The nine-class prompt uniquely forbade commentary, reasoning, and a chosen answer; removing that prohibition at matched cardinality and token budget recovered +0.1878 [+0.1623, +0.2134] and +0.1911 [+0.1648, +0.2181], while changing cardinality with the prohibition absent moved accuracy by -0.0013 [-0.0300, +0.0280] and -0.0214 [-0.0494, +0.0071]. The nine-class format returned no parseable distribution on 7.6 and 7.7 percent of patches, mostly zero vectors in the two least-textured classes, and deferring these failures first explained its measurable selective-prediction gain. Across four vision-capable models, accuracy did not grade the cost: two models matched on accuracy differed five- to sevenfold. First-token logit entropy routed better than any elicited signal, +0.1820 [+0.1722, +0.1974] versus +0.0493 [+0.0377, +0.0649] relative to each signal's random floor. Conclusions. Response format changes a medical vision-language classifier, and the operative component here was the instruction suppressing an answer. Use logits when available; otherwise request a short ranked list without prohibiting reasoning or a chosen answer.

papers.title: Structure-Exploiting Hierarchical Retrieval for Long Narrative Documents: A Precision-Oriented Alternative to Learned Abstraction Trees
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation over book-length documents must locate a small, coherent set of passages inside tens of thousands of tokens. Flat dense retrieval ignores document structure; RAPTOR instead builds a hierarchy by recursively clustering and summarizing with a language model. We study a complementary design that exploits the native structure of a document: a two-level retriever that (i) selects chapters with a hybrid BM25+dense match over chapter recaps, (ii) runs a chapter-filtered dense search, and (iii) expands top passages into contiguous, section-aware spans under a token budget, plus content-hash-gated delta ingestion to keep the index cheap to update. We evaluate on five public-domain books (113 chapter-localization queries) and on QuALITY and NovelQA (200K+ token novels). In-house, we find a seed-stable precision/ranking tradeoff: with section expansion off, hierarchical retrieval returns a higher fraction of chunks from the correct chapter (+3.3pp, Wilcoxon p=0.014); with expansion on, ranking improves (MRR, p=0.040). Accuracy differences are not significant. On QuALITY, hierarchical retrieval beats flat top-k (81.0% vs 70.4%, p=0.0019) and matches the full article (p=0.74). On NovelQA, hierarchical and flat retrieval are statistically tied (55.7% vs 56.8%, p=0.24); hierarchy helps aggregation questions while flat wins on localized facts. Against a faithful RAPTOR baseline we find a complementary tradeoff, not superiority. Delta ingestion reuses 94 to 99.7% of embeddings on incremental edits. We make no claim of semantic chapter-boundary inference and scope claims to English narrative prose.

papers.title: LiquidGazeNet: Towards Event-Based Near-Eye Gaze Estimation under Low-Light Conditions
papers.abstract: Near-eye gaze estimation under low-light nighttime conditions is challenging because the quality and effective temporal resolution of conventional intensity frames can be reduced. This paper presents LiquidGazeNet, an event-only gaze-estimation framework that combines polarity-aware spike-latency encoding with a custom LTC-based recurrent module. Positive- and negative-polarity events are represented in separate channels, while exponentially decayed time surfaces retain per-pixel temporal recency across successive event windows. A shared convolutional encoder extracts spatial features from each window, and a two-layer recurrent module composed of LTC-inspired cells integrates them causally over short temporal sequences. The network is trained using a hybrid objective that combines screen-space coordinate regression with centre-referenced directional consistency. The framework is evaluated on Gaze-FELL under cross-subject and cross-scene protocols and is further assessed through event-representation, temporal-module, window-duration, and computational ablations. LiquidGazeNet achieves mean errors of 3.75 degrees and 2.41 degrees under cross-subject and cross-scene evaluation, respectively. The results indicate that polarity-aware temporal-recency encoding, together with recurrent integration, is effective for event-only gaze estimation under the evaluated low-light nighttime conditions.

authors.name: Himanshu Kumar
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Bhopal

papers.title: Seeing Through Preferences: Recovering Hidden Local Preference Neighborhoods for Text-to-Image Alignment
papers.abstract: Aligning text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models with human preferences typically relies on large-scale pairwise annotations, which are expensive to obtain and provide only sparse supervision. Moreover, not all preference comparisons contribute equally to learning: comparisons between semantically distant images often reveal little about the fine-grained perceptual factors underlying human judgments. We argue that informative supervision can arise from local preference neighborhoods surrounding human-preferred images, where semantically aligned alternatives expose meaningful perceptual and structural differences. Motivated by this observation, we propose PrefLens, a framework that recovers local preference neighborhoods from sparse human feedback. Specifically, PrefLens generates controlled perceptual variations around preferred images that largely retain semantic identity and selects compact sets of informative neighbors in a reward-defined preference space induced by pretrained reward models. By transforming each human preference annotation into a structured neighborhood of informative comparisons, PrefLens enriches supervision without requiring additional human labeling. Our experiments and diagnostic evaluations show that the recovered neighborhoods capture human-relevant preference characteristics and provide effective supervision for preference alignment across diverse settings.

papers.title: Improved Omega results for Riesz sums of a class of $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We investigate a general class of $L$-functions satisfying functional equations with multiple gamma factors, and establish sharper lower bounds for the error terms associated with the Riesz sums of their coefficients. By integrating the resonance method with Riesz smoothing, we improve upon previously known omega results for the corresponding Riesz sums. We prove these estimates within a unified axiomatic framework under a precise set of hypotheses. Our general theorem can be applied to several classical arithmetic problems, including the $k$-fold Piltz divisor function $d_{\mathbb{K},k}(n)$ over a number field $\mathbb{K}$, as well as the lattice point counting functions for the circle, ellipse, and sphere problems. In particular, we sharpen the classical $\Omega$-bound for the error in counting lattice points in the ellipse $u^2+5v^2\le x$, strengthening a result of Nowak. Moreover, for the smoothed error terms corresponding to the divisor and circle problems, we improve upon previously known $\Omega$-bounds by increasing the exponent of the $\log\log x$ factor and sharpening the $\log\log\log x$ dependence by replacing exponential decay factors of the form $\exp(-c\sqrt{\log\log\log x})$ in previous results with an explicit polynomial power of $\log\log\log x$.

authors.name: Arindam Roy
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
