papers.title: Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA) for Energy Market Settlements: A Machine and Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach
papers.abstract: The integration of segmented energy markets into Independent System Operators (ISOs) like CAISO and MISO has increased settlement complexity. Automated transaction processing creates challenges for evaluating accuracy, compliance, and financial integrity. Traditional rule-based manual auditing is inefficient, error-prone, and cannot handle the data volume from automated markets.This research proposes Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA), a machine and reinforcement learning framework for settlement auditing via anomaly prioritization. ANNA integrates statistical anomaly detection, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), clustering, and Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning to flag potentially anomalous transactions from historical market data. The approach is evaluated as an analyst-support tool for prioritizing transactions needing further audit review.ANNA was tested against traditional statistical methods, clustering-based techniques, and supervised/reinforcement learning models. The study used three years of CAISO settlement data over 63 million source records across 32 charge codes and multiple counterparties. After preprocessing, approximately 2.9 million labeled transactions formed the working dataset, with model-specific subsets used for training and evaluation. Performance was assessed using precision, recall, computational efficiency, and false-negative detection.ANNA outperforms traditional methods by identifying hidden relationships in settlement data, while standard deviation thresholds, K-Means, KNN, and Q-Learning performed poorly across key metrics. The result is a scalable solution integrating machine and reinforcement learning for automated auditing of energy market settlements, contributing computationally efficient anomaly prioritization to settlement-auditing workflows.

papers.title: Bifurcation Structure and Coexisting Dynamical States in Two Inductively Coupled Josephson Junctions
papers.abstract: Inductively coupled Josephson junctions support coexisting stationary and running states whose selection depends on both circuit parameters and initial conditions. We investigate the model of a direct current-driven resistively and capacitively shunted junction pair as coupled nonlinear oscillators at zero external magnetic flux, allowing unequal bias, damping and inductive coupling parameters. Equilibrium equations, nullclines, and Jacobian spectra are combined with multiple-initial-condition simulations, finite-time Lyapunov spectra, and Poincar\'e returns to characterize changes in the system dynamics under varying initial conditions and parameter settings. The fixed-point bifurcation diagrams reveal the creation, destruction or annihilation of equilibria and non-monotonic changes in their number under asymmetric coupling. In representative asymmetric parameter slices, nondegenerate saddle-node bifurcations generate or terminate stable equilibria within intervals that also support periodic or chaotic running motion. The running dynamics exhibit period-doubling, period-cascading sequences and embedded periodic windows within chaotic regions, while the initial-condition scans resolve their coexistence with stationary states. These results connect the local equilibrium structure with the parameter-dependent organization and selection of dynamical regimes in the coupled-junction system.

papers.title: Free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem
papers.abstract: We compute the limiting free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem for every pseudodimension $d>0$ and every inverse temperature $\lambda > 0$ at the scale $n^{1/d}$. We show that the limit is given by a rigorous replica-symmetric formula determined by the unique solution of a recursive distributional equation on a Poisson-weighted infinite tree, confirming conjectures of Aldous and Talagrand. As a consequence, for a fixed inverse temperature $\lambda > 0$, we deduce exponential concentration of the cost of a Gibbs assignment and determine the exponential growth rate of the number of near-optimal assignments.

papers.title: Persistent Neutron Irradiation Effects and Partial Recovery in Thin-Film CdS/CdTe Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Thin-film CdTe solar cells are promising candidates for lightweight space power, but device-level studies of their response to neutron irradiation remain scarce. Here, we report the device performance of CdS/CdTe solar cells irradiated for 10 to 150 min in the thermal irradiator of a TRIGA reactor (90 kW), corresponding to nominal total neutron fluences of 3.3 x 10^14 to 5.0 x 10^15 n cm-2. The cells were characterized after 18 months of post-irradiation storage, once the residual activity has decayed to background levels. Co-irradiated FTO-coated glass reference substrates exhibit a wavelength-dependent transmission loss, with the transmittance at 500 nm decreasing from 80 % to 50 % after 60 min of irradiation. The irradiated cells retain rectifying behavior, but the reverse-bias dark current, photocurrent, and efficiency generally decrease with exposure time. Post-irradiation annealing at 70 {\deg}C under one-sun illumination initially improves Jsc and Voc, with the highest efficiency after 4 h. Prolonged annealing, however, causes substantial FF degradation despite continued photocurrent recovery. These trends suggest that irradiation-induced changes in the glass substrate, CdTe absorber, and contacts respond differently to annealing. Understanding underlying defect chemistry and correlating it with device behavior are necessary steps toward radiation-tolerant CdTe photovoltaics for space applications.

papers.title: Finite-Time Singularities of the $L_\beta$-Gradient Flow in a K\"ahler Surface
papers.abstract: We study finite-time singularities of the $L_\beta$-gradient flow of closed symplectic surfaces in a compact K\"ahler surface, with $\beta > 0$ fixed. We derive the evolution equation for the second fundamental form and obtain a lower bound on the blow-up rate of its maximum squared norm. Combining this bound with a local curvature propagation estimate and the weighted monotonicity formula, we rule out Type I singularities.

papers.title: Learning the Boltzmann Collision Operator with Structural Constraints for Fast Kinetic Simulation
papers.abstract: The high-dimensional integration in the Boltzmann collision operator is a major computational bottleneck in deterministic kinetic simulations. We develop a structure-preserving neural operator that provides an efficient approximation of this nonlinear collision mapping. The operator maintains the gain-loss structure of the original Boltzmann collision operator, and, by construction, is proportional to the square of the gas density. Conservative moment projection and entropy correction enforce conservation of mass, momentum, and energy, as well as entropy dissipation. By construction, the collision term also vanishes at all Maxwellians. In the numerical scheme for simulations of gas dynamics, we establish nonnegativity of the distribution function with the learned collision operator and prove exponential relaxation to the moment-matched equilibrium when a positive spectral gap is imposed. Numerical experiments for a constant collision kernel demonstrate a favorable accuracy-cost tradeoff relative to Fourier spectral evaluations. Although trained on smooth distributions, the same operator handles discontinuous distribution functions and is embedded without retraining in steady Couette flow, normal-shock, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity solvers. These results demonstrate a reusable approximation for repeated collision evaluations that retains kinetic structure and supports accurate deterministic simulation.

papers.title: FormaFin: Verifiable Financial Analysis with Solver-Guided Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Formally verifying financial analyses generated by large language models (LLMs) remains challenging as financial rules are largely expressed in natural language and rarely have corresponding formal specifications. Training language models to formalize these rules is hindered by the scarcity of labeled data and reliable training signals, while confidential financial data favor small models that run locally. We introduce FormaFin, a framework that trains small open language models to translate financial rules into reusable SMT formulas. FormaFin integrates teacher distillation with reinforcement learning using an SMT solver to compute rewards from numerical thresholds stated in financial rules. We evaluate FormaFin on corporate loan monitoring, in which lenders check borrowers' financial figures against loan agreements. To evaluate our framework, we curate \bench{}, a benchmark containing 143 loan agreements and 2,527 questions covering compliance, earnings cushion, and debt capacity. Our results show that a 7B formalizer achieves 94.8\% accuracy, outperforming open LLMs up to ten times larger. Across three model families, accuracy ranges from 92.6 to 96.8\%. Our framework also detects 95.6 to 99.7\% of errors in other LLMs' financial analyses. We make FormaFin and \bench{} publicly available.

papers.title: Spatial Ensemble Logic for Biomedical Imaging: Geometric Element Ensembles in Euclidean Space
papers.abstract: Ensemble Logic (EL) is a family of modal logics over metric monoids whose modal parameters are terms with quantified variables. We study its member over the Euclidian space, called Spatial Ensemble Logic (SEL), for biomedical images. Geometric element ensembles (GELs) represent atomic propositions by finite lists of effectively presented semi-algebraic sets, principally closed balls. Translation, dilation and erosion preserve individual balls up to emptiness in any dimension. Translation and dilation act element-wise, but element-wise erosion gives only an inner bound. For $k\geq 2$, finite unions of balls are closed under neither intersection nor erosion. We therefore separate record representation from the evaluation domain. Our main result is a satisfaction-preserving translation over GELs into the first-order theory of real closed fields. It yields computable semi-algebraic satisfaction sets, decidable model checking and finite real algebraic evidence. For a fixed formula and dimension, model checking has polynomial data complexity under stated rationality and bounded-degree assumptions. Combined complexity is PSPACE-hard and in EXPSPACE. On the line, rational interval data admit linear-arithmetic evaluation with rational evidence, under rationality assumptions on the norm, query and evaluation point. For $k\geq 2$, rational balls can force irrational witnesses. Lower and upper annotation bounds propagate through formulas. Synthesis of a ball ensemble is decidable within a prescribed budget of balls and undecidable without one. In a vascular use case, medial ball ensembles decide calibre and stenosis queries at stored centers by comparing stored numbers. We also examine how far evaluation can proceed element-wise when the union forming a support is deferred to the point of evaluation.

papers.title: TurboFHE: An Efficient and Scalable Multi-GPU Framework for Homomorphic LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving large language model inference but remains computationally intensive. Existing multi-GPU FHE inference systems rely on expert-crafted parallelization plans that generalize poorly across hardware platforms and applications. We present \fwName, a framework that automatically compiles CKKS inference programs into efficient multi-GPU executables. Its compiler can split different nodes of the same computation graph at the ciphertext and polynomial level. Guided by a measurement-based performance model, its hardware-aware planner jointly optimizes task partitioning, placement, operand residency, and transfer scheduling. %Critical-path-guided rewrites extract shared computation and restructure homomorphic sums. Its backend then generates optimized GPU kernels and executes plans using CUDA graphs and selective point-to-point transfers. \fwName adapts its plans to diverse hardware configurations and FHE inference algorithms for large-scale models. On a single A100 GPU, \fwName achieves a $24.5\times$ speedup over THOR's reported BERT-Base inference latency. For Cerium's Llama-3-8B workload, \fwName outperforms Cerium's expert-crafted plans by $1.14\times$, $1.16\times$, and $1.24\times$ on 2, 4, and 8 RTX PRO~6000 GPUs, respectively. On A100 GPUs, \fwName achieves $98.0\%$, $91.8\%$, and $79.3\%$ parallel efficiency for the same workload on 2, 4, and 8 GPUs, respectively.

papers.title: AscendFHE: Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption on Ascend NPUs
papers.abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption enables cloud servers to run neural networks on encrypted inputs. In CKKS, inference requires costly arithmetic on high-degree polynomials. On Ascend neural processing units, preparing operands and reconstructing intermediate results add to this cost, while limited local memory constrains parallel execution. We present AscendFHE, a CKKS backend that coordinates Ascend's matrix engines and vector cores for bootstrapping and encrypted inference. It uses balanced-byte encoding and exact modular reconstruction to reduce vector work and packs intermediate results in the next operator's input format to avoid redundant transfers. Its two-task pipeline reuses shared buffers after their last read to overlap matrix and vector execution within the local memory budget. On Ascend 910B3, AscendFHE achieves a 4.61$\times$ bootstrapping speedup and 1.59$\times$--2.00$\times$ encrypted-inference speedups across ResNet-20, BERT-base, and Llama 3 8B over our Vector-based Ascend port of Cheddar.

papers.title: Selling Training Data
papers.abstract: This paper studies the sale of supplementary training dataset to improve predictive model. The buyer not only has private knowledge of its own dataset, but also can choose the way to merge these two datasets. This flexibility imposes a new constraint on the menu, requiring the buyer's total net utility be monotonic in the Blackwell order on private datasets. Given that, we show that a single posted price for a fully informative dataset is optimal in hypothesis testing, under differential virtual-value condition. The result extends to multi-class classification in which private datasets share a clean component but differ in how their labels are contaminated.

papers.title: IADR: Interface-Augmented Neural Operator for Phase-Field Mean-Curvature Flow
papers.abstract: The Allen-Cahn equation is one of the standard phase-field models for mean-curvature flow (MCF), parameterised by the diffuse-interface width $\varepsilon$. Practical simulations span a range of $\varepsilon$, so a single model covering this range is needed. PDE-specific neural operators are accurate but must be retrained at every $\varepsilon$; general neural operators cover $\varepsilon$ in one model but lose the phase-field structure of the target. We introduce Interface-Augmented Diffusion-Reaction (IADR), a neural operator that addresses both shortcomings: a target network with a diffusion-and-reaction (DR) structure preserves the phase-field structure of the Allen-Cahn equation, while a hypernetwork that maps $\varepsilon$ to the weights of this target network amortises the dependence on $\varepsilon$ across the range. A single IADR matches the per-$\varepsilon$ specialists on in-distribution data within the prescribed range, retains their cross-shape generalisation under both $\varepsilon$- and geometry-out-of-distribution shifts, and retains their compact DR target structure with millisecond-scale inference. We further establish a conditional $K$-step rollout error bound under consistency and stability assumptions.

papers.title: Cold CCH and warm CH3CCH: complementary tracers in the massive star-forming complex RCW122 (NE & SW)
papers.abstract: AIMS: By combining CH3CCH and CCH, we present a first multi-transition analysis of the RCW122-NE and RCW122-SW regions in the massive star-forming complex RCW 122. The aim is to investigate and to constrain the nature, chemistry, and evolutionary stage of each region. METHODS: We performed observations with the Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX). The analysis is based on 39 CH3CCH lines with J=10-9 to 20-19 (170.8-341.8 GHz) and four hyperfine components of the CCH N=4-3 transition (349.1-349.6 GHz). We estimated excitation conditions using both local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and non-LTE methods, with rotational-diagram analysis and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) calculations. Gas-grain chemical models were performed with the Nautilus code to reproduce the observed abundances over timescales characteristic of high-mass YSO evolution. RESULTS: The excitation analysis of CH3CCH indicates two physical components suggestive of a thermal gradient. The NE region yields T~41-61 K and N_tot~1x10^{16} cm^{-2}, while SW exhibits T~33-48 K and N_tot~7x10^{15} cm^{-2}. In both regions, CCH traces cold gas below 15 K with an H_2 density of 0.5-4x10^6 cm^{-3}. The detection of the ^{13}C isotopologues of CCH indicates that C^{13}CH is more abundant than ^{13}CCH. Chemical models at various evolutionary stages, with cosmic rays as a key parameter, reproduce the observed CCH and CH3CCH abundances, although the two species form through chemically distinct routes. CONCLUSIONS: We provide a coherent scenario in which CCH traces colder gas at an early evolutionary stage, whereas CH3CCH traces a region characterized by a warmer temperature gradient, associated with chemically more evolved gas at a later stage. These results constrain the conditions governing the origin and survival of interstellar species in a thermally and chemically stratified medium.

papers.title: Hyperconvexity of pseudoconvex domains with continuous boundaries
papers.abstract: This is a reading note on a disc formula proof of hyperconvexity of bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$ with continuous boundaries.

papers.title: An order on the Leech lattice from a $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetric triple-octonion product
papers.abstract: We show that the Leech lattice $\Lambda$ admits the structure of an order in a 24-dimensional real algebra: the lattice is closed under a bilinear product on $\mathbb{R}^{24}$, assembled from nine octonion-multiplication blocks under cyclic $\mathbb{Z}_3$ permutation of three octonion factors. In Robert A. Wilson's sublattice description of $\Lambda$, closure turns on a transposition $\sigma$ of two imaginary basis units: $\sigma$ leaves the $E_8$ lattice $L$ invariant and is an octonion-algebra isomorphism, but moves Wilson's two sublattices of $L$. The proof reduces to four lemmas, three of which follow from the closure of one maximal order of integral octonions. More generally, for every linear map $g$ with $g(L) = L$, the triple product built from the $g$-twisted octonion product closes on $\Lambda$ exactly when Wilson's two sublattices are closed under that product. We determine the idempotents, the square-zero elements, and the automorphism group of the algebra, as well as the automorphism group of the order and the index of the span of its products. We discuss the construction in the context of related work. A historical appendix (1923--1946) traces $\sigma$ to Richard H. Bruck's repair of Johannes Kirmse's integral octonions. The research record of this human--AI collaboration is public.

papers.title: Where Does a Weight-Editing Agent Help? Blind Diagnosis and Repair of Deployment Faults in Vision Models
papers.abstract: Language-model agents can read and edit the weights of neural networks without gradients, and this is increasingly presented as a new way of repairing models. We ask what such an agent adds, in a setting with a known answer. A vision model moved into a new system may be broken by a preprocessing, weight-conversion or output-convention fault; an agent restricted to forward passes must decide whether a fault exists, name it, and undo it by editing the weights. Over 183 runs on classification, segmentation and detection, scored against the fault-free model, we find three things. When the kind of fault is known, the agent is not needed: a script written afterwards repairs 30 of 48 faults against the agent's 33. But the agent did not have to be told: on five fault types outside every script it repairs 15 of 15 where that script repairs 4, and it never edits any of 21 fault-free models. And its limits are predictable: it needs a trustworthy per-layer reference for the model's activations and a fault that is an invertible structured transformation; without them, small faults are missed and repairs stay partial. We derive guidance on when to use an agent and when a script.

papers.title: Draft Forcing: Target-guided Speculative Drafting and Learned Verifier for Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models enable streaming synthesis chunk by chunk, yet invoking the large model for every chunk remains costly. While chunk-level speculative decoding can offload chunks to a lightweight draft model, existing approaches suffer from two limitations: (1) an off-the-shelf draft diverges from the target's trajectory, compounding errors in history; and (2) they either omit verification or rely on costly post-decode aesthetic scores rather than verifying consistency against the target. We address both with Draft Forcing, a framework coupling target-guided drafting with an on-policy trained verifier. Specifically, to align the draft for high acceptance, we opt for feature-level drafting, conditioning it on multi-layer target hidden states persisted from committed chunks, whose outputs are pushed to match target trajectories with multi-aspect losses. For verification, we propose an on-policy trained feature-space verifier predicting CDF-calibrated frame-wise relative RMSE against the target. It is trained on speculative rollouts as contexts anneal from random to inference-aligned mixtures, and gates proposals without VAE decoding. On the 14B Self-Forcing target, Draft Forcing achieves $1.63\times$ DiT and $1.57\times$ end-to-end speedups on VBench with minimal quality loss, and up to $1.93\times$ DiT ($1.82\times$ end-to-end) when combined with orthogonal KV compression. It generalizes to accelerate a streaming variant of MiniMax-H3, generating over $50\%$ draft frames with competitive quality.

papers.title: Bug Bounty Programs in the AI Era: How Does Platform Anti-Spam Friction Affect Vendor Profitability?
papers.abstract: Since 2023, bug bounty platforms have introduced participation rules, such as proof-of-concept mandates, against a flood of AI-generated low-quality submissions. The platforms set these rules, but vendors running programs on them bear the cost when a vulnerability goes unreported and gets exploited. We ask whether the rules benefit the vendors they are meant to protect. Adding to Gal-Or, Hydari, and Telang's 2024 model a vendor triage cost per report reviewed and a participation cost paid in effort by the researchers reporting vulnerabilities, we locate a threshold in an effective triage-burden parameter, which captures the vendor's processing burden per unit of aggregate search effort, with the rules lowering profit below it and raising it above. Because attackers never use the platform, the participation cost falls on researchers alone and fewer take part. Bug-finding coverage falls and breach damage rises, which costs the vendor, while its triage bill falls, which helps.

papers.title: Same Seed, Different Picture? Deciding Early at Low Resolution for Seed-Faithful Few-Step Flow Sampling
papers.abstract: Few-step samplers make large text-to-image flow models fast, but from the same noise they no longer generate the image of the standard 50-step sampler. Subjects, attributes and layout change, not just fine detail. We trace this loss of seed fidelity to the start of sampling. The coarse part of the initial noise decides coarse structure first, while the noise level is still above 0.9. Few-step samplers cross this range in their first steps, which account for 25-52% of their distance to the 50-step reference. Because this decision is coarse, a half-resolution run from the same coarse noise can make nearly the same decision at a third of the cost. We therefore propose Decide-then-Render (DtR), a training-free sampler that decides the composition in a few low-resolution steps, rebuilds the full-resolution state with the seed's own noise and renders the details. On 4 large models, DtR runs 11-25$\times$ faster than the reference sampler. At each speed-up, it is closer to the reference and rated higher by ImageReward than every compared sampler, including few-step schedules calibrated per budget and published multi-resolution samplers. On FLUX.1-dev, it remains the most faithful sampler down to about $8\times$, ahead of caching accelerators. A user study on this model found DtR's samples closer to the reference in 86% of pairwise trials. DtR transfers to a held-out model and to video, and distilled models can serve as its renderers. Project link: https://duanhuiran.github.io/DtR

papers.title: On the Sensitivity of Fermi-LAT Maximum Likelihood Stacking
papers.abstract: Stacking sub-threshold gamma-ray sources has become common practice for understanding high-energy emission processes at the population level. In this procedure, one co-adds log-likelihood ratios, called TS values (TS = 2ln$(L_1/L_0)$), for a source class of interest. It is best practice to compare the population of sub-threshold targets against a population of control field test sources (CFs) selected to represent the unmodeled \gray\ background. Determining the significance of a TS measurement stack has typically been difficult. In this work, we find the necessary cumulative TS value ($\Sigma$TS) of a sub-threshold population of $N$ targets to achieve a $5\sigma$ separation from a like-sized population of CFs. We find that the $\Delta (\Sigma$TS) needed to achieve a $5\sigma$ separation is $\sim 70$. In taking this measurement, we characterize the source distribution corresponding to the measured $\Sigma$TS for a significantly detected stack and even predict new individual source detections in larger stacks.

papers.title: A Multimode-Fiber Speckle Sensing Node with a Press-Robust Quantized Network for Liquid-Cooling Thermal Monitoring
papers.abstract: Liquid-cooled AI and HPC racks concentrate heat at cold plates and manifolds, below the granularity of facility sensors. We present a self-contained edge node that turns one multimode fiber into a distributed thermal-event sensor over nine pipe segments, with a 450 nm laser, a camera and a Zynq UltraScale+ device that captures, infers, displays and reports over MQTT. The speckle decorrelates within tens of seconds at constant temperature, and a press can change it as much as a 1 degree Celsius rise. The node averages each 20 s window and feeds two planes, the mean pattern and a 19-dimensional temporal-feature map, to a 61.6k-parameter int8 convolutional neural network (CNN) that treats presses as hard negatives and runs in the programmable logic at 565 microseconds per frame. On a 59-session, 70,148-window dataset, session-held-out validation gives a pooled AUC of 0.961 against 0.876 for decorrelation, no alarm during the hold or the 45 s rebound in 23 press trials against 6 and 16, and a mean per-fold step detection of 83.8% at 0.4 false alarms per hour.

papers.title: Long-Term Evolution of Hills-Captured Stars with TDE Disk Collisions: Links to Repeating Nuclear Transients
papers.abstract: Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) and repeating partial tidal disruption event (rpTDE) candidates are widely interpreted as being powered by a star on an hours-to-years orbit around a massive black hole (MBH). Every such orbiter model presupposes a star delivered onto an extraordinarily compact orbit without being destroyed, but it is unclear whether this is achievable. We follow the coupled orbital and stellar evolution of stars captured by the Hills mechanism, combining gas drag and per-collision mass loss from recurrent TDE disks with gravitational-wave (GW) orbital decay and stochastic two-body relaxation in a Monte Carlo model. Conventionally, the EMRI-formation criterion is based on comparing the timescales of GW decay and orbital angular momentum relaxation. We find that this criterion severely overestimates the EMRI rate: for relaxation timescales shorter than a Hubble time, most Hills-captured stars are tidally disrupted before GW emission can circularize the stellar orbit. Instead, TDE-disk drag plays a crucial role in the orbital evolution and can boost the fraction of stars reaching QPE orbits by an order of magnitude or more, assuming that the disk aspect ratio is relatively large $H/r \sim 0.1$. We also find that collisional ablation imposes a minimum orbital period that rises with MBH mass and precludes sub-day orbits for $M_{\rm BH} \gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$, unless GWs alone can drive orbital decay faster than orbital relaxation. This can explain the observed preference of short-period QPEs for low-mass MBHs. Most known rpTDEs lie below the Hills-capture period minimum and thus require additional orbital decay, which TDE-disk drag can plausibly supply. These results support the viability of the orbiter model; our predictions of the MBH mass and orbital period distributions can be used to further test this model.

papers.title: Model Doubt, Risk Aversion, and the Threshold for Trading: A Geometry of Pricing Measures
papers.abstract: How much model doubt can an investor bear before they stop trading? Our investor treats every model within a given Kullback-Leibler divergence of their reference model as plausible. In a finite one-period market, they hold no risky asset exactly when this doubt reaches the smallest divergence of a pricing measure from their model, for every smooth, strictly increasing, strictly concave utility; non-traded claims then have intervals of no-trade prices. Below this threshold, for log utility and in a given market, doubt acts exactly like higher constant relative risk aversion; their robust pricing measure moves from the log-utility measure toward the pricing measure at that smallest divergence. With a century of U.S. data, a log investor who doubts the Black-Scholes mean return over its 95% confidence interval acts like a fully trusting investor with relative risk aversion of about 1.8 instead of 1. Implied doubt turns a quote into a radius; the mean VIX implies doubt beyond the threshold, but whether significantly so depends on the reference model. By a known identity, real-world, pricing, and share (stock-numeraire) measures form a triangle whose Pythagorean defect is a log risk premium; one side is half the squared (ideal) VIX times the horizon. Since 1990, the U.S. defect averages about 10% per year, about 1 point of it entropy premium.

papers.title: Effective Hamiltonians and asymptotic band coupling
papers.abstract: By a multiple-scale asymptotic expansion, we derive effective macroscopic models for a large class of tight-binding Schr\"odinger equations with slow spatial variations. For wave packets that are spectrally localized to some point $(K;E) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}$ in the unperturbed tight-binding dispersion relation, our effective models produce long-time approximations of the tight-binding dynamics, accurate to any prescribed order in the asymptotic parameter. Our framework allows the point $(K;E)$ to be degenerate, meaning that multiple (but not necessarily all) energy bands of the tight-binding Hamiltonian can attain the value $E$ at the frequency $K$. We construct an effective Hamiltonian on the relevant degenerate subspace, which quantifies the coupling between the degenerate and other bands. Several applications and numerical simulations illustrate the theory.

papers.title: Exploring new speciation patterns: architecture of genetic similarity networks
papers.abstract: We use an individual based model to identify signatures of speciation modes in genetic similarity networks. These networks group individuals based on their genetic similarity, defined through Hamming distances between binary strings representing their genomes. The results of our extensive simulations demonstrate that sympatric and parapatric speciation modes are clearly distinguishable and measurable through specific network metrics. In particular, structural properties -- including clustering coefficient, mean degree, geodesic distance, and assortativity -- show significant differences in both stationary values and transient phases, giving rise to a novel framework for distinguishing between speciation modes.

papers.title: Topology-Preserving Hodge--Laplacian Diffusion on Manifolds with Boundary
papers.abstract:
Overview: We study deterministic and stochastic Hodge--Laplacian diffusion of differential forms on a fixed smooth compact Riemannian manifold with boundary. Absolute and relative boundary conditions select harmonic spaces representing ordinary and relative cohomology. We investigate the preservation properties of these diffusion processes, their compatible cellular discretizations, and their implications for reverse diffusion models. Numerical experiments on an annulus and a solid torus illustrate the theoretical results.
  Mathematical Significance: Using the de Rham complex and its constant-sheaf interpretation, we distinguish preservation of harmonic coordinates from preservation of a cohomology class. We establish that deterministic heat flow preserves the harmonic projection and exponentially damps its orthogonal complement. For additive stochastic forcing, we prove that pathwise harmonic preservation is equivalent to the absence of harmonic noise. Exact forcing preserves closedness and the initial cohomology class for closed initial data, whereas harmonic-projected forcing need not preserve closedness. We further show that compatible cellular discretizations retain these properties, with an algebraic extension to fixed weighted cellular sheaves. Separating invariant preservation from time-step stability and covariance accuracy, we derive bounds on leakage arising from approximate harmonic projectors.
  AI Relevance: We develop a finite-dimensional conditional score formulation that confines reverse diffusion to a prescribed harmonic component or, for closed data, a fixed cohomology class. This provides a mathematically grounded framework for incorporating topological constraints into diffusion-based generative AI models on manifolds.

papers.title: A scalar arterial input function does not uniquely determine the perfusion residue: Theory and phantom MRI
papers.abstract:
Purpose: To relate the residue function of tracer kinetic models to blood velocity and cross-sectional tracer distributions at the arterial inlet, and show that a cross-sectionally averaged arterial input function (AIF) does not uniquely determine the residue.
  Theory and Methods: For steady laminar flow without radial diffusion, the residue function referenced to the cross-sectionally averaged inlet AIF was analytically derived from the velocity and inlet tracer distributions. In a straight tube with parabolic flow, two nonnegative inlet profiles sharing one measured AIF were compared for gamma-variate and rectangular arterial spin labeling (ASL) inputs. A straight-tube phantom was imaged at 3 T during gadolinium bolus passage, with uniform fills as controls.
  Results: In the phantom, enhancement during bolus arrival was greater near the lumen center than near the wall at all 11 stations and for all three boluses, whereas uniform gadolinium fills showed no such pattern. In the tube model, the two profiles produced tissue curves differing by up to 23.3% of the uniform-inlet peak and 0.30 s in time to peak for the gamma-variate input, and by 33.3% for ASL labels shorter than the fastest transit time. Their residues differed in initial amplitude and normalized temporal shape.
  Conclusion: Identical AIFs can produce different tissue concentration curves, depending on the spatial distributions of inlet tracer concentration and arterial flow velocity. Consequently, the residue-AIF tracer kinetic models may not be consistent with fluid mechanics or interpreted as tissue flow.

papers.title: Multi-location Newsvendor: An Interpretable Inventory Policy
papers.abstract: We study a multilocation newsvendor problem in which inventory is chosen before demand is observed and surplus stock can subsequently be transshipped to locations with shortages. The objective is to minimize expected holding, backlog, and transportation costs over a metric network. Under uniform transportation costs, the optimality conditions balance local and aggregate demand coverage and reduce to a scalar search under mild regularity conditions. We use this structure to develop an interpretable iterative heuristic for general metrics. The heuristic calibrates effective transportation costs from lateral shipments under independent stocking and uses them to construct location-dependent pooling weights. These weights have a direct operational interpretation through the cost of serving demand at other locations. Under the stated assumptions, the heuristic recovers the exact uniform-metric solution. Numerical experiments on structured and random networks show costs close to the sampled optimum on average and substantial savings relative to independent stocking.

papers.title: The Curved Exponential Family of Cylindrical Distributions: m-Projection, Curvature and a Test of the von Mises-Fisher Component
papers.abstract: Cylindrical data pair a vector in R^d with a direction in S^(m-1). We study a family in which the direction is von Mises-Fisher and, given the direction, the vector is Gaussian with mean affine in it; this generalizes the Mardia-Sutton model. The family is a curved exponential family inside a regular family with Fisher-Bingham directions. We state necessary and sufficient conditions for the maximum-likelihood estimator to exist and be unique. The estimator is explicit except for one scalar root and is the m-projection (Kullback-Leibler projection) of the moment-matching member. Every moment it does not match is a function of one residual, the gap between the sample and fitted second moments of the direction. The squared length of this gap in the Fisher metric is the classical score test of von Mises-Fisher against Fisher-Bingham directions, due to Cox on the circle and extended by Mardia, Holmes and Kent. Specific here are this reading and the exact invariance of its law to the regression part. The exponential curvature lies only in the directions of the regression matrix. In closed form, the information lost on this matrix against the expected information is m-1 observations for uniform directions and (m+1)^2/(m-1) in the limit of high concentration; conditioning on the directions recovers it. Finite mixtures are identifiable. On buoy records the test rejects von Mises-Fisher directions, and generalized von Mises directions raise the held-out log-density by 0.45 nats per observation with one component.

papers.title: Interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control for partitioned multiphysics systems
papers.abstract: We develop an interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) formulation for multiphysics systems, within an optimization-based partitioned coupling framework. The finite-element interface-input operator is projected onto the reduced space and kept fixed during identification, while the unknown state-dependent local dynamics are learned from trajectory data. The common interface control is recomputed online by minimizing the mismatch between the reconstructed physical interface quantities. The formulation accommodates local subproblems governed by ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and differential--algebraic equations (DAEs). For a DAE subproblem, tangent projection identifies the state dynamics, whereas a residualized normal regression identifies the pressure balance and provides an algebraic pressure reconstruction. We further propose regularized quadratic correction DMDc to enrich the tangent dynamics and, for DAEs, the normal pressure balance through jointly fitted linear and compact quadratic operators. Feature normalization and block-dependent regularization control the enlarged regression while retaining the prescribed interface operators and identified DAE geometry. The proposed framework is evaluated on problems involving both ODE--ODE and DAE--ODE couplings. The numerical results demonstrate accurate predictions and stable long-time behavior.

papers.title: Suppressing Chaos Without Silencing Excitable Oscillators
papers.abstract: A negative Lyapunov exponent is not a sufficient goal for controlling an excitable oscillator. A gain can remove chaos by removing the excitation that the model is meant to keep. This manuscript studies that failure mode in three models: the forced FitzHugh--Nagumo neuron, the forced Aliev--Panfilov cardiac cell, and the autonomous Hindmarsh--Rose neuron. Chaos is measured by the largest state Lyapunov exponent. Excitation is measured by threshold crossings, by the excursion of the fast variable, and by the firing rate. Recovery damping, tracking of an unstable periodic orbit, Pyragas delayed feedback, and a change of the fast time scale are compared on the same chaotic regimes. In the forced models, large damping and large rate changes reach regularity by silencing the cell, while tracking and delayed feedback keep firing. In the autonomous model, recovery damping raises the firing rate several-fold instead. A classical matrix-measure bound links these outcomes to the channel through which the gain acts. A constant-metric contraction certificate coexists with substantial firing only under tracking, which subtracts a gain from the fast direction.

papers.title: Multi-Sensor Fusion for False-Alarm Reduction by Timed Electromechanical Corroboration
papers.abstract: A physician checks the clinical electrocardiogram against other observations. A wearable monitor has no physician. This paper shows that a mechanical sensor worn beside the electrocardiogram can take over that check, and that the right added sensors lower false alarms further. A beat is accepted only when a mechanical contraction follows at the delay learned for the wearer. Beat-shaped artifacts injected into resting and exercise recordings passed the electrocardiogram alone almost every time. A seismocardiogram or phonocardiogram as the second channel rejected most while keeping nearly all true beats, strongly at rest and partly during exercise. Shifting the mechanical signal in time removed the benefit. A detection criterion scores an added sensor by the part of its response that the sensors in place cannot predict. With four sensors, this score ranked the sets as their measured false-alarm rates did. With the two sensors it selected, 6.2 percent of the artifacts passed while 95 percent of true beats were kept, half the rate of the best single sensor. In integer arithmetic on a low-cost microcontroller, the detector made the same decisions as the software. These rates come from injected artifacts, not alarms in patients. Natural motion and clinical events remain untested.

papers.title: Principal Eigenvalues for Transport-Nonlocal Operators on Compact Manifolds: Ergodic Averages and Quotient Reduction
papers.abstract: We study principal eigenvalues for transport--nonlocal operators on connected compact Riemannian manifolds. Transport changes the natural spectral threshold from the pointwise maximum of the potential to a maximal invariant average. We establish a necessary and sufficient criterion based on a resolvent spectral radius and derive sufficient existence conditions for uniquely ergodic flows and, through quotient reduction, for flows arising from compact abelian Lie group actions. Examples on the two-dimensional torus show that, for weak nonlocal coupling, transport can create or suppress principal eigenvalues, while sphere rotations illustrate how the quotient criterion accommodates singular orbits.

papers.title: Physical co-presence of workers is linked with the evolution of interfirm networks
papers.abstract: Inter-firm transaction networks underpin modern economies and are critical for economic growth and resilience. Previous studies have largely explained the formation of inter-firm ties through spatial proximity. Yet people routinely move across space, creating opportunities for encounters that extend beyond geographical proximity. How these opportunities relate to inter-firm transaction relationships remains poorly understood. Here, we combine large-scale mobile phone mobility data with a multi-year panel of transactions among 196,317 firms in Tokyo to quantify encounter opportunities between workers and examine their association with inter-firm transaction ties. We find that pairs of areas with greater opportunities for encounters one another are more likely to have transaction links and new link formation between previously unconnected firms. This association is particularly pronounced in information- and service-intensive industries, reflecting the importance of encounter opportunities for exchange involving intangible knowledge and service. Indirect connections through shared neighbors in the encounter network are also positively associated with subsequent transaction formation across industries, but not within industries. These findings suggest that urban policies shaping connectivity formed through human mobility could play a significant role in the development and resilience of economic networks.

papers.title: Cylindrical Ricci flows and the PDE-ODI principle
papers.abstract:
We derive precise asymptotics for ancient asymptotically cylindrical Ricci flows. We establish a dichotomy in which the leading deviation from the cylinder is either linear or quadratic in the axial variables. In the linear case, we show that the flow is exponentially asymptotic to a Bryant soliton times a Euclidean factor. For $\kappa$-solutions, we further show that the flow is isometric to such a product, up to parabolic rescaling. In the quadratic case, we obtain higher-order asymptotics governed by a finite-dimensional invariant. We also establish propagation of cylindrical regions and uniqueness of cylindrical tangent flows.
  These results closely parallel those in our earlier work on cylindrical mean curvature flows. Both analyses use the same PDE-ODI principle and yield a unified treatment of cylindrical Ricci flow and mean curvature flow. The essential new ingredient in the Ricci flow setting is a coherent harmonic map heat flow gauge, which allows us to apply this principle without assuming a sign for the curvature. The local analytic tools developed here also form part of a program aimed at constructing Ricci flow with surgery in dimension 4.

papers.title: Beyond Omission: Measuring Critical-Information Fulfillment of Large Language Models in Bengali and English
papers.abstract: Evaluations of multilingual trustworthiness often ask whether a model leaves out information that a user needs. We examine whether that question is sufficient. Using 157 matched tasks written in English (EN), natural Bengali (BN) and Bengali-matrix Bengali-English code-switching (BN-CS), we scored 1,413 responses from three models (GPT-6.1 Sol, Qwen3.5-9B and Gemma 4 12B) against required information units (RIUs) fixed before any model was run. The scoring separates outright omission from content that is present but incorrect, insufficient or only partly met. The prespecified primary estimand, the domain-equal paired difference in critical omission rate (BN - EN), showed no detectable difference (+0.003, 95% CI -0.014 to +0.015), with omission near zero in every condition. The Bengali deficit appeared in fulfillment instead. Critical coverage was 0.050 lower in Bengali (95% CI 0.022 to 0.079) and strict complete-task success 0.093 lower (95% CI 0.055 to 0.131); both gaps came from the two open-weight models, and Sol showed none. Code-switching recovered part of the loss in RIU coverage (+0.028, 95% CI 0.012 to 0.045). On these data, an omission count alone would have shown no language gap. The automated judge passed prespecified agreement gates after a documented failed first attempt. A blind native-speaker rating of 60 study responses agreed with it on RIU scores (alpha 0.84) and critical RIUs (98% exact) but fell short on Bengali RIU agreement (alpha 0.77) and on the unsupported-content check (93% exact), and a blind check of its reason codes agreed on whether a critical unit was omitted for 79 of 81 units. Data, rubrics, responses, scores and code are released.

papers.title: The fundamental solution of the logarithmic Laplacian is a function in dimensions 1 and 2
papers.abstract: We show that the fundamental solution of the logarithmic Laplacian in dimensions $1$ and $2$ is a locally integrable function. Together with earlier work of the first author, this resolves a conjecture of Chen and V\'eron. The key step is that the inverse Fourier transform of the high-frequency part of $1/\log(|\xi|^2)$ behaves like $|x|^{-d}(\log(1/|x|))^{-2}$ near the origin.

papers.title: MAS-BIT: A Multi-Agent System for End-to-End BraIn-to-Text Decoding
papers.abstract: Speech brain-computer interfaces aim to restore communication by translating neural activity into text, yet end-to-end decoders have historically trailed cascaded systems in accuracy. We introduce a Multi-Agent System for BraIn-to-Text (MAS-BIT), the first multi-agent framework for end-to-end brain-to-text decoding from intracortical recordings. MAS-BIT coordinates three specialized agents: a neural agent that interprets continuous neural representations, a phonetic agent that decodes soft phoneme posteriors, and an arbitration agent that integrates their complementary evidence with direct access to neural representations to generate the final transcription. The expert agents communicate with the arbiter through token-embedding-based latent communication, constructing continuous messages as probability-weighted combinations of token embeddings. These messages retain alternative token hypotheses and provide a differentiable interface through which sentence-level supervision jointly trains the neural encoders and specialized agents across participants. MAS-BIT achieves state-of-the-art end-to-end decoding performance on the Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 benchmarks, with word error rates of 6.929% on '24 and 3.606% on the '25 public test set (3.892% on the private test set). These results surpass the published BIT cascade on the '25 public set and narrow the gap on '24, without ensembling independently trained models or using external language-model rescoring.

papers.title: An asymptotic form of Thomasse's directed path conjecture
papers.abstract: Thomass\'e conjectured that every oriented graph of minimum out-degree $d$ contains a directed path of length $2d$. We resolve this conjecture asymptotically by proving that every such graph contains a directed path of length at least $2d-O(d\log\log d/\log d)$.

papers.title: Aggregation Dispersion: An Information-Geometric Diagnostic of Oversmoothing in Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Message-passing neural networks (MPNNs) learn node representations by iteratively aggregating information from neighbors, but stacking too many layers causes all representations to converge, an effect known as oversmoothing. We propose a geometric perspective on this phenomenon. At each depth $k$, the propagation operator assigns to every node $v$ a walk distribution $p_v^{(k)}$, a probability distribution over source nodes. These walk distributions form a point cloud on the probability simplex, whose contraction to a single point characterizes complete mixing of the propagation operator, and thus oversmoothing. To measure this contraction, we use the Fisher-Rao metric, the unique Riemannian metric on the simplex invariant up to scale under sufficient statistics, whose scaled chordal distance under the square-root embedding $p \mapsto \sqrt{p}$ is the Hellinger distance. The resulting diagnostic, the aggregation dispersion $D_k$, is the variance of the embedded point cloud on the unit sphere. We prove that: (i) $D_k = 0$ if and only if the $k$-th step propagation matrix has rank one, a necessary and sufficient condition for complete operator mixing; (ii) $D_k$ is non-increasing with depth; (iii) the spectral gap of the propagation matrix controls the rate of this decay; and (iv) for contractive MPNNs, the aggregation dispersion upper-bounds the representation dispersion up to graph- and initialization-dependent constants. Across 14 model configurations and 11 datasets, $D_k$ attains the highest mean absolute Pearson correlation with test accuracy across depths among eight diagnostics ($|r| = 0.721$, using log-transformed diagnostic values), numerically comparable to the post-training effective rank ($|r| = 0.688$), while requiring no training.

papers.title: Reducing Authorship Attribution Risk in Student Texts Through Style-Conditioned Rewriting
papers.abstract: Building NLP applications for education is constrained by data scarcity due to student privacy concerns and data regulations. To address this, we propose a style-aware approach to rewriting student forum posts that retains analytical value while reducing identifiability. Our method isolates content, structure, and style as separate conditioning channels and aggregates over student-disjoint exemplar partitions within style clusters, extending Differentially Private In-context Learning (DP-ICL) with cluster-restricted retrieval. Across three educational NLP datasets, our approach achieves high style fidelity, preserves downstream task performance, and reduces authorship attribution risk relative to the original student-written texts, including against a dedicated authorship-attribution model.

papers.title: AutoRPG: Harnessing Systematic AI for Non-Intrusive Low-Latency Mobile RPG Combat
papers.abstract: Automated combat in mobile RPGs plays a critical role in game quality assurance, requiring real-time behavior control that closely resembles human gameplay. However, existing approaches fail to satisfy these requirements, either because they lack fine-grained behavioral control or because they incur high inference latency. To address these challenges, we incorporate user gameplay experience to design AutoRPG, a systematic AI framework for automating mobile RPG combat. At a high level, AutoRPG decomposes the combat process into two stages: a high-level strategic planning phase that formulates the overall combat strategy, followed by a systematic execution phase powered by a suite of carefully designed lightweight modules encompassing target tracking, character movement, dodge maneuvering, and abnormal-state handling. Experiments on three popular mobile RPGs, i.e., Genshin Impact, Wuthering Waves, and Arknights: Endfield, demonstrate that AutoRPG consistently outperforms four competitive baselines across both combat quality and generalization capability, while behaving the most similarly to human players among all evaluated agents.

papers.title: Distinct Distances under Well-behaved Norms
papers.abstract: We improve our understanding of the Erdos' distinct distances problem under non-Euclidean norms, in two ways: (i) For norms that are definable in an o-minimal structure and whose non-line bisectors have a finite intersection, we obtain a lower bound of \(\Omega(n^{5/6})\) for the minimum number of distinct distances. In particular, this improves the current best bound of \(\Omega(n^{4/5})\) for all \(\ell_{p}\) norms with non-integer \(p > 1\). (ii) We derive the stronger bound \(\Omega(n^{6/7-\epsilon})\) under all semi-algebraic smooth norms. Our proof technique is based on deriving properties of bisectors under various norms.

papers.title: Characterizing Frozen SSL Encoders and Backends for Cross-Domain Speech Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) encoders are the dominant front end for speech deepfake detection, and the prevailing recipe fine-tunes the full encoder on a small spoofing corpus, maximizing in-domain accuracy at the cost of known degradation under domain shift. Taking a recent cross-attention fusion of SSL and constant-Q cepstral features as a fixed reference recipe, we freeze its encoder and ask which encoder and which backend behave best across domains. We cross two frozen encoders, the massively multilingual XEUS and Wav2Vec2 XLSR-53, with two backends, multi-head factorized attentive (MHFA) pooling and AASIST, and evaluate on ASVspoof 2019 LA, ASVspoof 2021 LA and DF, In-the-Wild (ITW), and ASVspoof 5, training every system in one pipeline over three seeds. We report three findings. First, encoder and backend interact: MHFA suits the stronger encoder, while AASIST recovers more from and stabilizes the weaker one. Second, within this recipe, the frozen encoder produces large, repeatable differences. With MHFA, frozen XEUS lowers error relative to frozen XLSR-53 by 58-77% on LA21, DF21, and ASV5, and more modestly on ITW. This ordering persists in a matched-aggregation ablation, and a capacity-matched WavLM Large diagnostic shows that parameter count alone does not explain XLSR-53's weaker performance. Third, against a three-seed fine-tuned baseline, frozen XEUS updates under 0.4M parameters versus 316M, wins on ASVspoof 5 (in EER and min-DCF) and modestly on LA21, trails on DF21 and ITW, and shows lower seed variation on three of the four out-of-domain sets.

papers.title: Which Layer to Trust? Layer Selection in Frozen Speech Encoders for Singing-Voice Deepfake Detection under Signal Corruption
papers.abstract: Frozen self-supervised speech encoders have been frequently used for audio deepfake detection. However, the layers are usually chosen from a development set. We examine this choice for singing-voice deepfake detection on CtrSVDD. We train one detection head per layer, plus a learned layer mix, on frozen XEUS (3-4 seeds) and XLS-R (2 seeds). We test on clean audio and under noise, reverberation and lossy coding. On clean audio, the middle layers beat the last layer in both encoders and the learned mix does not beat the best single layer. The layer chosen on the development set is 2.3 (XEUS) and 4.1 (XLS-R) percentage points of EER worse than the best test layer. Under noise and coding, XEUS's best layers stay in the middle, while under reverberation its upper layers catch up, whereas XLS-R's best layer moves shallower. In an exploratory analysis, XEUS detects a commercial synthesis attack best with an earlier layer, especially under noise. The layer therefore cannot be chosen reliably on an in-domain development set and clean audio alone.

papers.title: Synapse: An HBM-Coordinated HBF Near-Memory Computing Architecture for Pipelined Agentic AI Execution
papers.abstract: During multi-agent video reasoning, model weights and per-agent key-value caches can exceed high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) adds capacity, but agents still wait for GPU execution. Synapse, an HBM-coordinated near-memory computing architecture, overlaps HBF attention and expert execution with GPU computation across agents. It also reduces dispatch delays and unnecessary refreshes. Across three models, Synapse achieves 48.92-66.60% lower end-to-end latency, up to $2.98\times$ throughput, and up to 64.48% lower modeled energy per output token than GPU execution with passive HBF. Wear simulations project 46% longer HBF lifetime than block-wide refresh at equal workload rates.

papers.title: LeadVLA: Learning Follower-Aware Route Execution for Robot Leading
papers.abstract: Robot leading requires executing a route while continuously adapting to a designated follower. Existing robot-leading systems often mediate follower understanding and physical route execution through explicit states, planners, or modular interfaces; directly learning this coupling through end-to-end trajectory prediction can instead entangle route execution with follower response. We introduce LeadVLA, a structured multimodal policy that preserves the route as an explicit Path reference while learning a Pace for route progress and a Residual for local follower- and scene-conditioned adaptation. To make this problem trainable and measurable, we develop LeadInfra, a configurable Unreal Engine-based closed-loop data-generation infrastructure from which we instantiate an approximately 4M-sample training corpus, and LeadBench, a standardized benchmark with 108 fully held-out closed-loop episodes. LeadVLA achieves the highest task success (39.6%) among evaluated robot policies on LeadBench while maintaining strong route fidelity and follower responsiveness, and transfers to unseen real-world environments without real-world policy fine-tuning. Project Page: https://louiszengCN.github.io/LeadVLA_PAGE/

papers.title: What Makes Good Data for Training Coding Agents? A Systematic Study on SWE-Gym
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) trains coding agents on software tasks whose hidden tests decide the reward, yet task collections check these tests only against the reference fix. We ask what makes a task good training data, focusing on the correctness of its reward labels. We audit SWE-Gym with two LLM families, and a suspected error counts only if execution reproduces it. We find that unsolved often means mislabelled: 74% of the tasks that a 9B base model never solves have a test that rejects correct fixes (a false negative), versus 20% of those it sometimes solves. We repair or remove such tasks, and the audited tasks that remain train better policies. At equal size and matched difficulty, models trained on them score 2.4 and 2.7 points higher on held-out tasks from SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Pro than models trained on the original tasks, whereas simply dropping the never-solved tasks shows no such gain. We further find that wrong patches that pass (false positives) make up about a quarter of all passing patches, and that new tests that catch a quarter of them do not change held-out scores detectably. A pass rate shows whether a task yields reward, not whether that reward is right, so the reward labels themselves must be checked. To this end, we release SWE-Gym-Verified with its 1,087 audited tasks, every verdict with its executed evidence, our training sets, and the full audit pipeline.

papers.title: AdvMTO: Multimodal and Temporal Adversarial Object Attacks via 2D Gaussian Splatting for BEV-Based 3D Object Detection
papers.abstract: Adversarial object attacks pose a threat to BEV-based 3D object detectors in autonomous driving. Existing attacks typically target a single modality, coordinate camera and LiDAR observations at the current timestamp, or model temporal persistence mainly in camera streams. Without a unified construction of current and historical observations, attacks can leave part of the detector's accumulated evidence unsuppressed, limiting their effectiveness. In this paper, we propose AdvMTO, a 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) framework for suppressing detection of persistent adversarial objects. Its oriented surfels encode appearance, geometry, and opacity in one object state, from which camera images and scanline LiDAR returns are generated. AdvMTO then constructs current and historical inputs through detector-native processing, regenerating LiDAR returns in each native source sweep for fusion detectors. We optimize bounded appearance perturbations for each detector, propagating gradients through historical BEV memory for temporal camera detectors. For fusion detectors, bounded geometry refinement along local normals further perturbs both sensing modalities. Experiments on nuScenes demonstrate effective suppression of traffic-cone detection across three BEV detectors. Temporal ablations further highlight the importance of detector-native history modeling for both attack construction and optimization.

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Local Smoothing in Noncommutative Spaces and Its Applications
papers.abstract:
We prove local smoothing for planar half-waves with coefficients in a semifinite tracial von Neumann algebra $M$. For $N\ge2$ and $P_N=\psi(|D|/N)$ with $\psi\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$, we obtain $\|e^{it|D|}P_N f\|_{L^4([1,2]\times\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}\le C_\psi\sqrt{\log(2+N)}\|f\|_{L^4(\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}$ uniformly in $M$ and its trace. Pairing the Dirichlet energies for $M$ and its opposite algebra cancels a determinant contribution that can have either sign. At $p=4$, summation over frequency annuli gives local smoothing for every Sobolev order $s>0$. Interpolating the annular estimates before summation gives spacetime $L^p$ bounds for $2\le p\le\infty$ and Sobolev orders $s>\sigma(p)=\max\{0,1/2-2/p\}$, as well as logarithmically weighted bounds at $s=\sigma(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$. The finite-$p$ bounds transfer to quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes, answering the question of Hong, Lai and Wang about the range $s>\sigma(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$ on generalized Moyal planes.
  For $1<p<\infty$ and complex $\alpha$ with $\operatorname{Re}\alpha>\max\{2/p-1,1/p-1/2,-1/p\}$, we prove maximal inequalities over all radii for generalized circular means on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes. For an action $\beta$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ on $M$ by normal trace-preserving $*$-automorphisms with norm-continuous $L^p$ orbits, the orbit mean $A_{t,\beta}^\alpha x$ converges bilaterally almost uniformly to $\pi x/\Gamma(1+\alpha)$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $x\in L^p(M)$. We also obtain estimates for truncated cone multipliers on three-dimensional Euclidean and quantum Euclidean spaces, and full-radius row and column bounds for Stein's square function on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes.

papers.title: The system initial mass function of Orion OB1b from probabilistic Gaia DR3 memberships
papers.abstract: [ABRIDGED] Context: Whether the initial mass function (IMF) varies with environment remains a central question in star formation. The multiple populations of Orion OB1b provide an ideal laboratory to test possible IMF variations. Aims: We aim to characterise the stellar populations of Orion OB1b by identifying its constituent groups, assigning membership probabilities to individual sources, and determining their IMFs. Methods: Using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, we identified stellar groups through clustering analysis and assigned membership probabilities with a probabilistic mixture model. Stellar masses were derived from extinction-corrected photometry using pre-main-sequence evolutionary models. Results: We identified eight kinematically distinct groups and a non-clustered population, deriving ages and IMFs spanning ${\sim}0.08$--$10\,M_\odot$ for six groups, all consistent with being gravitationally unbound. Each IMF was fitted with a lognormal distribution below $1M_\odot$ and a power law above. The high-mass regime is statistically indistinguishable across all groups, while four groups also exhibit consistent IMFs over the full mass range. The remaining two groups show differences that may reflect membership uncertainties rather than intrinsic IMF variations. The combined IMF is characterised by $m_c=0.27^{+0.02}_{-0.02},M_\odot$, $\sigma=0.45^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$, and $\Gamma=1.85^{+0.16}_{-0.14}$. The non-clustered population exhibits a broader and more uncertain IMF, although residual field contamination cannot be ruled out. Conclusions: Our results support previous evidence for the complex internal structure of OB1b. The IMF in OB1b appears broadly consistent across its kinematically distinct groups and compatible with other young populations in Orion.

authors.name: Juan Jose Downes
authors.institution: Universidad de la República de Uruguay

papers.title: Linear forms in logarithms of rational numbers: an ineffective measure with the best possible exponent
papers.abstract: Let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be positive rational numbers without a nontrivial multiplicative relation. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a constant $C>0$, not effective, such that $|h_0+h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n| \ge C\max(1,|h_0|,\dots,|h_n|)^{-n-\varepsilon}$ for all integers $h_0,\dots,h_n$, not all zero. The exponent $n$ is best possible. For $n=1$ this is the known fact that the irrationality exponent of $\log a$ is $2$; for $h_0=0$ it gives the exponent $n$ for the linear forms $h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n$. The proof is an induction on $n$, starting from $n=1$. The step from $n-1$ to $n$ logarithms uses an interpolation determinant on $\mathbb{G}_m^n\times\mathbb{G}_a$ at the multiples of a rational point, in the manner of arXiv:2610.28079; its geometric part, a curve inequality, is proved by a second induction, on the number of torus coordinates, with the two-torus inequality of arXiv:2610.28079 as the base. The method is the interpolation and determinant method of OpenAI's preprint on the irrationality exponent of $\pi$; the case $n=1$ was obtained earlier by Liu, Jiang and Zhang (arXiv:2610.10192). The theorem and its corollary are verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the sources are in the ancillary files, on top of the Lean supplement of arXiv:2610.28079. This paper follows the formal proof: every definition, constant and intermediate statement is given in the form in which it is formalized, with the name of the Lean declaration.

papers.title: Neural Schr\"{o}dinger Bridge via Yasue Action with Applications to Generative Modeling
papers.abstract: We propose a novel neural solver for inferring the continuous state evolution of the Schr\"{o}dinger bridge problem. The proposed solver builds on a saddle point formulation involving the Yasue action functional. This allows us to realize the continuous state evolution by learning the optimal velocity for an ordinary differential equation, as opposed to learning the optimal drift for a stochastic differential equation. The proposed solver only uses the source and the target samples, and not the source and target distributions per se, which makes it particularly suitable for high dimensional applications arising in generative modeling. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solver using several numerical experiments in low and high dimensions, using both real and synthetic datasets.

papers.title: Quadruples of integers whose elementary symmetric functions are perfect squares
papers.abstract: While Euler had considered the problem of finding three integers whose elementary symmetric functions are all squares, an extension of the problem to four integers has not been discussed in the mathematical literature till now. In this paper, we describe a method of generating infinitely many quadruples of positive integers whose elementary symmetric functions are all squares.

papers.title: When Should We Trust Medical Image Models? Evaluating Confidence Reliability under Cross-Dataset Shift
papers.abstract:
Deep learning models for chest X-ray analysis often achieve strong performance on benchmark datasets, but their reliability under cross-dataset deployment remains unclear. In clinical practice, models trained in one hospital system may be applied to data from another, where distributional and labeling differences can affect both prediction accuracy and model confidence.
  We conduct a controlled empirical study of model confidence under cross-dataset transfer. We train ResNet-50 and DenseNet-121 on CheXpert and evaluate them on MIMIC-CXR across five experimental settings, focusing on Pneumothorax and Pleural Effusion. We measure predictive performance using AUC and confidence reliability using Expected Calibration Error (ECE), Brier score, and average confidence on incorrect predictions, all reported with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. We further evaluate post-hoc temperature scaling fit on the source validation set and use Grad-CAM to examine the mechanism behind cross-domain performance differences.
  Cross-domain AUC drops 7-13 percentage points, and the best in-domain model is not the best cross-domain model. Source-domain temperature scaling produces marginal ECE changes but systematically increases confidence on incorrect predictions across all four model-pathology combinations. Grad-CAM reveals that DenseNet relies on a concentrated spatial prior that fails to transfer, while ResNet's more distributed attention generalizes better. These findings argue for cross-site validation and safety-specific calibration metrics in medical AI evaluation.

papers.title: Improving semantic equivalence in research-level math formalization
papers.abstract: Formalizing mathematics in Lean is never a word-for-word translation of a paper: a Lean formalization changes definitions, strengthens hypotheses, splits arguments, and adds lemmas the paper never mentions. It stands to reason that a model that is good at autoformalization must be a good predictor of how a natural language source must differ from its faithful Lean formalization. With that in mind, we collect 4{,}076 audited examples of such changes from 832 Lean projects that formalize research-level mathematics, and use them to ask a practical question: how well can a model \emph{write} Lean inside a real research-level project that may contain tens of thousands of lines of code, and does training on discrepancies between natural language sources and their faithful Lean formalizations help? Our training set consists of 3{,}431 tasks from 141 repositories, and the test set consists of 645 tasks from the remaining 27 repositories. Training on in-project Lean nearly doubles complete proofs ($11\% \to 20\%$) and raises the share of statements in gold agreement with the project's own formalization by nearly a third ($30\%$ to $39\%$). The gain comes from the pairs themselves: an adapter trained only to predict how the Lean will differ, or a model told the difference in advance, barely helps. Training on where formalizations depart from their sources is thus an effective way of improving semantic equivalence in research-level formalization.

papers.title: Does a Frontier Large Language Model Know What It Can Solve? A 100-Conjecture Calibration Study
papers.abstract: How does confidence correlate with actual performance in large language models, when attacking open research-level math problems? We address this question by studying the performance of ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Ultra on a set of 100 open conjectures in geometric analysis. By construction, the model first selected open problems in geometric analysis that it assessed that it had at least a 50\% chance of proving or disproving, and then assigned a probability of success to each question. 13 questions were then excluded after an audit, and the model was asked to resolve the remaining 87 problems. Its mean stated resolution probability was $0.617$, versus an observed rate of $0.103$ (Brier score $0.351$, ECE $0.513$), thereby demonstrating that the model was systematically over-confident in its self-assessment. However, the scores retained ranking signal (AUROC $0.714$). The model was highly overconfident in probability magnitude but did more often than not assign a high probability of success to the problems that it did resolve, than the problems that it did not. Hence, its probabilities were numerically mis-calibrated but directionally correct. All proofs have been formalized in Lean, thereby verifying correctness, and have been run through a semantic equivalence pipeline to ensure semantic equivalence between the formalized and informal statements. These are exploratory campaign outcomes, not fixed-budget success probabilities. The certificates prove formal statements; for a couple of questions, some geometric inputs are assumed in the lean proofs.

papers.title: Flag algebras and the exact largest probability of a linear inequality between iid random variables
papers.abstract: How large can $\mathbb P[X_1+X_2+X_3<2X_4]$ be when $X_1,\dots,X_4$ are independent with a common law $\mu$ on $[0,\infty)$? Previous work gave lower bounds through explicit constructions and upper bounds through exchangeability. The best lower bound, $0.4006953723\ldots$, was conjectured by \citet{BF} to be the exact value of the supremum. We prove this conjecture and formalize the proof in Lean~4. The improved upper bound uses the fact that independence gives more than exchangeability: two subsamples are conditionally independent given their shared points. As in Razborov's flag algebras, this yields a semidefinite program on the sign patterns of a few sample points. The new ingredient is to record also whether one sample point exceeds a fixed multiple of another, at ratios read off the extremal construction: with three such cutoffs, four sample points give an exact certificate, while additive comparisons alone leave a gap at seven points. We extend this study to the functions \[ S_2(c) = \sup_\mu \mathbb P_\mu[X_1+X_2<cX_3],\qquad S_3(c) = \sup_\mu \mathbb P_\mu[X_1+X_2+X_3<cX_4] \] and determine their exact values on several intervals of $c$. On other intervals, we provide lower and upper bounds that certify eighteen discontinuity points of $S_2$ and five of $S_3$, consistent with a nested staircase structure. The certified jumps are explained by new winning patterns becoming feasible in the lower-bound constructions. We answer Problem~5.3 of \cite{BF} by showing that no coefficient $c$ satisfies $S_3(c)=1/2$, and prove the analogous statement for $S_2$. The thresholds $\sup\{c:S_2(c)\le1/2\}$ and $\sup\{c:S_3(c)\le1/2\}$ are respectively the golden ratio $(1+\sqrt5)/2$ and the silver ratio $1+\sqrt2$.

authors.institution: Environmental and Occupational Health Sciences Institute

papers.title: Classifying detectability and time of emergence across different Stratospheric Aerosol Injection strategies
papers.abstract: Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) can be deployed using different injection strategies with the same global-mean cooling target and result in distinct regional climate responses. The ability to identify the deployed strategy from observed climate depends on how large the regional differences are relative to internal variability. In this study, we ask whether five feedback-controlled SAI strategies from the GAUSS ensemble (CESM2(WACCM6), SSP2-4.5), all targeting 1.0$^\circ$C above pre-industrial levels, can be distinguished from annual global and regional means of near-surface temperature, precipitation, and polar sea-ice fraction, and when this distinguishability emerges. We use multinomial logistic-regression classifiers with leave-one-member-out cross-validation and define the emergence year using a family-wise error rate threshold computed from a restricted-permutation null, combined with a calibrated persistence requirement. We find that the strategies become distinguishable in the mid-to-late 2040s, about 8-14 years after deployment, with a peak accuracy of 0.87 on a model using both global and regional features. Additionally, we find that no model trained on a single region-variable pair performs as well as the models using global and regional means, suggesting the discriminative signal is small and distributed across regions and variables.
