The equatorial and high-latitude injection strategies are the most distinguishable. The classifier is able to recognize the multi-latitude strategy more easily at lower temperature targets. Our results suggest that annual climate features can identify with confidence which coordinated injection strategy has been deployed roughly a decade or more after deployment.

papers.title: Deterministic Proper Positive-Only Learning Is Independent of ZFC
papers.abstract: Binary classification from positive-only samples is a variant of PAC learning in which the learner receives i.i.d. samples only from the positive region of an unknown target concept, but is evaluated on the full distribution. Improper learnability in this model has a textbook characterization, whereas proper learnability has remained open for decades. Recent work characterized it for learners with access to randomness, and showed that, unlike in PAC learning, some classes are properly learnable with randomness but not without it, leaving the deterministic case open. We show that this case cannot be resolved within the standard axioms of mathematics (ZFC): there is a class of VC dimension two whose deterministic proper learnability is independent of ZFC, even though a randomized learner provably learns it. Moreover, no dimension of finite character, a desirable property shared by most dimensions in learning theory, characterizes deterministic proper learnability. We also show that the size of the domain is decisive. In ZFC, deterministic proper learnability has a combinatorial characterization on every domain whose cardinality is below a certain threshold, including every countable domain. In contrast, this characterization fails on every domain of sufficiently large cardinality. Under the generalized continuum hypothesis, this threshold is sharp: it is the exact cardinality at which the characterization starts to fail. Finally, our proofs introduce new tools, based on the Erdos--Rado partition theorem, that may be of broader interest.

papers.title: Semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Flash on H5N1 One Health questions
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) has re-emerged as a One Health concern since 2024, and the public is increasingly consulting large-language-model (LLM) chatbots for health information during outbreaks. Before a chatbot's accuracy can be meaningfully assessed, its consistency must first be understood, so that any single response can be trusted as a fair representative of the model's behavior. We characterized the semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 (OpenAI) and Gemini 3 Flash (Google) on 15 H5N1 One Health questions sourced from social media discourse by adopting and extending a centroid-based evaluation framework. Each question was submitted 30 times and reformulated using five Chain-of-Thought (CoT) variants with 30 runs each, yielding 5,400 responses. Pairwise cosine similarity was computed on MPNet embeddings, with sensitivity analyses across three additional transformers. Statistical inference combined standard nonparametric tests (paired Wilcoxon and Friedman with Holm--Bonferroni correction) with inter-embedding agreement statistics (ICC(2,k) and Cronbach's $\alpha$) introduced here as a methodological addition. Both models produced high mean consistency (0.93--0.97, rescaled to {[}0, 1{]}). GPT-5 showed reproducibility significantly higher than repeatability (W = 3.0, p = 0.0003), whereas for Gemini 3 Flash the two metrics were statistically indistinguishable (W = 42.0, p = 0.33). Differential Diagnosis ranked among the top two CoT framings for consistency in both models. The tested chatbots behave as semantically stable sources on H5N1 One Health questions, and the developed consistency evaluation framework is portable to other domains.

papers.title: A Classification of Low Genus Modular Curves
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ be an open subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$ satisfying $\det(G)=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^{\times}$ and $-I\in G$. Associated to $G$, there is a modular curve $X_G$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ which parametrizes elliptic curves with $G$-level structure. We give a classification of modular curves with genus equal to a fixed nonnegative integer $g$. In particular, we show that all modular curves of genus $g$ lie in finitely many families of $\mathbb{Q}^{\mathrm{ab}}$-twists of modular curves. We also describe an algorithm for computing all families of modular curves of a fixed genus $g$ and use this to compute projective models for these modular curves. This algorithm has been fully implemented for $g \leq 12$.
  In an appendix with Yongyuan Huang and Rakvi, we describe two algorithms, one for computing rational functions on modular curves given as quotients of two modular forms of the same weight, and the other for computing models for the generic fibers of universal elliptic curves $\mathcal{E}_G$, where $G\subset \mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$ is an open subgroup satisfying $\det(G)=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^{\times}$ and $-I\notin G$.

papers.title: Reducing Order Sensitivity in Decision Models
papers.abstract: Decision models are emerging as fast components of larger AI systems. Yet recent decision models, such as Jev, process options sequentially, leading to different predictions based on their ordering. Across ten open- and closed-source decision models, we find that \emph{order-sensitivity} is pervasive, causing substantial accuracy degradation and unreliable decision-making. These effects become more pronounced as the number of options grows and can compound across multi-step decisions. To address this problem, we systematically compare eight methods for mitigating order sensitivity in terms of robustness, predictive accuracy, and inference efficiency. Among these methods, we find that \emph{tree attention} is a surprisingly effective and efficient method. It achieves order invariance by processing options as parallel branches of a shared context. When used during training, it matches the baseline's average accuracy. Applied to the baseline without retraining, it also eliminates order sensitivity with only a 1.1-point drop in accuracy. Our findings demonstrate that order invariance can be enforced directly in decision models with little or no loss in predictive accuracy.

papers.title: Can Search Agents Correct Their Own Errors? Evaluating Retrieval, Evidence Delivery, and Answer Completion
papers.abstract: A search agent can leave an earlier error unresolved by missing the right source, overlooking a relevant passage, or failing to revise and deliver the answer after receiving the evidence. We evaluate these possibilities on BrowseComp-Plus by replaying each model's own wrong closed-book answer in conversation and intervening on what evidence reaches the model. In a supplied-evidence study spanning four open-weight checkpoints, 709 questions and 26,665 test conditions, a confident assistant prior reduced Nemotron's paired accuracy by 16.1 percentage points despite answer-bearing passages in context. When the user insisted on the prior, accuracy fell by 32.9 points for Nemotron and 12.6 for gpt-oss. Among gpt-oss responses that lost correctness in that condition, abstention was more common than repeating the prior. In separate search interventions with Qwen3.5 and Nemotron, placing a gold page first often left the decisive source unopened. Delivering a decisive passage in context improved accuracy over neutral delivery by 51.0 percentage points for Qwen3.5 and 22.4 for Nemotron. Even with the passage in context, Nemotron exhausted its search budget and returned no answer in 19 of 51 episodes. The tests distinguish failures of retrieval, passage delivery, correction and answer completion, giving system builders a way to test which changes resolve a recurring error.

papers.title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents
papers.abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) built on vision-language models are increasingly entrusted with long-horizon tasks in live desktop, web, and mobile environments, where the screen keeps changing on its own. However, current CUAs lack real-time situational awareness: they perceive the environment through discrete snapshots, and the substantial inference latency of VLMs, compounded by highly dynamic interfaces, opens a perception-action gap in which the observed state frequently becomes stale before the corresponding action is executed. To bridge this gap, we present NightWatch, a plug-and-play framework that endows any CUA with continuous, temporally grounded perception without changing the agent's model, prompt, or action space. NightWatch couples the VLM agent with NightWatch-0.8B, a lightweight System-1 model that performs streaming monitoring of the interface state and keeps the agent synchronized with the evolving environment at low computational cost and latency, thereby grounding each decision in the current state rather than an outdated snapshot and reducing both stale actions and idle waiting while preserving task success. Experiments on desktop and dynamic web environments (OSWorld-Verified and DynaCU-Bench) show that NightWatch, driven by a watcher of only 0.8B parameters, reduces non-reasoning wall-clock time by 33% and wasted time by 53% on OSWorld while keeping task success on par, raises success on DynaCU-Bench from 39.5% to 44.2% with the large VLM agent, and is more efficient than passive-watching baselines such as AOI and PUSV under the same screenshot-only input, as well as a System-1 decision model more than $30\times$ its size. Overall, NightWatch demonstrates that the timing of perception is as critical as its content, marking a step toward agents that maintain continuous awareness of their environment rather than perceiving it turn by turn.

authors.name: Long-Kai Huang
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

authors.name: Haiyan Yin
authors.institution: Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: A Camera-Based Single-Volume, Monolithic Compton Camera
papers.abstract: A Compton camera measures two events in a detector from individual gamma-rays to reconstruct the radiation source. Conventional scintillator-based Compton cameras consist of two separate scintillator volumes or a single segmented scintillator, resulting in drawbacks regarding detector bulkiness and efficiency. Their scintillator readout techniques struggle to resolve two nearby events in one monolithic scintillator. Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) cameras have recently been proposed for measuring scintillation events in various configurations. SPAD array sensors enable high-resolution photon-counting acquisition at high rates that is easily scalable to millions of pixels. Prior work has explored different optics and measurement arrangements as well as demonstrated measurement of single interaction locations. In this work, we extend these capabilities to demonstrate a practical radiation imaging device in the form of a Compton camera consisting of a SPAD camera and one compact, monolithic scintillator. Our Compton camera prototype successfully reconstructs a gamma-ray source over multiple locations that span a 4$\pi$ steradian field of view. Our approach is able to resolve two simultaneous events in one monolithic scintillator and enables Compton camera devices with compact, monolithic scintillator volumes for enhanced portability.

authors.name: Devanshi Jain
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: Motoric signatures to detect original authorship versus cognitive effort in instructed motor responses of an emerging speaker with ASD
papers.abstract: There is at present no objective, agnostic method to track levels of message authorship and agency in non-speakers who rely on assisted typing to communicate. Part of the problem is that nuances in spontaneous gestural movements of the typer transpire largely beneath awareness of both the typer and the communication-regulation-partner. Such spontaneous movements co-occur with the intentional ones producing the typed messages but are currently not considered part of the communication system. We introduce an assay that probes various levels of cognitive loads in an ecologically valid environment. Then, in collaboration with an emerging speaker-typer and his communication-regulation-partner, we empirically estimate motoric stochastic signatures during both independent and assisted typing. Under varying levels of cognitive loads, the assay and biometrics distinguish motoric patterns in spontaneous typing of phrases in response to open-ended questions from those in instructed typing of the same phrase. The non-dominant bodily motions, co-occurring with the dominant (typing) side reveal not only levels of cognitive mental effort and agency of the typer but also levels of creative thoughts through motoric preambles present only in open-ended mode. This level of semantic authorship is detectable in both the geodesic paths along the manifold representing the Gamma stochastic parameters of the motions fluctuations and those of the physical 3D spatial trajectories. The head and facial micro-motions capture these non-dominant-body nuances, offering a personalized motoric metric of cognitive effort, agency, authorship and a comprehensive suite of assays to open new research avenues for assisted typing with haptic support.

authors.name: Elizabeth B. Torres
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: On Cohen Generic Sets in Supercompact Prikry Extensions
papers.abstract: Let $\kappa$ be $\lambda$-supercompact for a regular $\lambda>\kappa$. We show that if $\lambda$ is not the successor of a singular of cofinality below $\kappa$, $\diamondsuit(S^\lambda_{\geq\kappa})$ implies that every ${<}\kappa$-strategically closed forcing of size at most $\lambda$ is a projection of the $\lambda$-supercompact Prikry forcing. We show that the situation for successors of singulars of small cofinality is independent. Finally, we provide more limitations about the class of $\kappa$-distributive projections of the $\lambda$-supercompact Prikry forcing and give examples of $\kappa$-distributive forcings of size $\lambda$ which cannot be projections of this forcing.

authors.name: Tom Benhamou
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: Trace-class perturbations of Voiculescu's free semicircular families
papers.abstract:
Let $\{s_j\}_{j\in\Lambda}$ be the standard free semicircular family on the full Fock space $\mathcal H=\mathcal F(\ell^2(\Lambda))$, where $|\Lambda|\geqslant2$.
  For any family $\{K_j\}_{j\in\Lambda}$ of self-adjoint trace-class operators with $\gamma=\sum_{j\in\Lambda}\|K_j\|_1<\infty$, we prove that the type $\mathrm{II}_1$ summand $\mathcal P$ of the von Neumann algebra $W^*(\{s_j+K_j\colon j\in\Lambda\})$ is isomorphic to the free group factor $\mathcal L(\mathbb F_\Lambda)$.
  As an application, we show that the set of irreducible operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is not dense in the trace-class norm.
  For each fixed $\gamma>0$, the possible values of the Murray--von Neumann dimension $\dim_{\mathcal P}(z_{\mathcal P}\mathcal H)$ form the interval $[1,1+\gamma)$, where $z_{\mathcal P}$ is the identity of $\mathcal P$.

authors.name: Tianze Wang
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: Nontrivial Expanding K\"ahler--Ricci Solitons and Automorphism Groups of Stein Domains
papers.abstract: We study complete nontrivial expanding K\"ahler--Ricci solitons with complete real holomorphic soliton fields. Let $\Omega$ be a relatively compact domain in a complex surface such that a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$ admits a holomorphic immersion into Euclidean space. We prove that such a soliton exists if and only if $\Omega$ is Stein and the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega)$ is noncompact. On such a Stein domain, a complete real holomorphic vector field is the soliton field of a complete nontrivial expander if and only if its flow has noncompact closure in $\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega)$. In higher dimensions, we establish existence criteria using the adjoint representation of automorphism groups, boundary geometry, and homogeneous positive closed $(1,1)$-currents. We give sufficient conditions for the holomorphic $\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$-action on the universal globalization of a proper holomorphic $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$-action on a Stein $n$-manifold to be free and proper. Applications include bounded convex and homogeneous domains, domains satisfying weak Kobayashi visibility, and certain finite-type domains.

authors.name: Soumya Ganguly
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: Probabilistic foreground diagnostics from dispersion measure excess in individual fast radio bursts
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide a unique probe of diffuse baryons through their dispersion measure (DM), but interpreting a large DM for an individual burst is limited by the uncertain contribution from its host galaxy, which is hard to directly observed. We address this gap with a source-level diagnostic framework that treats $\mathrm{DM_{host}}$ as a latent variable drawn from a shared lognormal population, thereby marginalizing over the uncertain host contribution. Applying an expectation--maximization (EM) inference scheme to 92 localized FRBs, we jointly estimate the host-DM population and obtain a model-conditioned host-DM distribution for each burst. We propagate these distributions into an excess cosmological DM for each sightline, quantifying both its uncertainty and the probability that a positive excess remains after accounting for the host contribution. FRBs previously reported to show evidence for foreground or intervening contributions preferentially exhibit high probabilities of retaining such an excess, indicating that this source-level probability can provide a useful statistic for prioritizing foreground follow-up observations. Using this diagnostic, we identify 18 additional localized FRBs as high-priority candidates for follow-up searches for possible intervening galaxies, groups, clusters, or large-scale structure.

papers.title: Two Actions from One State: Fork Futures Teach JEPA World Models to Compare
papers.abstract: JEPA world models are trained to predict logged transitions but used to compare counterfactual actions from one state. The logged behavior data show one action per state, and under a local linear approximation we prove the action response is unidentified along any direction the policy never varies within a state. We therefore supplement behavior data with measured outcomes of alternative actions from the same state. Our fork futures execute two actions from one restored state, and their outcome difference cancels the state term, identifying the action response on the sampled span. The resulting model, Fork-JEPA, matches predicted to measured differences, anchors the logged successor with behavior prediction, and adds a lookback head that keeps the predecessor recoverable, all at training time, leaving planning unchanged. On three visual control tasks, behavior-only training leaves the predicted action effect no better than a constant guess. Fork-JEPA makes it readable and raises planning success by up to 14\% over LeWM, its base model. Where the action response changes across hidden zones, it nearly doubles cross-zone success, and 1,024 fork pairs beat 1.2M extra behavior steps. Our project is available at https://fork-jepa.github.io/.

authors.name: Dongfang Liu
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of North Sichuan Medical College

papers.title: Knowing What You Carry: Scalable Physics-Anchored World Models for Robotic Planning with Liquid Payloads
papers.abstract: Payload-carrying robots, such as delivery robots and autonomous trucks, must choose motions that keep them and their payload safe, so their planners predict the outcome of each candidate motion. Modern planners compare thousands of candidates per step on a GPU, using world models such as batched simulators or learned predictors. Most of them assume a rigid payload, but a liquid payload keeps moving after a maneuver, and its state is rarely measured. Near a safety limit, small prediction errors can make an unsafe plan look safe. Coupled fluid simulations are accurate but too costly for every candidate, while low-order slosh models are cheap but accurate only away from resonance. We study this trade-off on a ground vehicle with a partly filled tank near its rollover limit. First, we build PLiMB (Parallel Liquid-MultiBody), a GPU-parallel slosh simulator that, to our knowledge, couples FLIP liquid two-way with many multibody vehicles for the first time. It provides training data and a high-fidelity reference. Second, we propose a scalable physics-anchored world model that combines a modal-slosh and roll prior, an estimate of the hidden liquid state from the vehicle's own motion history (no sensor in the tank), and a learned correction. Without simulating the fluid, it scores thousands of candidate plans in one batched pass within a 20 Hz control tick on one GPU. We judge each world model by the plans it leads a planner to choose. Near the rollover limit, planners that treat the liquid as a rigid payload or use published low-order slosh models repeatedly pick unsafe plans when a safe one exists. Ours never does in our standard tank and makes about half as many in a wide tank whose sloshing mode lies in the maneuver band. There, the liquid state left by earlier driving can change the best plan, and reading it from the vehicle's history halves our model's near-limit prediction error.

authors.name: Yicheng Zhu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Coupled Dynamical System for Sparsemax Attention
papers.abstract: We present a family of coupled dynamical systems that compute sparsemax attention. Each system fuses query-key similarity and normalization into a single physical relaxation. Specifically, we cast sparsemax attention as a constrained energy minimization problem and derive a pair of coupled differential equations: one drives the energy minimization and the other enforces the constraint. At equilibrium, the system state gives exactly the sparsemax attention probabilities. We realize this formulation with continuous Ising spins and with Kuramoto oscillators. These relaxations run natively on emerging non-von Neumann platforms such as Ising machines, which have demonstrated orders-of-magnitude higher energy efficiency than digital processors, yet have so far been used mostly for unconstrained quadratic combinatorial optimization. Because analog hardware has limited precision and is noisy, we simulate both systems under these non-idealities, and inference quality degrades gracefully. Our formulation extends these emerging computing substrates from combinatorial optimization to attention, opening a path toward a new class of physical accelerators for transformer inference.

papers.title: Independent and end-faithful spanning trees in infinite graphs
papers.abstract: Spanning trees rooted at the same vertex are independent if, for each vertex other than the root, the paths from the root to that vertex are pairwise distinct and internally vertex-disjoint. Zehavi and Itai conjectured that, for every positive integer $k$, every finite $k$-connected graph has $k$ independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. We show that every $2$-connected graph, finite or infinite, has two independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. For locally finite $2$-connected graphs, both trees can be chosen end-faithful. We also prove that every locally finite $3$-connected chordal graph has three independent end-faithful spanning trees. Counterexamples show that local finiteness is essential for the version with independent end-faithful spanning trees. We further show that every $3$-connected graph with a universal vertex or a finite vertex cover has three independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex.

papers.title: AIRPiano: Piano Score Following with Tabletop Hand Gestures
papers.abstract: AIRPiano aims to bring sound to the common practice of rehearsing piano music on a tabletop. Guided by a known score, users make piano-like finger movements on a flat surface without reproducing absolute keyboard positions. The score supplies pitches, while hand motion determines which score events to play and when. We formulate this interaction as online alignment between tabletop hand motion and symbolic score events. To address the ambiguity of tabletop motion, its differences from piano-playing motion, and the scarcity of aligned motion-score data, we develop motion and score representations, build a data processing pipeline, and train a Transformer with supervised attention on existing piano performance recordings. We further design a streaming inference framework that combines local alignment predictions with sequence tracking for real-time interaction. We construct two evaluation sets, VSF-Piano and VSF-Tabletop, to assess alignment on piano and tabletop performances, respectively. After a post-hoc global timing adjustment, AIRPiano achieves a mean chord alignment rate of 74% within a 133 ms tolerance on the paired subset of VSF-Tabletop, compared with 79% on VSF-Piano.

papers.title: AutoSECO: Automated Skill Evolution for Cross-Problem Combinatorial Optimization with General-Purpose LLM Agents
papers.abstract: General-purpose large language model (LLM) agents can develop complete solvers for combinatorial optimization problems. Their specialization, however, often relies on workflows engineered for individual problems, limiting the reuse of development expertise. We propose AutoSECO, an automated skill evolution method that learns reusable solver-development guidance from experience. The challenge is that external evaluation measures the completed solver, while the skill guides decisions during development. AutoSECO connects this feedback to guidance deficiencies by tracing performance shortfalls through solver code and recorded development decisions. Revisions are expressed as general instructions and retained only if a fresh solver developed under the revised skill achieves a lower mean evaluation gap. Evolved solely on the traveling salesperson problem (TSP), the skill guides fresh agents in developing solvers for capacitated vehicle routing, job-shop scheduling, and three-dimensional bin packing without further skill evolution. On TSP, the final mean benchmark gap is 0.52\%, compared with 0.98\% for the skill-evolution baseline SkillOpt. Across all four problems, the evolved skill achieves better aggregate results than no skill guidance, the initial skill, and SkillOpt. The same frozen skill also supports solver development under alternative model--harness configurations. These findings suggest that solver-development experience can be retained as reusable expertise for general-purpose LLM agents.

authors.name: Cong Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Contrastive Decoding for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Contrastive decoding (CD) mitigates object hallucination in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by contrasting token distributions under different conditions to adjust token scores. However, existing generative and discriminative benchmarks primarily measure final task scores, which can be confounded by candidate filtering, changes in generation trajectories, and response biases, making it difficult to isolate the effects of the underlying contrastive adjustments. To address these limitations while complementing existing evaluations, we introduce CONCOR (Contrastive Correction Evaluation), a controlled benchmark that directly evaluates the competition between ground-truth and different types of hallucinated candidates using the Contrastive Grounding Margin (CGM). CGM also enables analysis of directional consistency, composition, and reliability of contrastive corrections. Our evaluation reveals that existing CD methods exhibit distinct correction behaviors: some consistently favor ground-truth candidates, whereas others produce strong corrections but also introduce more errors. Crucially, these differences help explain their contrasting responses to increased contrast strength, which improves some methods while degrading others. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating the contrastive correction itself, rather than relying solely on final-output performance, and CONCOR provides a controlled and interpretable framework for understanding and improving CD methods for hallucination mitigation.

authors.name: Ting Chen
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Selection-aware inference of supernova kicks
papers.abstract: Observed compact objects (isolated or in binaries) used to infer natal kicks are selected by class membership, which depends on disruption, subsequent evolution, and discovery. Ignoring this selection can bias the inferred kicks. To demonstrate this bias in a comprehensive inference framework, we construct a differentiable model for key components of binary evolution, including correlated remnant-mass and kick prescriptions as well as survival probabilities. As initial conditions prior to the first SN, we use a fiducial COSMIC analysis. Using conventional statistical methods to assess bias due to omitted selection factors in a likelihood, we demonstrate this bias concretely. Reliable natal inference requires a forward prediction for both the observed properties and the probability of observing them. Our framework provides a novel method to enable robust neutron star population inference combining heterogeneous observations of multiple NS-pertinent observations.

papers.title: Stochastic climate emulation at reduced cost with ACE2.5-ERA5
papers.abstract: We introduce ACE2.5-ERA5 (Ai2 Climate Emulator of ERA5, version 2.5), a stochastic autoregressive weather-climate AI model that produces calibrated weather ensembles with realistic small-scale structure on timescales from days to centuries. Its deterministic predecessor, ACE2-ERA5, retains 36% of its ERA5 target's precipitation spectral power at total wavenumbers 100--179; ACE2.5-ERA5 retains 86%. In weather forecasts its ensemble spread matches its error to within 4% from day 3. Time-mean climate is on par with or better than ACE2-ERA5, the precipitation response to ENSO is improved, and the model is stable over 1000 years. Interannual variability of global mean surface temperature is shown not to be calibrated in either ACE2.5-ERA5 or its predecessor. ACE2.5-ERA5 differs from ACE2-ERA5 in three ways. Noise-conditioned layer normalization, trained with a combined CRPS and spectral energy score loss in place of mean squared error, makes it stochastic. Spectral bottlenecking with grouped convolutions cuts the Spherical Fourier Neural Operator's spectral filter parameters by more than two orders of magnitude and leaves a model a tenth the size of ACE2-ERA5. Its time step is daily rather than 6-hourly. ACE2.5-ERA5 has 3.2 times the inference throughput of ACE2-ERA5. A 6-hourly variant has weather prediction skill similar to ACE2-ERA5. A 4-degree variant reaches comparable climate skill at an order of magnitude lower training cost, enabling rapid iteration during development. We release 1-degree daily, 4-degree daily and 1-degree 6-hourly checkpoints.

papers.title: A symplectic Hilbert hotel
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth global symplectomorphism of an infinite dimensional separable Hilbert space mapping a ball of large radius to a subset of a cylinder of small radius. This symplectomorphism and its inverse map bounded sets to bounded sets. This example shows that Gromov's non-squeezing theorem does not generalize to infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces without further assumptions.

papers.title: From raw magnetoresistance to reliable cyclotron masses: A practical guide to processing quantum oscillation data
papers.abstract: Quantum oscillations are an essential probe of the Fermi surface in conductors, and cyclotron masses extracted using the Lifshitz-Kosevich (LK) formula are used to evaluate correlation strength and the assignment of topological states. These masses depend on choices in signal processing, including the field window, method of background subtraction, and spectral window applied before the Fourier transform. These choices are often guided by visual inspection, yet they can alter spectral features and bias the extracted masses. We show that (1) representing a finite field interval by a single effective field can underestimate the cyclotron mass; (2) polynomial background subtraction can attenuate and shift low-frequency peaks; and (3) spectral tapering can reduce mass bias from leakage between neighboring peaks, at the cost of frequency resolution. We demonstrate these effects using numerical calculations and Shubnikov-de Haas experiments on the rare-earth tritellurides RTe3 (R = Pr, Nd, Gd, Tb) with a dense low-frequency spectrum in the charge ordered state. The examples reveal masses shifting by tens of percent with the field window, apparent peak shifts produced only by the background fit, and a reported departure from LK behavior that resolves into two neighboring frequencies.

papers.title: Intrinsic volume fraction can decouple from hydrodynamic size in p(NIPAm-co-AA) microgels
papers.abstract: Quantifying the packing fraction of microgels is key to understanding their rheology and transport properties. Often, packing fractions are extrapolated from the hydrodynamic size and intrinsic volume fraction under the assumption that particle size and polymer volume change are proportional. Here, we test this assumption for p(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-acrylic acid) [p(NIPAm-co-AA)] microgels of two crosslinker concentrations (1 wt\% and 7 wt\% methylenebisacrylamide) using capillary viscometry and light scattering (static and dynamic) above and below the pKa of acrylic acid (AA). At pH 8, where AA is fully ionized, the microgels do not undergo a pronounced volume phase transition because electrostatic repulsion hinders thermal collapse, and both measures of hydrodynamic volume are equal. At pH 4, however, p(NIPAm-co-AA) microgels are weakly charged and exhibit a volume phase transition near the lower critical solution temperature of pNIPAm; the magnitude of the size change is greater for the less-crosslinked microgel. Above the volume phase transition temperature, the volume change from hydrodynamic radius decouples from that from viscosity. The ratio of the radius of gyration and hydrodynamic radius R_g/R_h of p(NIPAm-co-AA) microgels at high temperature exceeds the value theoretically predicted for homogeneous spheres and the deviation increases with the extent of crosslinking, suggesting that a non-uniform internal distribution of polymer gives rise to the anomalous decoupling at high temperatures. Our results indicate that care must be taken in extrapolating packing fractions for multi-responsive copolymer microgels, and suggest that copolymer composition and crosslink density may be used to tune bulk properties such as rheology through the internal microstructure.

papers.title: On a simple family of Ricci-flows of O(3)-hypersurfaces: Counterexamples to the theorem on the preservation of positive definite Ricci curvature everywhere
papers.abstract: This note provides a concise derivation of the equation of Ricci \'aows on O(n)-rotational hypersurfaces in En+1 which consists of a pair of parabolic equations (cf. Lemma 2 of {\ss}4) via simple applications of classical theorems of rotational surfaces in E3, governing the Ricci-evolution of their generating plane curves. Furthermore, the second equation can be transformed to that of the evolution equation of their "curvature pro\"Oles" (cf. Lemmas 3 and 3\'iof {\ss}4). In {\ss}5, we consider a speci\"Oc family of initial generating curves of "curvature pro\"Oles" that are only tiny modi\"Ocations of the constant function K= 1 R ;R 1, in a very small vicinity of the symmetric middle point as indicated in Fig. 2. Note that the short-time unique existence of analytic solutions of such a simple system of parabolic equations follows simply via Nash-Moser Theory. The simple estimate of {\ss}5 shows the curvature k1( t(0)) is already becoming negative at a very short time (cf. {\ss}5.3).

papers.title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation
papers.abstract: Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages. Onboard computing resources rarely allow the solution of a cold-started, long-duration nonconvex optimal control problem, especially in dynamically challenging regions such as the cislunar to translunar corridor of the Earth-Moon system. This paper develops data augmentation and training techniques that enable a neural network to predict accurate initial costates of the indirect method. A recovery trajectory is then built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm. Training data are produced by the backward generation of optimal examples method, extending prior approaches to the circular restricted three-body problem. A novel anchor trajectory approach is developed to cover the relevant state space, and costate rescaling and a Hamiltonian loss term are used to improve learning. The method is demonstrated on Earth-Moon transfers from a high Earth orbit to halo orbits about L1 and L2. Under navigation errors and thruster outages, a spacecraft reaches the target orbit more often with the proposed method than with nominal-trajectory tracking or fully numerical reoptimization. Onboard computation is reduced by more than an order of magnitude compared with reoptimization.

papers.title: Rough structure. I. Exclusion among series-parallel graphs
papers.abstract: This is the first in a series of papers about rough structure theorems: graph properties that are implied by the exclusion of some graph as a minor, and imply the exclusion of some larger graph of the same type. Here we look at the structure of the series-parallel graphs that do not contain a given series-parallel graph as a minor. We prove that for every series-parallel graph $H$, there exists $m$ such that every simple two-connected series-parallel graph that does not contain $H$ as a minor admits a tree-decomposition of height at most $m$, where each "torso" is either an outerplanar graph or a planar dual of one. We prove similar theorems about the series-parallel graphs that exclude an outerplanar graph, the series-parallel graphs that exclude a dual of an outerplanar graph, the graphs of tree-width three that exclude a series-parallel graph, and the general graphs that exclude a fan.

papers.title: The Temporal Residual: Fast and Effective Retrofitting of Latent Feedback into Pretrained Language Models
papers.abstract: A transformer language model computes a deep hidden state for every token but uses it only to sample that token. Existing latent-feedback designs, which feed hidden states back across tokens, are mostly built in during pretraining and gain little when added to a pretrained model. We introduce the temporal residual, a second residual stream that every sublayer reads and writes and that is carried from each token to the next. It adds 2,752 parameters to a 4.2B-parameter model and starts exactly at the pretrained network. Retrofitted onto Qwen3.5-4B-Base with 5B tokens of training, it beats a standard model trained on the same data by 7, 13 and 5 points on AIME 2024, AIME 2025 and AMC 2023, writes shorter solutions, and stays ahead at matched training compute. The separate stream matters: prior designs that feed state into the existing stream recover at most 40% of the gain when retrofitted. Validation loss can mislead: the recipe with the lowest loss gains nothing at decoding. Trained with filler tokens in place of reasoning, the model reasons in its hidden state: its GSM8K accuracy with no visible reasoning rises from 21% to 40%, and falls back when the carried state is zeroed.

papers.title: Solids activated by multi-body nonreciprocity
papers.abstract: Field-mediated forces between particles can be both nonreciprocal and irreducibly multi-body, giving rise to emergent activity in systems of individually passive particles. While prior work extensively studied how multi-body nonreciprocity can activate few-body systems, fuel intermittency, and drive liquid-like behavior, the effect on the solid state of large particle ensembles is less explored. Here we use two-dimensional, close-packed rafts of identical, athermal, acoustically levitated microspheres to show how multi-body nonreciprocity injects activity in solids. At the level of both individual particles and collective dynamics, crystalline rafts exhibit persistent circulations with no net handedness. The rafts also exhibit a phonon-like dispersion relation corresponding to a large Poisson ratio, indicating an induced softness to shear. Within the bulk, lattice symmetry masks microscopic nonreciprocity, although it can manifest in renormalized, reciprocal elastic coefficients. At dislocations and raft edges, where this symmetry is broken, multi-body nonreciprocal interactions act as local generators of activity. A coarse-grained microscopic model of multi-body nonreciprocity, calibrated on three-particle simulations, recovers the rafts' experimentally observed dispersion relations and localized activity. Using these findings, we illustrate how to harness defect-induced activity for programmable movement by arranging microscopic dislocations to drive macroscopic propulsion and rotation of a whole raft.

papers.title: Eigendecomposition for instantons via infinity-category
papers.abstract: Suppose $L$ is a framed link in a balanced sutured manifold $(M, \gamma)$. We construct a link spectral sequence in sutured instanton homology. For properly embedded surfaces in $M$ disjoint from $L$, we refine the spectral sequence to preserve the induced multi-grading. We use $\infty$-categories to encode homotopical information from instanton theory. In particular, we obtain a simultaneous eigendecomposition of homotopy-coherently commutative operators on a chain complex or a hypercube complex. As the algebraic foundation for subsequent work of the second author and collaborators, we construct the mixed hypercube by combining the hypercubes of positive and negative bypass maps. This construction is compatible with the eigendecomposition associated with the surface multi-grading on sutured instanton homology.

authors.name: Fan Ye
authors.institution: Jiangsu Provincial Key Laboratory of New Environmental Protection

papers.title: Estimating M Dwarf Ages using their Transiting Brown Dwarf Companions
papers.abstract: Determining M dwarf ages remains challenging because of their slow main-sequence evolution. We investigate using transiting brown dwarfs to constrain system ages through their measured masses and thermal emission. We report Palomar/WIRC secondary-eclipse observations of two close-in brown dwarfs, LP 261-75C and AD 3116B, measuring eclipse depths of $6.1 \pm 0.3$ parts per thousand (ppt) in $K_s$ and $9.1 \pm 0.6$ ppt in $J$, respectively. Combining these observations with space-based transit photometry, radial velocities, and host star spectra, we infer brown dwarf internal luminosities and, assuming coevality, host star ages using five sets of atmospheric and evolutionary models. For LP 261-75C, model-dependent median ages span 1.3-2.9 Gyr, substantially older than the previously proposed age of 0.1-0.2 Gyr based on presumed membership in the AB Doradus moving group. This result, the host star's high metallicity, and the companion's measured radius disfavor AB Dor membership. The revised age implies a mass of $\approx 62$-$68$ $M_{\mathrm{Jup}}$ for the wide-orbit companion LP 261-75B, compared with an earlier estimate of $\approx 21$ $M_{\mathrm{Jup}}$. AD 3116B, a member of the 0.6-0.8 Gyr Praesepe cluster, provides a test of brown dwarf evolutionary models through independent constraints on its mass, age, and luminosity. Its inferred age depends strongly on cloud treatment, spanning 0.4-0.6 Gyr for cloudy models and 1.0-1.3 Gyr for cloudless models. Among the models considered, Sonora Diamondback, which includes cloud condensation and cloud clearing across the L/T boundary, provides a plausible simultaneous match to the observed eclipse depth and radius. These results demonstrate a new method to constrain M dwarf ages using emission observations of their brown dwarf companions, while highlighting the sensitivity of the inferred temperatures and ages to evolutionary model differences.

papers.title: A Fractional Chern Semimetal: Exact Wavefunction and Conformal Criticality
papers.abstract: Unlike fractional quantum Hall states in uniform Landau levels, fractional Chern insulators can host dispersive anyon bands, raising the question of what happens when the anyon gap closes. We construct an exact finite-bond-dimension tensor-network state for a fractional Chern semimetal by Gutzwiller projecting a critical parton state. This state exhibits divergent correlation lengths in charged sectors but a fractionally quantized many-body Chern number of $1/3$. Although it has one electron per unit cell, its modular $S$ and $T$ matrices and entanglement spectrum match those of the $\nu=1/3$ Laughlin state. We identify a $(1+1)$--dimensional $U(3)_1\times SU(3)_1$ conformal field theory (CFT) governing the wavefunction norm in the infrared, an unexpected result for a state with $U(1)_3$ topology. The $SU(3)_1$ sector is a nonlinear sigma model whose Wess--Zumino level and kinetic stiffness are determined by the parton Chern number and Fubini--Study metric, respectively. Under renormalization, it flows to the conformal fixed point, with an initial distance to this fixed point controlled by the idealness of parton quantum geometry. Favorable geometry enables precise agreement with CFT predictions even on narrow cylinders.

papers.title: Gradient-Free Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision Models via Agentic Coding
papers.abstract: Adapting a vision model to new classes from a few labeled images usually relies on gradient fine-tuning, which is unstable with so few images. We ask whether a coding agent can replace gradient descent for this task. We propose the Agent edit, a method in which a coding agent writes a program that sets the new class weights in the class head of a frozen COCO-trained detector, with no gradient step. The agent runs the detector on the labeled images a limited number of times and sees how much its edit lowers COCO mAP; the program rebuilds the weights without the agent. In the same head and with the same labels, the Agent edit outperforms full-decoder fine-tuning at five shots on 2 of four fine-grained sets, by 11.2 and 12.3 F1 points, and ties on the rest. At ten shots, fine-tuning ties with or outperforms it. Moreover, when the new classes are scored jointly with the COCO classes, the AP of the COCO class to which they belong falls by up to 33.3 points, and limiting that loss lowers F1 on the new classes. Most of the agent's programs share three parts, which we write as a formula that needs no agent. A classifier on frozen backbone features reaches a higher F1 than every method inside the head on every set. Hence a coding agent can replace gradient descent only in part: inside the head and at five shots.

papers.title: Why High-Spin Prograde MAD States Are Not Realized for AGN in Nature: Consequences for AGN Phenomenology
papers.abstract: Quasar-like and other bright active galactic nuclei are typically radio quiet despite strong evidence that many host rapidly spinning black holes. In contrast, general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations show that high-spin prograde black holes in magnetically arrested disk (MAD) states produce the most powerful relativistic jets. We show that these results are not in conflict but instead correspond to physically distinct and mutually limiting evolutionary pathways. If accretion proceeds through radiatively efficient thin disks, then as the innermost stable circular orbit decreases with increasing prograde spin, radiative output and radiation pressure rise sharply, driving strong disk winds that remove the conditions required for effective jet formation. In this branch, high-spin prograde systems are therefore expected to be jet-suppressed. Alternatively, if accretion transitions to radiatively inefficient flows capable of producing MAD states, then the spin-up to near-maximal prograde rotation proceeds on timescales that exceed the age of the universe for the relevant systems, preventing the realization of the extreme high-spin prograde MAD configurations explored in GRMHD simulations. Within this framework, powerful jets need only be produced efficiently in counterrotating systems, not maximized there, preserving the time-dependent spin evolution central to the counterrotation versus corotation paradigm of Garofalo et al. (2010). We thus reconcile GRMHD results with observations and provide a unified interpretation of the radio-loud/radio-quiet dichotomy and the cosmic evolution of powerful radio sources.

papers.title: PAWP-TTS: Phoneme-Aware Weight Programming for Compact Bilingual English-Nepali Speech Synthesis
papers.abstract: This paper presents PAWP-TTS, a compact non-autoregressive text-to-speech system for English, Nepali, and English-Nepali code-mixed speech at 24 kHz, with no language model at inference. Deterministic pronunciation knowledge lives in a rule- and lexicon-based bilingual frontend that preserves native Nepali contrasts and avoids Hindi phonology, so the network only models acoustics. Counting every learned inference tensor, including the waveform decoder, PAWP-1.5M (1,490,390 parameters, 5.98 MB) reaches 1.50% English and 1.75% Nepali character error rate under a single ASR recognizer, and 5.04% / 4.02% Nepali / English phoneme error rate (PER) on 600 untouched test utterances. Decoder-centric 281K-parameter models (1.1 MB) stay intelligible across three independent seeds, with equal-budget dense models (5.53 +/- 0.08% NE, 5.34 +/- 0.28% EN PER) outperforming K=2 cross-layer shared-basis models (6.35 +/- 0.11% NE, 6.57 +/- 0.47% EN PER). Fixing a frontend/label version mismatch nearly halved Nepali PER, more than any architectural or weight-level change. The paper then studies weight-space programming: inspection-guided, zero-training weight edits. Under strict controls (validation-only selection, one-shot test, paired bootstrap, matched random and same-parameter gradient baselines), edits show real selectivity (27:1 on word-boundary pauses with 96 weights; zero cross-lingual collateral inside language-gated residuals) but no accuracy gain beyond controls. Two apparent targets proved to be label or phonology artifacts. Code, ONNX graphs, and CC BY 4.0 weights are released.

papers.title: Monte Carlo Power Analysis for Small-System A/B Trials: Detecting Differences in Newsletter Engagement
papers.abstract: Good experimental practice and predicting the scientific usefulness of an experiment or experimental platform require power analysis: estimating, *a priori*, how likely the experiment is to detect the intended effect if indeed it exists. While simple experimental designs admit well-understood power analysis methods, more sophisticated experimental designs and settings often require bespoke techniques to avoid either over- or under-estimating experimental power. We present the Monte Carlo method we use to estimate the power of experiments intended to increase user engagement with personalized e-mail newsletters of recommended news articles.

papers.title: Every IVUS Frame in Its Place: A Zero-Install Browser Tool for Registering Intravascular Ultrasound to the Coronary Angiogram, and a Path to Angiography-Only Plaque Imaging
papers.abstract: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) shows plaque composition, calcium and stent apposition that the coronary angiogram cannot, but relating each IVUS cross-section to its position on the angiogram is still largely done in the operator's head. Commercial co-registration is tied to vendor consoles and to set-up at acquisition, so archived angiograms and pullbacks cannot be co-registered, and paired data for training AI models remain scarce. We present a semi-automatic registration tool that runs entirely in a web browser, with no installation and no upload. The clinician picks a contrast-filled reference frame (aided by automatic contrast and cardiac-phase analysis), selects or traces the vessel centerline (aided by Frangi vesselness and minimal paths), and pins the pullback ends and visible landmarks; a monotone piecewise-linear map then places every IVUS frame on the vessel, and each case exports as a frame-level training record. The original Python analysis runs unchanged in WebAssembly and videos are decoded frame-accurately with WebCodecs. On 6 angiographic runs the in-browser analysis was bit-identical to the server pipeline on identical frames; browser decoding differed by at most 2 grey levels, suggested reference frames agreed in all runs and the default automatic centerline in 4 of 6. A 546-frame pullback decoded in 5.3 s. On 36 phantoms with known ground truth, the clinician-guided trace stayed inside the lumen along 87-99% of the vessel, whereas the fully automatic centerline fell from 83% to 0% as noise rose and contrast fell. In a registered Left Main case, one side-branch landmark moved mid-pullback positions by 17.5% of the segment. We map where AI can enter each step, up to predicting a virtual IVUS from the angiogram alone, and make the tool freely available online with a one-click demo.

papers.title: Close the Loop on the Retrievability Gap
papers.abstract: A frozen vision-language encoder now guides image restoration and later indexes what it produced. Over a fixed set of eighteen pansharpening systems on one WorldView-III test set, the fidelity index that ranks them, $Q2^n$ with a reference and HQNR without one, picks the less retrievable of two systems one time in three and one in two; the disagreement lies between the pixel-supervised and the language-conditioned family, and even the best system falls short of the reference, small objects first. We call this the retrievability gap and trace it to the area weighting of position-averaged losses. LEDGER closes the loop around the encoder: it indexes the input into a set of named concepts, generates, re-encodes the output alone with the same frozen encoder, and minimises a set-level soft-Jaccard loss on the coverage of that set, a label-free target available at test time, so that every present concept of a scale receives a gradient share independent of its area. Measured outside the loop by label-grounded probes, held-out retrievers, language-free evaluators, detectors and human raters, LEDGER matches or exceeds the strongest baselines in fidelity on four sensors, raises retrieval by seven to nine points within its vocabulary and two to five outside it, closes two thirds of the reduced-resolution gap to the reference, lifts extraction on raw SpaceNet imagery above the vendor product in each of four cities, and transfers to existing generators as a training-only loss at no inference cost.

authors.name: Jiaqi Zhang
authors.institution: Key Laboratory of Automobile Materials, Ministry of Education, Jilin University

authors.name: Haoyu Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: "I feel like AI is just everywhere": A longitudinal qualitative study on parents' perceptions, use, and mediation of GenAI
papers.abstract: GenAI has developed rapidly over the last few years, yet few longitudinal studies exploring how individuals' experiences with GenAI have changed over time exist. Even fewer studies have focused on families with children, despite the opportunity to explore how parents have balanced their needs, their children's development, and the fast pace in which technology changes. To better understand how parents' perceptions, use, and mediation of GenAI shifted over two years, we interviewed 10 parents who had participated in a prior study about their families' experiences with GenAI. Parents had shifted from thinking GenAI was novel to feeling like it was unavoidable, characterizing GenAI as a limited tool to believing GenAI development needed to be regulated, and focusing on their personal mediation strategies to wanting systemic plans to curb GenAI's long-term consequences. We position our findings within the context of parental mediation of technology and increasing collective mitigation of GenAI-related risks.

papers.title: Risk aversion with two risks for state-dependent utilities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the concept of Arrow-Pratt risk aversion within a two-attribute, state-dependent utility framework, where a primary risk is accompanied by a background risk. Within this setting, we investigate the interrelationships among risk aversion toward one risk in the presence of another risk, the structure of state-dependent two-attribute utility functions, and the degree of correlation between the two risks. More specifically, we establish conditions on the state-dependent two-attribute utility function under which risk aversion toward primary risk is preserved when a background risk is involved, considering various correlation structures between the two types of risks. Additionally, a new concept, uniform risk aversion in the presence of a background risk, is introduced. We show that the above established conditions on the state-dependent two-attribute utility function are equivalent to uniform risk aversion toward primary risk in presence of a background risk. These findings offer new insights into state-dependent preferences for correlated risks. Two applications in the contexts of fair insurance contract and optimal prevention within a two-period model illustrate the practical usefulness of the proposed risk aversion with two risks under state-dependent utilities.

authors.name: Jiehua Xie
authors.institution: Jiangxi University of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: ComplexIF: A Challenging Multi-Turn, Multi-Constraint Instruction-Following Benchmark
papers.abstract: As frontier LLMs saturate existing instruction-following benchmarks, measuring further progress requires harder tests that remain faithful to real use. In practice, users often combine several constraints, add them at different turns of a conversation, and expect all of them to hold in the assistant's response. We introduce ComplexIF, a challenging benchmark for this setting, together with the automatic pipeline that generates it. The pipeline expands seed requests into multi-turn conversations, weaves constraints into their turns, and keeps only tasks that a strong model can solve, so difficulty can be raised by adding constraints or turns while every task stays solvable. ComplexIF's two splits test complementary sides of instruction following: a verifiable split of format constraints, checked by programs, and a rubric split of semantic instructions, such as a tone or an audience, checked with an LLM judge. Across 14 proprietary and open-weight models, even the strongest satisfies every constraint on fewer than half of the verifiable tasks, and no model leads on both splits.

authors.name: Zhichao Xu
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

authors.name: Haoyu Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: SA-GLRT-D: Sidelobe-Aware GLRT-Based Detector for FMCW Radar
papers.abstract: This paper investigates adaptive detection for frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar in multi-target complex scenarios, where reference-cell contamination, spectral leakage from the cell under test (CUT), and the resulting sidelobe interference severely degrade detection performance. A sidelobe-aware detector based on the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT), termed SA-GLRT-D, is proposed. Unlike conventional filtering-then-constant false alarm rate (CFAR) schemes, the proposed method explicitly accounts for the non-ideal frequency-domain energy spreading of the CUT induced by the finite-window effect. Accordingly, conventional single-cell target detection is extended to local-region detection, and decision statistic construction, CUT-related parameter estimation, and sidelobe interference suppression are jointly accomplished within a unified hypothesis-testing framework. Furthermore, to reduce computational complexity, a fast implementation of SA-GLRT-D is developed, together with a dedicated parameter initialization strategy to enhance the stability of numerical optimization. Simulation and real-measurement results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high-accuracy target detection while maintaining a constant false alarm rate, with favorable computational efficiency.

authors.name: Jiachen Zhu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

authors.name: Ming Xia
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: $K3$ Picard--Fuchs equations with initial conditions in the Hodge line
papers.abstract: Lam and Litt conjectured that a formal horizontal section of a Gauss--Manin connection is algebraic if and only if it is integral, if and only if it is $\omega(p)$-integral. We prove it for families of $K3$ surfaces over a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra in a number field, when the initial condition lies in the Hodge line. In this case, all three conditions are equivalent to the vanishing of the Higgs field on the Hodge line. Along the way, we show that a smooth projective family $X\to S$ with $H^0(X_s,T_{X_s})=0$ is constant on an \'{e}tale neighborhood of $s$ if and only if its Kodaira--Spencer class vanishes near $s$.

papers.title: HandXFM: Semantic-Structural Distillation for Hand Radiograph Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Hand radiographs support diverse clinical tasks, including skeletal maturity assessment, rheumatoid arthritis scoring, abnormality screening, and anatomical localization, yet existing models are typically trained separately for each task and dataset. We present HandXFM, a domain-specific foundation model that leverages cross-modality knowledge for comprehensive hand X-ray understanding. HandXFM distills semantic priors from BiomedCLIP and structural cues from a chest X-ray Vision Transformer (ViT) through a unified alignment framework, integrating complementary medical knowledge in an interpretable way. After pretraining, HandXFM can be adapted to a range of musculoskeletal tasks, including bone age estimation, SvH score prediction, abnormality detection, joint localization, bone segmentation, and visual question answering. It consistently outperforms task-specific and single-expert baselines, achieving up to 0.11 improvement in Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) for bone age prediction and a 12\% accuracy gain in abnormality classification. Moreover, HandXFM generalizes to unseen datasets and yields cross-attention maps linking clinical terms to anatomical regions. These results demonstrate that multi-expert distillation effectively unifies semantic and structural supervision within a single pretrained model, establishing HandXFM as an interpretable and generalizable foundation model for hand radiograph analysis.

papers.title: A simple counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem for excited states
papers.abstract: For an even number of non-interacting fermions on the one-dimensional unit torus, a semi-explicit counterexample to the Hohenberg--Kohn theorem for excited states is exhibited. Indeed, for each $n = 2l$, it is shown that there exist constants $m \in (0, 1)$ and $\ell > 0$ such that an $n$-body system with the rescaled Lam\'e potential $v_*(x) = 2m \ell^2 \operatorname{sn}^2(\ell x; m)$ has a simple first excited energy and a first excited-state particle density which is constant on the torus. By translating this potential, we exhibit a non-trivial one-parameter family of potentials, all of which have a constant first excited-state density. As such, the potential-to-density map is not one-to-one in this setting. Under a spectral nonresonance assumption, we obtain the same nonuniqueness at a simple excited energy for odd $n \geq 3$. We also explore connections to the classification problem of elastica in the plane when $n = 2$, and outline some related questions of interest.

papers.title: Triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes
papers.abstract:
We study fractional triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes, unifying the settings of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions and the high-dimensional Dirac problem for Steiner triple systems.
  We prove that every sufficiently large two-dimensional simplicial complex with minimum degree at least $(1-d_1)n$ and maximum missing codegree at most $d_2n$ admits a fractional triangle decomposition, provided $d_1/0.21+d_2/0.27\leq 1$. As an immediate consequence, we prove the asymptotic form of Lee's high-dimensional Dirac conjecture: every sufficiently large admissible $3$-uniform hypergraph with minimum codegree at least $(3/4+\varepsilon)n$ contains a Steiner triple system.
  We also provide constructions establishing lower bounds on this fractional decomposition threshold problem.

papers.title: A Principled Framework for PDE-Based Shock Capturing in High-Order Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
papers.abstract: PDE-based artificial viscosity (AV) captures shocks in high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods by solving an auxiliary PDE for a smooth viscosity field. The behavior of that field is set by how the terms of the AV PDE scale with the element size $h$ and polynomial degree $p$, and by how its coefficients are parametrized. This work derives both choices from analysis and studies the impact these choices have on the implicit steady-state solver. First, an $L^2$-projection analysis shows that the thinnest shock a polynomial space can represent monotonically scales with the resolution length $\bar h = h/p$, and a scaling analysis of the AV PDE gives concrete conditions on its diffusion and source terms for the solution to be self-similar in $\bar h$. Prior formulations satisfy them only under $h$-refinement at fixed $p$; the AV PDE is scaled so that they hold under $hp$-refinement, and the captured shock thins accordingly. Second, a Green's-function analysis of the steady AV PDE gives closed-form expressions for the width and magnitude of the AV. In the standard parametrization the two are coupled: raising the diffusion coefficient widens the AV but lowers its peak. An alternative parametrization of the decay coefficient removes the coupling in the Green's-function response and inverts it in the coupled state-AV problem, so that widening the AV raises its peak instead of lowering it. Third, a parameter study on a Mach 5 viscous flow over a half-cylinder characterizes how the choice of solution variables and the AV PDE's time, width, and magnitude coefficients affect the robustness and cost of the implicit solve. The choice of variables dominates robustness, with entropy variables converging over the largest region of the width-magnitude parameter space. Together, the three contributions make PDE-based AV more predictable to tune and its implicit solve more robust.

papers.title: Bruhat Shellings of the Quasisymmetric Flag Moment Complex
papers.abstract: The quasisymmetric flag variety gives rise to a regular cell complex whose maximal cells are cubes indexed by fully supported noncrossing partitions. Two maximal cubes can meet along several faces. We describe each cube using the block arcs and parent connectors of its indexing partition, and determine its intersection with the union of the preceding cubes in Bruhat order. For each nonempty face, we determine the first maximal cube containing it by applying an outer-block merging operation to its Bruhat-maximal noncrossing-partition label. The first-carrier theorem provides an explicit description of how each cube attaches to the preceding subcomplex. More precisely, the intersection is a union of coordinate facets which, for every cube except the first, forms the closed star of a face in its boundary. Consequently, every linear extension of Bruhat order on the maximal-cell labels gives a shelling of the regular cell complex. In particular, its barycentric subdivision is shellable, hence homotopy Cohen--Macaulay and Cohen--Macaulay over \(\mathbb Z\) and every field.

papers.title: Almost-Isometric Embeddings of Graphs into Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: Graphs represent objects as vertices and relationships as edges; positive edge weights define shortest-path metrics. Metric embeddings leverage target-space geometry to analyze distances. Foundational results target linear spaces: Nash embedded Riemannian manifolds isometrically into Euclidean space, and Bourgain embedded $n$-point metrics into Hilbert space with $O(\log n)$ distortion. By contrast, the manifold hypothesis places high-dimensional data near low-dimensional smooth manifolds, making such manifolds themselves target spaces. What distortion is needed to embed a finite graph metric into such a manifold with its intrinsic distance? Although the star $K_{1,3}$ cannot embed isometrically into any complete Riemannian manifold, we prove almost-isometric embeddings always exist: for $\varepsilon>0$ and any finite connected positively weighted graph, we construct a smooth connected closed orientable surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ admitting a noncontractive $(1+\varepsilon)$-embedding of its vertices, with $\varepsilon$ arbitrarily small and independent of graph parameters. This construction transfers communication schemes between graphs and surfaces. For independent unicasts, fractional routing splits flows across paths while network coding lets relays combine messages. Space information flow permits relays anywhere, charging bandwidth times distance. Whereas coding advantage (optimal routing over coding cost) equals one in Euclidean space, we prove coding advantages on finite positively weighted undirected graphs transfer to smooth closed surfaces within factors approaching one. Counterexamples to the multiple-unicast conjecture and amplification yield smooth closed surfaces with unbounded coding advantage. Conversely, coding advantage is at most $C\log(g+2)$ on finite undirected graphs of orientable genus $g$ and smooth closed orientable surfaces of genus $g$, for absolute $C$.

papers.title: An $n^{1/O(\log^* n)}$ Lower Bound for Online Coloring of $k$-Colorable Graphs
papers.abstract: In online coloring, the vertices of a graph arrive one at a time with their edges to earlier vertices, and each vertex must be colored irrevocably on arrival. For graphs promised to be $k$-colorable, with $k\ge 3$ fixed, the best deterministic algorithms use $n^{1-\Theta(1/k^2)}$ colors, while the best lower bound was Vishwanathan's $\Omega(\log^{k-1}n)$ from 1990 until Li recently proved $2^{\Omega((\log n)^{1/3}(\log\log n)^{2/3})}$. For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, we prove a lower bound of $n^{1/(\log^*n+3)}$ colors for deterministic online algorithms on $n$-vertex $k$-colorable graphs, and the same lower bound in expectation for randomized online algorithms. Both bounds hold on a single triangle-free $3$-colorable graph: even an algorithm that is shown this graph in advance, but is not told which of its vertices each arriving vertex is, can be forced to use this many colors by a suitable arrival order. The hard instances are iterated blow-ups of a clique, in which every vertex becomes a block of independent vertices and every edge a private server in the earlier block; each blow-up keeps the forced colors and replaces the chromatic number $\chi$ by about $\log\chi$, so about $\log^*n$ blow-ups bring it down to $k$. We also show that deterministic lower bounds for different values of $k\ge 3$ are polynomially equivalent, and that no adversary presenting such iterated blow-ups can force more than $n^{1/(\log^*n-O(1))}$ colors. All numbered results are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: But Can You Draw It Live? The Emergence of AI Duidus for Adjudicating Suspected Generative AI Use in Digital Art Commission Communities
papers.abstract: Generative AI poses new challenges for digital art commission communities, where a commission's value often depends on human labor and authorship. We examine a novel community-developed dispute resolution mechanism called an AI duidu, or livestreamed drawing bet, used when an artist is suspected of using generative AI. In an AI duidu, an accuser challenges an artist to create a new artwork live, and community members vote on whether the artist created the disputed artwork without AI assistance. Often, both parties stake money with an intermediary, who releases it after the vote. Through interviews with 17 accusers, accused artists, or intermediaries, we examined how the AI duidu emerged and how participants perceived its effectiveness and risks. We found that AI duidus shift authorship verification from the artwork itself to the artist, using livestreamed creative labor, community adjudication, and wagering to establish provenance and negotiate community norms surrounding AI use.

papers.title: Tabular Foundation Models for Weighted Regression and Classification
papers.abstract: Weighted regression and classification have applications ranging from missing-data analysis and causal inference to insurance pricing and particle physics. Existing weighted methods must be fitted and tuned on each dataset, which is costly for flexible nonlinear learners. Tabular foundation models avoid this cost. A Transformer is pretrained once on many simulated datasets and then predicts on a new dataset by in-context learning, using its observations as context without further fitting. Recent models such as TabPFN-3.5 surpass tuned conventional methods, but they cannot use sample weights. We develop a general pipeline that adapts such models to weighted prediction through weighted attention, a normalized weighted loss, and pretraining on synthetic weighted prediction tasks from missing-data problems. Applied to TabPFN-3.5, it yields WeightedPFN, which performs strongly on real datasets, both in missing-data problems and in out-of-distribution causal tasks, while running about as fast as linear baselines. We also establish a statistical theory showing that a suitably pretrained weighted Transformer attains the nonparametric minimax rate for weighted regression on new datasets without further fitting.

authors.name: Junwen Xia
authors.institution: Shanghai Institute of Measurement and Testing Technology

papers.title: Training Dynamics of Large State-Transition Models
papers.abstract: Next-token prediction relies on learned token embeddings whose dimension $d$ is much smaller than the vocabulary size $V$. Existing analyses of training dynamics either fix the embeddings with $d\ge V$ or train them only in restricted settings. It remains unclear whether jointly training the embeddings by gradient-based methods from random initialization leads to accurate prediction when $d<V$. In this paper, we study this question in the simplest setting where it is already nontrivial, namely next-token prediction with a one-token context, which we refer to as a state-transition model. The model consists of an input embedding and an output embedding, either untied or tied, and is trained from Gaussian initialization by perturbed gradient descent with weight decay on the population cross-entropy loss. We consider ground-truth transition laws whose centered log-probability table has low rank and bounded entries, and measure the prediction quality by the relative prediction gain (RPG). It is zero for the uniform predictor and one for the optimal predictor. For the untied model, we show that when $d=\Omega(\sqrt V)$, with probability at least $1-e^{-cd}$ for some constant $c$, the RPG is above $7/8$ at every iterate in the final $1-1/d$ fraction of training iterations. For the tied model trained on a subset of states, we prove that the RPG on the observed states is $1-O(V/d^2)$, and under a coverage condition on the ground truth and a bound on the learned embeddings, we further prove a prediction guarantee on the unseen states. Our analysis is based on the bounded trace of the Hessian of the softmax cross-entropy loss, which implies that the approximate second-order stationary points reached by training have high prediction gain. Numerical experiments with practical parameter choices illustrate the persistent training gain and the transfer of the tied model.

papers.title: On the extension of non-faithful and non-normal traces of von Neumann algebras to their affiliated operators
papers.abstract:
Let $\tau$ be a positive tracial functional on a finite von Neumann algebra ${\mathcal{M}}$, not necessarily normal. For a positive self-adjoint operator $A$ affiliated with ${\mathcal{M}}$ we define ${\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}}(A)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}\tau(A(\mathrm{I}+hA)^{-1})\in[0,\infty]$. We show that $\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(A)=\sup_R\tau(\min(A,R \mathrm{I}))$.
  We prove that ${\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}}$ is additive on positive affiliated operators, by a form--resolvent comparison valid for arbitrary positive traces. As a consequence, $\tau$ has a positive linear extension to the span $\mathscr D_\tau$ of the positive affiliated operators of finite extended trace, and $\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(T^*T)$ defines a pre-Hilbert structure for every positive trace. For every trace, $\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(|S+T|)^{2/3}\le \tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(|S|)^{2/3}+\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(|T|)^{2/3}$; hence the operators $T$ with $\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(|T|)<\infty$ form a ${\mathcal{M}}$-bimodule $\mathscr L_Y^1$, on which the linear extension is defined and cyclic. It turns out that $\mathscr L_Y^1=\mathscr D_\tau$; $d(S,T)={\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}}(|S-T|)^{2/3}$ is a translation-invariant pseudometric on $\mathscr L^1_Y$ and is a metric iff $\tau$ is faithful. On the approximation side, a Chernoff family in ${\mathcal{M}}$ forces affiliation of its generator. Trace defects of Chernoff families need not converge to ${\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}}(A)$, even for faithful normal traces, while two-sided resolvent comparison suffices. For faithful normal traces, ${\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}}$ is the canonical extension and the associated space $\mathscr L_Y^p$ coincide with the classical $L^p({\mathcal{M}},\tau)$ as well as their norms ($1\leq p<\infty$).

papers.title: FToken: Factors as Tokens for Dual-Axis Cross-Sectional Return Prediction
papers.abstract: On a given trading day, a stock-factor panel describes both how stocks differ across factors and how each factor varies across stocks. Most stock Transformers model relationships among stocks or across time. We introduce FToken, which also models relationships among factors.
