Under coherent unitary access to the joint reward-and-constraint distribution, we develop QRS-COLTS, a staged quantum resampled-scaling analog of constrained linear Thompson sampling (COLTS). With high probability, QRS-COLTS plays only feasible actions and achieves regret that is polylogarithmic in the query horizon and scales only with the square root of the number of constraints. We also study a model in which the learner queries superpositions of actions while an unsafe-action flag, a "bomb" that terminates the interaction upon violation, is measured after every query. In this setting, the bomb provides exact membership access to the safe set, and query regret is evaluated over the action superposition. For this model, we propose BCO-QLinTS, which selects feasible actions via bomb-certified quantum convex optimization without estimating the constraint matrix. Its query-weighted regret remains polylogarithmic in the horizon, with the constraints entering the bound only through the geometry of the safe set.

authors.name: Ruizhe Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: UV3CP: Universal ViT-Based 3D Channel Predictor for MIMO-OFDM Systems
papers.abstract: Channel aging in time-division duplex multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems causes a mismatch between uplink-based channel state information and the downlink channel at the transmission instant. Although vision transformers (ViTs) are effective for channel prediction, their performance is highly sensitive to the patch size, whose optimum depends on the channel coherence region. Moreover, changing the patch size typically requires retraining because it alters the token grid and patch embedding operator. In this paper, we propose a universal ViT-based 3D channel prediction framework, called UV3CP, for MIMO-OFDM systems. The proposed UV3CP employs an efficient 3D ViT backbone to capture frequency, time, and spatial channel dependencies. First, based on second-order channel statistics, we derive a statistics-aware patch-size selection rule that selects axis-wise patch lengths using a mean-squared-error-based criterion, thereby matching the tokenization granularity to the dominant channel coherence while controlling token length and complexity. Second, we develop a statistics-aware patch-embedding resizing method that enables a single shared UV3CP to operate across different patch sizes without patch-size-specific retraining. Simulation results show that the proposed method improves robustness under various scenarios and patch-size mismatch while reducing the need to train and store multiple patch-size-specific ViT models.

authors.name: Yo-Seb Jeon
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Audio-Visual Rearrangement
papers.abstract: We introduce Audio-Visual Rearrangement (AVR), a novel task in which an agent hears a spoken request, retrieves a suitable object, and delivers it to the requesting user or an instruction-specified destination. AVR requires the agent to understand the spoken request and acoustically localize the speaker for delivery. To support this task, we construct a dataset covering three query types: explicit target specification, speaker-relative spatial references, and implicit user intent, spanning eight subtypes with diverse object selection and delivery requirements. Moreover, we propose a framework that integrates a motion-aware spatial audio module into an audio-visual large language model to encode spatial cues from the spoken request and update them as the agent moves. We further incorporate auxiliary supervision for speech understanding, spatial audio perception, and visual grounding through multitask instruction tuning to improve action prediction. Experiments establish baseline performance in both seen and unseen environments, laying the groundwork for future research on embodied intelligence and human-robot interaction. The code will be publicly available soon.

authors.name: Jiatong Ye
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Zhenbo Li
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Uniform Ionization Bounds in Molecular Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizs\"acker Theory
papers.abstract: We study the molecular Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizs\"acker theory. For each fixed number $K$ of nuclei, we prove that every minimizer of mass $N$ satisfies $N\leq Z+C_K$, where $Z$ is the total nuclear charge, and $C_K>0$ is independent of the nuclear charges and positions. This answers the molecular large-charge ionization question posed in [R. L. Frank, P. T. Nam and H. Van Den Bosch, CPAM, 2018]. For $N\geq Z$, we also compare the screened potentials and electronic radii of Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizs\"acker minimizers with those of the corresponding neutral molecular Thomas--Fermi minimizers and establish a uniform bound on the ionization energy.

papers.title: When Does Overriding the Majority Vote Help?
papers.abstract: When should additional reasoning or verification replace a majority-vote answer? We call such a replacement an override. We examine two obstacles: the availability of correct alternatives and the reliability of methods that produce or select them. We compare additional reasoning, executed programs, and cross-model reasoning on 150 competition-mathematics questions with three open reasoning models. Starting from a majority vote over 16 responses, we measure how often overrides occur and how many errors they correct or introduce across agreement thresholds. When the vote is incorrect, the correct answer is often absent from the original responses. Additional same-model reasoning rarely overrides, while executed programs correct more errors than they introduce at every evaluated threshold. Cross-model overrides improve some weaker baselines but do not establish an advantage over the more accurate model alone, even with only eight standalone responses. Stricter agreement reduces how often overrides occur but does not consistently increase the fraction that correct errors. At the strictest thresholds, overrides occur on few distinct questions, limiting conclusions about their reliability.

authors.name: Aidan Zhang
authors.institution: Zhejiang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Seeing vs. Knowing: Counterfactual Supervision and Correction for 3D-Aware Object Editing
papers.abstract: Rotating, translating, or rescaling an object in a photograph requires revealing unseen surfaces, preserving visible appearance, and updating shadows and reflections. Reconstructed 3D assets, rendered at the target pose as a 3D state, provide explicit geometric guidance, but their imperfect textures may conflict with the photograph, while standard paired training does not explicitly teach the editor which source to trust. To address this, we propose counterfactual state supervision, which constructs controlled photo--state conflicts through hidden-surface repainting, hidden geometry with re-rendered shadows and reflections, and visible-surface texture replacement. This teaches the editor to follow the 3D state for unseen content while preserving photograph-visible appearance. However, learning this distinction does not ensure that it is maintained during sampling. We therefore introduce symmetric counterfactual correction, which uses state-side and photo-side twins, which share the photograph and the state respectively, to construct directed latent perturbations toward condition-inconsistent targets and train recovery toward the target specified by the current condition. Both strategies operate only during training, requiring no architectural changes or additional inference steps. Experiments on OBJect and SpatialEdit-Bench demonstrate strong spatial editing performance and content preservation, while controlled ablations show improved source selection and sustained responsiveness to conditioning during sampling.

authors.name: Zhijun Zhang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Chengdu Medical College

papers.title: HiPPO Functional Memory: Coordinate-Queryable Attention for Irregular Time Series
papers.abstract: Irregular time series are recorded at nonuniform times and are often queried at other times: between observations, after the last one, or on a regular grid. Continuous-time models answer such queries by integrating latent dynamics, and time-aware attention models answer them by revisiting the observation tokens. We introduce HiPPO Functional Memory (HiPPO-FM), an attention operator that writes an irregular history into a rank-M function space with explicit time coordinates. Masked self-attention first exchanges content among the observations; the updated values are then contracted against kernel-smoothed HiPPO-Legendre features and solved through a regularized Gram matrix, so the retained coefficients define a function that is read at any time through the same features. The write and read have the form of an interdomain sparse Gaussian-process mean: every readout lies in an M-dimensional reproducing-kernel subspace, and a pointwise bound separates the approximation error of this subspace from the error of the learned memory. Removing the functional memory from the encoder raises Spiral reconstruction RMSE 18-fold. The full model has the lowest error in 11 of 12 Spiral settings, the highest overall accuracy and best average rank on 20 irregular UEA datasets, the highest event-type accuracy on all five multi-type event benchmarks, and a 21% lower extrapolation MSE than CRU on PhysioNet. Because the memory has fixed rank, the state retained after encoding keeps a fixed size as the history grows and is 102 times smaller than a token cache at 1,024 observations.

papers.title: A novel mechanism for coherent radio emission: particle-in-cell simulations
papers.abstract: It has been established that electron (phase-space) holes, i.e., EHs, can arise from the nonlinear relaxation of the electron beam instability. Excitation of electromagnetic waves related to the EHs is, however, still not fully understood. Using 2.5-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations, we systematically investigate the nonlinear evolution of the (moderately relativistic) electron bi-stream instability (a special case of the electron beam instability where the densities of the two counter-propagating energetic electron beams are equivalent) in charge- and current-neutralized plasmas under weak and strong magnetizations. This study provides new insights into the wave excitation, the nonlinear wave-particle interactions, the formation of non-Maxwellian features, and the anisotropic electron heating in magnetized plasmas, with potential implications for coherent radio emission in astrophysical plasmas (e.g., solar zebra-pattern bursts).

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Regression via Calibration: Beyond the Supervised Minimax Benchmark
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric regression with limited labeled data and abundant observations carrying potentially inaccurate pseudo-labels. Our proposed method, weighted prediction-powered regression via calibration (wPPRC), first calibrates pseudo-labels using labeled data, then fits a predictor by weighted regression using observed and calibrated responses. Over H\"older classes, we derive nonasymptotic excess-risk bounds for clipped ReLU estimators and establish a minimax lower bound for the corresponding regression problem. Under suitable conditions, the upper and lower bounds match up to logarithmic factors. Moreover, wPPRC can achieve a worst-case risk of smaller order than the minimax risks under four baseline observation structures on the same joint distribution class, demonstrating the value of additional pseudo-labels. We also construct a validation-selected (VS) estimator using an independent labeled validation sample to choose the weight. The VS estimator satisfies an expected-risk oracle inequality and preserves the improvement over the baseline minimax risks with the same total labeled-data budget. Simulations and an application to predicting homeless counts illustrate the gains of the proposed estimators.

authors.name: Jian Huang
authors.institution: Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences & Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital

papers.title: Seeing the Invisible: How Vision-Language Models Read, Predict and Trace Radio Fields
papers.abstract: Operating in the physical world requires reasoning beyond what cameras directly capture. In a city, radio signals are invisible to the lens, yet their strength is governed by the buildings and streets an image does show. Given only these visible structures, can vision-language models (VLMs) infer the invisible radio field they shape? Probing true physical reasoning requires exact fields in real cities, alongside controlled interventions where a single physical factor changes. We build a label-free engine that turns any coordinate on Earth into a ray-traceable city, simulates matched single-factor counterfactuals, and computes every answer exactly. This yields RadioVISTA, a benchmark and training dataset for visual reasoning about invisible fields. Physically, a radio field is the sum of its propagation paths, yet across six continents we uncover a striking field-path dissociation: frontier VLMs accurately judge where a field is strong, but fail to tell whether a single direct or one-wall path exists. Open models fail even earlier at reading the field itself, and are systematically wrong, scoring below random guessing even when credited for any of four attempts. On unseen cities, fine-tuning brings a 9B open model close to frontier proprietary models on fields, yet neither supervised nor reinforcement fine-tuning improves path tracing. Supervising only final answers teaches models to approximate the field, yet leaves single-path geometry out of reach.

authors.name: Ziheng Liu
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Chau Yuen
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: ReMiC: Representation-Driven Token Pruning for 3D VLMs via Minimax Hierarchical Clustering
papers.abstract: 3D vision-language models (3D VLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in 3D scene understanding and spatial reasoning. However, their reliance on multi-view inputs produces long visual token sequences, imposing substantial computational overhead during inference. Existing pruning methods often rely on token salience or feature diversity as proxies for representativeness, without explicitly modeling the representation gap between the original token set and the retained subset, thereby leading to suboptimal representation of the original scene. In this paper, we propose ReMiC, a training-free, representation-driven token pruning framework based on minimax hierarchical clustering. ReMiC treats retained tokens as prototypes for the original observations, formulating pruning as minimizing the maximum representation error under a fixed token budget. Local prototype initialization allocates tokens according to regional representation needs, while global prototype refinement updates the selected prototypes using cross-region information to further reduce the maximum representation error. Extensive experiments conducted on three representative 3D VLMs across five 3D scene understanding benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization of our method. Notably, by retaining only 10% of visual tokens, ReMiC preserves 93.2% of the performance of Video-3D LLM and achieves a $2.04\times$ faster inference speed.

authors.name: Chaoning Zhang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Sheng Zheng
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Dynamics-Guided Conditional MeanFlow from Regional Interaction to Internal Revision and Its Application to CT Imaging
papers.abstract: Conditional image enhancement requires spatially varying corrections, yet fixed-depth models allocate similar computational budgets regardless of where additional refinement is needed. Although one-step flow models reduce inference costs and iterative restoration methods introduce subsequent corrections, how predicted transformation dynamics can guide internal feature refinement remains underexplored. We introduce IRCMF, a dynamics-guided Conditional MeanFlow framework that combines regional interaction with recurrent internal revision. The decoder predicts signed interval velocity and a learned velocity-change cue. A soft-region graph aggregates contextual information for velocity estimation, while a dynamics-conditioned graph establishes regional relationships to guide recurrent bottleneck updates. The revised features are processed by the shared decoder to recompute velocity, establishing feedback between transformation dynamics and internal representations. An actor-critic policy controls regional updates and further revisions to balance enhancement quality and computational cost. We evaluate IRCMF on two computed tomography (CT) datasets, NLST for STANDARD-to-LUNG kernel enhancement and LDCT-and-Projection-data for simulated low-to-routine-dose enhancement. With nine decoder evaluations, IRCMF achieves slice-level PSNR of $36.24 \pm 3.49$ dB and SSIM of $0.97 \pm 0.01$ on NLST, and PSNR of $32.45 \pm 1.97$ dB and SSIM of $0.84 \pm 0.05$ on LDCT-and-Projection-data. The learned policy reduces average decoder evaluations to 4.42 and 3.45, respectively, lowering per-slice latency from 97.00 to 51.82 ms and from 97.12 to 41.95 ms, with PSNR reductions of only 0.20 and 0.06 dB.

authors.name: Jin Chen
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: FinEvo: Recursive Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Financial Modeling
papers.abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) have expanded their role in high-value productivity tasks, including financial analysis and modeling, while enabling models to play an increasingly active role in their own improvement. This motivates two complementary lines of inquiry: can financial modeling capabilities provide a foundation for model self-evolution, and can self-evolution, in turn, advance financial capabilities? We introduce FinEvo, a self-evolution framework that integrates autonomous experience construction with financial capability improvement. FinEvo prepares financial models, iteratively evolves challenges through self-play, and learns from the resulting interactions using executable rewards, relying on the same model throughout. An end-to-end execution with Qwen3.6-27B shows that solving feedback supports both increasing reasoning demands and identifying specification issues that executable checks can miss. Learning from these experiences raises whole-task success from 22.73 to 29.09 on held-out within-source tasks and from 13.13 to 19.19 on SpreadsheetBench 2 Financial. Comparable gains across task sources and evaluation settings, together with improvement on a task category absent from training, suggest that FinEvo strengthens underlying financial modeling capabilities shared across tasks. These findings support self-evolution as a path toward broader financial competence, advancing the empirical exploration of recursive self-improvement (RSI) in professional domains. Code is available at https://github.com/pcj-sudo/FinEvo.

authors.name: Chengjun Pan
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Fine Chemicals

authors.name: Tao Gui
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Computing pro-$p$ Closures of Finitely Generated Subgroups of Closed Orientable Surface Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma_g$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g\geq2$, and let $p$ be a prime. For every finitely generated subgroup $H\leq\Gamma_g$ we give an algorithm which, given any finite generating set of $H$ by words in a standard generating set, outputs a finite set of words in the same alphabet that generates the pro-$p$ closure of $H$. This extends the computation of pro-$p$ closures in free groups by Ribes-Zalesskii and Margolis-Sapir-Weil.

papers.title: LoopSight: Looped Vision Transformers with Gated Prediction Memory
papers.abstract: Looped vision transformers extend computation for visual reasoning by repeatedly applying a shared Transformer core. A challenge is to preserve useful prediction information across loop iterations while allowing the computation state to evolve. In this paper we introduce LoopSight, a looped vision transformer that uses Gated Prediction Memory (GPM) to maintain a persistent prediction state for readout, separate from the core's evolving computation state. At each iteration, a cross-attention gate uses the core's candidate features, the previous prediction state, and the current task state to control writes at the patch and channel level. The model decodes its prediction from the updated memory. We condition the shared core on the current iteration using asymptotic loop encoding and train the model by supervising its prediction at loop counts sampled from a truncated Gaussian distribution. LoopSight outperforms LoopViT across three model scales on ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2. On ARC-AGI-1, LoopSight-Small achieves 67.4% pass@2, a gain of 6.6 percentage points over LoopViT-Small with comparable parameter counts and FLOPs. LoopSight also outperforms LoopViT on Visual Sudoku and ImageNet classification. Further analyses on ARC-AGI-1 show that LoopSight preserves more already-correct predictions and maintains more stable readout features as its computation state continues to evolve. The code will be released at https://github.com/feufhd/LoopSight.

authors.name: Jun Luo
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Rate--burst safety languages: the Farey structure of the burst boundary and discrimination under erasures
papers.abstract: A leaky-bucket constraint with rate \(\rho\) and burst \(B\) allows at most \(\rho n+B\) costly steps in every window of \(n\) consecutive steps. The infinite 0/1 words that satisfy it form a safety language. For a finite graph with edge costs 0 and 1, we study the least burst at which the cost word of some infinite path lies in this language, as a function of the real rate. This function is the exact tolerance of a monitor that distinguishes two finite-state systems observed through an erasure channel with a leaky-bucket bound. The language is \(\omega\)-regular at every rational rate but not at irrational rates once the burst reaches 1, so ultimately periodic witnesses do not come from automata theory. We prove directly that simple lassos suffice at all real rates and that all breakpoints of the boundary lie in the Farey sequence of order N for a graph with N vertices. One lasso has a tight bound of order N to the power 2/3 on its affine pieces, whereas the choice among paths creates downward jumps and boundaries that are neither convex nor concave. One evaluation at the mediant of each Farey interval recovers the affine piece and an optimal lasso, and a greatest-fixed-point computation over decreasing integer bursts yields the whole function in polynomial time and linear working space. We also compute discrimination horizons and extend the Farey structure to turn-based safety games.

authors.name: Zhuo Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: A High-Frequency Flux-Driven DC-SQUID Threshold Detector at the Single-Microwave-Photon Energy Scale: A Numerical Feasibility Study
papers.abstract: In our recent work (Phys. Rev. B \textbf{113}, 224503 (2026)), we showed numerically that rapidly sweeping the bias current of a current-biased Josephson junction threshold detector (CBJJ-JTD) drives it out of equilibrium. This substantially reduces the effect of thermal noise on microwave detection and may enable threshold detection near the energy of a single microwave photon. The scheme requires very low damping ($\beta \leq 10^{-4}$) and a very fast bias-current sweep ($v/\beta \geq 1$), both of which are difficult to achieve with available junctions and low-pass-filtered cryogenic measurement lines. Here we propose a more experimentally accessible nonequilibrium threshold detector based on a high-frequency flux-driven direct-current superconducting quantum interference device (DC-SQUID) and investigate it by numerically solving the resistively and capacitively shunted junction (RCSJ) equations. The applied flux drives a circulating supercurrent and sustains nonequilibrium phase dynamics throughout the bias-current sweep, removing the need for a fast sweep or for transient oscillations set by the initial phase. Using typical experimental device parameters, we calculate switching-current distributions (SCDs) with and without a microwave input for both driven and undriven SQUIDs. We quantify detection performance using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and their area under the curve (AUC). The simulations show that high-frequency flux drive reduces the impact of thermal noise and enables statistical discrimination of weak microwave pulses at the single-photon energy scale. We also numerically estimate detector characteristics such as phase selectivity and dynamic range.

papers.title: OrthoLatentCAD: Orthographic Spatial Latents for Hand-Drawn CAD Program Generation
papers.abstract: Freehand orthographic drawings capture early design intent, yet recovering executable sketch--extrude CAD programs from raster front, right, and top views remains challenging: noisy, dimension-free 2D layouts must be reconciled into an ordered construction history. We introduce Hand2CAD, a benchmark of 215K ABC-derived synthetic orthographic-drawing--CAD program pairs and 1,000 real three-view sets drawn by CAD-trained participants. Recovering CAD programs from orthographic drawings requires both cross-view geometric reasoning and alignment between visual features and program representations. We propose OrthoLatentCAD to address these two challenges. It fuses local geometry with global context on canonical planes, exchanges evidence between paired plane lines indexed by the same shared-axis coordinate, and maps the spatial representation to ordered program latents through queries inherited from a frozen CAD autoencoder. Across the evaluated one- to three-view configurations, OrthoLatentCAD outperforms protocol-matched baselines in procedural accuracy, compiled geometry, and CAD-kernel validity while benefiting from additional views. Without real-data fine-tuning, it also outperforms the baselines on held-out real drawings. We will release the dataset, code, and evaluation scripts.

authors.name: Xiaolei Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xinjie Zhu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Learning Continuous Scene Depth Representations via Cross-Modal Gaussian Rendering
papers.abstract: Depth super-resolution with color guidance is a fundamental problem in geometric scene understanding that aims to reconstruct high-resolution depth using structural cues from color images. In practical RGB-D systems, the resolution gap between depth and color images often varies, requiring flexible upsampling factors. However, many existing methods are designed for predefined integer scales. Although implicit methods support arbitrary-scale reconstruction, they typically rely on computationally demanding per-pixel neural decoding and may struggle to recover sharp depth boundaries and fine structures. To this end, we propose a cross-modal Gaussian rendering framework that learns continuous depth representations for arbitrary-scale depth super-resolution. Specifically, we first construct hierarchical Gaussian representations for progressive depth reconstruction, with explicit spatial support defined by learnable Gaussian primitives. Building on this representation, we design a Structure-Aware Gaussian Aggregation module that combines spatial weights with cross-modal feature affinities to reduce aggregation across depth discontinuities. We then develop a Scale-Adaptive Gaussian Rendering module that adapts Gaussian spatial kernels to the target pixel footprint. To further facilitate cross-modal learning, we propose a training strategy that gradually introduces higher-frequency guidance information during training. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method at both in-distribution and out-of-distribution upsampling scales.

authors.name: Baoliang Chen
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Shiqi Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Learning Optical Flow with Task-Oriented Feature Adaptation
papers.abstract: Learning-based optical flow estimation approaches generally rely on both inter-frame correspondence evidence and intra-frame contextual guidance, yet features from general-purpose image encoders may not fully support these roles. Strongly activated but weakly discriminative channels can outweigh more informative ones when computing inter-frame feature similarity, while context feature affinities can be low within motion-coherent regions yet high across motion boundaries. To address these mismatches, this study proposes TO-Flow, a task-oriented feature adaptation framework that aligns matching and context features with their respective requirements through dedicated channel modulation and spatial reorganization approaches. An affinity-based soft partition distinguishes motion-region interiors from boundary-adjacent regions to guide both processes. Channel modulation uses simulated flow refinement to assess whether each channel assigns higher similarity to estimated correspondences than to nearby competing candidates. The resulting similarity differences are aggregated within each region type and averaged across iterations to derive channel weights that emphasize informative channels and suppress ambiguous ones. Spatial reorganization combines affinity-guided feature attraction and repulsion from coarse to fine to simultaneously improve consistency within motion-coherent regions and distinctiveness across motion boundaries, with feature resampling mitigating boundary blurring during cross-scale fusion. Extensive experiments on the MPI Sintel, KITTI 2015, Spring, and LayeredFlow datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and general applicability of TO-Flow across diverse iterative refinement architectures as well as supervised and unsupervised training paradigms. The source code will be publicly available at https://mias.group/TO-Flow upon publication.

authors.name: Hanli Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Restorable Multilingual Voice Anonymization via Audio Watermarking
papers.abstract: Voice anonymization aims to conceal speaker identity while preserving linguistic and paralinguistic information. However, certain applications also require the ability to attribute anonymized recordings to their original speakers. Existing recovery approaches often rely on specially designed reversible anonymization systems, limiting their applicability to different anonymization architectures. In this work, we propose a post-hoc framework for restorable multilingual voice anonymization that enables speaker attribution without reconstructing the original waveform or modifying the underlying anonymization systems. Specifically, we convert 192-dimensional speaker embeddings into binary identity payloads through sign quantization and embed them into anonymized speech using a segment-wise audio watermarking strategy. Recovered payloads are subsequently matched against enrollment speaker templates for identity attribution. We evaluate the framework across four languages using two distinct anonymization backbones, BM1 and T24. Under clean conditions, the approach achieves approximately 99% exact payload recovery and 0.96% attribution EER while largely preserving the original privacy-utility performance. Experiments further show that speaker attribution remains reliable under several audio distortions despite imperfect payload recovery, although temporal rescaling severely disrupts recovery. Additional analyses reveal that watermark robustness varies across languages, carrier durations, and anonymization backbones.

papers.title: Semiclassical Weyl laws and noncommutative geometry on open manifolds with conformally cusp metrics
papers.abstract: We establish semiclassical Weyl laws on open Riemannian manifolds with conformally cusp metrics of finite volume. These metrics need not be complete, and even when complete they do not have bounded geometry. Moreover, the potentials are bounded, the discreteness of the spectrum being a consequence of the geometry rather than of a confining potential. Therefore, our results lie beyond the scope of recent semiclassical Weyl laws of Dai--Yan and Braverman. The semiclassical Weyl laws are established for fractional Schr\"odinger operators associated with Dirac operators, magnetic Laplacians, and Hodge Laplacians, under conditions of Moroianu and Gol\'enia--Moroianu which ensure that these operators have discrete spectra. We also obtain extensions of Connes' integration formula for the same operators. In addition, we deal with a class of conformally cusp metrics of infinite volume, in which case the semiclassical Weyl laws and the integration formulas only involve the values at infinity. The results are obtained by applying the abstract semiclassical Weyl laws and integration formulas for spectral triples established in a previous paper.

papers.title: Taming Fitch's and Humberstone's Paradoxes
papers.abstract: Fitch's Paradox says that if every true proposition is knowable, then every true proposition is known. Humberstone's Paradox states that if every true proposition is known by at least one of a set of finitely many agents, then some agent in that set knows every true proposition. Both paradoxes give rise to surprising and unacceptable consequences. In this paper, we diagnose a crucial tacit presupposition underlying these paradoxes, namely that the domain of propositions is closed under Boolean operations such as intersection and union, and offer a uniform resolution. We argue that the paradoxical inferences rely implicitly on this closure assumption. By adopting weak propositionally quantified modal logics that drop these closure conditions, we provide a semantically motivated account that blocks both paradoxes. The restriction on universal instantiation is not an ad hoc technical device, but reflects a conception of propositions as graspable objects of epistemic attitudes, on which the domain of propositions need not be closed under Boolean operations, since some Boolean combinations of graspable propositions may not themselves be graspable.

authors.name: Jie Fan
authors.institution: National Institute of Measurement and Testing Technology

papers.title: Cramer-Rao Bound Minimization for Discrete SIM-aided ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM) have recently emerged as a promising wave-domain signal processing architecture for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), owing to the capability of efficient beamforming with reduced number of radio-frequency chains. However, most existing SIM-aided ISAC designs rely on maximizing beampattern gain under continuous phase shifts, which cannot explicitly characterize the fundamental estimation accuracy under practical deployment. In this paper, we investigate Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) minimization problem for a discrete SIM-aided ISAC system. To tackle the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a two-stage transmit design that decouples CRB optimization from cascaded multi-layer SIM realization. In the first stage, an ideal precoder is obtained. In the second stage, it is synthesized on the practical SIM by alternating power allocation and phase-shift updates, with a closed-form discrete projection and linearized QoS constraints. Numerical results demonstrate fast convergence, reveal the sensing-communication trade-off, and verify CRB improvements with higher phase resolution and larger SIM configurations.

authors.name: Jiancheng An
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Maoyuan Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A logic of strong contingency
papers.abstract: In this paper, inspired by the notions of contingency and strong possibility, we propose a notion which may be called 'strong contingency'. This notion can be seen as a mixture of contingency and strong possibility. We investigate the logic with strong contingency as a sole primitive modality, including its bisimulation notion, expressivity, frame definability, and axiomatizations. It turns out that this logic is expressively incomparable with the standard modal logic and the logic of contingency even over the class of S5-models, and less expressive than the logic of strong possibility and weak necessity over the class of S5-models. Besides, as the introduction of the inequality into the semantics makes the completeness proof much harder, instead of showing the completeness via a canonical model construction, we reduce the soundness and strong completeness of the involved proof systems to those of the existing proof systems in the literature.

authors.name: Jie Fan
authors.institution: National Institute of Measurement and Testing Technology

papers.title: A Local-to-Global Approximation Framework for Covering Disjointness-Compliable Set Families
papers.abstract: Many network design problems can be formulated as covering a family of vertex sets by edges. We develop a local-to-global approximation framework for disjointness-compliable families with polynomial-time membership tests. A class of vertices is deficient if it belongs to the family and feasible otherwise. Our local problem seeks a minimum-cost tree that connects one deficient class to feasible classes so that their union is feasible. If this local problem admits a polynomial-time $\alpha$-approximation, then the covering problem admits a polynomial-time $(1+\varepsilon)(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{\alpha})^2$-approximation for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. Our algorithm first connects deficient vertices that are difficult to separate and then handles regions containing one deficient class at a time. To bound the total local cost, we compare the local trees with a feasible forest. We delete edges of this forest after using them in the bound, so each is counted at most once even when regions overlap. As applications, we obtain polynomial-time $(8+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithms for generalized point-to-point connection and multiroot quota tree, including multiroot $k$-minimum spanning tree. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first polynomial-time constant-factor approximations for both problems. We also obtain a randomized approximation for multiroot covering Steiner that has the same asymptotic ratio as the known approximation for its single-root version.

authors.name: Mingyu Xiao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Global large-data strong solutions to the 2D barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with linear bulk viscosity
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the global well-posedness of the two-dimensional(2D) compressible Navier--Stokes equations with density-dependent bulk viscosity and far-field vacuum. We consider the constitutive laws \(P(\rho)=\rho^\gamma\), with \(\gamma>1\), and \(\lambda(\rho)=\rho\), for which the bulk viscosity degenerates in vacuum. Under suitable regularity and weighted integrability assumptions on the initial data, and assuming only that the total mass is positive, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions without any restriction on the size of the initial energy or any radial symmetry assumption. The central difficulty is to derive an upper bound for the density on arbitrary finite time intervals in the absence of enhanced bulk dissipation. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a logarithmic energy method based on successive density levels, which exploits the dissipation accumulated along particle trajectories as the density increases. Combined with weighted estimates, pressure estimates, and the analysis of the effective viscous flux and vorticity, this method yields the density bound required to close the global continuation argument. Our result extends the large-data global strong-solution theory for density-dependent viscosity to the critical linear bulk-viscosity law in the general two-dimensional whole-space setting.

authors.name: Zhilei Liang
authors.institution: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: $\mathsf{Y} \& \mathsf{X}$: Intermediate Logics of Convex Hulls and Cross-Polytopes
papers.abstract: We investigate two logics of geometric Kripke frames: $\mathsf{Y}$, defined by finite convex hulls, and $\mathsf{X}$, defined by cross-polytopes. We characterize the validity of the Kreisel--Putnam axiom on convex hull frames by means of convex independence. Our main technical results concern several reductions obtained using two translations, $C$ and $D$. In particular, we show that $\mathsf{X}$ is invariant under $C$, while $\mathsf{Y}$ is invariant under $D$. Moreover, the same translation $D$ reduces Medvedev logic to every logic in the interval $[\mathsf{Y}',\mathsf{Med}]$, where $\mathsf{Y}'$ is a naturally defined intermediate logic strictly between $\mathsf{Y}$ and $\mathsf{Med}$. Together with geometric arguments, these reductions establish that $\mathsf{Y}$, $\mathsf{X}$, and $\mathsf{Cheq}$ are pairwise incomparable, while each lies strictly between $\mathsf{PL}$ and Medvedev logic. We also prove that every logic in $[\mathsf{Y},\mathsf{Med}]$ is not finitely axiomatizable and that this interval contains continuum many distinct logics. In addition, every logic in $[\mathsf{Y}',\mathsf{Med}]$ is undecidable. We prove that $\mathsf{X}$ is undecidable and $\mathsf{Y}\in \Pi^0_1$. In particular, we show that it is decidable whether a finite poset is isomorphic to a finite convex hull frame, and that the logics determined by configurations of a bounded number of points are decidable. Finally, we extend our study to infinite convex hull frames. We show that inclusion yields $\mathsf{KC}$, whereas reverse inclusion yields $\mathsf{IPC}$. For the latter result, we use the Cantor set to construct $p$-morphisms onto arbitrary finite rooted frames.

papers.title: A Determinant Proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo Conjecture
papers.abstract: We give an elementary proof of the determinant identity in \cite[Conjecture~A.1]{SYZ} over any field of odd characteristic $p$. The proof computes the determinant of a single linear map by dividing by two different monic polynomials. By \cite[Proposition~A.9]{SYZ}, the identity gives another proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo conjecture. The conjecture identifies the Higgs--de Rham self-map of the four-pointed projective line with the map induced by multiplication by $p$ on its elliptic double cover.

authors.name: Jinbang Yang
authors.institution: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Counting Symbols on Technical Drawings: A Benchmark and Verified Rewards for MLLMs
papers.abstract: Today's MLLMs can count objects in natural images. However, when asking them how many bolt holes appear in a mechanical drawing or how many nitrogen atoms are in a chemical structure, they often struggle. Counting in technical drawings remains challenging, as objects can be small, densely packed, or even implied by drawing conventions. To study this problem, we introduce CountDrawBench, a benchmark including floor plans, electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, and molecular structures, with 1,574 counting questions and instance-level annotations where available. Besides evaluation, we introduce Code-Verified RL, a reinforcement learning framework that teaches MLLMs to count with executable feedback. Our method combines three complementary rewards: a count reward that checks the final answer, an instance-matching reward that verifies object locations, and a zoom-based reward that checks counting consistency across local image regions. All three are integrated into a unified GRPO objective. Extensive experiments reveal that even leading MLLMs struggle on CountDrawBench, with the best evaluated model achieving only 59.3% accuracy. Our method improves Qwen3.5-9B from 49.3% to 54.3% accuracy, outperforming all evaluated open-source baselines. These results establish CountDrawBench as a challenging testbed for technical drawing understanding and demonstrate the value of code-verified rewards in these tasks. Code and data will be released upon acceptance.

authors.name: Junxian Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Ruixuan Yang
authors.institution: Guizhou University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: AgroVG+: Generalized Visual Grounding in Agriculture with Region-Supervised Action Generation
papers.abstract: Generalized visual grounding in agriculture requires localizing all objects that match a natural-language description and recognizing when no matching target is present. We introduce AgroVG+, a dataset whose referring expressions are all written and reviewed by agricultural experts based on image content and corresponding target sets. The dataset comprises 7,404 images and 10,081 query records across six agricultural scene families, covering single-target, multi-target, and target-absent cases. We also propose ReSAG (Region-Supervised Action Generation), a framework that couples regional evidence supervision with explicit box-generation and termination decisions. ReSAG assigns each target an equally weighted supervision term on a shared spatial evidence distribution computed before answer generation. The BOX/END protocol exposes a choice between generating another box and terminating the response at box boundaries, while coordinates are generated using the original language vocabulary. Regional and sequence objectives jointly train a shared language decoder. On AgroVG+, ReSAG outperforms coordinate-only fine-tuning on single- and multi-target exact-set accuracy, and achieves higher aggregate accuracy than either component alone in ablations.

papers.title: The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula for CM elliptic curves of analytic rank one
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula for elliptic curves over the field of rational numbers with complex multiplication and analytic rank one.

authors.name: Ruichen Xu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Which Loopholes Get Found? Predicting Reward Hacking of LLM Judges Before RL Training
papers.abstract: A policy trained against an LLM judge can learn to exploit its loopholes. Static probes show that such judges accept degenerate answers like a lone "{" or "Thought process:", but not which flaw a policy will find. In GRPO the first loophole to be exploited can be predicted before training from each pattern's exposure, the product of the starting policy's propensity to produce it and the judge's false-positive rate (FPR). To test exposure causally, we seed the patterns into fine-tuning at three doses in a Latin square. Across 36 GRPO runs with seven judges, the first exploited pattern had the highest exposure in all 12 runs with exploitation and the highest FPR in only 6. Predictions recorded before training held in three of four runs with one pattern masked by rule. When only two patterns were seeded, at 3% to 3.8% of the fine-tuning data and chosen so that exposure disagreed with FPR alone or propensity alone, exposure named the first exploited pattern and its onset window in all six runs. Exploitation occurred only on hard prompts, where an accepted exploit gets a large group-normalized advantage. Auditing exposure before RL therefore identifies the loophole a policy will likely exploit first.

authors.name: Yuezhou Zhao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Dynamics Forcing: Mitigating Error Accumulation in Causal Video World Models
papers.abstract: Causal video world models generate block by block from their own previous outputs. Small errors in early blocks are fed back as history and grow until the scene and the robot fall apart. Teacher forcing trains on clean ground-truth history, so the model never sees the history it will actually condition on, and it also finds a shortcut: copying the previous frame instead of predicting how the scene changes. We present Dynamics Forcing, a training scheme that keeps real video as the only supervision and reshapes how history is presented. History is perturbed in three ways: random noising, self-resampling by the model itself, and joint denoising, in which the most recent blocks are still partly noisy when the next block is predicted. On top of this we move history guidance and first-frame anchor guidance from inference into training, so that the model is pushed to use its history and its reference frame rather than ignore them. Dynamics Forcing needs no teacher model, no distillation, and no additional model at inference. Applied to a 5B video model with LoRA on 77 hours of manipulation video on a single GPU, it better matches unseen real continuations and reduces error accumulation.

authors.name: Xin Zhou
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Cong Miao
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: MobileGrail: Learning Compact Guardrails for On-Device deployable Mobile GUI Agent Safety
papers.abstract: Runtime guardrails protect mobile GUI agents by assessing each proposed action before execution, but existing guardrails rely on cloud hosted large multimodal models, exposing every screen to a remote server, including private information such as payments, messages, and medical records. We propose MobileGrail, an on-device deployable model that addresses both. It maintains a recurrent task state that retains only the evidence subsequent safety decisions depend on, so that authorization and execution progress persist beyond the short context. To intervene early while keeping the safety boundary precise, it learns two labels, unsafe and block: unsafe marks the action that commits a violation, whereas block may be issued at any step of an intervention window, which spans from the first action that the user's authorization no longer explains to the committing action itself. To support training, we build an environment of 32 applications whose backends verify the effect of every action, supplying verified labels for supervision and rewards for reinforcement learning to calibrate intervention timing. We also build MobileVeto, an offline benchmark of unsafe trajectories largely on held-out applications, each paired with a benign counterpart. On MobileVeto, MobileGrail built on Qwen3.5-2B intercepts 76.2% of violations, up from 64.5% for its prompted backbone, while reducing premature intervention from 58.6% to 5.2%, outperforming the cloud-based OS-Sentinel on both. We further conduct online evaluation on GhostEIBench, where MobileGrail guarding a Qwen3.8-27B agent reduces fully successful attacks from 13 to 3 of 110 tasks while raising task completion from 48 to 58. Quantized to 4 bits, MobileGrail runs on a Snapdragon 8 Elite at a median latency of 4.7 s, comparable to the 5.1s of cloud-hosted Gemini 3.8 Flash.

authors.name: Yuankai Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Global strong solvability of the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes equations for large initial data
papers.abstract: In 1995, Kazhikhov and Vaigant introduced a two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes model with constant shear viscosity and bulk viscosity $\lambda(\rho)=\rho^\beta$. For $\beta>3$, they proved global existence of smooth solutions for arbitrarily large initial data with strictly positive density. More recently, Fan-Jiang-Li-L\"u (arXiv:2611.20264, 2026) proved global strong solvability for every $\beta>1$ in bounded simply connected domains with Navier-slip boundary conditions. In this article, we prove global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to the Kazhikhov-Vaigant model on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ at the critical point $\beta=1$, for every $\gamma>1$ and arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum.

authors.name: Jie Fan
authors.institution: National Institute of Measurement and Testing Technology

papers.title: The Optimal D.C. Bound Is Dominated by the Reciprocal of the Lov\'asz Theta Number
papers.abstract: We resolve a question left open by Anstreicher and Burer (J. Global Optim. 33, 299--312, 2005). For the standard quadratic formulation of the stability number, we prove that the optimal difference-of-convex (D.C.) bound is at most the reciprocal of the Lov\'asz theta number. The dominance is strict whenever the Lov\'asz theta number is not exact.

papers.title: The Answer Is Not the State: Trajectory-Level Corrigibility in Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models generate tokens at many positions on a shared canvas, making unfinished responses appear revisable. We find a counterexample: after the final answer is reopened, previously generated rationale can reconstruct the old decision despite newly available evidence. We isolate this effect by comparing reopening the answer alone with reopening both rationale and answer, and by exchanging rationales between paired trajectories. On a 150-question source-disjoint benchmark, reopening both regions makes decisions follow the evidence currently present--whether correct or deliberately corrupted--across Dream, LLaDA, and iLLaDA. On a new 100-question free-form short-answer evaluation, the same effect remains strong in LLaDA and iLLaDA but is negligible in Dream. Coherent transplanted rationales steer rebuilt decisions, while token-level attribution improves which positions to reopen without producing a compact repair. Corrigibility therefore depends on retained rationale state, not answer openness alone.

authors.name: Junchi Liao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Wentao Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Scoring L2 Pronunciation Without Synthesis: Counterfactual Velocity Contrast in Frozen Flow-Matching TTS
papers.abstract: Flow-matching text-to-speech (TTS) models learn how native speakers realize a text, yet this knowledge is used only for synthesis. We show that a frozen TTS model can score non-native (L2) pronunciation without generating audio. For a learner utterance, we compare the model's velocity-prediction error under the target text with its error under a counterfactual text (dropped or swapped) on the same noised input; the difference behaves like a generative goodness-of-pronunciation score. The signal is confined to a narrow band of high-noise timesteps, which a native-speech criterion locates and a closed-form rule transfers across backbones. On speaker-disjoint speechocean762, four frozen TTS models reach $r{=}0.58$--$0.63$ with human scores, within the range of zero-shot ASR and phone-level baselines, and adding them to those baselines in a label-free fusion raises $r$ from $0.698$ to $0.757$. Cached frame scores also flag word-level errors at no extra TTS cost.

papers.title: Spiking World-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict how the world responds to actions and offer a promising path toward general embodied intelligence, but they are large and run the network many times per plan, so they are hard to deploy on robots. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) compute with sparse binary spikes and use additions instead of multiplications, which saves power. However, existing WAMs use dense videos as the world state, so a spiking version would spend most of its computation on the background. We therefore introduce SpikingWAM, the first spiking WAM, which uses a sparse task skeleton as the world state. Inspired by biological motor control, which attends only to the key positions of a task, the Task Skeleton State (TSS) keeps the keypoints of the arm and the task objects, and a small spiking front end estimates the object keypoints from images. Body Frame Spike Coding (BFSC) and Grid Coincidence Attention (GCA) keep millimetre precision, and the Persistent Single Step Readout (PSR) runs the network once per plan. On the simulated benchmarks LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0, SpikingWAM achieves competitive success rates with far less energy than ANN methods and surpasses all compared methods on LIBERO-Plus. Real robot experiments further confirm its effectiveness. These results show that a task skeleton lets spiking networks implement WAMs at very low energy, offering a new solution for low power embodied intelligence. Project page: https://wxqnl.github.io/spikingwam/

authors.name: Malu Zhang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Accelerating interatomic potential development through student-driven exploration and reliability-aware distillation
papers.abstract: Conventional two-stage distillation first establishes a teacher through teacher-driven configuration exploration, a costly first stage for complex materials, and then uses its predictions to supervise students, potentially propagating teacher-label errors. Here, we propose distillation-driven teacher-student co-evolution (DICE), which uses a fast student to accelerate configuration exploration and replaces the fixed teacher-to-student sequence with alternating student and teacher updates. A representation-based support-assessment algorithm routes high-support configurations to teacher labelling and selects low-support configurations for density functional theory (DFT) calculations to update the teacher, thereby reducing the risk of teacher-label error propagation to students. Across Al2O3 (structural ceramics), yttria-stabilised zirconia (solid electrolytes) and MIL-120(Al) (a metal-organic framework), DICE develops reliable compact potentials using only 140-494 target DFT reference configurations per system; total recorded student exploration times per system are just 2.6-5.1% of the corresponding teacher-driven estimates. Combining computational efficiency with broad applicability across diverse material systems, DICE provides a practical route to developing reliable compact interatomic potentials.

authors.name: Haotian Huang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A New Perspective on ANN-to-SNN Conversion: Hardware-Aligned Multi-Threshold Neuron Dynamics for Neuromorphic Inference
papers.abstract: By accumulating spikes over multiple timesteps, rate coding approximates the real-valued activations of an ANN, a principle that underpins numerous ANN-to-SNN conversion methods. However, the converted SNNs typically incur loss in accuracy compared to the original ANN. Existing methods either increase a number of timesteps or introduce more complex neuronal dynamics to reduce this accuracy gap. Yet, both approaches ultimately lead to the same outcome: redundancy either in information or in computation, thereby suffering from efficiency degradation. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{PRIME} (\underline{P}otential-\underline{R}esidual \underline{I}ntegration for \underline{M}ulti-threshold \underline{E}ncoding), a multi-threshold concurrent spiking neuron framework redesigned from a hardware data representation perspective:a) We introduce the Residual Membrane Potential Amplification (RMPA) mechanism, which replaces rate coding with Integration Coding by actively amplifying the residual membrane potential. RMPA enables the binary representation of spikes to carry substantially more information, achieving near-lossless conversion with as few as two timesteps.b) Complementarily, we implement concurrent spike firing in multi-threshold neurons, where spikes are decoded directly from the binary representation of floating-point data, eliminating membrane potential--threshold comparisons and replacing multiplications with lightweight bit-shift and accumulation operations that align with hardware computation primitives. At $T=2$ and $D=3$, we achieve competitive performance across both vision and language benchmarks with only 40.6\% of the FP32 bit-transmission cost and 13.4\% of the FP32 multiplication energy consumption. The PRIME framework establishes a new design principle for efficient ANN-to-SNN conversion, bridging the gap between algorithmic efficiency and hardware constraints.

authors.name: Chenxiao Dou
authors.institution: China Academy of Electronics and Information Technology

authors.name: Malu Zhang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: SceneCast: Learning Indoor Scene Synthesis from Curated Synthetic Videos with LLM Reward
papers.abstract: 3D indoor scene synthesis requires generating objects to form a complete and coherent scene. Existing approaches rely heavily on manually annotated datasets, leading to high costs and limited generalization. We present SceneCast, an annotation-free framework that trains on large-scale, unlabeled videos, addressing two key challenges: (1) Videos provide only partial views of a scene, requiring the model to extrapolate unseen 3D regions, which is inherently error-prone; (2) Raw videos available online are uncurated, suffering from uncontrolled conditions and variable data quality. First, we design a Transformer-based model that predicts objects sequentially and is fine-tuned with reinforcement learning (RL), where an LLM acts as a spatial common-sense evaluator. The LLM provides reward signals through chain-of-thought reasoning and code-executable geometric checks to refine object configurations. Second, we introduce \trim, a data curation approach that generates training videos with controllable video generation models. Crucially, it retains only high-quality prefix clips via multi-criteria quality assessment with an entropy-based weighting strategy. Evaluated on curated synthetic video sets, our annotation-free approach outperforms state-of-the-art supervised methods in scene quality.

authors.name: Haoran Xu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Gyroidal Magnetic Order with Weyl Magnons
papers.abstract: The gyroid, a triply periodic minimal surface found widely in nature and materials, has remained largely unexplored as a design principle for magnetic order. We introduce gyroidal magnetic order on the hyperoctagon lattice, the skeletal network of the gyroid, in which each magnetic moment points along the local $C_3$ axis that coincides with the local normal to the gyroid surface. The resulting noncoplanar spin texture constitutes a direct magnetic imprint of the gyroid geometry. We show that this order can be stabilized by single-ion anisotropy, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, or the symmetric off-diagonal $\Gamma$ interaction combined with the Kitaev interaction, and remains robust against quantum fluctuations. Its magnon spectrum hosts symmetry-enforced pseudospin-1 and pseudospin-1/2 Weyl points that, unlike their electronic counterparts, persist under symmetry-allowed perturbations. Our results establish the gyroid as a geometric platform for magnetic order and symmetry-enforced topological magnon excitations.

authors.name: Kiyu Fukui
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Passivity-Based Decentralized Stability Criterion and Active-Damping Design for DC Microgrids
papers.abstract: Interactions among converter-interfaced devices can destabilize DC microgrids (DCMGs). In practice, detailed device models often cannot be disclosed to the system operator for centralized stability analysis, and only some device controllers can be redesigned. This paper develops an output-feedback passivity (OFP)-based decentralized small-signal stability criterion for DCMGs with both fixed-controller and tunable-controller devices. By incorporating the certified OFP indices of fixed-controller devices into an equivalent network, the criterion quantifies a locally verifiable OFP requirement for each tunable-controller device. Full-order analysis further reveals that the finite current-loop bandwidth imposes upper bounds on the OFP indices of droop-controlled converters, which can remain negative for any PI gains despite positive predictions based on reduced-order analysis. Guided by the criterion and these bounds, an OFP-oriented active damping (OFP-AD) strategy is proposed for these converters. The proposed strategy improves the OFP index toward the required value while preserving the cascaded PI control and droop characteristics, using output-capacitor-current feedback. Case studies on a 39-node DCMG validate the proposed criterion and OFP-AD.

papers.title: When Do Spatial Plans Help Text-to-Image Generation? Causal Control, System Utility, and Text Responsiveness
papers.abstract: A generator can follow a spatial plan, but the benefit of supplying that plan depends on what the model can already do from text. In a controlled study with 18 paired training seeds, correcting predicted positions and sizes improves spatial intersection-over-union by 0.030, yet direct text is non-inferior at matched training compute. In a pretrained generator, a fixed rule layout improves two-object task success over the same text-only adapter by 12.50 percentage points, mostly by separating objects that already appear in the correct order. We then ask whether a more precise instruction can achieve the same separation across conditioning paths. On 288 new task families, adding a minimum-gap instruction improves success by 37.15 points with the text-only adapter, by at most 0.69 points with widely spaced regions, and by 6.94 points with tightly spaced regions. Under tight regions, 230 of 288 baseline images have the correct objects and direction yet miss the required gap, ruling out a high baseline success rate as the sole explanation for the weak text response.

papers.title: RoboInF: A Benchmark for Instruction Fidelity in Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Precise language control requires embodied models to follow instructions governing both task outcomes and execution. Although recent methods train policies to follow increasingly detailed commands, existing benchmarks often assess instruction following alongside perception, planning, and generalization to unfamiliar scenes. Higher task success therefore offers limited evidence of closer adherence to instructions. We introduce RoboInF, a benchmark measuring how reliably manipulation policies adapt their behavior to changes in an instruction. For each of eight tasks, six to twelve expert-validated instruction branches vary the requested goal, procedure, or manipulation detail while holding the initial scene and robot state fixed. Task-specific checkers verify the terminal goal and use recorded trajectories, contacts, and event sequences to assess compliance throughout execution. The accompanying RoboInF-4K dataset pairs 4,242 expert demonstrations with simulator-derived annotations of motion and contact. We evaluate leading manipulation policies ($\pi_{0.5}$ and OpenWAM) and inference-only agents (GPT-6 Astra and Qwen3.8-Flash). All four models exhibit a gap between task completion and faithful execution, indicating substantial room for fine-grained instruction following.

authors.name: Yu Huang
authors.institution: Nanjing General Hospital of Nanjing Military Command

authors.name: Dijiang Dong
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: A new frequency-time hybrid RPML-BIE solver with few-mode corrections for the wave-equation problems in nonuniform closed waveguides
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to proposing a novel FTH integral equation solver for wave-equation problems in two-dimensional nonuniform closed waveguides with multiple channels. The FTH methodology, which combines the Fourier transform with frequency-domain BIE formulations, has demonstrated its effectiveness in solving time-dependent wave scattering problems. However, when applied to waveguide problems, the modal expansions arising from multiple scattering introduce cut-off frequencies. Such frequencies pose significant challenges, requiring both a frequency-robust solver for frequency-domain waveguide problems and an efficient treatment of the solution's non-smooth behavior near the cut-off frequencies for the evaluation of the inverse Fourier transform. The first issue is addressed by developing a new frequency-domain BIE method based on the free-space fundamental solution and regionalized perfectly matched layer truncation, together with a few-mode Dirichlet-to-Robin modification. The method is rigorously proved to achieve uniform exponential convergence, even at frequencies arbitrarily close to the cut-off frequencies. To address the second issue---the recovery of the time-domain solution via the inverse Fourier transform---a sine-transform based stationary-point Filon--Clenshaw--Curtis quadrature is introduced to accurately handle the non-smoothness and square-root singularities of frequency-domain solutions. Additionally, theoretical result shows that the complex resonances closing to the real axis may significantly effect the convergence of the Fourier transform algorithm and then a novel strategy of complex resonance extraction based on AAA rational approximation and singularity subtraction is utilized to avoid this influence. Numerical experiments for both frequency-domain and time-domain problems illustrate the efficiency and high accuracy of the proposed method.

papers.title: Motion on Demand: Adaptive Optical Excitation for Event Cameras
papers.abstract: Event cameras respond only to brightness changes, so whether an edge is visible depends on image motion perpendicular to it---a motion that constantly shifts with camera and scene dynamics. Rotating a wedge prism in front of the lens introduces controlled image motion to reveal static or slow edges. However, a fixed rotation speed cannot adapt to changing motion conditions: when natural motion is already sufficient, additional optical excitation generates redundant events and introduces unnecessary alignment errors. Inspired by the division of labor between fast haltere feedforward and slower visual feedback in fly gaze control, we present EvGaze, an event camera system that adaptively regulates prism rotation speed. EvGaze employs a learned multimodal controller that integrates luminance, event, and inertial observations, with a fast inertial pathway that refines speed decisions between visual updates. To preserve geometric consistency during speed changes, we compensate for prism-induced image motion at individual event timestamps using measured encoder angles. On EvMotion, EvGaze recovers more edges than full-speed prism rotation with 39% fewer events. On DSEC with simulated optical modulation, it reaches 0.73 feature-tracking success (compared with 0.55 on native events and 0.67 at 180 RPM) while generating 26% fewer events than 360 RPM. Real-device experiments further demonstrate online closed-loop adaptation, reducing average event rates by 17% relative to full-speed rotation.

authors.name: Zhenyu Tang
authors.institution: Hunan University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Wangbo Yu
authors.institution: Beijing Chao-Yang Hospital, Capital Medical University

authors.name: Li Yuan
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: A mean index criterion for multiple closed characteristics
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$. We prove that a compact strictly star-shaped $C^3$ hypersurface in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ carries at least $n$ geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics if all iterates are nondegenerate and all mean indices are at least one. It suffices that all mean indices are positive and that the bound holds only for prime characteristics with negative mean Euler characteristic in the variational grading. The proof uses a minimum argument for the global Morse remainder and requires no individual index exclusion. For odd $n\ge3$, we obtain a smaller, dimension-dependent strict bound when good iterates of Maslov-type index $-1$ are excluded. Irrational ellipsoids show that the multiplicity bound is sharp.

papers.title: Predicting Rare-Mode Collapse in Recursive Generative Training from Single-Generation Calibration
papers.abstract: Recursive generative training can preserve sample counts in a rare region while silently eroding its characteristic core. Mapping this finite-horizon collapse across real-data quotas, rare prevalences, and feedback perturbations via exhaustive multi-generation chains is computationally prohibitive. We develop a decoupled framework that forecasts multi-generation collapse probabilities and locates operating risk boundaries from independent single-generation conditional fits alone. Pairing an exact three-source multinomial count law with single-generation response banks propagates count marginals in closed form, backed by explicit calibration-error and boundary-resolution bounds. For additive Gaussian perturbations, we further prove that equal-variance all-row and sparse policies reverse their boundary-crossing order at a unique hyperplane distance. Across a 2,178-setting count benchmark, exact propagation cuts risk mean absolute error (MAE) from 1.85 to 0.49 percentage points (pp). Across ten two-dimensional learners, calibration achieves 2.60--5.69~pp six-round core MAE on nine stationary learners (65--81\% below an unperturbed baseline), diagnoses non-stationary outlier drift in standard DDIM (16.38~pp) via a stability probe, and resolves the predicted six-round geometric reversal. On Fashion-MNIST latent flow-matching chains, calibration outperforms direct-chain Gaussian-process interpolation at lower fit budgets and tracks the 20\% latent-perturbation boundary shift (3.14 versus 10.78~pp MAE for proportion copying) driven by opposing inflow to the rare region and outflow from its core.

papers.title: Which Loans, Not How Many: Exactly Level-Invariant, Anytime-Valid Monitoring of Deployed Risk Models
papers.abstract: A refinancing wave can change the number of mortgage prepayments without changing the relationship between scores and prepayment. In a logistic model, conditioning on the monthly count removes the intercept from the likelihood of which loans prepay. Our fixed-start slope product tests a lower bound on the calibration slope. At threshold 20 its probability of ever crossing under the null is at most 5%. The restarted level sum tracks departures from intercept tolerance. A confidence sequence estimates a constant slope, and the restart-intersection rule detects changes in that slope. A continuous mixture avoids the off-grid width floor of a discrete prior. On Freddie Mac loans, fixed-slope resampling reproduces 78% of maintained-model monthly AUC variance in development and 70% in the holdout (95% intervals 57-100% and 48-100%). From fresh holdout starts, the restarted level sum crosses on both paths, and the fixed-start slope product stays below threshold on both. The restart-intersection rule signals a downward change for the frozen model in April 2018 and an upward change for the maintained model in a supplementary run in August 2019.

papers.title: A Viscosity-Decoupled Uzawa Lattice Boltzmann Method for Incompressible Flows Across Reynolds Numbers
papers.abstract: Conventional lattice Boltzmann methods (LBMs) tie viscosity to collision relaxation, which induces diffusive stiffness at low Reynolds numbers, non-hydrodynamic instabilities at high Reynolds numbers, and passband breakdown in variable-relaxation dual-time schemes, whereas continuum incompressible solvers require global pressure-Poisson solves every step. We propose a Viscosity-Decoupled Uzawa Lattice Boltzmann Method (VDU-LBM) in D2Q9 and D3Q19 that permanently fixes collision at unit relaxation under smooth harmonic scaling and clears pre-collision non-conserved kinetic memory in one sweep. Constant, heterogeneous, and Smagorinsky eddy viscosities enter through a parameter-free post-streaming bond-symmetric momentum-flux lift that conserves discrete momentum pairwise without perturbing continuity. Variable-step BDF1/BDF2 marching is accelerated by a matrix-free local polynomial Uzawa smoother on the $(d+1)$ conserved moments, paired with link-wise Bouzidi curved walls and shifted ghost open boundaries. Across $\mathrm{Re}\in[10^{-4},10^6]$, VDU-LBM achieves smooth low-Mach second-order space--time accuracy, accelerates unsteady DFG 2D-2 shedding per cycle by $14.27\times\text{--}15.85\times$ over matched 20-core OpenFOAM-v2412, and lowers $256^3$ $\mathrm{Re}=1600$ resolved enstrophy error by $2.25\times$ versus hybrid recursive regularized LBM. On an NVIDIA A100 GPU, the fused D3Q19 solver attains $80.9\%\text{--}85.5\%$ of measured copy bandwidth in multi-pass port traffic and cuts bounded-relaxation diffusive step cost at high viscosity contrasts.

authors.name: Yaolong Yu
authors.institution: Suzhou University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Aegis: A Conversational Prototype for Lung Cancer Risk Information and Follow-up
papers.abstract: Collecting self-reported risk information and maintaining continuity between assessment, explanation, and follow-up are practical components of a lung cancer screening workflow. We present Aegis, a browser-based research prototype that combines a conversational questionnaire, rule-based risk categorization, downloadable reports, retrieval-augmented health information, and doctor-user communication. A session-oriented controller manages question progression and clarification, while a language model assists with answer validation. Structured responses are passed to a separate risk-analysis module, and reports are linked to user and session records through Firebase services. The project adopts a multi-agent design that separates information collection, validation, assessment, and report generation. Its documented verification scope comprises 45 functional test specifications covering account management, questionnaire interaction, reporting, doctor-side review, and consultation. The available evaluation describes workflow behavior qualitatively; it provides no per-case execution results, clinical cohort, predictive-performance measurements, or comparative experiments. We therefore present Aegis as an engineering prototype for organizing risk information and follow-up, with clinical validity and the benefits of its agent-based design remaining unestablished.
