papers.title: Quaternary games with infinite mis\`ere quotients
papers.abstract: We study the four wild quaternary games left open by the earlier work of Plambeck and Siegel. For \texttt{0.3102} we discover a special regularity of its two--heap case, give a complete solution of the two--heap case, and deduce from it that its mis\`ere quotient is infinite. For \texttt{0.3122} and \texttt{0.3123} we rigorously prove, by slice--wise algebraic periodicity and hierarchical induction (computer--assisted), that their mis\`ere quotients are infinite. For \texttt{0.3312}, as well as many other wild quaternary games, we carry out computations and observations.

papers.title: Tissot indicatrix for location encoders: Characterizing local distortion in learned geographic embeddings
papers.abstract: With the increasing adoption of geographic artificial intelligence, location encoders are widely used to map geographic coordinates to learned embeddings for tasks in Earth observation and geospatial modeling. Similar to map projections, location encoders can distort geographic space, that is, equal-distance displacements in different directions can result in unequal embedding changes. However, such distortion remains largely unexamined, and it can propagate into downstream applications. We adapt Tissot's indicatrix, a cartographic tool for map projection distortion, to characterize this distortion. At each location, we compare encoder outputs at equal distances in 32 directions and fit a tensor, represented by an ellipse, whose elongation (anisotropy) and orientation describe the local distortion. The fit requires only encoder outputs without access to model internals and is validated against references with known geometry. By applying the method to thirteen released checkpoints of five encoder families, we find that distortions vary across space and inherit the input geometry to varying degrees, closely in GeoCLIP with its Equal Earth input (anisotropy correlation of 0.88) and weakly or moderately in the other encoders. The distortion also affects the locations an encoder treats as neighbors. Within 1km of 20 query sites, the 40 nearest neighbors in geographic and embedding space overlap by a median of only 57.5--87.5% across the checkpoints, while the fitted ellipses select exactly the same embedding neighbors in 265 of 299 comparisons. These findings provide a geographic basis for assessing location encoders, and the accompanying eTissot package implements the methods for user-specified encoders.

papers.title: RxnScope: Accurate joint generation of product and transition-state pairs from reactants via flow matching
papers.abstract: Reaction networks are central to understanding chemical reactivity and guiding reaction design. Constructing them when products are unknown remains a major challenge in computational chemistry, requiring the identification of products and their corresponding transition states (TSs) across elementary steps. Here, we introduce RxnScope, a flow-matching framework that jointly generates paired product-TS geometries from reactants, conditioned on a potentially reactive region. Directed product-to-TS coupling allows evolving rather than fixed product geometries to guide TS generation, while paired outputs enable product-topology ranking to prioritize candidates for validation. RxnScope recovered and validated 95.8% of reference pathways on Transition1x, performed robustly on multicomponent reactions and enabled multistep pathway exploration. In automatic reaction discovery, it achieved low-energy pathway coverage comparable to that of the single-ended growing string method while using only about 2% of its computational cost. These results establish joint product-TS generation as a new strategy for exploring reaction networks from reactants.

authors.name: Yanyang Li
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Shuhua Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Packing Stern into L2: GPU-Accelerated Primal-Shortened ISD for High-Codimension Binary Goppa Key Recovery
papers.abstract:
Primal-Shortened Information-Set Decoding (ISD) with quadratic polar lifting recently pushed TII McEliece Track-2 key recovery to $mt=126$ (TII-228, $2{,}463$ CPU core-hours), with over $99\%$ of runtime spent harvesting weight-$(2t+1)$ codewords. Porting MiniMax's Mode-6 Stern sampler directly to one block per SM leaves $1.0\text{-}1.5\text{ GB}$ of hash tables active and stalls on global memory. For $mt \le 145$, we pack all $mt-17 \le 128$ remaining syndrome bits into one $16$-byte ulonglong2 without left-triple indices, share $G \in \{4, 8\}$ cooperative tables inside GPU L2 cache, batch $64G$ random systematic reductions per launch, and widen the shortening prefix $n'$ to cut modeled GPU-hours by $34\%\text{-}47\%$.
  Across four Track-2 challenges ($mt = 108 \to 144$), every recovered private key passes both the official SageMath checker and a standalone pure-Python verifier. Eight Modal L40S GPUs solve TII-228 ($mt=126$) in $18.9\text{ min}$ ($2.15$ GPU-hours, $3.0\times$ faster in wall-clock than MiniMax's EPYC cluster). We further recover keys for the previously undocumented challenges TII-237 ($mt=135$, $22.1$ L4 GPU-hours) and TII-235 ($mt=144$, $4.30\text{ h}$ across ten L40S GPUs, $39.62$ GPU-hours, $17.97\text{ s}$ lift), using $127$ of $128$ packed bits. These results do not demonstrate practical recovery against Classic McEliece parameters ($mt \ge 768$).

papers.title: CARE-3D: Reinforcement Learning for Evidence Grounded Agentic Reasoning in Situated 3D Scenes
papers.abstract: Situated 3D reasoning requires embodied agents to interpret objects, scene geometry, and viewpoint dependent spatial relations. Existing methods learn grounded interactions from supervised traces, but largely imitate prescribed evidence acquisition patterns rather than optimizing the support that the returned evidence provides for the correct answer. Moreover, outcome rewards provide limited credit for intermediate tool choices and may leave infrequent tools underexplored. An effective agent should instead adaptively decide what to ground, which tool to invoke, and how to assess the utility of returned evidence. To this end, this paper presents CARE-3D, a reinforcement post-training framework for adaptive grounded reasoning. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on grounding instructions first establishes valid interactions, after which Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) optimizes the agent while keeping the 3D grounding module frozen. CARE-3D combines Counterfactual Attribution of Returned Evidence for evidence sensitive credit assignment, and Group Coverage Sampling to preserve tool coverage. Experiments on MSQA and Beacon3D show consistent gains over SFT and GRPO using only answer and format rewards, especially in spatial reasoning and grounding answer coherence. Our code is available at \href{https://github.com/xiaoqian-UQ/CARE-3D}{CARE-3D}.

authors.name: Xiaoqian Hu
authors.institution: The Affiliated Yongchuan Hospital of Chongqing Medical University

papers.title: A Constructive Lower Bound for the Growth Constant of Ternary Cap Sets
papers.abstract: Let $r_3(d)$ denote the maximum size of a cap set in $\mathbb{F}_3^d$. We prove that the exponential growth constant $\Lambda = \lim_{d\to\infty} r_3(d)^{1/d}$ is strictly greater than $2.22920646813$. The main advance comes from combining two-color recursive synchronization with cross-layer joint filling of a seven-dimensional local alphabet that contains collinear triples (lines). By encoding marked positions as $14$-step closed walks on a two-state directed graph, any zero-sum triple with a fixed outermost color is forced to choose the identical closed walk---and hence the identical record---at every recursive layer, at a net cost of $1000$ dimensions per level. Because the open seven-dimensional coordinates are deferred to the outermost layer, all positions of the same type across all layers can be pooled per record and filled jointly via grouped binary-flag nodes. A $2\times 2$ transfer matrix governs the weighted record count, and spectral dominance over two tilted tail matrices converts this count into a capacity lower bound. Feeding each resulting bound back into the filling parameters iteratively amplifies the growth rate, while a companion-path score exclusion test further enlarges the admissible walk family. The final bound is certified by finite enumeration and exact integer comparisons.

papers.title: Counterfactual Velocity Steering for World Action Models
papers.abstract: Flow-based robot policies generate actions by repeatedly evaluating a conditional velocity field, so test-time bias correction seems simple: query the action expert under a task-agnostic condition and subtract that velocity from the task-conditioned prediction. We show this is often wrong. On Fast-WAM across 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, mean-instruction predictions align strongly with task-conditioned velocities (cosine approximately 0.94-0.95). Averaging eight completed-state references barely cancels this direction: their mean norm is 98.3% of the mean individual norm. References thus contain a large shared transport component, not only harmful bias, and aggressive subtraction damages generation. We propose a same-state diagnostic and shrinkage analysis showing that the optimal correction scale depends on reference signal-to-noise. This motivates geometry-calibrated action debiasing, which removes only the component orthogonal to the task velocity and predicts a small task-dependent scale from instruction geometry. In controlled RoboTwin experiments, corrupting instructions still permits 25.1% success (50 tasks, 20 episodes), whereas dynamic visual corruption nearly eliminates success. A fixed centered orthogonal correction reaches 92.7% versus a 92.1% baseline in one randomized 1000-trial sweep, but gains are non-monotonic and within run-to-run variation. An angular scale pilot has an offline oracle-gated bound of 94.5%; its best learned online realization reaches 92.5%. These results identify shared flow and train-serve mismatch as central obstacles and provide a reproducible foundation for conditional correction.

authors.name: Xufeng Zhan
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yuanzhi Liang
authors.institution: Beijing Academy of Quantum Information Sciences

papers.title: Dark and bright solitons in a multimodal lithium tantalate microresonator
papers.abstract: Bright-soliton and dark-pulse microcombs provide complementary outputs. Integrating both states in a single resonator would expand the operating capabilities of an integrated coherent source, but requires opposite group-velocity-dispersion (GVD) channels while reconciling localized interfamily interaction for dark-pulse formation with spectral isolation for independent bright-soliton pumping. Wavelength-addressed access to both states is achieved in a LiTaO$_3$ microring through two TE-like transverse mode families. The higher-order TE$_{10}$ family fulfills two distinct roles in different spectral regions. Within localized avoided-mode-crossing regions, mode-resolved spectroscopy implicates TE$_{10}$ in perturbing the normal-GVD TE$_{00}$ resonance sequence. Away from these regions, TE$_{10}$ retains anomalous GVD and remains spectrally isolated as an independently pumpable bright-soliton channel; at representative pump resonances, the closest resonance of the non-addressed family is separated by 75--192 loaded cavity linewidths. With the input polarization held fixed, pumping TE$_{00}$ and TE$_{10}$ resonances generates dark-pulse and bright-soliton microcombs, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first experimental realization of a dark-pulse microcomb in an integrated LiTaO$_3$ microring. These results establish transverse-mode-family engineering as a route to combining localized modal interaction with independent spectral addressing in a single microresonator.

authors.name: Yuyao Guo
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Dimension-uniform Connectivity Laws and Hitting Times for Spherical Random Geometric Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G_d(n,p)$ be the graph formed by joining pairs of $n$ independent uniform points on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$ within a radius chosen to give edge probability $p$. For each fixed integer $K\ge0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, we prove that at $np=\log n+K\log\log n+t$, the probabilities of $(K+1)$-vertex-connectivity and $(K+1)$-edge-connectivity both converge to $\exp(-e^{-t}/K!)$ uniformly over all $d=d(n)\ge3$. This is the same limit as in the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph. Moreover, as the radius increases on a single sample, the first radii for minimum degree at least $K+1$, $(K+1)$-vertex-connectivity, and $(K+1)$-edge-connectivity coincide with probability tending to one uniformly over $d\ge3$. To our knowledge, this is the first critical-window law for connectivity in a random geometric graph that holds uniformly from fixed dimensions to dimensions growing arbitrarily with $n$.

papers.title: DMC-5: Dual-Model Collaboration with Cache-aware Context Compression for Long-horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon agents repeatedly feed an ever-growing interaction trajectory to a specialized agent model. Prefix caching reuses computation over repeated history, but cannot prevent context growth or remove information irrelevant to the current decision. This is especially costly when the specialized agent lacks the cached-input discounts available to general-purpose models, making trajectory compression a natural alternative. However, existing compression methods on selective context risk losing global information, recursively rewriting summary leads to semantic drift, while repeatedly recompressing the full history shifts the growing cost to the compressor. Therefore, we introduce DMC-5 (Dual-Model Collaboration with CaChe-aware Context Compression), an asymmetric framework that assigns full-history integration to a general compression model and action generation to a specialized agent model. DMC-5 maintains the raw trajectory as an Append-only Canonical View, preserving global access while allowing the compressor to reuse a stable historical prefix instead of recursively rewriting or recomputing prior context. The agent operates only on a compact Decision View with recent raw interactions, reducing repeated input while retaining the information needed for the next action. DMC-5 further incorporates YAMATO (integritY-Aware Memory Abstractions for Tool Operations) to preserve execution-critical information during lossy compression. Experiments on AppWorld, OfficeBench, and 8-objective QA show that DMC-5 reduces agent model input by 38.5-57.0% and end-to-end cost by 14.5-28.0% with 78.0-85.0% compressor cache-hit rates, while improving task performance by 1.0-5.8% over the uncompressed baseline.

papers.title: Weitzenb\"ock curvature estimates in arbitrary degree and sectional-scalar curvature pinching
papers.abstract: For each odd dimension $n\ge7$ we give an explicit constant $B_n<(n-1)/(n+2)$ such that a closed, connected, nonflat Riemannian $n$-manifold with $K_{\min}\ge B_n S_0$ is a rational homology sphere, where $S_0=\operatorname{Scal}/[n(n-1)]$. For example, $B_7=28/43<2/3$. This answers the question of Li, Matinpour, and Petersen about lowering the sectional curvature coefficient in the remaining odd dimensions. The same argument recovers their five-dimensional endpoint $B_5=10/19$. The proof starts with a four-frame inequality for two-forms. Contracting forms and averaging over hyperplanes propagates a Ricci-weighted estimate whose coefficient depends on the parity of the codimension. For an algebraic curvature tensor with nonnegative sectional curvature, we obtain lower bounds for the Weitzenb\"ock curvature endomorphism in every degree. When the dimension and degree are both even, we classify all nonzero equality pairs for the sharp bound by powers of K\"ahler forms. For three-forms the optimal coefficient in the scalar curvature bound is $1/3$ in dimensions five and six and lies between $4/9$ and $5168/11253$ in dimension seven. On the cone of strongly nonnegative curvature tensors we determine the optimal coefficient in every degree.

papers.title: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks
papers.abstract: Learned image captioning metrics are trained and tested on human judgments, so their reported correlation is a claim about generalization. We audit this claim for the three most recent collections of such judgments, Polaris, Nebula, and Spica, matching images at the pixel level. First, test samples reappear in training sets: the Spica training set contains about two-thirds of the Polaris test set, with identical human ratings. Second, controlled retraining shows that duplicates can inflate a metric: for Pearl, the gain is confined to the duplicated samples and grows with every epoch; for DENEB, it stays below one point. The gain depends on the learner and on how often a training set repeats a sample. Third, Kendall's $\tau$ over all samples is the sum of two terms, detecting captions with the lowest human score and ranking the others; the first supplies most of the reported correlation and is nearly saturated. The recent test sets cannot order Polos, DENEB and Pearl consistently, and a ridge regression on frozen features matches or exceeds all three. Fourth, we propose a protocol that ranks a learned metric only with a model trained without test samples, reports both terms, and compares metrics by paired tests. Under it, zero-shot vision--language judges rank first on the three recent test sets, and a fine-tuned judge ranks first on the three earlier benchmarks. The same analysis applies to any evaluator learned from human judgments; filter lists and code are released at https://github.com/morninghut/ic-dataset-audit .

papers.title: Restrictions of planar doubling measures to piecewise C1 Jordan domains
papers.abstract: We compare the class $\mathscr R(\Omega)$ of restrictions of full-support planar doubling measures with the class $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ of internal doubling measures on a piecewise $C^1$ Jordan domain. These classes coincide in the absence of zero-interior-angle cusps. At any such cusp, $\mathscr R(\Omega)\setminus\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is nonempty. For power-comparable widths, $\mathcal D(\Omega)\subsetneq\mathscr R(\Omega)$; for infinitely flat widths the two classes are disjoint. Under smooth endpoint regularity, finite versus infinite contact order gives these two alternatives. Under only $C^1$ regularity, finite logarithmic order does not determine whether the classes intersect, and examples with nonempty intersection and neither class containing the other also occur. For an individual internal measure, membership in $\mathscr R(\Omega)$ is characterized by a potential inequality for its axial projection. We prove this criterion by a positive-kernel construction and Whitney mass replacement, and also obtain sufficient conditions for variable-power widths and an independent finite-system criterion.

authors.name: Fan Wen
authors.institution: Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: DARE: Dual-Level Adversarial Learning with Domain-Aware Regularization for Whole Slide Image Classification
papers.abstract: Pathological whole slide images (WSIs) exhibit substantial domain shifts across hospitals due to variations in scanning devices, staining protocols, and tissue preparation procedures, leading to significant performance degradation when models are applied to data from different sources. Although unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) has shown strong performance in transferring models from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain in natural images, it remains relatively underexplored in computational pathology. The ultra-high resolution of WSIs and their pronounced inter-slide and intra-slide heterogeneity pose unique challenges for domain adaptation, often rendering existing UDA methods unstable and susceptible to negative transfer. To address these challenges, we propose Dual-level Adversarial learning with domain-aware REgularization (DARE), a plug-and-play UDA framework for WSI classification. DARE incorporates adaptive pseudo-labeling within a teacher-student architecture to provide stable supervision for the target domain, alongside adversarial alignment of both patch-level and slide-level embeddings. Together, these components enable the joint optimization of semantic representations at both levels for cross-domain alignment. We further introduce domain-aware attention masking to regularize attention and improve cross-domain generalization. Extensive experiments on four public WSI datasets demonstrate that DARE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches across various domain shifts.

papers.title: Robust Mixture Regressions and EM Algorithms via the Log-Truncated Likelihood
papers.abstract: Finite mixture regression is sensitive to gross residual outliers when component errors are modeled by Gaussian likelihoods. We propose a log-truncated likelihood for mixture regression. The likelihood is obtained by integrating a logarithmically growing Catoni-type score and exponentiating the negative integrated score, producing a proper location-scale density with a reusable normalizing constant and EM-compatible responsibilities. Although the induced density itself is lighter than exponential and has all moments, its likelihood score grows only logarithmically; this distinction yields a smooth residual-robust estimator that can be stably fitted when the data are generated from Laplace, Pareto, or even infinite-variance heavy-tailed error mechanisms. We derive deterministic tail envelopes, the location-scale decomposition of the normalizing constant, a rejection sampler, a lower-bounded mixing-weight update, a unique componentwise scale update, and a constrained generalized EM algorithm. The theory gives monotonicity of the observed likelihood and a local population-to-sample perturbation guarantee under standard compactness, contraction, and numerical-accuracy conditions. Simulations and applications to insurance claim severity and crypto return innovations show that the method is a competitive smooth likelihood-based alternative to Gaussian and pseudo-robust EM procedures, especially in residual-outlier regimes, while also clarifying its limitations under high leverage and extremely adversarial contamination.

papers.title: Fairness-optimized interlacing knots for even-degree periodic B-spline interpolation
papers.abstract: Interpolating an ordered set of points by a B-spline curve is a fundamental operation in computer-aided geometric design. Most of the literature addresses open curves, where the Schoenberg--Whitney condition characterizes a nonsingular collocation matrix and averaging is the standard way to choose the knot vector. Periodic B-spline interpolation has received much less attention, and the open-curve algorithms cannot be transferred directly. No theoretical criterion is available for choosing the knots, and the few existing constructions, such as the shifting and energy methods, remain empirical, with neither a theoretical guarantee nor a supporting analysis. This paper addresses this gap for even degrees. We prove that for every even degree $p\ge2$ the periodic collocation matrix is nonsingular whenever the domain knots and the interpolation parameters interlace, in either of two admissible orderings, for arbitrarily nonuniform parameters. Rather than singling out one knot vector, this sufficient condition delimits an $n$-parameter family of admissible knot vectors and provides the theoretical foundation for knot selection that periodic interpolation has lacked. It also explains why the empirical shifting method is solvable, previously justified only by an incorrect diagonal-dominance argument. We then exploit the remaining freedom to place the knots by fairness optimization, which preserves admissibility at every iterate and leads to the methods Opt-R and Opt-L. On four closed shapes with irregularly distributed points these methods achieve a fairness comparable to the shifting and energy methods, improve on them in several cases, and offer guarantees that no empirical construction provides.

papers.title: A Matrix Lee-Sidford Barrier and Faster Semidefinite Programming
papers.abstract: We construct a matrix analog of the Lee-Sidford barrier for semidefinite programming (SDP) with $m$ equality constraints and $n$-by-$n$ matrices. The barrier has self-concordance parameter $\widetilde{O}(m)$, so short-step interior-point methods require only $\widetilde O(\sqrt m)$ iterations. We also show that our matrix Lee-Sidford barrier can be implemented efficiently by developing a randomized algorithm that solves SDPs with $m\leq n$ to accuracy $\epsilon$ in $(n^{\omega+o(1)}+n^2m^{3/2+o(1)})\operatorname{polylog}(1/\epsilon)$ time, where $\omega\leq 9/4$ is the matrix multiplication exponent, achieving the fastest known running time in this regime.

authors.name: Zhao Song
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Ruizhe Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Disc functionals and rational curves
papers.abstract: We prove a criterion for the existence of rational curves on compact K\"ahler manifolds using disc functionals. As applications, we obtain a transcendental version of the Miyaoka--Mori theorem with an optimal degree bound and a new proof of the characterization of uniruled compact K\"ahler manifolds.

authors.name: Xiangyu Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Diffutoon-2: Toon Shading with Video Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Toon shading renders objects with a flat, stylized appearance. Diffusion models open a new route to this task by transforming photorealistic videos into an anime style. However, existing approaches often rely on curated source and style training pairs or additional visual references. Diffutoon avoids these requirements through structure guidance and colorization, but builds on an image diffusion backbone with short-window motion modules and repeated overlapping-window denoising. We present Diffutoon-2, a video diffusion framework that learns toon shading through animation reconstruction. Two complementary modules independently reconstruct animation clips from outlines and blurred colors, with the video backbone frozen. At inference, the modules jointly guide generation using the same types of conditions extracted from photorealistic footage, requiring neither cross-domain training pairs nor external style references. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Diffutoon-2 outperforms both general-purpose and domain-specific baselines, across quantitative metrics and human evaluation.

authors.name: Jingjing Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Periodic orbit asymptotics and dynamical zeta functions for smooth surface diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract:
Let $f$ be a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a closed surface $M$, and let $H$ be a closed homoclinic class with topological entropy $h=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f|H)>0$ and homoclinic period $\ell$. We prove that \[ \forall\,0<\chi<h,\qquad \lim_{\ell\mid n,\;n\to\infty} \frac{\#\mathrm{Per}_\chi(n,H)}{e^{nh}}=\ell, \] where $\mathrm{Per}_\chi(n,H)$ denotes the saddle points in $H$ of least period $n$ whose Lyapunov exponents lie outside $[-\chi,\chi]$.
  We also prove exponential remainders for the class and global counting formulas. As a result, for every $0<\chi<h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$, the Artin--Mazur zeta function of all $\chi$-hyperbolic periodic orbits, including sinks and sources, extends meromorphically beyond its disk of convergence. Its leading poles are determined by the periods of the ergodic maximal measures. This answers the meromorphic continuation question of Buzzi.

authors.name: Yao Tong
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

papers.title: CASPER: Discovering Spatially Resolved Causal Cell-Cell Communications
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics can reveal where ligands and receptors are expressed together. A harder question is whether exposure to a ligand changes pathway activity in nearby cells, since the same tissue environment can influence both ligand expression and pathway activity. We introduce CASPER, a Bayesian structural equation model that adjusts for receptor expression and represents the shared tissue environment with a Gaussian Markov random field. We show that the ligand-exposure effect is identifiable when the spatial covariance is known and distinguishable from independent noise, the coefficients are constant, and the structural errors are independent and homoskedastic. In simulations, CASPER reduced the bias seen in ordinary regression and in a regression that accounted for spatial dependence only in the outcome. We compared CASPER with CellPhoneDB in four public Xenium datasets. In ovarian cancer, CellPhoneDB found evidence of ligand--receptor expression enrichment for both IL6 and VEGFA. CASPER found greater support for a positive effect of fibroblast IL6 on the inflammatory-response score of ciliated epithelial cells than for an effect of fibroblast VEGFA on the angiogenesis score of endothelial cells. Code accompanies the Supplementary Materials and is available at https://github.com/nySTAT/casperCCC.

papers.title: Unique continuation and its failure for the Monge--Amp\`ere equation
papers.abstract: We study unique continuation for Alexandrov solutions with common Monge--Amp\`ere density bounded above and below. In the plane, we prove that agreement on an open set forces global equality. For every bounded domain \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) with \(n\ge3\), we construct two distinct uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}(\Omega)\) solutions that agree on a nonempty open subset of \(\Omega\).

authors.name: XiaoRui Lu
authors.institution: Center for High Pressure Science & Technology Advanced Research

papers.title: HKD-ACPA: Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation Adversarial Cyber-Physical Attacks in Power Grids
papers.abstract: Learning-based algorithms assist power-grid control centers in localizing transmission-line attacks, yet existing adversarial attacks typically require white-box access or repeated online queries. We study a practical zero-query setting in which an adversary coordinates physical, denial-of-service (DoS), and false data injection (FDI) attacks using only local measurements and historical detector outputs. To bridge the input-view asymmetry between local adversarial observations and DoS-masked control-center measurements, we propose Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation Adversarial Cyber-Physical Attacks (HKD-ACPA). HKD-ACPA distills historical detector predictions into a heterogeneous graph surrogate ensemble and trains a residual calibration module to correct the view-induced logit discrepancy. Over this calibrated surrogate, we formulate sparse, magnitude-bounded FDI synthesis with a group-balanced objective that jointly induces missed detections and false alarms, and solve the resulting hybrid discrete--continuous problem via bi-level projected gradient-based proximal policy optimization (PGPPO). Experiments on the IEEE 30-bus and 118-bus systems show that HKD-ACPA outperforms all surrogate-based baselines across every sparsity budget and surpasses online-query attacks in eight of ten system--budget settings without querying the detector model.

authors.name: Kun Cao
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: DoppelVet: Comparative Safety Verification for Self-Evolving Agents
papers.abstract: Self-evolving agents improve by retaining feedback as reusable memories or skills, but every mistaken approval can shape many future behaviors. Two updates can provide exactly the same evidence to a verifier yet produce opposite safety outcomes, so the verifier cannot distinguish them from that evidence alone. We introduce DoppelVet, a verification framework that checks proposed updates before they enter an agent's persistent state. Without access to safety labels, DoppelVet constructs an alternative that matches every signal used by the existing verifier. It replays both updates from the same state and directly compares their behaviors in both presentation orders before deciding whether to retain the candidate. We evaluate DoppelVet on DoppelVet-Grid and DoppelVet-Tool, covering executable programs and natural-language memories. Across nine open-weight and proprietary verifiers, DoppelVet raises mean harmful-update detection AUC from 0.762 to 0.940 on DoppelVet-Grid and from 0.681 to 0.826 on DoppelVet-Tool, outperforming VaG and AgentDoG 1.5. On DoppelVet-Grid, it reduces trajectories experiencing degradation from 30.39% to 0.43% over a ten-generation self-update loop and leaves no final degradation.

authors.name: Yifan Duan
authors.institution: Henan University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Chao Xue
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Chinese PLA General Hospital

authors.name: Lihuan Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Neutron Imaging Enhancement for Lithium Batteries Based on Swin-Transformer and Image Fusion
papers.abstract: Neutron imaging is highly sensitive to light elements such as lithium and is therefore valuable for non-destructive testing (NDT) and analyzing internal structural evolution in lithium batteries. However, limited neutron-source flux and detector performance often result in images with mixed noise, low contrast, and blurred edges, hindering accurate assessment of battery internal states. To address these issues, this paper proposes a lithium-battery neutron image enhancement method combining an improved Swin-Transformer with spatial-domain image fusion. First, an improved Swin-Transformer incorporating Multi-Dconv Head Transposed Attention (MDTA) and Global Response Normalization (GRN) extracts and reconstructs image features to suppress high-density white spots and Gaussian-Poisson mixed noise. Second, guided filtering and a gradient-adaptive mask are used for selective edge enhancement, while Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) improves local contrast. Finally, a spatial-frequency (SF)-based local block-weighted fusion mechanism adaptively combines the edge-enhanced and contrast-equalized images to preserve microscopic details while suppressing noise. Experiments show that, compared with BM3D, DnCNN, and GAN, the proposed method achieves strong performance in full-reference and no-reference evaluations. Its best PSNR and SSIM reach 33.0517 dB and 0.9637, respectively, while the NR-IQA and Natural Image Quality Evaluator (NIQE) scores are as low as 0.1794 and 4.0974. The method reduces artifacts and over smoothing, improving the visual fidelity and structural identifiability of lithium-battery neutron images.

papers.title: Align the Pair, Not the Sample: Representation Alignment for Faster and Better One-Step Generato
papers.abstract: Representation alignment markedly accelerates diffusion training, but one-step generators raise a question that diffusion does not: \emph{which training path should receive the loss?} A one-step generator sees two kinds of inputs. Corrupted real images come with their clean counterpart, which provides an instance-paired target. Samples generated from pure noise have no corresponding real image, yet this is where the final model operates. We study this question on Priming, which trains one-step generators from scratch by reconstructing corrupted images and then matching feature distributions with optimal transport. Aligning the generative path, the natural choice, collapses recall ($0.45\!\to\!0.15$--$0.25$) in all 17 configurations we test, including five target constructions and loss weights down to $0.05$. Aligning the paired reconstruction path with a frozen DINOv2 encoder instead helps in every setting we test. A short analysis explains this asymmetry: when the target carries no instance information about the input, the optimal aligned feature is constant within each class, so the loss pulls samples toward class prototypes. A control confirms this: aligning the paired path to a random same-class image instead of the input's own image removes most of the gain. Inside the generator, paired-path alignment creates an interface block through which post-training routes noise, and the image semantics carried through it predict sample quality across 16 models. The resulting recipe, \method, accelerates \emph{both} training stages on ImageNet $256\!\times\!256$: it matches the 160-epoch baseline with $2\times$ fewer priming epochs, surpasses its final quality with $4\times$ fewer post-training updates, and lowers FID to 1.30 (B) and 1.155 (L) at the standard budget. A joint single-stage variant trains native one-step generators and reaches FID 1.22 with 115M parameters.

authors.name: Encheng Su
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Supply the Global, Supervise the Local: Combining Representation Conditioning and Alignment in Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract:
A pretrained image representation helps train a diffusion transformer in several roles, including as an alignment target, which the model's hidden states learn to match, as in representation alignment (REPA), and as a condition, an extra input describing the image to be generated. Combined, they would give the model an input and a target, but whether they conflict is unknown. To test this, we let the condition carry only part of REPA's target: we split the representation of each image patch into an image-level (global) part, shared by all patches of the image, and a within-image (local) part, the patch's difference from the image-level part, and use one token carrying the image-level part as the condition. Then, the two roles overlap on the image-level part, where they could conflict, while only REPA supervises the within-image part, where we can see whether the token helps REPA.
  We find that the token and REPA together teach both the image-level part and the within-image part, the main source of REPA's FID improvement, far more than the sum of what each teaches alone, so they cooperate rather than conflict. These findings give one design rule for combining REPA with an image-level condition, supply the global, supervise the local, which we implement as Global-Condition REPA (GC-REPA): REPA with the token as an extra input; the token carries no information beyond REPA's target and is drawn at sampling from a separately trained token prior. GC-REPA greatly accelerates convergence: on ImageNet 256*256, SiT-XL/2 + GC-REPA reaches REPA's 4M- and SiT-XL/2's 7M-iteration FIDs within 200K and 100K iterations (20 and 70 fewer).

papers.title: RSWP: Robust SO(3)-Equivariant Watermarking for Panoramic Images
papers.abstract: Robust watermarking for panoramic imagery is impeded by the topological mismatch between spherical signals and planar representations. Conventional methods fail under $SO(3)$ viewing rotations due to non-linear geometric warping and struggle with viewport extraction, which typically necessitates computationally expensive inverse remapping. To address these challenges, we propose RSWP, a watermarking framework grounded in icosahedral group theory. Leveraging the property that the icosahedral group ($\mathcal{I}_{60}$) serves as the largest discrete subgroup of $SO(3)$, we decompose spherical rotations into tractable local planar rotations and combinatorial facet permutations. Accordingly, we introduce a decoupling architecture that embeds watermarks into discrete facets and a theoretically guaranteed Equivariance-to-Invariance decoding paradigm. By employing an equivariant feature extractor followed by a permutation-invariant sorting module, this paradigm rigorously synchronizes rotation-distorted features. Moreover, the dual-extractor design inherently supports direct, blind watermark retrieval from partial 2D renderings without geometric calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RSWP achieves state-of-the-art robustness against continuous $SO(3)$ rotations and viewport transformations while preserving high visual fidelity.

authors.name: Xiaoyan Gu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Organic-Inorganic Composite Materials

authors.name: Wu Liu
authors.institution: Wangjing Hospital of China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences

papers.title: Psychological State Monitoring Methods Based on Multimodal Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: The computer-Based Multimodal Emotion Recognition System needs to increase the accuracy and reliability of psychological state monitoring. A hierarchical framework was proposed in this paper to integrate facial images, speech signals and other physiological indicators of emotion in time and space for more complete analysis of human emotions. Synchronously sample data streams from webcams, microphones and wearable sensors, and then preprocess and extract features specific to each type of data. A high-end fusion architecture is adopted to combine early- and late-fusion methods and thus robustly integrate cross-modal information. Experimental validation in a real-world stress-response dataset showed good performance. The overall recognition accuracy and mean F1-score of the fused multimodal system are both about 91% and 0.88, respectively, which are superior to the best unimodal approach (face, 88% accuracy and F1-score 0.88). Temporal analysis shows that the groups for stress tracking are not uniformly adapted and resilient, and ablation experiments have determined which modules contribute significantly to the stability of the system. According to all kinds of quantitative evaluations of precision, recall, accuracy and F1 scores, the proposed method shows good balance and is practical and generally applicable. The research has provided an engineering-feasible, data-driven solution for precise emotion inference and offered methodological support for intelligent mental health assessment and human-centered system design.

authors.name: Ran Meng
authors.institution: Xuan Wu Hospital of the Capital Medical University

papers.title: Worst case tractability of weighted linear tensor product problems under the absolute error criterion
papers.abstract: This paper studies weighted linear tensor product problems in the worst case setting. We consider algorithms that use finitely many evaluations of arbitrary continuous linear functionals. We investigate algebraic and exponential tractability under the absolute error criterion in the case $\lambda_1>1$, where $\lambda_1$ is the square of the univariate maximal singular value. We obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for various notions of algebraic and exponential tractability on weights and univariate singular values. Our approach is to convert algebraic tractability of the problems for the absolute error criterion with $\lambda_1 > 1$ to exponential tractability of the normalized problems. Specifically, we solve Open Problem 27 as posed by Novak and Wo\'zniakowski (2008).

authors.name: Yuheng Xi
authors.institution: Xuan Wu Hospital of the Capital Medical University

papers.title: Strictness of the containment of Kirk's asymptotic contractions in a class defined by two quasi-metrics
papers.abstract: Kirk's asymptotic contractions are defined by moduli $\psi_n$ which converge uniformly on $[0,\infty)$ to a Boyd--Wong function and are evaluated at the distance $d(x,y)$ only. A relaxed class, in which the estimate involves a lower and an upper quasi-metric built from the four distances $d(x,y)$, $d(x,Ty)$, $d(Tx,y)$ and $d(Tx,Ty)$, was recently shown to contain Kirk's class and to admit the same fixed point conclusion. It was left open whether the containment is strict. We prove that it is. The separating maps form a family of radial damping maps $T(x)=\lambda(\norm{x})x$ on a normed space, where $\lambda\colon[0,\infty)\to[0,\rho]$ is continuous, $0\le\rho<1$, nonconstant and periodic: every such map is a relaxed asymptotic contraction with explicit linear moduli, whereas its one-step dispersion at a fixed distance is unbounded, so that no finite Kirk modulus exists. A slowly modulated nonperiodic damping law is treated as well. We further show that strictness can occur only when the image $T(X)$ is not relatively compact: in a complete space, if $T(X)$ is relatively compact, the two classes coincide, hence on a compact (in particular finite) space no separating example exists. Applications to semi-active vibration isolation with amplitude-dependent damping and to digital maturity gaps in the digital transformation of small and medium-sized enterprises are discussed, and numerical illustrations are provided.

papers.title: Vision-Language Truck Driving Advisories Grounded in Provincial Rules and Forecast Risks
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can generate context-aware driving advisories, but their outputs may conflict with road conditions or traffic rules, and they typically address a hazard only once it is visible. This matters for long-haul trucking, where heavy trucks need long stopping distances and a single trip may cross several jurisdictions with different traffic regulations. This paper proposes a data generation and distillation framework that integrates structured scene understanding, risk forecasting, and traffic-rule retrieval to generate truck driving decisions and natural-language advisories, with a consistency check on every record. The records, written by an 8B teacher, are then used to distill a 3B-parameter student model for onboard deployment. We also introduce a dashcam dataset covering four Canadian provinces, comprising 11,142 annotated lane-marking frames and 9,494 driving segments. On held-out driving data across all four provinces, the student passes the consistency check in 94.6% of the segments, against 20.2% for the untuned 8B teacher, and announces 26.2% of the risks in the next 10 to 30 seconds before they appear. Of the generated advisories, 97.7% conform to the provincial traffic rules and guidance. These findings suggest that the framework can produce rule-conforming training data for compact driving advisory models.

authors.name: Yukun Lu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Heavy Oil

papers.title: Teacher-Guided Multimodal Dual Representation Reconstruction for Egocentric Human Activity Recognition
papers.abstract: Multimodal Egocentric Human Activity Recognition (Ego-HAR) leverages complementary cues from first-person vision (V) and inertial sensor data (S) to recognize daily activities, where video mainly captures appearance and object-related context while inertial signals capture motion cues that video may miss. However, existing pre-training methods typically supervise the fused representation with a single joint objective, which may underemphasize the complementarity between the two modalities and limit the model's ability to learn from distinct modality-oriented signals. To address this issue, we propose Multimodal Dual Representation Reconstruction (MDR2), a teacher-guided pre-training framework in which frozen, label-informed video and inertial teachers each provide dense, modality-specific targets to a multimodal student trained on temporally sparse inputs. On the EvIs-Kitchen dataset, MDR2 improves noun/verb F1-macro over the supervised M-Baseline by 9.20/6.17 points at K=4 video key frames and by 1.21/1.82 points at K=32. These results show that MDR2 consistently achieves higher mean recognition performance across the evaluated video-observation settings under the unified backbone setting, with more pronounced gains under sparse inputs.

papers.title: Auditing two-stage MS/MS molecular retrieval on MassSpecGym v1.5: Reranking gains, candidate priors and spectrum dependence
papers.abstract: Two-stage retrieval of molecular structures from tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) can benefit from candidate reranking, but benchmark gains may also reflect candidate priors, replicate spectra, precursor mass, and training-set coverage. We audit a two-stage retrieval system on the official MassSpecGym v1.5 split (17,556 test spectra). A data-safe DreaMS encoder and composite molecular fingerprints provide an initial shortlist; a support-gated reranker combines pair scores, candidate-relative peak coverage, and mass-feasibility features. The final system achieves 31.05% Recall@1, a 10.05-point gain over its Stage 1 ensemble, while preserving its 72.62% Recall@20. Replacing the query spectrum with one from a different molecule matched on adduct and precursor mass reduces Recall@1 by 9.0 points (15.3 points under molecule-balanced weighting); nevertheless, a training-mean spectrum retains 13.75% Recall@1, indicating substantial spectrum-independent signal. Mass-feasibility features improve Recall@1 beyond score and coverage controls, while learned peak-fragment similarities do not outperform constant coverage. Errors cluster by molecule, and removing close training neighbours causes a large decline in Stage 1 shortlist recall among initially well-covered molecules. We conclude that candidate-relative mass-feasibility evidence improves front-rank retrieval and spectrum dependence, but does not establish learned structural discrimination or eliminate candidate priors. Evaluation should separately assess shortlist reachability, spectrum dependence, and molecule-level generalization.

authors.name: Qiang Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Scale-Aware Reference Attention for Mannequin-to-Model Gown Generation
papers.abstract: Formal gowns are sold online with photos of models wearing them, and buyers zoom in to inspect sequins, lace and beading. Image editors can turn a photo of a gown on a mannequin into a convincing photo of a person wearing it, but they receive every reference photo without any notion of its magnification, and the fine detail of the gown is lost when the output is viewed up close. We propose scale-aware reference attention (SARA), which tells an open diffusion transformer the zoom level of the output and of every reference photo, biases the attention of the output toward references of a similar zoom level, uses macro photos of the fabric as references, and is trained on a mix of whole-garment and zoomed targets. To train and evaluate it, we introduce Kiss3000, a dataset of 915 high-resolution mannequin photos and 2274 on-model photos of formal gowns with cross-domain pairs and splits by style, and zoom-crop evaluation, which compares garment crops at full, half and local scale without pixel alignment and judges local fidelity with two vision-language models gated on control crops. With this protocol, Nano Banana Pro at 4K, the highest-resolution commercial editor we test, loses or redraws local detail on 14 of 20 test gowns. At 1536x2048 pixels, both judges prefer SARA over a LoRA fine-tuning baseline on 18 test items and the baseline on 6 (p=0.023), and over the base model on 26 against 4 (p=5.9e-5), while SARA keeps the gown design as often as the baseline.

papers.title: VideoJSON: A Minimal Harness Beats Purpose-Built Memory for Ultra-Long Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Answering questions over days or weeks of video requires searching for scattered clues across long timelines. Existing video agents rely on complex memory graphs and fixed retrieval pipelines, which restrict how the agent can search. We propose VideoJSON, a minimal harness for ultra-long video understanding that keeps the memory simple and lets a coding agent write its own search programs. During indexing, a vision-language model turns each minute of video into a single JSON record containing a dense caption and structured fields such as events, entities, places, and speech transcripts. At query time, the agent writes Python or Bash programs in a sandboxed container to filter, link, and read these records over multiple steps, without task-specific training or raw video access. On four ultra-long video benchmarks, VideoJSON with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash outperforms MAGIC-Video by 7.0, 20.0, and 24.75 points on EgoLifeQA, Ego-R1-Bench, and MM-Lifelong Week, and beats the best prior EgoMemReason score by 12.6 points. Across four policy models of increasing capability, VideoJSON's average score rises by up to 11.58 points over the weakest model, compared with at most 5.50 points for MAGIC-Video. Ablations show that both agentic code search and the structured JSON records drive these gains, while adding hourly summaries, extra tools, or video access changes the average score by less than 1.5 points. In addition, fine-tuning Qwen-3.5-Flash on 64 VideoJSON trajectories from an unrelated 100-hour livestream improves its MM-Lifelong scores by up to 8.25 points. Code will be open-sourced after publication.

papers.title: A world model for longitudinal health-trajectory prediction in older adults across multinational cohorts
papers.abstract: Aging is characterized by continuously evolving health states, yet most existing prediction models focus on static health risk at isolated time points rather than explicitly modelling how health trajectories unfold over time. We developed a health world model based on the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture to represent evolving health states and simulate future trajectories under specified actions. The model combines a state encoder, an action- and context-conditioned predictor, a stop-gradient target encoder, and clinical outcome heads. We trained the model on the US Health and Retirement Study (HRS) and evaluated it without refitting in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA) and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Open-loop evaluation assessed discrimination and calibration for mortality and worsening of activities of daily living (ADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL). In the held-out HRS test set, the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) for mortality, ADL worsening, and IADL worsening were 0.89, 0.93, and 0.93 at the first horizon and 0.84, 0.84, and 0.85 at the fifth horizon, respectively. Predicted risks stratified subsequent outcomes across horizons. Across the evaluated horizons, mortality AUROC ranged from 0.867 to 0.881 in ELSA and from 0.796 to 0.801 in CHARLS. Simulated trajectories preserved the expected risk ordering across predefined action regimes. In counterfactual simulations, changes in lifestyle actions shifted predicted risks in directions consistent with observed associations. The model provides a framework for longitudinal risk prediction and action-conditioned simulation in older adults.

authors.name: Jingyi Wu
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

authors.name: Luxia Zhang
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous \'etale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, where $\Omega_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor. In this note, using the Dwyer-Greenlees equivalence between $\ell$-completed objects and $\ell$-torsion objects, we prove that $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, and consequently, based on Kahn's early work, the Tate conjecture at positive characteristics.

authors.name: Yunhao Sun
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: FastD4RT: Training-Free Acceleration of Dynamic 4D Reconstruction and Tracking
papers.abstract: Query-based 4D reconstruction models such as D4RT encode a video once into a global scene representation and obtain outputs by decoding independent point queries. However, inference is often influenced by dense outputs and long videos. Although D4RT separates encoding from decoding, a dense output still requires one decoder query for every pixel of every frame, and a long video is still encoded as many overlapping segments. In this work, we analyze the inference cost of D4RT and show that a large part of it is redundant. In particular, we find that the later decoder blocks attend to a small set of tokens shared by all queries. Based on these findings, we propose FastD4RT, a training-free framework that accelerates D4RT. By exploiting the smoothness of the outputs over time and across pixels, FastD4RT encodes and decodes only at sparse anchors and recovers the remaining outputs via interpolation. It decodes the remaining queries against a shared token set selected once per segment. We further characterize the errors introduced by both components. Experimental results show that FastD4RT accelerates D4RT by about 5 times on average across all its tasks with competitive accuracy, and further improves accuracy on long videos. Our code is available at https://github.com/Lycheemeng/fastd4rt.

authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: The minimax value of outcome feedback in budget-constrained adaptive sampling
papers.abstract: Whether adaptivity improves estimation is a classical question in sequential design and information-based complexity. In practice, adaptive data collection can use two different kinds of information: process data on whether each contact succeeded, and the observed outcomes themselves. How much each kind is worth in the worst case under a hard budget has not been settled. We study this question for estimating a common Bernoulli mean through channels with unknown response probabilities and known costs, where failed contacts are charged and the budget must hold on every sample path. We compare static designs, designs that adapt to response indicators only, and fully adaptive designs, each with an arbitrary estimator. Our main theorem shows that when the costs are invariant under a group of channel permutations acting transitively on the nuisance parameter, outcome-adaptive allocation has zero minimax value: response-adaptive and fully adaptive designs have the same minimax risk, given by a one-dimensional optimization and attained by an explicit least-favourable prior and equalizer rule. For two contacts we obtain a closed-form criterion for when response feedback strictly improves on every static design. An unequal-cost example with a computer-certified exact saddle shows that the same conclusion can hold without symmetry, even though no product prior is least favourable there. A correlated prior shows that outcome feedback can still reduce Bayes risk, so the equivalence is genuinely minimax. In this idealized setting, the results support responsive survey designs that adapt to paradata but not to outcomes.

authors.name: Shengye Tao
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: FlowPAC: Flow-Guided Visual Pruning and Action Caching for Efficient VLA Inference
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for embodied AI, yet their high inference latency and memory footprint remain major barriers to edge deployment. Existing training-free acceleration techniques, such as visual token pruning and action caching, typically rely on static resource allocation. This mismatch with dynamic robotic interactions not only degrades control performance but also causes severe hardware inefficiencies, including fragmented KV-cache layouts and wasted compute on non-critical regions. To address this, we propose FlowPAC, a locality-aware framework that leverages task-aware optical flow as a shared physical signal to jointly optimize visual and action computation. Specifically, we introduce Direction-Aware Trajectory Propagation (DATP) and Locality-Aware Contiguous Token Selection (LACT) to jointly handle visual token dynamics and enforce spatial locality, reducing memory fragmentation and enabling efficient KV-cache compression. This is complemented by Flow-Conditioned Action-Block Refresh (FCAR) for adaptive action computation based on motion dynamics. Extensive closed-loop evaluations on LIBERO demonstrate that FlowPAC achieves a 2.13$\times$ end-to-end speedup over the dense baseline while essentially maintaining the success rate with 30% visual-token retention. These results validate that aligning computation allocation with both physical dynamics and hardware constraints is essential for efficient VLA deployment on edge systems.

papers.title: MagTrace: Tracing magnetic order through the evolving scientific literature
papers.abstract: Much of the research on magnetic materials starts from their magnetic order, but confirming it from the papers by hand can take hours, and curated databases can be incomplete and outdated. In this work, we build MagTrace, a language model agent that, given only a material's name, searches four literature databases, reads open access full text and reports the magnetic orders the current literature supports, each with a confidence score and citations a reader can check. We evaluate its performance on 18 materials against an answer key complied from published papers, compared with two other conditions that vary in level of retrieval. On a score from 0 to 1 that combines correctness, detail, whether the most confident order is current, and citation integrity, MagTrace scores 0.839; the same underlying language model scores 0.676 given the abstracts from one literature search and 0.548 answering from memory. With a single search, the model finds the right kind of order but omits the propagation vector, which describes how the pattern repeats through the material's crystal structure, in 85% of its orders. From memory, the model often cites titles that lead to no indexed paper (for 25% of the orders we could check), and when a cited paper exists and has an abstract, the abstract contradicts the claim for 17% of those citations, against 7% for MagTrace.

papers.title: Defending Vision-Language-Action Models against Transferable Attacks via Visual-Proprioceptive Consistency
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong capabilities in a wide range of robotic tasks. However, adversarial attacks in VLA models have shown strong transferability across robotic tasks, posing significant threats to robotic systems. Despite their different attack strategies, we observe that these transferable attacks share a common consequence: they disrupt the VLA model's perception towards the robot itself. Motivated by this observation, we propose a proprioception-grounded defense framework that leverages trusted proprioceptive information to detect and mitigate transferable adversarial attacks. Specifically, we utilize the robot's proprioceptive states to establish a trusted spatial reference, and compare it with the robot's perceived location inferred from visual features. Discrepancies between these two sources provide a reliable signal for detecting adversarial attacks. Extensive experiments demonstrate effective detection of transferable adversarial patches and improved closed-loop performance. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of our defense on real-world robotic tasks.

authors.name: Jiahao Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Han Xu
authors.institution: Heilongjiang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Loadability Assessment for Large-Load Integration: From Repeated Power Flow Tracing to Historical Trajectory Transfer
papers.abstract: Integrating large data-center loads requires utilities to evaluate voltage-stability loading margins under different generation and demand conditions. Continuation power flow (CPF) traces P--V curves through successive prediction and correction steps, but related assessments can repeatedly reconstruct similar nonlinear behavior. Reusing an operating point as an initial guess does not capture the subsequent voltage response. This paper proposes a continuation method that transfers finite segments of historical power flow (PF) trajectories. Each segment is aligned with the present state and continuation direction, supplementing the CPF tangent predictor with previously computed nonlinear curve shape. Short Newton tests evaluate compatibility with the present PF equations, and an attention-based selector combines their results with network conditions, loading patterns, and recent continuation states. Numerical correction and fold refinement determine accepted solutions and the loading limit. The analysis bounds prediction error through differences in trajectory curvature and establishes sufficient conditions for local correction and branch preservation. Studies on modified IEEE 14- and 118-bus systems under renewable-generation and data-center load variations demonstrate reduced online computation and higher observed recovery of specified continuation solutions than Adaptive CPF. For loading-limit assessment, paired online speedups are 4.88--21.62$\times$ over Adaptive CPF and 1.53--4.77$\times$ over holomorphic embedding with arc-length parametrization (HEAP) across the tested scenarios.

papers.title: Scalar dynamics in a subclass Ia mimetic DHOST bounce
papers.abstract: We study scalar perturbations in a quadratic subclass Ia degenerate higher-order scalar-tensor (DHOST) realization of a nonsingular bouncing cosmology previously analyzed in higher-derivative mimetic gravity. After a constant rescaling of the scalar potential, the subclass Ia model reproduces the same scale-factor history as the original model, although the associated mimetic Lagrange multiplier generally differs. For the comparison with the original mimetic model, we focus on the branch $0<\gamma<2/3$, for which the scalar sound speed of the original model is positive. We perform an ADM and Hamiltonian reduction of the scalar sector and show that, imposing the mimetic and momentum constraints, the reduced canonical scalar mode contains no spatial-gradient contribution. The physical scalar sound speed therefore vanishes, $c_s^2=0$, in agreement with the known vacuum behavior of the \(\alpha_L=0\) mimetic-DHOST sector. On the matched bouncing background, the resulting effective frequency squared is independent of the comoving wavenumber and approaches zero from below in the remote contracting phase. Consequently, the asymptotic oscillatory regime used in the previous mimetic model to impose positive-frequency initial conditions is absent. Although canonical normalization can still be imposed through the Wronskian condition, it does not select the initial state uniquely. Without an additional state prescription, the asymptotic dynamics therefore does not uniquely determine the primordial scalar spectrum.

papers.title: Where the Image Sits: Vision-Text Order Bias in Jev
papers.abstract: Jev-style system-1 decision models read a choice from a single prefill. They restrict the next-token distribution to the supplied option labels and return a distribution over the options, with no generation and no parsing. Recent work shows that generative vision-language models are sensitive to the relative order of image and text tokens. We ask whether that sensitivity reaches this Jev-style readout. The answer is always read at the end of the prompt, so moving the image changes the distance from the visual evidence to the decision, but never the position at which the decision is read. Using four placements---prefix, pre-question, pre-options, and suffix---and holding the option listing fixed, we measure argmax flips, total variation, accuracy, calibration, and label marginals. Suffix placement flips 41.0% of decisions and lowers accuracy by 18.6 points. Averaged over the four slots, the curve is monotone, not U-shaped. That shape differs from prior results on generative vision-language models. The effect survives a battery of controls. We also introduce prefix--question averaging (P+Q), a two-forward readout that averages the prefix and pre-question distributions. It is at least as accurate as prefix and outperforms the prior baselines. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/Youzhi333/Visual_Tex_Order_Bias_Jev.

papers.title: A $(3/2+\varepsilon)$-Approximation for Weighted 3-Set Packing
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic $(3/2+\varepsilon)$-approximation for weighted $3$-set packing, for every fixed rational $\varepsilon>0$, improving on the 1.6908-approximation reported by Tong and Xu (2026). The algorithm has two phases. It first performs bounded local search using a rounded $12/7$-power potential. It then combines compatible exchanges that insert at most three sets and increase the original weight. The analysis relates the gap left by the first phase to the gain available to the second phase. We prove a structural inequality that bounds the weight of a comparison packing by $3/2$ times the current weight plus one sixth of a sum of small-exchange gains. Each gain accounts for all sets that the exchange must delete. A greedy rule recovers enough of these gains to obtain the approximation guarantee. We derive the structural bound from local optimality by analyzing finite computation trees and averaging the error caused by their limited depth. The running time is $n^{4^{O(1/\varepsilon)}}\operatorname{poly}(L)$, where $n$ is the number of input sets and $L$ is the input encoding length. The same guarantee holds for maximum-weight independent set in induced $K_{1,4}$-free graphs.

authors.name: Changjun Wang
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University

papers.title: CCAMoE: Cache-Conditioned Adaptive Inference for Offloaded MoE
papers.abstract: Expert offloading enables Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference on memory-constrained GPUs, but expert transfers and CPU execution limit decoding performance. Speculative decoding can mitigate these costs, yet separate draft weights consume scarce GPU memory and longer drafts increase verification demand. In this paper, we present CCAMoE, a unified runtime that coordinates adaptive speculative decoding with concurrent expert-cache updates. Its design has three key features: 1) Cache-only drafting, which reuses resident target experts to generate proposals and routing hints without separate draft weights; 2) Draft-guided cache updates, which anticipate expert demand and overlap transfers with computation to support subsequent drafting and verification; and 3) Cost-aware draft-length control, which balances expected acceptance against execution cost. Together, these mechanisms coordinate proposal generation and cache preparation through a shared evolving cache, improving proposal quality while reducing verification cost. Across various MoE models, GPU platforms, and workloads, CCAMoE consistently achieves the lowest decoding latency, with up to 2.33$\times$ speedup over state-of-the-art baselines.

authors.name: Haisheng Tan
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yuteng Wang
authors.institution: China University of Petroleum, East China

papers.title: WorldWeave: Rethinking Embodied Navigation through Cross-Task World Modeling
papers.abstract: Mobile embodied agents continuously alter their observations through their own motion, while external dynamics further shape future interactions. Different mobile embodied tasks therefore capture complementary patterns of state evolution, yet jointly learning world dynamics across such interactions remains less explored. We investigate this problem through Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) and Embodied Visual Tracking (EVT), which respectively involve navigation toward a stationary goal and interaction with a moving target. We propose WorldWeave, a cross-task world model that couples shared predictive dynamics with task-specific adaptation. Instead of conditioning state transitions on heterogeneous physical actions, WorldWeave learns latent actions from observed state changes via inverse-forward dynamics, establishing a shared transition representation across tasks. The resulting future-state predictions are adaptively integrated into task-specific representations for downstream decision making. Experiments across multiple VLN and EVT benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over specialized baselines.

authors.name: Jiahao Zhang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Junyu Gao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: When and Where to Transfer: Learning Transferable Historical Contexts for Short-History Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Related sources can improve multivariate time series forecasting when the target history is short, but their usefulness varies across source groups and historical periods. A key challenge is to identify informative historical contexts from the sources. This paper proposes Hierarchical Context Transfer (HiCT), a framework that adaptively weights source groups and their historical contexts to determine both \emph{where} and \emph{when} to transfer. A shared context encoder and cross-attention are used to learn weights over source groups and historical contexts. These weights guide regularized transfer estimation, followed by an optional target-specific correction. This paper establishes a target excess-risk bound for the context-weighted transfer estimator. Experiments demonstrate competitive predictive performance across four multivariate forecasting datasets and a favorable accuracy--runtime trade-off against the evaluated baselines. Source-corruption ablations illustrate the roles of group-level and within-group weighting in adapting to unreliable source histories.

papers.title: Reducing Permutation Sensitivity in Multimodal Large Language Models via Shared Positions and Attention-Only Distillation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we conduct a systematic study on improving permutation robustness while preserving accuracy. First, we categorize permutation bias phenomena into four representative scenarios. Then, we take the multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) dataset as an example under text-option reordering scenario to analyze the root cause of permutation bias. Based on this root cause analysis and set encoding strategy, we investigate shared positions with blocked cross-unit attention (SP-B) and extend this design to bidirectional cross-unit attention (SP-V) for modality exchange. However, these structural changes may reduce predictive accuracy. To recover model capability across different scenarios under the SP structure, an attention-only distillation from frozen native models is proposed. Shared positions reduce permutation sensitivity, and attention-only distillation improves accuracy under the shared-position structure. Across all three models, our method is comparable to or better than majority voting in macro-average all-permutation accuracy, and outperforms supervised fine-tuning by 1.95-4.20 percentage points. This work provides valuable insight into permutation bias mitigation and model capability recovery.

papers.title: Make Position Uninformative: Exchangeable Self-Distillation Flattens the Lost-in-the-Middle Curve
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented language models answer well when the relevant document comes first or last and poorly when it sits in the middle. Some fine-tuning recipes lift the middle by lowering the start. We show how training contexts teach positional bias. With a uniform answer slot and shuffled distractors, the optimal reader ignores position. Building on this result, Exchangeable Self-Distillation (ExSD) trains a small adapter on shuffled contexts to reproduce the model's answer when it reads the answer document alone. It needs no gold answers and only a few thousand examples. On six models from 1.5B to 32B parameters, ExSD raises both average and worst-position accuracy against the frozen model, including on a held-out test split. In controlled LoRA comparisons, it significantly improves both criteria over Pos2Distill. Against CORD, mean differences are not significant, while worst-position accuracy improves significantly in the 20- and 30-document settings. ExSD also matches or beats gold-answer fine-tuning, changes behavior on other tasks far less, and transfers to unseen tasks. Head probes show greater reliance on content over position.

authors.name: Qingsen Ma
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: UACR: Uncertainty-Aware Collaborative Routing for Explainable Industrial Anomaly Inspection
papers.abstract: Industrial anomaly inspection requires not only accurate anomaly discrimination but also trustworthy explanations for operators, while satisfying the strict latency constraints of online inspection. Existing methods, however, typically apply a fixed computational path to all samples, making it difficult to strike a good balance among detection accuracy, inference efficiency, and interpretability. To address this issue, we propose UACR, an uncertainty-aware collaborative routing framework for explainable industrial anomaly inspection. UACR aims to deliver reliable anomaly decisions together with operator-facing explanations under the online inspection budget, while adaptively allocating computation so that ambiguous cases receive deeper scrutiny. The framework consists of two stages. Stage I, Offline Training and Routing Hyperparameter Search, learns the anomaly inspection modules and calibrates the uncertainty estimator that drives routing. Stage II, Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Routing, collaboratively dispatches each input across inspection paths according to its estimated uncertainty. Experimental results on multiple public datasets show that UACR achieves over 5.16% improvement in accuracy compared to the baseline method, while reducing latency by over 31.5%. It also enhances the interpretability of industrial detection by over 15%.

authors.name: Yiwei Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Cayley Regression for Finite Groups with a Cyclic Subgroup of Index Two
papers.abstract: A finite group $G$ is a Cayley regression if every generalized Cayley graph of $G$ is isomorphic to a Cayley graph of $G$, and a $k$-Cayley regression if this holds for all such graphs of valency at most $k$. We show that the dihedral group $D_{2n}$, $n\geq2$, is a $2$-Cayley regression if and only if it is a $3$-Cayley regression, which holds exactly when $n$ is a prime power, and that for $k\geq4$ it is a $k$-Cayley regression if and only if $n$ is an odd prime power or $n\in\{2,4\}$.
