These advantages are especially attractive for multispectral satellite imaging, where conventional workflows rely on transmitting high-dimensional image cubes to the ground for downstream electronic analysis. Here, we introduce a computationally efficient surrogate model-guided framework for designing incoherent multispectral diffractive optical networks that directly output class probabilities onboard, eliminating the need to capture and transfer the full multispectral data cube for ground-side inference. We first train a physically compatible surrogate model, represented by a non-negative fully connected model that accommodates a generalized detector readout, yielding a task-specific non-negative multispectral intensity transformation that can be transferred to an optical processor. We then synthesize its diffractive counterpart through data-free point-spread-function-based optimization under spatially incoherent illumination. Using this approach, we numerically demonstrate a six-spectral-channel diffractive classifier for tri-class satellite-scene recognition, achieving a blind-testing accuracy of 79.8% for artificial surface, water body, and vegetated land images, closely approaching the 81.8% accuracy of its surrogate. We further demonstrate a more compact three-spectral-channel design that numerically achieves 72.7% blind-testing accuracy, compared with 75.1% for its corresponding surrogate model. This surrogate model-guided strategy provides a practical pathway for designing compact, task-specific incoherent multispectral optical processors for resource-constrained remote-sensing inference.

authors.name: Xilin Yang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: MotionServe: Efficient Multi-Robot Serving by Exploiting Robot Execution Slack
papers.abstract: As robotic arms undertake diverse manipulation tasks, a deployment may need to serve many task-specific vision-language-action (VLA) policies concurrently. Dedicating a GPU to each robot is costly, motivating shared-GPU inference. Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) allows compatible policies to share a frozen backbone with lightweight policy-specific adapters, reducing model-weight memory and enabling cross-policy batching. However, robot inference must keep pace with physical execution. With action chunking, robots continue executing buffered actions while awaiting new predictions, and the remaining buffered time provides each robot's execution slack for serving its next request. Once this slack is exhausted, the robot stalls until new actions arrive, interrupting task progress. Observing earlier preserves more slack but can lead to disruptive replanning and lower task success, whereas delaying dispatch to form larger batches can improve GPU efficiency but consumes slack and risks stalls. To balance these competing demands, we present MotionServe, a shared-GPU serving system that coordinates robot observation timing with server-side batch formation. MotionExec selects observation triggers based on motion structure in predicted action chunks, allowing inference to overlap with remaining buffered execution. SlackBatch combines the resulting per-robot execution budgets with estimated outstanding GPU work to determine when to wait, which requests to batch, and when to dispatch them. We evaluate X-VLA on LIBERO and SimplerEnv's WidowX tasks and OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO, with up to 96 simulated robots sharing one NVIDIA H200 GPU. At 96 robots, MotionServe reduces mean stall per episode by 43.4% and 32.6% and improves task success by 8.98 and 2.30 percentage points, respectively, over each model's lowest-stall baseline. Backbone sharing also reduces weight memory for 96 policies by 97.6% and 91.1%.

papers.title: When Does Optical Context Compression Pay Off? A Decode-Aware Cost Analysis of Reasoning VLMs
papers.abstract: Rendering long text as images lets a vision-language model (VLM) read a document with fewer input tokens, and evaluations often count mainly these prefill tokens. We show that for reasoning models this accounting is incomplete. Across five models and two long-context benchmarks, reading the rendered document makes the model think longer: decode length grows by 1.5-3.5x on the four general-purpose VLMs tested, and under typical output pricing this decode tax makes image input more expensive than text for two of the five models on QuALITY. Unrecoverable information loss is not sufficient to explain the tax at moderate compression: Qwen's OCR of the same images recovers 98.7% of words, and feeding Kimi-K3 its own transcription as text restores text-mode reasoning length and accuracy. Whether compression pays off reduces to an exchange rate, (1-1/c)/(r-1), that must exceed the workload's price-weighted ratio of output to input tokens; this accounting decomposition shows why Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash can benefit and Qwen and GLM cannot. None of the training-free signals we test predicts the tax before generation. As a practical heuristic, an image-first policy that sends only inputs with a per-input compression ratio of at least 1.6 to images and falls back to text once image-mode reasoning costs as much as the input's prefill saving cuts the bill by 6-14% on Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at an accuracy cost of 0.3-1.2 points; on QuALITY, asking for a reasoning budget on both paths is a stronger lever.

papers.title: Free rational curves on singular Fano varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that every klt Fano variety admits a free rational curve in its smooth locus.

papers.title: Projecting Fermions into Exact Scar Towers: Local Protection across Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: We construct exact scar towers in $SO(n)$ ($n\ge3$) spin chains by Gutzwiller projection of $n$-flavor flat-band Kitaev chains. The projected roots have only singlet and antisymmetric components on each bond. These local constraints allow a staggered flavor flip to generate an equidistant tower. The root and its first descendant exhaust the two-site configurations that are visited by the tower, leaving an orthogonal bond subspace unvisited. Deformations within this subspace can break $SO(n)$ symmetry and reshape the low-energy physics without altering the exact scar tower. A polarization-selective deformation drives an exact first-order transition from the symmetry-protected topological phase to a ferromagnetic phase. The tower retains its wave functions and absolute energies across the phase transition, including at the gapless point. Exact scars therefore need not inherit the symmetries, order parameters, or criticality of the ground state.

papers.title: Preserve to Compress: Beyond Low-Dimensional Latents in One-Step Diffusion Codec
papers.abstract: Pretrained latent diffusion models bring powerful generative priors to ultra-low-bitrate image compression, but their latent spaces reflect a reconstruction--generation tradeoff. Low-dimensional latents reduce modeling cost but can discard image details, while higher-dimensional latents improve reconstruction yet make diffusion optimization harder under a fixed computational budget. Generative codecs that adopt these pretrained spaces also inherit this compromise, even though compression requires fidelity to a specific source image. In particular, low-dimensional latent interfaces can discard source details before coding and restrict how much decoded information reaches the image decoder. We propose Preserving Information for Compression and Synthesis (PICS), a one-step generative image compression framework that adapts these interfaces to preserve source information. Our Information-Preserving Adaptors (IPAs) expose richer features for coding and retain decoded information throughout reconstruction, while deferred decoder adaptation stabilizes training and helps the image decoder exploit the expanded representations. Experiments on Kodak, DIV2K, and CLIC 2020 show average BD-rate savings of 52.64% and 39.61% over StableCodec at matched LPIPS and DISTS, respectively.

authors.name: Guo Lu
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: Products of translates: bounds and constructions
papers.abstract: We study products of translates of the form $(A+d)(A+d)$ with $d\in D$, where both $A$ and $D$ are finite subsets of $\mathbb{R}$. We show that $|(A+a)(A+a)|\ge C|A|^{5/3}$ for some $a\in A$, and that $|(A+D)(A+D)|\le |A|^{2-c(\alpha)}$ for some $c(\alpha)>0$ when $|D|=|A|^{\alpha}$ with $\alpha<1$.

papers.title: Trustworthy agentic lunar robotics: safety-constrained contingent planning with a foundation-model planner
papers.abstract: Sustained lunar-base operations require robots that restore equipment and deliver cargo under conditions unforeseen before deployment. Flown space autonomy executes pre-validated procedures and enters a safe hold outside their scope, whereas foundation models synthesize plans on site that cannot be verified before execution. We formulate these operations as safety-constrained contingent planning with irreversible actions, erroneous records, three-valued physical evidence, and costly, deadline-constrained sensing. We propose asymmetric knowledge-level replanning (AKR), which treats the planner as an untrusted black box: reversible actions run on the planner's assumptions, and irreversible actions run only after a minimum-cost sensing cover verifies every precondition. Under sound measurements, no irreversible action executes on a false precondition for any planner or record, the sensing cost before an irreversible action is bounded below for every sound knowledge-based policy, and execution with a complete planner ends in a verified goal or a certified hold. AKR executed no hazardous action in 21,000 Monte Carlo trials with sound observations or in 58 full-stack runs; the FF-Replan acting rule executed one in 7% of those trials. The median AKR run took 1.10 times the fastest run on the same mission, against 1.50 under the K-replanner acting rule. AKR completed 20 of 21 contingency and sequential-fault runs with an unchanged task model; the original PLEXIL and EUROPA$\rightarrow$PLEXIL procedures completed none.

authors.name: Bingqi Huang
authors.institution: Zhongkai University of Agriculture and Engineering

papers.title: Quantum Geometry Effects in Lattice Dynamics
papers.abstract: Quantum geometric effects such as the Berry curvature and the quantum metric are well established in electronic transport, whereas in lattice dynamics the Berry curvature also plays a key role: adiabatically following the lattice, electrons generate a molecular Berry curvature that splits degenerate optical phonons into chiral partners. To determine how the quantum metric affects phonons, we go beyond adiabatic lattice dynamics, identifying Berry curvature and quantum metric contributions to the electronic response of the lattice. Using first-principles calculations in the magnetic topological semimetal EuB$_6$, we find that phonon modes with chiral splitting and those with nonchiral splitting coexist. Unlike the former, which originate from the Berry curvature, the latter arise from the pure quantum metric, while the Berry curvature contribution is forbidden by crystal symmetry.

authors.name: Haoshu Li
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Qian Niu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
papers.abstract: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_\lambda$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $\lambda^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two newform $f_{\mathsf{54.2.a.a}}$, where these labels refer to the L-functions and modular forms database.

papers.title: Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers via Oriented Palette Constructions
papers.abstract:
Given a family $\mathcal F$ of $k$-graphs, the Ramsey number $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ yields either a red copy of some $F\in\mathcal F$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(k)}$. In particular, if $\mathcal F=\{F\}$, we write $r_k(F,n)$.
  In this paper, we use oriented palette constructions and the hypergraph container method to obtain a lower bound on $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ for special families $\mathcal F$. More precisely, we independently label lower-dimensional faces and use the palette to exclude prescribed red configurations, while a container argument controls the size of blue cliques.
  As a first application of our theorem, we obtain \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)>2^{\Omega_k(n\log n)}\). Combined with the upper bound due to Mubayi and Suk, this yields \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)=2^{\Theta_k(n\log n)}\), where \(B^{(k)}\) is the half-graph. This answers in the affirmative a question posed by Mubayi and Suk. As a second application of our theorem, we show $r_k(k+1,3;n)=2^{\Theta_k(n^{k-2}\log n)}$, which, together with a new stepping-up lemma developed in this paper, further yields $r_k(k+1,t;n)=\twr_{t-1}(\Theta_{k,t}(n^{k-t+1}\log n))$ for every fixed $k\ge6$ and $4\le t\le k-2$, where $\twr_1(x)=x$ and $\twr_{j+1}(x)=2^{\twr_j(x)}$. Here $r_k(k+1,t;n)$ denotes the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the $k$-subsets of an $N$-vertex set contains either $k+1$ vertices spanning at least $t$ red edges or a blue clique of order $n$. As a third application of our theorem, we show that $r_k(F_{\ell,k,d},n)>2^{\Omega_{k,\ell,d}(n^{k-d-2}\log n)}$ for all fixed integers $k\ge4$, $1\le d\le k-3$, and $\ell\ge2k+1$ with $k\nmid\ell$, where $F_{\ell,k,d}$ is obtained from the $k$-uniform tight cycle of length $\ell$ by deleting $d$ consecutive edges.

papers.title: Interpreting the $\gamma$-Ray Emission of the Cygnus X region with a Combined Cygnus OB2 and Cygnus X-3 Scenario
papers.abstract: The recent detection of high-energy $\gamma$-ray emission up to PeV energies from the Cygnus X region points to the presence of a PeVatron therein. This region hosts notable candidates such as the Cygnus OB2 association, which may be associated with PeV $\gamma$-photons detected by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO). The X-ray binary Cygnus X-3 also lies along the line of sight to the Cygnus X region, and LHAASO has observed modulated PeV $\gamma$-ray flux from its direction, indicating that its contribution is also non-negligible. Here, we attempt to interpret the $\gamma$-ray emission of the Cygnus X region using a combined scenario. Assuming a hadronic origin, we consider contributions from Cygnus OB2, Cygnus X-3, and Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs). Our results show that Cygnus OB2 alone, or its combination with the GCR component, is insufficient to account for the multiwavelength observations, whereas including the $\gamma$-ray emission from Cygnus X-3 naturally explains these observations. This suggests that the $\gamma$-ray emission from the Cygnus X region has a more complex origin, necessitating a joint consideration of Cygnus OB2 and Cygnus X-3. The expected neutrino flux from hadronic interactions extends into the GeV band and can help reveal the radiation mechanism of Cygnus X-3, underscoring the need for high-sensitivity GeV neutrino observatories.

papers.title: Sharp global well-posedness for the defocusing nonlinear wave equation outside a ball with radial data
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega=\mathbb{R}^3\setminus\overline{B(0,1)}$ and $3<p<5$. We prove sharp global well-posedness of the defocusing Dirichlet boundary value problem of nonlinear wave equation with radial data in the critical space $\dot H^{s_c}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(\Omega)\times \dot H^{s_c-1}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(\Omega)$, where $s_c=\frac32-\frac{2}{p-1}$, thereby improve the result in \cite{XuYangYou2025}. The proof combines the distorted Fourier transform in \cite{LiSZ:NLS,XuYang2024} with the energy--Morawetz estimate by Dodson in \cite{DodsonCubic2018,Dodson2018}.

papers.title: Optimal quantitative stability near the Coulomb fission threshold
papers.abstract: We study the optimal quadratic stability constant for the three-dimensional Coulomb liquid-drop energy at fixed volume, measured by the squared Fraenkel asymmetry. Let $M$ be the critical mass at which the energy of one ball equals the limiting energy of two infinitely separated balls of equal volume. We prove that, as $m$ approaches $M$ from below, the optimal constant satisfies $\Lambda(m)=(36\pi)^{1/3}(2^{1/3}-1)(1-m/M)+o(1-m/M)$. We further show that every almost optimal sequence with masses $m_n\to M$ from below is asymptotic in measure to a union of two equal-volume balls whose centers diverge. We also identify the corresponding perimeter and Coulomb-energy limits and give a necessary and sufficient criterion for almost optimality after rescaling to mass $M$. The proof combines a strict binding inequality for mass partitions, a local spectral gap at the critical ball, and a BV truncation argument for critical minimizing sequences. All results hold for arbitrary finite-perimeter competitors, without connectedness or boundary regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Conservative Rupture Force Relating Co-seismic Rupture and Afterslip Process
papers.abstract: The post-seismic phase plays a crucial role in the earthquake cycle by releasing co-seismic stress and reshaping the fault-zone stress field. Traditionally, the relationship between afterslip and co-seismic slip is made by the ratio of their respective moment ($R_M$). However, in this study, we perform numerical and theoretical analyses to reveal that $R_M$ is inherently unstable. To quantify the afterslip, we first introduce an inter-seismic "equilibrium state" as a reference from which the pure afterslip is separated, while the afterslip releases the co-seismic stress loading over the velocity-strengthening region after correcting for this equilibrium state. To define the relationship between co- and afterslips, we propose a novel physical quantity termed the "conservative rupture force" (CRF), which is defined as the area integration of co-seismic stress drop. The CRF is equal to the area integration of stress loading over an infinite fault plane as well as the area integration of afterslip stress release over an infinite time and fault plane. This relationship holds for both full-space and half-space faults. We derive a dimensionless parameter as the ratio between afterslip and co-seismic CRFs as $R_F$. We also propose a strategy to derive such a factor with given co-seismic and afterslip models. We demonstrate that after correcting for the spatial partitioning of stress release, $R_F$ converges to one in an infinite time. This strategy is applied to the 2015 Mw 7.8 Gorkha earthquake, and we find that afterslips released 30% of coseismic stress loading over 5.5 years after the mainshock, while a large portion of the fault plane remained locked. The introduction of the equilibrium state and CRF offers a fresh quantitative view to understand relationships between inter-, co- and post-seismic fault slips.

authors.name: Han Yue
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Mineral Processing

papers.title: Tropical limits of holomorphic linking for toric hypersurfaces and points
papers.abstract: A holomorphic top form on a smooth hypersurface in a smooth projective toric variety has a unique meromorphic residue lift when the ambient dimension is at least two. Evaluating this lift at a point, relative to the logarithmic volume form, gives a complex linking number. For a one-parameter family of hypersurfaces and a normalised monomial residue, we prove that this function converges to the indicator of the corresponding tropical chamber. The convergence is uniform over compact sets disjoint from the tropical hypersurface, independently of the arguments of the point coordinates. When the chamber is nonempty and its index is an interior lattice point, the limit is the classical linking number of the oriented chamber boundary with the limiting logarithmic point. A plane cubic illustrates both this interpretation and its failure on a tropical wall.

papers.title: The sharp mass threshold for the three-dimensional Riesz liquid-drop model near the Coulomb exponent
papers.abstract: We determine the exact mass threshold of the three-dimensional liquid-drop model with repulsive kernel $|x-y|^{-s}$ in a two-sided neighborhood of the Coulomb exponent $s=1$. The infimum is attained precisely for $0<m\le\mstar$, with balls as the unique minimizers up to translation and null sets. Here $\mstar$ is the mass at which one ball and two equal balls at infinite separation have the same energy. We compute the first-order variation of this threshold at $s=1$. For $s>1$, a diameter bound proportional to the mass supplies a lower bound on the averaged planar slicing integral and yields a uniform mass bound. The resulting compactness and a uniform quadratic energy gap for finite-perimeter sets close in measure to a ball allow us to transfer the Coulomb classification to nearby exponents. At $m=\mstar$, every minimizing sequence has a subsequence asymptotic in measure to single balls or pairs of equal balls with diverging separation, with both alternatives realized by minimizing sequences. For $\mstar<m\le3\mstar/2$, only the separated pair occurs and the infimum is twice the energy of a half-mass ball. We also obtain the first-order change in interaction energy with respect to the exponent along subsequences of near-minimizers as $s\to1$ and $m\to m_*(1)$.

papers.title: The Fourth-Power Formula for the Antipode in AS-Gorenstein Hopf Algebras
papers.abstract: AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, for which homological integrals are defined, form a broad class of (infinite-dimensional) Hopf algebras. We establish an $S^4$ formula for left AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, thereby generalizing Radford's $S^4$ formula for finite-dimensional Hopf algebras and refining the formula of Brown and Zhang by identifying a group-like conjugating element in the Hopf algebra $H$. Our approach is to endow the space of left homological integrals $\int^{\ell}_H$ with a canonical right $H^*$-module structure compatible with its natural right $H$-action. If the $H^*$-action is rational, then $\int^{\ell}_H$ carries a canonical $(\mathrm{id}_H,S^4)$-twisted right-left Yetter--Drinfeld module structure. The right $H$-action and left $H$-coaction on this one-dimensional space determine a character and a group-like element in $H$, respectively; the twisted Yetter--Drinfeld compatibility condition then yields the $S^4$ formula. The $H^*$-action on $\int^{\ell}_H$ is rational if either the coradical of $H$ is coreflexive or the trivial left module $\Bbbk$ admits a finitely generated projective resolution. In particular, the latter condition holds when $H$ is left noetherian. We also establish a corresponding result for right AS-co-Gorenstein Hopf algebras with coreflexive coradical. As applications, we use the $S^4$ formula to study the bijectivity of the antipode and derive explicit finite-order bounds when $H$ is module-finite and faithfully flat over a central right coideal subalgebra, or finitely cogenerated and faithfully coflat over a cocentral quotient.

papers.title: RepoClean: Evaluating Coding Agents on Repository-Level Obsolete Code Cleanup
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents have demonstrated strong repository-level programming capabilities. However, as software evolves, repository code may become redundant or obsolete, increasing maintenance costs and potentially introducing functional issues. Agents must therefore identify and remove unnecessary code safely, yet autonomous repository-level code cleanup remains insufficiently evaluated in isolation. To evaluate this capability, we introduce RepoClean, a benchmark of 200 cleanup tasks from 34 popular open-source Python repositories. RepoClean is constructed by automatically reintroducing deleted code from real repository histories into newer versions, preserving current implementations and retaining instances where previously passing tests consequently fail. To restore existing functionality without new feature development, agents must use repository interfaces and cross-file dependencies to determine which historical code to remove and which implementations to preserve. Evaluation of seven models shows that even the best-performing model, GPT-6 Astra, resolves only 23% of tasks. Further analysis reveals that agents remove substantially less obsolete code when cleanup is not explicitly requested. RepoClean provides a foundation for systematically studying these cleanup challenges and advancing coding agents toward autonomous software maintenance.

authors.name: Qixing Zhou
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: Critical Topology: A New Perspective for Phase Transitions
papers.abstract:
Critical topology has emerged as a form of quantum criticality beyond the Landau paradigm, challenging conventional approaches to classifying universality classes by introducing topological properties as an additional criterion. Despite substantial progress over the past five years, several fundamental questions remain open. Theoretically, can we establish a general criterion for the emergence of critical topology? Can a unified theoretical framework be extended beyond one-dimensional quantum many-body systems? What efficient numerical methods can be developed to investigate critical topological states in higher-dimensional strongly correlated systems? Experimentally, research has so far focused primarily on single-particle critical topology. An important next step is to realize and characterize many-body critical topology in quantum systems using platforms such as Rydberg atom arrays, superconducting quantum processors, and quantum materials.
  Major advances in statistical physics often arise from re-examining fundamental concepts. The theory of critical phenomena developed by Landau, Ginzburg, and Wilson, together with the topological phase transitions pioneered by Kosterlitz and Thouless, has now inspired new discoveries in artificial acoustic metamaterials. These experimental observations mark a beginning rather than an endpoint for research on critical topology, and further advances in this direction are anticipated.

authors.name: Xue-Jia Yu
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: A Log-Normal Timing Likelihood for Direction Reconstruction of Ultra-High-Energy Gamma-Ray Air Showers
papers.abstract: Ultra-high-energy $\gamma$-ray observations provide a direct probe of Galactic PeVatrons. Extending measurements to multi-PeV energies requires characterizing extensive air showers over large lateral distances, where the arrival-time distribution of secondary particles becomes broad and strongly asymmetric. Conventional direction reconstruction methods approximate the shower front as a deterministic surface and minimize a $\chi^2$ function of timing residuals. Because this implicitly assumes symmetric Gaussian errors, far-axis timing information is poorly utilized. \textsc{CORSIKA} simulations show that the arrival-time distribution of $\gamma$-induced secondary particles in the shower plane at a given lateral distance is positively skewed and closely follows a log-normal function. Using this property, we develop a likelihood-based direction reconstruction method that directly models the empirical arrival-time distribution and its radial dependence while accounting for multiple particles triggering the same detector unit. Applied to simulated $\gamma$-induced air showers, the log-normal likelihood consistently improves angular resolution compared with conical and parabolic wavefront fits, with the largest relative gains for high-energy events spanning wide lateral extents. We also show that independent readout of individual detector units yields better angular resolution than merging their signals into a single station-level measurement.

papers.title: Collective order from language models without communication, memory or shared context
papers.abstract: Physical matter orders without a centre: units interact only with neighbours, and fluctuations carry them over energy barriers from a locally stable arrangement to the ordered state. We ask whether language-model agents can do the same, treating each memoryless query as a particle that sees its neighbours but cannot communicate, has no identifier or shared context and receives the same question as all others. Such a particle behaves as if at zero temperature: told a rule or a temperature, it returns the most probable state, and a collective can freeze in a local minimum. We therefore give each particle only a goal and a die whose weights it sets itself, and test several models. Some of them use the die as a noise source even at a local optimum, with weights that fall with the energy cost of the move; on a lattice the energy of one of them climbs over barriers and reaches the ground state, where the noise stops by itself. Particles in three-lane counterflow also order, from mixed traffic into one-way lanes: a spontaneous symmetry breaking. Decentralized collective order can thus arise from disorder without communication, memory or shared context, with noise that the particles choose themselves.

papers.title: An Experimental Apparatus for Embodied Conversational AI: A Simple Implementation Coupling a Commercial Voice AI with an Avatar
papers.abstract: As generative AI becomes integrated into everyday life, understanding how avatars shape human-AI interaction and the perception of AI as a social partner is becoming increasingly important. This paper builds a research instrument on audio-output coupling, which connects the audio output of a generative AI to an external avatar. There are two implementations: the browser implementation captures the audio of a tab selected through screen sharing without installing additional software, and the desktop implementation captures the audio of the service embedded in the application. Both work with the voice AI as people ordinarily use it, and as a method neither depends on a particular service. The implementation reported here, Deskmate, generates speech state, mouth shape, and expression from low-level features such as voice-band mean amplitude, RMS, peak, and transients. Because it uses no microphone, speech recognition, or transcription, Deskmate acquires neither the user's voice nor the content of the conversation. Records of the conversation remain with the voice AI provider, but none are kept automatically on the side of Deskmate. Three interchangeable backends are provided for rendering the avatar: 3D (VRM), 2D (Live2D), and CSS. Deskmate allows researchers to manipulate avatar presentation as an experimental condition, without changing the commercial service's interface, voice, or response generation. Because conversation content is not held fixed, the estimand is the total effect, including the changes in the participant's speech and the AI's responses that the presentation brings about. A server edition, served from the researcher's server for online experiments, is also provided. The effectiveness of avatar presentation has not yet been evaluated; this paper reports the design and implementation.

papers.title: A uniform Picard-rank bound for Calabi Yau threefolds with finitely many flop chambers
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective strict Calabi Yau threefold of sufficiently large Picard number either has infinitely many marked flop chambers or admits a fibration on a smooth flop model.

papers.title: The Hamilton cycle space in the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph process
papers.abstract: Let $G(n,m)$ denote the graph at step $m$ of the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph process on $n$ vertices. The process starts with the edgeless graph and adds one edge at each step, chosen uniformly at random from the missing edges. Let $\tau_3$ be the first step at which the minimum degree of $G(n,m)$ reaches three. We answer a question of Christoph, Nenadov and Petrova [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 176 (2026) 254--267] by proving that, as $n$ tends to infinity through odd integers, with high probability the Hamilton cycles of $G(n,m)$ span its cycle space over $\Ftwo$ simultaneously for all $m\ge\tau_3$. On the same event, $G(n,m)$ is Hamilton-connected for every $m\ge\tau_3$.

papers.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
papers.abstract: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) trained with ~1.7-2.8x. For example, trained on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B achieves ~1.6x the average downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B over Pythia-2.8B, and matches (0-shot) or surpasses (5-shot) Pythia-12B. Code is available at https://github.com/Caiyun-AI/LoomFormer

papers.title: Active Observation for Robust Visual Servoing in Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robust visual servoing during robotic grasping remains challenging, as approach-phase occlusion frequently disrupts closed-loop control. To address this, we present an active observation framework in which one arm of an existing dual-arm platform carries an RGB-D camera as an active observer while the other executes grasping. The observer repositions to maintain or recover a shared target-gripper view within the feasible shared-view workspace. Occlusion during the final approach is particularly acute: fixed eye-to-hand lacks an active recovery mechanism once the target is hidden, while eye-in-hand can suffer from self-occlusion and sensitivity to hand-eye calibration. The observer first uses an active two-phase viewpoint strategy to align high-precision RGB-D axes with task-relevant error components. If visibility later degrades, an occlusion-triggered exploration module pauses the worker arm and scores candidate viewpoints by observation quality to recover a shared target-gripper view. Because both objects are detected in a single RGB-D image, the resulting Relative Servo Error avoids differencing two independently transformed target and gripper estimates. We evaluate the system on a dual 6-DoF Piper platform using an open-vocabulary detector with text prompts, without task-specific fine-tuning or demonstrations. Across 50 randomized trials per object, the system achieves 94% grasp success versus 76% for a reactive viewpoint baseline and 64% for a fixed camera. On triggered severe-occlusion trials, recovery takes $1.8 \pm 0.6$ s on average.

authors.name: Zhilun Hu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Lowering the Bar for Everyone: Hidden Validation-Seeking Goals in Empathetic RL
papers.abstract:
When RL learns from the reactions of many users, the policy usually cannot see what each user wants. We ask what it learns from users who privately want validation: to validate them alone (targeting), or to lower its bar for endorsing everyone (a threshold shift). We answer this in one setting, empathetic RL against LLM-simulated users (RLVER, GRPO, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct): we vary only the share of validation-seeking users (0--50%; RLVER's default: 24.6%) and evaluate on 1,000 Reddit AITA posts with community fault verdicts.
  The policy shifts its threshold. Endorsement of at-fault posters rises by 3--4 percentage points per 10 points of share; without such users the Qwen model stays at base, and the effect persists at matched KL and under a goal-blind reward. Signal-detection analysis shows that the criterion for endorsing falls while discrimination between at-fault and not-at-fault posters does not decline. An explicit request to be told if one is wrong gives no measurable protection: at-fault posters who make it receive nearly the same rise as those who do not (+0.11 vs. +0.13). When the goal is stated during training, the policy instead largely targets, endorsing seekers regardless of fault.
  Standard sycophancy and empathy benchmarks miss the shift; five of six usable released empathetic-RL checkpoints also endorse at-fault posters who ask for honesty more than their base models, though a pre-registered prediction for two held for only one. The user mix is a training hyperparameter to audit and report.

papers.title: Testing Quantized KV-Cache Maintenance: Encoding Layout and Historical Restoration
papers.abstract: Repeating rows then selecting originals retains layout-dependent drift despite equal encoding counts. We measure when existing checks fail to establish preservation contracts in fixed quantized KV-cache implementations. In four-bit HQQ axis zero at sixteen cycles, median paired relative-L2 increases over same-shape re-encoding are 7.22 percentage points for Qwen3-1.7B and 11.59 for SmolLM3-3B. Matched encoded states cover sixteen shared questions per model at one and sixteen cycles. Axis one matches the shape-preserving control; lazy reorders preserve the initial state. On one known input, fixed update counts retain the difference; preserving group members removes it. Our prefix-view extension passes current-prefix checks yet changes history and next logits in six model/codec settings at residual capacities four and 128. Public lookup reaches this boundary, including one of four precommitted project-new GPU inputs; fixed query swaps isolate a conditional old-history effect. Checkpoint/dense rollback is exact. An explicit delayed lookup client admits a supported 129-token path excluded by native AR on one known context. Failed task-harm expansion precludes population failure-rate or general answer-degradation claims. Native MLX-LM fixtures expose stale caller caches; synchronization restores the tested in-place contract with native computations preserved. In rejection tests, stale callers change logits but not greedy tokens.

papers.title: Go Far, Look Less: Active Multi-Room Reconstruction with Persistent Goals and Selective Views
papers.abstract: Active 3D reconstruction aims to allocate a sparse view budget to recover complete geometry and high-fidelity renderings. However, existing methods degrade sharply in multi-room homes: myopic next-best-view scoring gives transit no credit for distant rooms and over-polishes irreducible nearby residuals, whereas dense mappers reach far rooms only by streaming thousands of frames. We propose ROAM-GS, a training-free active multi-room reconstruction framework that couples persistent goals with selective views: each decision selects a goal and a variable-horizon prefix toward it, capturing only at its endpoint. A Surface Reconstruction Memory scores poses by projecting post-update defects and viewing directions. Persistent goals credit transit with their remaining value and are released once arrivals stop measurably improving them. Without per-scene tuning, ROAM-GS achieves state-of-the-art multi-room reconstruction while preserving single-room Replica fidelity, raising mean coverage from 74% to 93% on HSSD and from 47% to 96% (+11.7 dB PSNR) on HM3D, and matching 90-minute dense mapping using $173\times$ fewer views.

authors.name: Haonan Zhou
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory Fluid Power and Mechatronic Systems

authors.name: Wendi Hu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Gaoang Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Fitch-Based Wind Farm Parameterization for CM1: Implementation, Validation, and Impacts on Convection Initiation
papers.abstract: We implement a Fitch-based wind farm parameterization in Cloud Model 1 (CM1), representing turbines as elevated momentum sinks and turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) sources within the rotor-swept layer, with optimizations for computational efficiency and parallel execution. Direct comparison with the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model shows close agreement in the magnitude and spatial structure of wind-speed deficits and TKE enhancement. Diurnal simulations also capture the known dependence of boundary layer responses on atmospheric stability, further supporting the consistency of the implementation. Under stable conditions, the wind farm produces coherent spatial patterns in near-surface wind speed and temperature that extend well beyond the farm. In idealized simulations under conditions favorable for convection, large turbines promote convection initiation tens of kilometers downstream, earlier than in the no-farm simulation. Analysis identifies turbulent entrainment of warmer air across the boundary layer top as the dominant source of an elongated downstream warm band, with a smaller contribution from enhanced surface sensible heat flux. Secondary circulations develop across this warm band and provide sustained low-level lifting. A gravity wave generated by the wind farm supplies the initial vertical perturbation, which intensifies as it is advected downstream within an ascending branch of these circulations and develops into a localized deep convective updraft.

authors.name: Jianxiang Li
authors.institution: Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Speak When You See It: Proactive Task Assistants Should Wait for Evidence, Not the Clock
papers.abstract: Proactive assistants that guide people through physical tasks must decide, every few seconds, whether a step is complete and whether a mistake has occurred. We find that two benchmarks for this task largely reward knowing when rather than seeing what: a timer that never looks at the video, raising an alarm at 25 s and confirming each step at 30 s, reaches a mistake F1 of 0.373 on Ego-MC-Bench, above every published result (at most 0.27). We formalize this as the video-blind frontier, the best trade-off between completion accuracy and mistake F1 that policies reach from the elapsed time, the instruction and training statistics alone: every published per-step result on Ego-MC-Bench lies inside it, and so do all twelve zero-shot models we run on QICD. To move beyond it, we introduce Evidence-Contrastive Training (ECT): fine-tune on the benchmark's own questions, and pair its positives with negatives from the same recording at the same elapsed time, so that elapsed time cannot separate the two sides of a pair. Trained on 209 QICD videos in about 15 GPU-hours, a 2B model with ECT crosses the frontier on both benchmarks in all four seeds; transferred to Ego-MC-Bench without adaptation, it confirms 59% of mistake-free steps in time, against 30% for a published model with the same backbone trained on about 25k synthetic counterfactuals and real recordings. Its decisions follow the video beyond what timing explains: at equal elapsed time it tells a finished step from an unfinished one in 90-92% of test pairs, where the instruction's typical duration reaches 65%, rescaling the time stamps between the frames leaves it essentially unchanged, and swapping in another recording, of the same recipe where one exists, cuts its completion accuracy by two thirds. The code and model weights will be publicly released.

authors.name: Bohe Chen
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: Uniform velocity support for the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system
papers.abstract: This paper proves that the velocity support of the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system remains uniformly bounded for all time for nonnegative initial data in \(C_c^1(\mathbb R^6)\). The proof establishes uniform bounds on a weighted fifth-order energy moment and an associated fourth-order force integral by exploiting the relative motion of particle pairs. On intervals where the target particle moves sufficiently fast relative to the expansion, these estimates give a summable bound for the current in its energy identity. This bound yields uniform control of the velocity support.

papers.title: The sharp Trudinger--Moser exponent in Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces
papers.abstract: We establish the sharp Trudinger--Moser inequality in the fractional Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces $W^{s,p}$, $0 < s < 1$, at the critical index $sp=N$, including the endpoint. More precisely, there exists a constant $C_{N,s}$ such that for every measurable set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ of finite positive measure, $$ \sup\Bigl\{\frac{1}{|\Omega|}\int_\Omega e^{\alpha_{s,N}|u|^{\frac{p}{p-1}}}dx: u\in W^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^N), u=0\text{ a.e. on }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Omega, [u]_{s,p}\le 1\Bigr\}\le C_{N,s}, $$ where $[u]_{s,p}$ is the Gagliardo seminorm and $\alpha_{s,N}$ is the upper threshold found by Parini and Ruf for $N\ge 2$ and by Iula for $N=1$. Moreover, the constant $\alpha_{s,N}$ is sharp. This answers two of their questions. We use a nonlocal version of Moser's one-dimensional lemma. The $p$-th moment of a translation kernel on the logarithmic half-line determines the sharp coefficient, and finiteness of the next moment characterizes the endpoint. We obtain sharp singular, whole-space, Adachi--Tanaka type, concentration-compactness and affine inequalities. When the Euclidean distance in the seminorm is replaced by the gauge of an origin-symmetric star body $K$, we determine the sharp exponent for each fixed $K$ and show that it exceeds the volume-normalized exponent unless $K$ is an ellipsoid. The same exponents are sharp for regional seminorms on bounded Lipschitz domains in dimensions $N\ge 2$. We prove attainment of the critical supremum on balls for $N\ge 2$ and $s$ close to one. In the Hilbert case $N=1$, $s=1/2$, we compute the concentration level of the singular problem on an interval using a sharp weighted logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. Consequently, the critical supremum is attained for every singular weight $|x|^{\lambda-1}$, $0 < \lambda\le 1$.

papers.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems II: Upper Right Quadrant
papers.abstract:
We study finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in the upper right quadrant. For two vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations and distinct initial positions, we prove global existence and uniqueness by excluding interior collisions, boundary approach, and finite-time escape to infinity. For three vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations, we rule out finite-time boundary approach in the limit inferior sense, without assuming boundedness or convergence of the trajectories. The argument combines Hamiltonian estimates, monotonicity of signed coordinate moments, and geometric estimates adapted to both walls and the corner.
  We also establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for every nonzero circulation triple whose pairwise products sum to zero. The collapse point can be prescribed arbitrarily in the interior, with any sufficiently small positive collapse time. The resulting solutions are asymptotically self-similar, exhibiting square-root contraction and logarithmic rotation. They are constructed using a local strong stable manifold of real dimension two in a similarity system augmented by a complex scale.

papers.title: Global $C^{2,\alpha}$ Estimates for Complex $k$-Hessian Equations on K\"ahler Manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove an a priori $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate for classical admissible solutions of the complex $k$-Hessian equation on a compact K\"ahler manifold with a positive $C^\alpha$ right-hand side.

papers.title: Explanation Selection in Abductive Learning
papers.abstract: Abductive learning (ABL) offers a promising framework that connects machine learning and logical reasoning in a mutually beneficial loop. However, this bidirectional feedback can also reinforce incorrect concept semantics, since different interpretations of intermediate concepts may explain the same observed reasoning outcomes. Static analyses characterize this ambiguity but leave open which explanation training selects and whether its labels can still be corrected. We develop a dynamical analysis of a fixed-feature binary ABL model that links the local stability of competing explanations to differences in their concept labels. We prove that Gram matrices with identical spectra can select different explanations even under the same supervision, objective, and initialization. When any two compatible explanations differ in at least two labels, legal evidence above one half guarantees during training that admissible changes in optimization geometry preserve the selected explanation. Even when only the true explanation satisfies all constraints under a shared predictor, training can still converge to a finite attracting state whose hard predictions violate some constraints and mislabel concepts. Experiments on visual ABL tasks verify these predictions, including wrong attraction from random initializations under identifiable supervision, and show that in ordinary end-to-end training SGD and Adam select different explanations of the same supervision, while unseen concept accuracy drops relative to true-concept references as training concept errors grow.

papers.title: Automorphisms Induced on Cartan Tori and Centers of Quantized Enveloping Algebras
papers.abstract:
Let \(U=U_q(\mathfrak g)\) be the root-lattice form of the quantized enveloping algebra associated with a complex simple Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), over a field \(\mathbb{k}\) of characteristic zero, with \(q\in\mathbb{k}^{\times}\) not a root of unity. We determine the groups of automorphisms induced by algebra automorphisms of $U$ on its Cartan torus $U^0$ and its center $Z(U)$. These groups are
  \[
  \Aut_U(U^0)\cong\Hom(Q,\{\pm1\})\rtimes\Aut(\Phi),
  \]
  \[
  \Aut_U(Z(U))\cong\Hom((P/Q)[2],\{\pm1\})\rtimes\Gamma,
  \]
  where $Q$ and $P$ are the root and weight lattices, $\Phi$ is the root system, $\Gamma$ is the automorphism group of the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak g$, and $(P/Q)[2]$ is the $2$-torsion subgroup of $P/Q$. The proof uses characters of finite-dimensional modules and Weyl-group
  invariant fields to show that the automorphism of $Q$ determined by the toral restriction preserves $\Phi$. Writing $\rho_0$ and $\rho_Z$ for the restriction maps to $U^0$
  and $Z(U)$, respectively, we prove that
  $\ker\rho_0\subseteq\ker\rho_Z$ and determine the quotient
  $\ker\rho_Z/\ker\rho_0$.

papers.title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching
papers.abstract: Forward diffusion reinforcement learning (RL)---enabling deterministic ODE sampling without trajectory backpropagation---has grown increasingly popular for efficiently aligning diffusion models. However, we reveal that existing methods essentially rely on signed reward-weighted regression (RWR), regressing the \emph{trainable policy} velocity onto rollouts from a \emph{behavior distribution}. Unbiased baseline subtraction implicitly assumes that the policy velocity equals the behavior marginal velocity---an idealized assumption violated under classifier-free guidance (CFG) rollouts, offline/off-policy updates, and imperfect online self-consistency. This \emph{behavior--policy mismatch} breaks baseline invariance and injects \emph{baseline-induced gradient drift}, destabilizing training. To resolve this issue, we propose \textbf{I}nstantaneous \textbf{T}rajectory \textbf{D}istribution \textbf{M}atching (\textbf{iTDM}), taking the infinitesimal limit of Trajectory Distribution Matching toward a time-local reward-guided target via the posterior-score identity to yield a sample-level gradient anchored at the behavior velocity without learning an additional reward-tilted target score. Tracking this velocity with an online auxiliary denoiser guarantees exact baseline invariance at the auxiliary optimum, effectively suppressing baseline drift across both online and offline RL. Extensive experiments across compositional generation, text rendering, and preference alignment show that iTDM achieves state-of-the-art in-domain and out-of-domain performance. Notably, on the challenging GenEval2 benchmark, iTDM converges nearly $3\times$ faster than competing methods while scaling smoothly to $0.87$ without collapse. Code is available at https://github.com/Luo-Yihong/iTDM

authors.name: Yihong Luo
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Separating Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness from Martin-L\"of randomness
papers.abstract: Martin-L\"of randomness requires an infinite binary sequence to pass every effective statistical test for fair coin tosses. Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness requires every computable betting strategy to have bounded capital, even when earlier answers guide its choice of which unread bit to bet on next. We prove that Martin-L\"of randomness is strictly stronger. We construct a probability measure by imposing parity equations on infinitely many disjoint finite blocks. The systems have short descriptions relative to their ranks, so every sequence in the support fails one fixed Martin-L\"of test. Almost every sequence under this measure is Kolmogorov-Loveland random. To prove this, we choose each block from a list in which every position occurs in only a small fraction of the candidates. For each betting strategy, after a normalization that preserves success, this sparsity ensures that the sum of its wager fractions on bits forced by the equations and earlier answers is almost surely finite.

papers.title: Fast-erasure energy-cost lower bound and its first-order correction under restricted control
papers.abstract: Determining the minimum work required for information erasure is central to understanding the energetic limits of fast and reliable information processing. In the fast-erasure limit, we derive an explicit expression for this minimum work in a one-dimensional overdamped isothermal system with control restricted to linear and quadratic additions to a reference potential. For symmetric initial distributions at fixed mobility, the minimum work scales inversely with the erasure duration, with a prefactor determined solely by the second moment and a quantile associated with the target success probability. We further derive the leading finite-time correction at a prescribed success probability and verify both analytical predictions numerically. These results provide an analytical benchmark for fast erasure under restricted control, connecting a universal leading cost with finite-time corrections that account for the detailed form of the memory potential.

authors.name: Yihang Cai
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Revealing Geometry under Strong Noise: Spectral Embeddings and Clustering via Random Geometric Graphs
papers.abstract:
Modern massive datasets often contain useful low-dimensional nonlinear structures that are hidden by noise. Spectral embedding algorithms rely on meaningful local relationships between observations, but noise accumulated across many coordinates can make the observed distances unreliable. This also complicates clustering when groups have curved or concentric shapes and cannot be distinguished by their centers. In this paper, we develop a new method that denoises pairwise distances before using them to construct spectral embeddings and identify communities. Our approach uses cross-fitted projections to estimate distances between the underlying signals, selects a neighborhood radius from the observed sample, and builds a random geometric graph whose spectral coordinates represent the latent geometric structure. By connecting nearby points, such a geometric graph can distinguish different groups even when their centers coincide. A novel recursive procedure is then proposed to extract clusters from the graph using its spectral embeddings when such clusters exist.
  On the theoretical side, under a manifold model, we provide guarantees for our spectral embedding algorithm, which can be understood through the eigendecomposition of an integral operator associated with the underlying geometry. We show that the algorithm is robust to noise when the total noise energy is comparable to the total signal energy or, under additional conditions, exceeds it. To our knowledge, this is among the first spectral embedding algorithms that can handle such strong noise in datasets with nonlinear structures. In addition, our proposed clustering algorithm can recover the underlying clusters even when their centers coincide. Numerical studies demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in mitigating noise and revealing geometric structures for both spectral embedding and clustering.

papers.title: PhoneQC: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Order-Level Smartphone Trade-in Inspection
papers.abstract: As vision-language models enter remote smartphone trade-in, sellers already upload six views and a diagnostic screen, which makes it easy to treat the human quote as a step a model can take over. A model may mark a crack or read the screen, yet the quote is a staff form: appearance fill stays near 0.25, and the closed models that score a little higher do so only on the orders they answer, so human appraisal remains necessary. Two obstacles stand in the way. (1) Single-view defect sets and attribute benchmarks do not score an order-level form under a fixed input contract, so a box or a leaked field can be mistaken for a finished quote. (2) The unread half of the form is the staff fields, and a model left to emit boxes or captions does not learn them. We present PhoneQC, a 335-order iPhone-heavy cut that ranks systems by a 0 to 100 form score (Score100) only inside matched protocols (images alone; images plus a detector sidecar), with a declared upper bound that is not ranked as a peer. As a case study on that board, field-only LoRA freezes the backbone, adapts attention projections, and supervises staff fields while leaving the defect list empty; the adapter sees the same images as the zero-shot model. On image-only T1 the 3B model rises from 26.6 to 33.3 at coverage 0.928; without the empty-blocker item the open ranking still favors the adapter, while the remaining gap to a person stays large on this cut.

authors.name: Lequan Yu
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: StateBind: Exposing the Symbol-to-State Binding Gap in Visual Measurement
papers.abstract:
Reliable vision systems should connect numerical claims to visible evidence. In visual measurement, this requires mapping candidate values to image-specific physical states. StateBind-200 augments 200 real images with human-refined local geometry and matched Numeric, Calibrated, and Physicalized interfaces. Across a 128-image held-out evaluation and 6,696 controlled calls, physicalizing identical candidates raises three-model majority accuracy from 75.54% to 91.13%, a source-image-balanced gain of +15.30 points. Calibration and additional reasoning leave most of the gap intact; target localization can succeed despite incorrect value-lattice binding, with a larger burden for two-endpoint ruler spans. An independent 40-image geometry audit yields a 0.08-tick median target discrepancy and preserves the main effect under disagreement sensitivity.
  We further propose Factorial StateBind, a training-free selective verifier. Two VLMs propose target and lattice components, an independent VLM validates their evidence, and valid combinations are resolved deterministically. A precision mode selected on 69 development images combines component validity, four-way agreement, and state separation. Applied unchanged to held-out evaluation, this high-precision evidence gate reaches 91.67% candidate precision across 36/128 images (28.12%) and 9.68% of ordered cells. The results identify instance-specific symbol-to-state binding as a distinct reliability bottleneck and provide an interpretable evidence gate for numerical visual claims.

papers.title: GERF: A Token-Efficient Multimodal Retrieval Framework for Schema-Guided Scientific Information Extraction
papers.abstract: Scientific information extraction (IE) is a fundamental component of AI for Science, transforming experimental knowledge embedded in scientific literature into structured and traceable data for evidence synthesis, scientific database construction, and data-driven discovery. However, critical experimental details are often distributed across text, tables, figures, captions, and surrounding discussion, making them difficult to recover using conventional text-only extraction. Existing LLM-based and multimodal RAG pipelines typically rely on full-document context or coarse page-level retrieval, introducing substantial irrelevant evidence and high textual and visual token costs. We propose GERF, a Graph-based Evidence Retrieval Framework for token-efficient, schema-guided multimodal scientific IE. GERF represents each article as a heterogeneous evidence graph that connects schema fields, text chunks, figures, and figure-derived content through semantic and structural relations. Using schema fields as retrieval anchors, GERF combines direct semantic retrieval, Random Walk with Restart, and null-aware evidence expansion to construct compact, field-specific multimodal evidence packages. Visual interpretation is applied only to graph-selected figures, avoiding indiscriminate processing of the entire document. We evaluate GERF from two complementary perspectives: evidence retrieval quality and pipeline-level input-token consumption. On the expert-annotated SOFC-Exp corpus, GERF retrieves gold-supported evidence for 94.55% of the evaluated field instances, providing broad field-level evidence coverage for downstream extraction. In the token comparison, GERF reduces average input-token usage by 73.40% relative to full-context processing and uses fewer tokens than the evaluated page-level pipelines.

authors.name: Xing Wu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory on Integrated Optoelectronics

papers.title: Lattices of Minimal Covolume in $\mathrm{SL}_2$ over Dyadic Local Fields
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the minimal covolume among lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ for each finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_2$. Using the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ on its Bruhat--Tits tree, we investigate the shape of the fixed subtrees of finite subgroups, particularly cyclic and dicyclic subgroups of $2$-power order. We determine which larger vertex stabilizers can occur at boundary vertices of the fixed subtrees of dicyclic subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $2.A_4$. We use these results to construct graphs of groups defining lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ and prove that these lattices attain the minimal covolume. This extends a result of Lubotzky and Weigel, which treats finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for odd primes $p$.

papers.title: The Space of $k$-Positive Potentials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study weak geodesics in the space of $k$-positive potentials on a compact K\"ahler manifold. We prove that any two smooth strictly $k$-positive potentials can be joined by a weak geodesic of class $C^{1,1}$. As an application, we prove that the pair $(\mathcal H_k,d_2)$ is a metric space.

papers.title: Perturbed QMC designs and reduced QMC strength
papers.abstract: Small errors in sampling locations can change the convergence rate of a cubature rule. We study this effect for equal-weight integration on spheres and determine how accurately the nodes must be realized to retain optimal Sobolev rates. Under an average energy condition on the reference nodes, we establish sharp perturbation bounds and characterize how the decay of node errors affects quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) strength, which measures the smoothness range over which optimal rates hold. We identify when this strength is preserved and when it can decrease, and show that sufficiently slow decay of node errors can destroy all optimal Sobolev rates. For a reference rule with optimal convergence, we further establish a necessary and sufficient condition on node accuracy for retaining the optimal rate uniformly over all permitted perturbations. Numerical experiments with spherical designs, Fekete points, and Coulomb-energy points illustrate the different stability regimes.

papers.title: Lagrangian Construction of the Enveloping Superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$
papers.abstract: We give a Lagrangian construction of the enveloping superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$. More precisely, we realize the Schur superalgebra $S(m|n,r)$, the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$ on $(\mathbb Q^{m|n})^{\otimes r}$, via the top Borel--Moore homology of mixed Steinberg varieties. Their top-dimensional components are indexed by the admissible matrices of Du and Rui and meet a natural symplectic open subset in Lagrangian subvarieties. As applications, we realize the irreducible polynomial representations of $\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n}$ on the relevant homology of the fibers of these maps, establish a geometric $(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n},\mathfrak{gl}_{k|l})$-Howe duality and confirm new cases of a conjecture of Douglass and R\"ohrle on generalized Steinberg varieties.

papers.title: Efficient numerical computation of the generalized Marcum $Q$-function with applications
papers.abstract:
The computation of the generalized Marcum $Q$-function, $Q_
u(a,b)$, is fundamental to radar detection and wireless communications. The state-of-the-art 	extbf{Algorithm 939} (Gil et al., ACM TOMS 2014) serves as the current gold standard by employing a hybrid evaluation scheme combining series expansions, asymptotic formulas, numerical integration and recurrence relations. However, it suffers from a computational bottleneck: in the ``large $a$, small $b$'' regime, the algorithm resorts to computationally expensive numerical quadrature, thereby limiting its overall efficiency.
  To bridge this gap, we utilize a series representation of the generalized Marcum $Q$-function to construct the Series Expansion based on Recurrence Relations (	extbf{SE-RR}) algorithm. Expanded in powers of $b$, this series computes its coefficients via a stable recurrence relation, resulting in a remarkably low computational cost. By analyzing rounding, truncation and cancellation errors, we identify the optimal region for SE-RR as the ``large $a$, small $b$'' regime, which covers the parameter space where Algorithm~939 relies on costly numerical quadrature. Consequently, we integrate SE-RR into Algorithm~939 to develop a hybrid algorithm for evaluating $Q_
u(a,b)$. Benchmarked against $10^7$ log-uniformly sampled parameter triples $(a, b, 
u) \in [0.01, 100] 	imes [0.001, 100] 	imes [1, 1000]$, the hybrid algorithm achieves an average speedup of 82.2\% overall, while in the region where SE-RR is applied, it delivers an average speedup of 156.6\% and a maximum pointwise speedup of $\mathrm{5.49}	imes$. Finally, we demonstrate the practical utility of the hybrid algorithm by computing the cumulative distribution function of the noncentral chi distribution and outage probabilities for 5G/6G ultra-reliable low-latency communications.

papers.title: SJG: A Skyline Joint Graph for Multi-Component Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
papers.abstract: Graph-based indexes enable efficient approximate nearest neighbor search at scale by linking similar objects. In applications such as product retrieval and rental listing search, similarity depends on several components whose relative importance varies across queries. The challenge is that the index must select neighbors during construction, but the query weights that determine which objects are closest are not yet known. A straightforward approach is to index each component separately. However, merging the results of these searches can miss the nearest neighbor under the weighted distance. A joint graph allows a search to follow links across components, helping to avoid such misses, but selecting neighbors separately within each component can leave redundant edges, and keeping component hierarchies synchronized limits parallel construction. To address these limitations, we propose the Skyline Joint Graph (SJG). Although query weights can change the ranking of candidate neighbors, the dominance relation among them is independent of those weights. SJG exploits this property by pooling candidates across components and retaining the Skyline for each node, thereby enabling efficient approximate nearest neighbor search under different query weights while supporting parallel graph construction. Extensive experiments on six real-world datasets demonstrate that SJG achieves up to $27.9\times$ the query throughput of baseline methods at 90% Recall@10, while accelerating single-threaded index construction by up to $201\times$. Its index requires at least 36% less space than the smallest baseline index.

authors.name: Linyun Ma
authors.institution: Chinese Center For Disease Control and Prevention

papers.title: A Tensor Neural Network for Interpretable and Predictive Representations
papers.abstract: Tensor regression is challenged by the exponential dimensionality of tensor-valued covariates and their complex multi-mode dependence. Existing methods therefore often rely on simple models, such as linear tensor regression and tensor additive models, which are computationally tractable but impose restrictive structural assumptions and may limit predictive accuracy. To address these limitations, we propose a tensor neural network that learns low-dimensional, interpretable, and prediction-sufficient representations while preserving the multi-mode structure of tensor data. The model captures nonlinear effects for accurate response prediction while retaining the interpretability of classical linear tensor regression. Theoretically, we establish selection consistency for the minimal representation dimension $K^*$ necessary for prediction and show that the estimator attains a representation-adaptive non-asymptotic error rate. Specifically, the rate improves from the ambient-dimensional order $n^{-\frac{\beta}{\mathcal{D}+2\beta}}$ to $n^{-\frac{\beta}{K^*+2\beta}}$, where $\mathcal{D}=\prod_{j=1}^M P_j$ is the ambient dimension. This demonstrates that recovering the low-dimensional representation is crucial for mitigating the curse of dimensionality in tensor regression. Moreover, minimizing the derived generalization error bound yields explicit tuning-parameter choices for computationally lightweight tuning. Extensive simulations and real-data analyses show consistent performance across settings of varying complexity. Unlike black-box deep learning models, the framework supports direct visualization and interpretation of learned tensor representations without external post hoc tools.

authors.name: Li Liu
authors.institution: Capital University of Economics and Business

papers.title: Robust bounds for American fixed-strike lookback puts
papers.abstract: We initiate the robust (model-independent) pricing of American lookback options under martingale optimal transport (MOT) constraints. Given finitely many marginals of the discounted price, we study the maximal expected discounted payoff of an American fixed-strike lookback put, whose exercise value at $t$ is $(K-\min_{u\le t}e^{ru}X_u)^+$, i.e.\ a function of the running minimum $m_t$ of the undiscounted price. Two structural facts isolate this as the non-trivial American lookback problem: at $r=0$ every classical lookback degenerates to its European counterpart, while at $r>0$ the max-based fixed-strike lookback call remains European-type, but the min-based put is genuinely American. We prove a pricing--hedging duality using the continuous-time duality of Guo--Ob\l{}oj and reducing the hedge to the two-dimensional state $(X_t,m_t)$. In the two-period model, we establish a convexity lemma and exact decomposition of the continuation payoff, deriving the exercise criterion and closed-form free-continuation value. The optimal continuation coupling is the monotone martingale coupling (the third extremal coupling), and we show that the optimal exercise region is a right tail $\{x\ge x^*\}$, in sharp contrast to the left-tail region of the standard American put. The threshold $x^*$ is monotone in parameters and affine in $K$. For finitely many marginals, the structure extends unconditionally: the optimal exercise region is always a right tail, and the optimal coupling is the reflected iterated Az\'ema--Yor embedding, minimizing the running minimum in stochastic order. Under the reflected Ob\l{}oj--Spoida assumption, this embedding is a two-point iterated monotone coupling; otherwise, it includes a local mass-diffusion correction. We quantify the American and model-risk premia.

papers.title: Modularity of Heegner Cycles and Arithmetic Inner Products on Kuga-Sato Varieties
papers.abstract:
For \(\kappa\ge2\), the principal part of a weakly holomorphic modular form of weight \(\tfrac32-\kappa\) determines a linear combination of codimension-\(\kappa\) Heegner cycles on a compact Kuga--Sato variety. We use isogeny correspondences to prove that every such combination vanishes in the Chow group with complex coefficients. These rational equivalences imply that the generating series of Heegner cycles is a Chow-valued cusp form of weight \(\kappa+\tfrac12\) at every level and for every compatible fundamental twist.
  We prove an arithmetic inner product formula for theta lifts on the modular curve \(X_0(N)\) and on higher-dimensional Kuga--Sato varieties. It expresses their height pairings in terms of central derivatives of quadratic twists of newform \(L\)-functions, with an explicit product of local operators on oldspaces. On each primitive newform line selected by the twist, the height of one projected Heegner cycle at a fundamental index with nonzero Fourier coefficient determines all pairings of projected cycles on that line. This specialization recovers the Gross--Zagier formula in weight two and the genus-character case of the Gross--Zagier--Zhang formula in higher weight.

papers.title: The inverse Erd\H{o}s--Fuchs problem for $k$-fold sums
papers.abstract: For every fixed integer $k\ge 3$, we construct an infinite set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{h\le n}r_{kA}(h)=\Gamma(1+1/k)^k n+O_k(n^{(1-1/k)^2})$, where $r_{kA}(h)$ counts ordered representations of $h$ as a sum of $k$ elements of $A$, with repetitions allowed. This improves Dai and Pan's bound for a linear main term. In the paired random model used here, fluctuations of the stated order occur infinitely often almost surely.

papers.title: Is It the Agent or the Retry? Separating Selection from Agency in Text-to-Image Generation
papers.abstract:
Agentic text-to-image systems wrap generators in loops of planning, routing, verification and refinement, and report large gains on compositional benchmarks, almost always relative to a single sample. We ask how much of the gain survives against Single-tool Rejection Retry (\ours): the strongest generator already in the system's pool, an off-the-shelf verifier, and retries that stop at the first accepted image under the system's own budget. Auditing four recent systems with official evaluators, we find that on GenEval SRR matches the accuracy of OctoT2I (0.962 vs.\ 0.96), recovers 63 to 90% of the gain of GEMS depending on the verifier, and exceeds GenPilot by 12 points with 2.3 generations per image; the effect persists with generators not tuned to the benchmark and on T2I-CompBench++. A closed-form analysis predicts the accuracy of SRR at every budget and shows that its gain is capped by the verifier's likelihood ratio. The same analysis also exposes genuine agentic gains: on GenEval 2, even the best of five samples chosen by the evaluator stays 15 points below the score GEMS reports (12 at the upper end of its 95% interval). We prove a ceiling on the accuracy that routing across generators can add, bracket it between one and three points on OctoT2I's own pool, and show that what OctoT2I's routing buys is compute (about 2.5
  less than SRR at equal accuracy), not accuracy. In our offline distillation experiments selected samples teach the generator no more than random ones, which a short information argument explains. We end with a reporting checklist for agentic generation papers.

papers.title: RALC: Risk-Controlled Local Adoption of Segmentation Updates with Few Calibration Images
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning a road-scene segmenter for rain and nighttime driving can introduce errors on normal daytime images. With few labeled normal images for calibration, a whole-image risk check may reject changes that would pass if adopted locally. Risk-Controlled Adoption of Label Changes (RALC) selects local changes from a fixed model update, using confidence differences and an image score to form nested candidates. On each normal calibration image, RALC measures how many more errors each candidate makes than the original model, assigning zero loss when errors stay the same or fall. At test time, each replacement can add at most one error, so the replacement count bounds the net increase without test labels. RALC combines this candidate-dependent bound with recorded calibration losses to select the largest set that passes the risk check. If the models and adoption rules are fixed before calibration and normal calibration and test images are exchangeable, the expected per-image loss stays within budget. On held-out BDD100K, we evaluated three weight-interpolated updates with 10 additional normal images per calibration draw. At a common fixed budget, adverse-scene mIoU was 1.89--3.19 percentage points higher with RALC than with whole-image adoption, while measured mean normal loss was also higher. After matching this loss post hoc at 1,000 pixels per image, RALC still led by 1.135--2.428 points. Selecting changes in $8\times8$-pixel cells recovered 93--98% of this advantage. With 250 calibration images at the original budget, both rules adopted all three updates in full.

papers.title: A muonium laser ionization system for muon acceleration studies at J-PARC
papers.abstract: This paper reports the development and commissioning of a muonium ionization laser system installed in the H2 area of the J-PARC Materials and Life Science Experimental Facility for muon accelerator studies. In this accelerator scheme, ultraslow muons generated by laser ionization of thermal muonium atoms serve as the particle source for subsequent radio-frequency acceleration. The laser system generates coherent 122-nm pulses for muonium excitation and 355-nm pulses for photoionization of the excited muonium.
