The study extends research on algorithmic management, attribution in distributed work, and information and communication technologies for development (ICT4D), and it proposes outage-aware design for platform rating and reputation systems.

papers.title: Using the Tool That Replaces You: Generative AI and the Adoption Bind among Bangladeshi Platform Freelancers
papers.abstract: Platform studies show that generative AI has reduced demand for freelance writing and image work, and experiments show that it makes individual workers faster. This letter asks how these two findings look to workers who are both users of the technology and exposed to it. I analyze 30 interviews with Bangladeshi online freelancers, conducted in Bangla between May and August 2025. Twenty-one participants used generative AI in their own work, sixteen said that it was replacing freelance work, and thirteen said both. Eleven of the sixteen placed replacement on others: on beginners and workers who do not update their skills, on "basic" tasks, or on other sectors. Participants also described how prices fell as tasks became faster, and how clients cited AI to offer less. I propose the term adoption bind for this pattern: each worker adopts generative AI to stay on the safe side of the line, while the same tools, in the hands of competitors and clients, lower what the market pays for the work. The bind suggests that productivity gains measured for individuals can become price losses for workers as a group, and that these losses fall first on entry-level work.

papers.title: From Low-Dimensional Chaos to High-Dimensional Dynamics in Self-Attention Systems
papers.abstract: Continuous-time particle models of self-attention are often studied under symmetry assumptions that yield a gradient structure and constrain the dynamics to convergence toward equilibria. We investigate the behavior of these systems beyond the gradient setting, considering autonomous projected self-attention models with constant query, key, and value matrices and particles constrained to an ellipse. For three particles, the equations define a vector field on the three-dimensional torus. We derive explicit synchronized periodic solutions and compute their Floquet multipliers, establishing the existence of non-gradient dynamics. Numerical explorations using bifurcation diagrams, Poincare sections, periodic-orbit continuation, a nd Lyapunov exponents reveal attracting periodic orbits, invariant-torus-like behavior, and strong evidence of chaos. We then construct higher-dimensional systems by coupling these low-dimensional building blocks through masked and multi-head attention mechanisms. We discuss the persistence of normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds under weak coupling and investigate how the coupling architecture influences the resulting dynamics. Numerical experiments reveal the emergence of additional expanding directions, including a 60-particle system in which 26 of the 40 computed Lyapunov exponents exceed 0.01. These results demonstrate the richness of the dynamical behavior possible in simplified self-attention systems and motivate further investigation of the invariant structures organizing their high-dimensional dynamics.

papers.title: Contact rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants
papers.abstract: We study $C^0$-rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants on closed contact manifolds. We prove that Poisson commutation is closed under uniform convergence, establish weak rigidity for pairs without common zeros, and obtain lower semicontinuity under quantitative control of Reeb derivatives. A three-dimensional counterexample shows that unrestricted weak rigidity fails. For partitions of unity, the contact bracket itself controls the Reeb derivatives. Using monotone homogeneous quasi-morphisms and the Cant--Kilgore--Zhang spectral invariant, we derive positive lower bounds for invariants of open covers and configurations of compact subsets. Applications include a quantitative contact big fiber theorem, bounds on Hamiltonian chord durations and Reeb travel times, and deformations of contact one-forms.

papers.title: Fast 4-bit KV-Cache Decoding on Hopper GPUs: Why Existing Kernels Are Slow and How to Fix Them
papers.abstract: A 4-bit KV cache reads about half the bytes of FP8, but Hopper GPUs have no FP4 hardware and little instruction-issue capacity per byte of memory bandwidth, so 4-bit values must be decoded in software. On H200, vLLM's NVFP4 KV path (FlashInfer's decode) reaches 10-20% of memory bandwidth and is up to 1.7x slower than FP8. NVBit instruction counts show two causes: the kernels behind vLLM's 4-bit paths (FlashInfer NVFP4, Triton UltraQuant) execute 2-6x Hopper's issue budget per byte and serialize loading, decoding and matrix multiplies. Our Hopper-native decode kernel overlaps a TMA producer warp with two compute warpgroups, lays the cache out at write time so decoded values feed the tensor cores from registers, and swaps the matrix operands so small query groups need no padding. On H200 it reaches 67-75% of peak bandwidth at batch 32-128 and at all 11 shapes is 1.12-1.49x faster than the faster of XQA and FlashAttention-4's proposed native FP8. Inside vLLM, with an accuracy recipe (K mean removal and rotation, 4 BF16 sink tokens, BF16 layer 0), it decodes 1.12-1.64x faster per step on Llama-3.1-8B than vLLM's FlashInfer FP8 path at batch 8 and above (1.04-1.24x over FlashAttention-4's FP8), is level at batch 1, and holds 1.63x as many tokens. On one H200 under a reasoning-like request stream, the highest rate at which 99% of requests meet the latency targets is 1.23-1.32x FP8's on Llama-3.1-8B and 1.67-2.20x on Qwen2.5-72B, as the cache becomes the limit; prefill-heavy streams are worse (7% slower prefill). On five 7B-32B models, repeated runs show no significant accuracy difference from BF16 KV. In Qwen2-family models, whose reasoning variants collapse under FP8 KV, layer 0's key mean is almost entirely the key-projection bias identified by prior work, seen through RoPE and computable from the weights alone; keeping that layer in BF16 restores FP8 KV and, with K mean removal, 4-bit KV.

papers.title: Multi-Order Passive Macromodeling from Layouts via Nested Port-Hamiltonian Learning
papers.abstract: Compact, passive state-space macromodels of interconnects and power-delivery networks are essential for stable transient signal- and power-integrity simulations. However, conventional flows require costly per-layout full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations, while both traditional fitting and prior learning surrogates rely on post-hoc fitting or passivity perturbation that degrades accuracy without guaranteeing convergence. In this work, we propose an end-to-end macromodeling framework that learns directly in the passive space, mapping physical layout graphs to multi-order port-Hamiltonian (pH) macromodels. Specifically, our network encodes each layout graph into unconstrained matrix blocks and assembles them via a complete, prefix-nested pH parameterization that guarantees continuous-frequency passivity and stability by construction, yielding valid $k$-state macromodels via direct state slicing in one forward pass. To train all orders without reference realizations, we supervise the network directly on S-parameters through a progressive order-growth curriculum. Evaluated on 27k unseen test structures from a 270k-structure advanced-packaging dataset, our framework reduces mean S-parameter error by $42\%$ on average (up to $65\%$) over established macromodeling tools fitted to ground-truth EM responses, achieves zero passivity violations across $459{,}000$ exported models, and accelerates macromodel generation by $11{,}000$--$39{,}000\times$ ($36$--$85$~ms per layout).

papers.title: Reward Blindness: A Theoretical Framework for Diagnosing Reinforcement Learning Reward Limitations in Text-to-SQL
papers.abstract: Text-to-SQL systems let users without programming expertise query relational databases in natural language. Reinforcement learning has become the dominant way to train such systems, yet progress is still judged by a single number, execution accuracy, which counts correct queries but says nothing about which kinds of semantic error survive training. This paper develops a theoretical framework that examines text-to-SQL from the perspective of reward design. We introduce Reward Error Sensitivity, a measure of how strongly a reward function separates queries that contain a given error type from queries that do not, and prove a Reward Blindness theorem: when this sensitivity is zero, policy-gradient training carries no systematic signal for removing that error. Using fourteen published finegrained error signals for four text-to-SQL systems on the BIRD benchmark, we build error profiles and estimate sensitivities for common reward designs. Predicate and result-level errors are the most frequent, firing on up to 27 percent of queries, while structurally deep errors such as suboptimal joins persist at 5 to 12 percent. Each reward family has a distinct and predictable set of blind spots, and inexpensive database-level checks that need no language model calls detect 45 to 60 percent of semantic errors. Controlled training simulations confirm that executiononly reward leaves output-preserving errors untouched, whereas a signal-grounded reward removes them even when the detectors are noisy.

papers.title: Measure-class classification of achievable Cantorvals
papers.abstract: An achievable Cantorval is a Cantorval that is the set of subsums of a convergent series of positive terms. We construct an explicit achievable Cantorval whose boundary has Lebesgue measure at least $2\prod_{j\ge 1}(1-2^{-j})=0.5775\ldots$. This answers a question of G{\l}{\k{a}}b and Prus-Wi{\'s}niowski and gives a counterexample to the conjecture of Nowakowski and Prus-Wi{\'s}niowski that every achievable Cantorval is standard. The example is generated by a hybrid series of Pratsiovytyi, Vynnyshyn and Vynnyshyn. The lower bound comes from an isolated-digit criterion, which produces a Cantor subset of the boundary whose measure is an explicit infinite product; after rescaling, the boundary measure can be made arbitrarily close to $1$. We also prove that the boundary of every achievement set is either Lebesgue null or has positive measure near each of its points. Consequently, up to homeomorphisms that preserve Lebesgue null sets in both directions, there are exactly two achievable Cantorvals, distinguished by whether the boundary is null. For boundaries of positive measure, the homeomorphism can be chosen so that it changes the normalized boundary measure of every Borel set by a factor arbitrarily close to $1$. For general Cantorvals we classify the case of a relatively clopen boundary support and show that further invariants appear beyond this case. Finally, the null-set preserving self-homeomorphisms of a Cantorval always form a meager subgroup of its homeomorphism group. This subgroup is dense exactly when the support of Lebesgue measure on the boundary is empty or the whole boundary; in particular, it is dense for every achievable Cantorval.

authors.name: HanYu Dong
authors.institution: Liaoning University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Randomized Weighted Distance Nearest Neighbor Classification
papers.abstract: The nearest neighbor classifier is known to be memory-inefficient, and a popular solution is to compress its training data. Recently, a compression algorithm based on weighted distance nearest neighbor (WNN) was proposed, which has elegant theoretical properties and effective classification performance. However, its compression process is computationally expensive, for it performs a greedy search of the densest homogeneous balls in data space. In this paper, we propose a randomized variant RWNN. It simply randomizes the ball search process, and results in substantially reduced compression time (often 0.1%--1% of WNN's) and similar classification accuracy. RWNN also inherits several theoretical properties of WNN including consistency and a generalization bound. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate its efficacy.

papers.title: Grothendieck--Serre for quasi-split groups over two-dimensional regular local rings
papers.abstract: We prove the Grothendieck--Serre conjecture for quasi-split reductive group schemes over two-dimensional regular local rings, that is, every generically trivial torsor under a quasi-split group scheme $G$ over a regular local ring $R$ of dimension two is trivial. Our main result is new when $R$ is ramified and generalizes Nisnevich's result by removing the assumption that the residue field is infinite. By formal patching of torsors and valuative criteria, we are reduced to showing a product formula when $G$ is semisimple and simply connected. Then, we take advantage of relative simple reflections and relative Bruhat decomposition to prove a generation by rank-one subgroups. The analysis on Dynkin diagrams with Galois actions reduces us to $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and three-dimensional $\operatorname{SU}$ factors. For the special unitary case, we treat Hermitian forms by using stabilizations and cancellation to finish the proof.

authors.name: Ning Guo
authors.institution: North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: From Compact Orientation Distributions to Texture Evolution: GSH-Initialized Orientation-Aware Deep Material Networks
papers.abstract: The orientation-aware deep material network (ODMN) is a micromechanics-based surrogate for full-field crystal-plasticity simulations of representative volume elements (RVEs). The conventional ODMN learns the crystallographic orientations together with the interaction directions, so that a complex texture may require many material nodes and a high online cost. This study introduces an ODMN initialized by generalized spherical harmonics (GSH), termed the GSH-ODMN. The initial RVE texture is compacted into the \(2^N\) weighted orientations of a network of depth \(N\) by a volume-weighted GSH procedure. They are assigned to the material nodes and kept fixed, so that offline training identifies only the interaction directions. The best GSH truncation order increases with the network depth. The online Newton system is solved with a tree-structured lower-upper (LU) factorization that exploits the binary-tree sparsity of the network, so that the cost per iteration scales as \(O(2^N N^2)\) instead of \(O(8^N)\) for a dense solution. The framework is verified against full-field direct numerical simulations of two Inconel 625 (IN625) RVEs, one with a nearly random texture and one with a rolling texture, under isothermal and thermomechanical load-unload-reload paths. Compared with the conventional ODMN, the GSH-ODMN improves the predictions of the macroscopic stress and the texture evolution. At \(N=8\), the normalized texture-difference index between the predicted and reference textures remains below \(0.03\) in all cases. Finally, the GSH-ODMN is embedded at every integration point of a two-scale L-bracket model under cold and hot bending cycles, at an estimated cost three to four orders of magnitude below that of a concurrent full-field analysis.

authors.name: Ting-Ju Wei
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University

papers.title: On p-Group Actions and Index Divisibilities
papers.abstract: We prove a mod-$ p $ divisibility result for indices of elliptic operators assuming a smooth action by a finite $ p $-group on the base manifold of dimension $ n\le 2(p-1) $ with no stationary points and which lifts equivariantly to the operator bundles. We show as one consequence that if such manifolds are spin or stably almost complex, with the group action lifting to the relevant structure, then their class in the relevant bordism theory modulo $ p $ is fully determined by one genus, and indeed vanishes for $ n<2(p-1) $. We show as another consequence that there exists no closed connected $ 24 $-dimensional spin manifold $ M $ satisfying $ {\hat{A}(M)=1}, {\hat{A}(M;T_\mathbb{C}M)=0} $, and for which there exists a smooth non-trivial action by the monster group, resolving a question of Hirzebruch.

affiliations.raw: University of South Florida

papers.title: On the theorem of F. Riesz on Blaschke products and on inner functions in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^{n}
papers.abstract: For a convergent Blaschke product $f$ in the unit disc of $\mathbb C$, let $G(f)$ be the set of all points $t$ on the unit circle for which $|f(rt)| \rightarrow 1$ as $r \rightarrow 1$. By a classical F. Riesz theorem $G(f)$ is of full measure, which describes $G$ metrically. We describe $G$ topologically by proving that it is a $G_{\delta}$ set. The same description is true in general for inner functions not only in the unit disc but also in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^n$.

papers.title: Stably irrational algebraically elliptic Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We establish algebraic ellipticity in the sense of Gromov of a general hypersurface of bidegree $(2,2)$ in $\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$. According to a theorem of B\"ohning and Graf von Bothmer, a very general such hypersurface is a stably irrational Fano threefold.

papers.title: Interface invariants of rhombohedral graphene with layer-dependent potentials and couplings
papers.abstract: Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.

authors.name: Yuelong Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Double-dimer loops in the biased Aztec diamond converge to a diffeomorphic image of nested $CLE_4$
papers.abstract:
We superimpose two independent domino tilings of the Aztec diamond of order $N$, with vertical weight $a>0$ and horizontal weight $1$. Represent each domino by the edge joining the centers of its two squares. The edges used by exactly one tiling form loops. After rescaling by $N^{-1}$, the full loop collection converges in law to the image of the nested conformal loop ensemble $\CLE_4$ under the diffeomorphism \[
  w\longmapsto
  \frac{2(\Re w+\ii a\,\Im w)}{\sqrt{1+a^2}\,(1+|w|^2)} \] from the unit disk onto the liquid region of the rescaled diamond. Thus the bias rescales the horizontal and vertical coordinates of the unbiased limit. The topology of convergence records loop multiplicities and the order of traversal around each loop, up to reversal. Transfer estimates in the Krawtchouk basis control slab traversals and opposite crossings along entire sections, including where they meet the arctic ellipse. These estimates give tightness and, together with finite-puncture observables, identify the limit and rule out backtracking.

authors.name: Zhongyang Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Improved Singular Adams-type inequalities and the existence of extremals in dimension four
papers.abstract:
Let $H_0^2(\Omega)$ denote the Sobolev space on $\Omega$, where $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ is a smooth bounded domain containing the origin, and let $\lambda(\Omega)$ denote the first eigenvalue of the bi-Laplacian $\Delta^2$ on $\Omega$ subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish the following singular Adams inequality of Adimurthi-Druet type: for $0<\beta<4$ and $0\leq\alpha<\lambda(\Omega)$, \[ \sup\limits_{{u\in H_0^2(\Omega),\|\Delta u\|_2^2=1}}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) u^2(1+\alpha\|u\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx < +\infty. \] Moreover, this supremum is infinite for $\alpha>\lambda_1(\Omega)$. Furthermore, we show the existence of extremal functions, that is, for sufficiently small $\alpha>0$, there exists $u^*\in H_0^2(\Omega)\cap C_{\mathrm{loc}}^4(\Omega\setminus{0})$ with $\|\Delta u^*\|_2^2=1$ such that \[ \int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) {|u^*|}^2(1+\alpha\|u^*\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx=\sup\limits_{{u\in H_0^2(\Omega),\|\Delta u\|_2^2=1}}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) u^2(1+\alpha\|u\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx. \]
  These results can be regarded as a further development, in the singular setting, of the theory on the existence of extremals established by Lu and Yang [Adv. Math. (2009)]. Our proof relies on the blow-up analysis of the subcritical maximizers, combined with biharmonic truncation adapted to the singular weight, capacity-type estimates on annular regions and a test function argument.
  A key novelty of our approach lies in carrying out the blow-up analysis without relying on an explicit expression for the limiting profile near the blow-up point, which is unavailable in the present setting. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to perform such a blow-up analysis without the explicit form of the limiting profile.

papers.title: On the linear stability of elliptic relative equilibrium in planar restricted $(n+1)$-body problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the restricted $(n+1)$-body problems, where the $n$ primaries forming an a homographic motion generated by the planar central configuration, and the massless particle is attracted by this $n$ primaries. We are interested in the linear stability of the elliptic relative equilibria of the massless particle under the pulsating coordinates. The main contribution of this paper first lies in the investigation of a general $(\alpha,\beta)$-system (1.7). We obtain large-range spectral instability and small-range stability results valid for arbitrary eccentricity. The restricted $(n+1)$-body problem arises as a special case of this system. Accordingly, we derive several criteria for spectral instability and linear stability for this problem. As a final application, we establish some stability results of elliptic relative equilibria for massless particle under some special central configurations.

affiliations.raw: School of Mathematics, Shandong University

papers.title: Global Patterns and Drivers of Terrestrial Surface Albedo Dynamics from 2001 to 2025
papers.abstract: Terrestrial surface albedo is a fundamental determinant of the global radiative balance, yet a spatially integrated understanding of its long-term trajectories and multi-sphere environmental drivers remains lacking. Utilizing MODIS observations (2001-2025), this study integrates Theil-Sen trend analysis, standardized anomaly diagnostics, and a pixel-wise multiple linear regression framework to quantify global albedo dynamics and attribute them to biophysical drivers. Our results reveal that global albedo change is characterized by profound spatial heterogeneity rather than a uniform trend, with 23.3% of the land surface exhibiting significant brightening, while 18.9% showed significant darkening. Multi-driver attribution demonstrates a clear zonal organization of controls: snow cover dominates albedo variability in northern high latitudes (46.9% of classified area), while NDVI (41.0%) and soil moisture (12.1%) govern tropical vegetated regions and moisture-limited transitional zones, respectively. These findings underscore that while terrestrial albedo is a robust indicator of Earth system change, its interpretation depends strongly on regional cryospheric, biophysical, and hydrological contexts.

papers.title: A sharp threshold in the Li--Lin open problem
Seeing Is Locating: Spatial Awareness and Geographic Bias in Decision Language Models
papers.abstract: Decision models, which output probability distributions over candidate labels instead of generating text, are increasingly used as classifiers and evaluators for inputs associated with real-world locations. However, it remains unclear whether they can leverage spatial context and whether their predictions are geographically biased. We introduce GeoDecisions, a multimodal benchmark for evaluating the spatial awareness and geographic bias of decision models. GeoDecisions comprises two tasks: (1) geo-aware image classification, and (2) location rating on objective and subjective topics. Evaluating six decision models against supervised task-specific models, we find that spatial awareness requires vision: textual coordinates alone provide insufficient context for classifying everyday photos and satellite images. We also find substantial geographic bias. On everyday photos, despite achieving higher accuracy, open-weight decision models exhibit more spatially clustered errors than supervised models. Moreover, across all five subjective topics, every decision model gives lower ratings to locations with lower socioeconomic conditions. Finally, we propose a training-free method that combines decision models with a location prior to improve their spatial awareness without substantially increasing performance bias. Our code is available at https://github.com/cruiseresearchgroup/GeoDecisions.

papers.title: Dynamic Channel Gain Map Reconstruction via Object-Attached Gaussian Propagation
papers.abstract: Channel gain maps describe location-dependent propagation, but moving vehicles can change reception beyond their physical footprints. Reconstructing these changes requires connecting local object states to regional power. We consider a fixed transmitter and predefined receiver areas, with historical static and dynamic radio supervision and continuing delayed, noisy vehicle-state messages. We propose OA-GS, an object-attached Gaussian propagation model with a shared area correction. Each vehicle carries anisotropic kernels whose effective attributes are supplied by offline-calibrated templates and affine condition generators. Closed-form Gaussian integrals along finite propagation segments evaluate an effective attenuation model, while directional scattering terms account for additional power. These interactions modulate a learned static reference and contribute to regional channel gain. A shared multilayer perceptron then uses object, propagation, and receiver-area features to predict a bounded path-loss residual that compensates for errors in the compact propagation model. All learned parameters remain fixed during deployment, and reconstruction uses arrived vehicle messages without current-traffic radio measurements. In a fixed-scene ray-tracing study over four development traffic sequences and three initializations, OA-GS reduces map and strong-event dynamic-response root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) from 2.503 to 1.272 dB and from 5.965 to 3.563 dB, respectively, relative to a task-adapted GS-CG baseline receiving eight initial radio reports. The shared correction reduces strong-event dynamic-response error from 3.962 to 3.563 dB under the same propagation backbone, demonstrating the benefit of combining explicit propagation structure with learned regional correction.

authors.name: Junting Chen
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: Uniform dominance of Golod local rings
papers.abstract: We prove that every Golod local ring $R$ is uniformly dominant. More precisely, we show that its dominant index is at most the embedding dimension of $R$. The proof is based on a numerical criterion for formality of bounded complexes whose homology is annihilated by the maximal ideal.

papers.title: Hermitian connections and holonomy with parallel torsions
papers.abstract:
Let $(M^n,g,J)$ be a connected Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n\geq2$, and let $\nabla$ be a Hermitian connection with nonzero parallel torsion. Assuming that its restricted holonomy acts irreducibly on $T^{1,0}M$, the author proved that the first Ricci curvature must vanish. In this paper we derive a Berger like complete list of its holonomy representations: the complexified adjoint representation of a compact simple Lie algebra, and the standard seven-dimensional complex representation of compact $\Gtwo$. Curvature of such a connection is proven to be parallel.
  Secondly, without irreducibility assumption, we derive an explicit local normal form for the metric whose Chern connection has parallel trosion, which includes holomorphic warpings and nontrivial holomorphic extensions of hyperk\"ahler manifolds. For complete metrics with bounded Chern curvature, the characters associated with nontrivial global restricted-holonomy blocks vanish. Compact metrics admit an unwarped local form, are balanced, and have a unimodular vertical Lie algebra. On their universal covers, suitable K\"ahler factors split off and the remaining factor has vanishing first Chern Ricci form. A compact simply connected elliptic bundle over a K3 surface explains why this local classification does not give a global product classification. This extends the classification result of Zheng and author on Hermitian manifolds whose Chern connection is Ambrose-Singer. In particular, the analysis shows that if the metric is not K\"ahler its Chern curvature must satisfies $\Rm_{(\cdot), (\cdot)}X=0$ for some parallel nonzero vector $X\in T'M$.
  In appendix we include a by-product: On a compact complex homogenous space $M$ with finite fundamental group, any Hermitian metric whose Chern connection has parallel torsion, must be K\"ahler.

papers.title: Free-boundary minimal varifolds I: zero boundary mass
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a $k$-varifold in a compact Riemannian manifold $M^n$ with smooth nonempty boundary, where $2 \le k < n$. Assume that $V$ is stationary with free boundary and almost minimizing modulo two in every sufficiently small relative annulus about each point of $M$. We prove that $V$ is integral and that the trace of the boundary second fundamental form on $T_x V$ vanishes at $\|V\|$-almost every boundary point. On all of $M$, the first variation is $\delta V = \nu\,\sigma$, where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal and $\sigma$ is a nonnegative measure on $\partial M$ singular with respect to $\|V\|$. A strict sign for the trace on all tangent $k$-planes at each boundary point forces zero boundary mass. For hypersurfaces in ambient dimensions three through seven, strict mean convexity gives smoothness and proper embeddedness. In every bounded smooth Euclidean domain $\Omega$, we obtain $\|V\|(\Omega) \ge c_{\Omega,k}\|V\|(\overline{\Omega})$ with $c_{\Omega,k} > 0$. For smooth connected free-boundary minimal submanifolds in $\overline{\Omega}$, assuming a volume bound and a common annular almost minimizing condition at a fixed scale, then their first Dirichlet eigenvalues uniformly bounded above.

papers.title: Development of a Hybrid Scintillator Strip-Drift Tube Muon Detector for the FCC-ee
papers.abstract: The Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee) is a proposed high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ collider for precision measurements at the electroweak, Higgs, and top-quark energy scales. A high-performance, cost-effective muon system is essential for muon identification, triggering, momentum measurement, and long-lived particle detection. We present the R&D of a hybrid muon detector concept combining fast extruded plastic scintillator strips with precision drift tubes. The scintillator strips were produced at Fermilab, while detector prototypes with SiPM readout and pressurized drift tubes were designed, constructed, and integrated at the University of Michigan. The hybrid detector was tested at the CERN test beam facility in 2025 and 2026. The scintillator strips achieved a position resolution of 1.6 mm and a time resolution of approximately 350 ps, while the drift tubes provided a single-hit spatial resolution better than 100 $\mu$m. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a high-performance hybrid muon spectrometer for the FCC-ee.

papers.title: When Rubrics Do Not Decide: Silent Value Completion in LLM Evaluation
papers.abstract: Multi-criterion LLM judges often evaluate responses without specifying how conflicting criteria resolve, leaving the winner undetermined even under exact criterion scores. Issuing a strict verdict without declaring the required trade-off premise constitutes silent value completion. We introduce TradeoffBench to isolate this failure by separating rule execution from response scoring. On authoritative criterion vectors, six open-weight non-reasoning judges pass all dominance and equality controls yet pick unsupported winners on 9%-81% of 1,345 conflicts. All 577 order-stable choices follow an explicitly banned majority rule. Reasoning-enabled configurations drop anonymous-vector violations to 2 in 9,720 judgments under an explicit rule, yet cannot bridge omitted trade-offs or divergent component scoring. On raw TradeoffBench text with unspecified trade-offs, GPT-6.1-sol omits its completion premise in 29.8% of 400 verified conflicts. Even under an explicit rule on four-rater-consensus MultiPref conflicts, four reasoning judges still issue strict verdicts on 16/45 (GPT-6.1-sol) up to 35/46 and 25/29 (open-weight judges) of valid presentations. We propose identified-first evaluation, decoupling specification support, explicit completion, and target agreement. In MultiPref human-score audits, peer-mean substitution raises directional disagreement from 0.6% to 28.8% on 2,707 shared targets. A single-peer ablation confirms a 29.38-point gap on 2,175 targets, ruling out averaging as the cause. In HUMAINE, declared partial trade-offs add 2.5 percentage points of coverage, yet newly decided pairs incur 3.9% disagreement versus 0.9% for Pareto. Reliable LLM judging, therefore, requires auditing, specification support, declared trade-offs, and human target agreement separately.

papers.title: Solvability of one-dimensional sub-quadratic BSDEs with unbounded stochastic coefficients
papers.abstract: This study is devoted to solvability of the unbounded solutions of a class of one-dimensional sub-quadratic backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with unbounded stochastic coefficients and general time horizons. In a general sub-exponential moment integrability space linked with the stochastic coefficients, we first establish existence of an unbounded solution of the preceding BSDE when the generator $g$ has a one-sided linear growth in the state variable $y$ and a sub-quadratic growth in the state variable $z$, and then prove a comparison theorem of the unbounded solutions of such two BSDEs when either of generators satisfies an extended convexity/concavity condition in $(y,z)$ with unbounded stochastic coefficients, yielding naturally the uniqueness of the solution. Particularly, the unbounded stochastic coefficient before the state variable $y$ is supposed to take values in $\R$ such that the required integrability condition of the terminal value may be weaker than that under the usual situations. These findings incorporate and generalize some corresponding known results.
