papers.title: RAPID: Codec-Aware Video Decoding for Efficient Long-Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Recent vision-language models (VLMs) can process hour-long videos, but the large number of input frames incurs substantial inference overhead. Existing approaches to efficient long-video understanding largely overlook video decoding, which can take longer than LLM prefill. We propose RAPID (Reference- and Access-Point-Informed Decoding), a codec-aware framework that exploits information embedded in compressed bitstreams to reduce both frame decoding and selection costs. RAPID consists of two components. RAPID-Dec exploits reference-frame information and random access points to skip unnecessary frames and decode the retained frames in parallel while preserving exact reconstruction of the target frames. It achieves up to a 3.7x decoding speedup over the fastest baseline on H.264/AVC videos. RAPID-Sel uses keyframes as coarse representatives of video segments, avoiding the dense candidate decoding and scoring required by existing frame selection methods. It achieves comparable accuracy with up to a 3.0x preprocessing speedup. Together, RAPID achieves a 4.9x time to first token (TTFT) speedup on hour-long videos over a state-of-the-art frame selection method using the fastest baseline decoder.

papers.title: Arithmetic Winding Curves in $\mathbb{F}_1$ Geometry
papers.abstract: We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two. Valuation covers carry these periods on the curve $Y_K$. Their normal coordinates realize deck shifts as Schwartz operators in Meyer's arithmetic trace formula, and their puncture differentials give the finite Euler factors of $\zeta_K$. We construct a sheaf on $Y_K$ for which the middle Fourier--Poisson representation embeds as a $C_K$-module in ordinary first sheaf cohomology. The Dedekind-zeta component is an equivariant direct summand. The injection uses valuation monodromy at the finite places and adelic Poisson summation on the archimedean charts. The cup product of two image classes vanishes with tensor-product coefficients, also after conjugating one factor. On the section side, tensor degree and integral jets give multiplicative lattices, explicit duality quotients, and relative theta identities. A principal cyclotomic twist with determinant one on truncated jets yields a quadratic lower bound for the logarithmic index in a family of increasing rank. The fixed-weight Poisson quotients preserve finite collections of Mellin derivatives at Hecke zeros of orders below their respective multiplicities.

papers.title: Positivity and multivariate extensions of two-parameter Askey-Wilson moments
papers.abstract: Kim and Stanton showed that certain specialized Askey--Wilson moments are polynomials with integer coefficients after normalization, and conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative. We refine this into the conjecture for the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments and prove the refinement by establishing a manifestly positive recurrence. We also construct a combinatorial model that expresses the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments as weighted sums of decorated partial matchings. This model specializes to the partial matching model for the mixed moments of continuous $q$-Hermite polynomials. Finally, we consider the corresponding multivariate moments and prove that their minimal numerators have nonnegative coefficients up to an explicit sign.

papers.title: Learning Dense Head-Object Contact Estimation with Synthetic Data
papers.abstract: Head serves a critical role in human cognitive and perceptual functions while remaining vulnerable to external impacts, making the understanding of head contact essential for human safety. Despite its importance, dense head-object contact estimation remains largely unexplored, primarily due to the absence of head-object contact data. Recently, it has been shown that synthetic data can serve as powerful training data in limited data scenario, implying the potential of synthetic data in head-object contact estimation. There are two core challenges for dense head-object contact estimation. First, head-object interactions are highly diverse, resulting in substantial variations in contact regions and patterns across different objects and interaction types. Second, head contact regions are often heavily occluded by hair, making direct visual observation of the actual contact regions difficult. To address these issues, we introduce HEad COntact estimation (HECO) with synthetic data. To handle diverse head-object interactions, we leverage semantic context from text features that encode semantic relationships between head regions and interacting objects. To resolve hair occlusion issue of actual head contact regions, we introduce occlusion-aware contact learning that learns to infer head contact beyond visible information from images via amodal inpainting. As a result, we enable head-object contact estimation with HECO trained with our synthetic dataset, overcoming the issue of absence of contact data. The codes will be released.

papers.title: Interaction-driven ordering of multiple pseudospins and anomalous Hall metals in Bernal-stacked graphene
papers.abstract: Recent observations of anomalous Hall states in Bernal-stacked tetralayer graphene raise a fundamental question: How do electron-electron interactions organize multiple low-energy pseudospin sectors within each spin-valley flavor? Within the Hartree-Fock approximation, we analyze interaction-driven pseudospin ordering and spin-valley polarization as functions of displacement field and carrier density. We find a rich phase diagram shaped by the interplay between the two pseudospin doublets, including mixed flavor orders at charge neutrality and anomalous Hall metals upon doping. In particular, we identify topological states with $\sigma_{xy} \approx 6e^{2}/h$, consistent with recent experimental observations. Our results highlight the central role of multiple pseudospin doublets in the interaction-driven phases of even-layer Bernal multilayers.

papers.title: DiffSimp: Differentiable Mesh Simplification for Gradient-Based Low-Poly Modeling
papers.abstract: Differentiable mesh extraction enables gradient-based optimization of detailed 3D geometry across diverse tasks. However, compact meshes are commonly obtained through post-processing simplification, leaving simplification-induced errors outside upstream optimization. We introduce DiffSimp, a training-free, drop-in differentiable mesh simplification layer built on QEM-based parallel edge collapse, enabling existing geometry optimization pipelines to optimize their final simplified meshes. We formulate simplification under a fixed collapse history as a locally differentiable collapse map, enabling gradient propagation without relaxing discrete collapse decisions. We combine fast, high-quality parallel simplification with a factorized backward formulation that exploits differentiable vertex quadrics and quadric reduction forests for efficient gradient propagation. Experiments on low-poly mesh reconstruction and inverse rendering demonstrate improved fidelity over post-processing simplification, with additional gains from gradient propagation that increase under tighter vertex budgets. DiffSimp supports diverse geometry optimization frontends, with 1.00-1.25$\times$ the end-to-end runtime of unsimplified baselines in evaluated pipelines.

papers.title: Learn the Effects, Not the Examples: Implicit ICL via Attention Patching
papers.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables language models to adapt to new tasks from demonstrations, but repeatedly including multiple examples increases context length and inference cost. Many existing implicit ICL methods encode demonstrations as fixed vectors, limiting adaptation of the intervention to individual queries and token positions. We propose Attention-Patching, an implicit ICL method that models contextual changes in self-attention outputs through task-specific updates to attention output projections. Using query-answer pairs processed with and without a fixed demonstration set, Attention-Patching fits layer-wise affine transformations from non-contextual attention representations to the demonstration-induced output changes. Across 12 classification benchmarks and four model families, Attention-Patching achieves higher average accuracy than the evaluated implicit ICL baselines while maintaining performance comparable to explicit ICL at near zero-shot inference cost. Further experiments on diverse generation tasks demonstrate its applicability to autoregressive multi-token generation.

papers.title: Individuality from information and intervention: lineages, separation and persistence in cellular automata
papers.abstract: We propose a notion of individuality for deterministic dynamical systems, developed for cellular automata, based on algorithmic information and interventions. A lineage is a sequence of regions of space-time whose contents determine each other up to a few bits, and into which perturbations of earlier regions are carried forward. Two exact copies of an object cannot be told apart by their contents; they are distinguished by their causal relations, since perturbations of one need not reach the other. Individuals are classes of lineages between which perturbations pass, and they form a genealogy with fission, fusion and reticulation. Chains of cheap steps define a directed bottleneck ultrametric, so the threshold yields a filtration and a persistence structure that grades individuality. No region is prescribed: the descendants of a region are the regions that can be located by a short program, recover its perturbations, are connected, and are of nearly minimal size. Considering all source regions at once gives a canonical nested structure, and an autonomy condition marks preferred scales. All notions are invariant under computable isomorphisms of the intervention structure and use no metric on space. We show that, up to constants, the interventional conditions are pointwise versions of known interventional Shannon quantities, while continuity of lineages is genuinely algorithmic: whether it localizes an object depends on the complexity of that object. We prove that neither ingredient suffices alone: systems with identical runs, and even identical dependence structure, can differ in their individuals. For the parity rule on the square lattice we prove that a parent of side q splits into four separated individuals by time q, that the split persists over a range of thresholds of order q^2, and that at large powers of two all descendant regions lie at the four fronts.

authors.name: Konstantin Doubrovinski
authors.institution: The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

papers.title: Sharp signature-weighted total-curvature bounds for complete minimal submanifolds
papers.abstract: Let $i:M^n\to\R^{n+p}$ be a complete connected minimal immersion, with $n\ge3$. We get a sharp bound of $\int_M |A|^n\dd\mu$ from below in terms of the number of ends and the mod-two Betti numbers of $M$. As an application, if $\int_M |A|^n\dd\mu<\gamma_n$, then $i(M)$ is an affine $n$-plane. Moreover, if $\int_M |A|^n\dd\mu=\gamma_n$, then $i(M)$ is an $n$-catenoid in an affine $(n+1)$-plane, where $\gamma_n=\frac{[n(n-1)]^{n/2}}{n-1}\Vol(\Sn^n)$.

papers.title: What Makes Recurrence Generalize Across Lengths?
papers.abstract: Multi-step reasoning requires models to preserve and update intermediate information as computation unfolds. State tracking captures this fundamental requirement, but models that succeed within a fixed range of state transitions may not generalize when substantially more updates are required. Recurrent Transformers offer a natural mechanism for addressing this challenge by repeatedly applying shared Transformer blocks, allowing computation to scale with problem length. We study when such recurrent computation generalizes beyond the training range in a controlled state-tracking task, varying operation representation, positional encoding, and recurrent capacity. We find that recurrence alone is insufficient: multi-token template representations and absolute positional encoding can severely limit extrapolation, whereas atomic operation representations enable substantially stronger length generalization. The effect of positional structure also varies with recurrent depth, with periodic positional encoding achieving the strongest mean performance at greater recurrent depth. Most importantly, scaling the recurrent operator extends the extrapolation horizon, reaching 35.1% exact-match accuracy on sequences of 20-40 operations after training only on 2-10, while substantially larger fixed-depth Transformers remain at 0%. Additional recurrent computation at test time can extend the range over which the model generalizes, but does not eliminate failure on much longer sequences. These results suggest that recurrent computation can support length-generalizable state tracking, but that its effectiveness depends critically on whether the learned computation remains reusable across sequence lengths.

authors.name: Yoonsung Jung
authors.institution: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Skill-Adaptive Noise Scheduling for Diffusion Policies
papers.abstract: Recent advances in diffusion policies have demonstrated strong effectiveness when integrated into hierarchical skill-based learning frameworks, leveraging offline data to capture multimodal and temporally abstracted behaviors. However, prior approaches have rarely considered the diffusion process as a learnable component, adopting fixed noise schedules applied uniformly across skills, regardless of their distinct behavioral contexts. Such a design fundamentally limits the achievable performance, particularly for contact-rich and dexterous manipulation tasks where different skills exhibit distinct couplings between action dimensions. In this paper, we present a skill-adaptive noise diffusion framework (SaND) which introduces a learnable, skill-conditioned noise schedule that modulates the diffusion process per action dimension, adapting the noising dynamics to each skill. To prevent the learned noise schedule from collapsing into trivial solutions, we employ an auxiliary inverse objective that reconstructs the skill embedding from the Legendre coefficients of the derivative of the noise schedule, encouraging the schedules to remain skill-discriminative. This formulation naturally enables adaptive control over the denoising steps for each skill, where noise schedules are clustered in the Legendre coefficient space, and the appropriate number of denoising steps is determined at the point where reconstruction error abruptly increases. At inference, we identify each skill embedding's cluster from its noise schedule and apply the corresponding number of denoising steps, dedicating more compute to skills requiring fine-grained control and less to simpler ones. In simulation and on real robot hardware, SaND outperforms existing skill learning and planning baselines on contact-rich and dexterous manipulation tasks, achieving higher success rates while requiring fewer denoising steps.

papers.title: Digital Twins for Multi-Agent Systems: When to Trust, What to Change
papers.abstract: Digital twins of agent networks need to flag unreliable forecasts and help users choose interventions. Both decisions depend on what happens over several steps: an error can spread through the network, and an edit whose trajectory is easy to predict may still yield a poor collective outcome. We ask when information about error propagation improves failure detection and whether a learned twin can select effective network edits despite imperfect forecasts. We propose Propagation-Aware Validation for Networked Digital Twins (PAV-Twin). Its monitor combines Jacobian-based propagation features with recent errors and ensemble disagreement to estimate the risk that a forecast exceeds an error threshold. Its planner simulates each candidate edit and ranks the edits by their predicted collective outcomes. In simulations, the monitor gained 0.13 in area under the precision-recall curve on larger oscillator networks with familiar topologies and 0.09 on larger networks with held-out topologies, relative to a graph baseline without propagation features. Gains were small in contractive consensus. Giving the graph baseline the same features narrowed the gap. In a separate planning study, ensemble simulation recovered about 99% of the possible improvement over random intervention selection in oscillators and nearly all of it in consensus. With a simplified oscillator twin, selecting by predicted outcome also gave lower regret than selecting by trajectory fidelity. These results show when propagation features help flag unreliable forecasts and why the quality of intervention choices should be measured directly.

authors.name: Phuoc Nguyen T. H
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

papers.title: The coordinate dependence of numerical rank: charts adapted to level sets
papers.abstract: Sampling a smooth field on a grid can give an array of high numerical rank even when the field is simple. A Gaussian ridge rotated off the grid axes is the standard example: in coordinates which follow the ridge, the same field has rank one. The rank therefore depends on the chart, that is, on the coordinates in which the field is sampled. We ask which properties of a chart control this rank. For a field which depends on position only through a function $\phi$, a chart whose coordinate lines follow the level sets of $\phi$ gives rank one. Building on this, we show four things. First, mesh quality does not control rank: a chart whose cells have perfect size and shape can still give infinite rank. Second, when a chart follows the level sets of an estimate of $\phi$, the extra rank depends on a single quantity, the defect, which measures how much the true field varies along each coordinate line. Its size matters only logarithmically, its complexity through a count which cannot be improved in general, and when the defect is simple across the level sets the cost stays small. Third, whether the defect is simple can be checked by differentiating the true level function along the flow which builds the chart. Fourth, rank and invertibility fail differently. When the curve behind an offset chart is perturbed, the rank grows slowly, but the chart stops being invertible abruptly, once the offset exceeds the distance at which neighboring normals of the curve first cross. A chart built from the level sets of a field estimate stays invertible when the gradient of the estimate does not vanish on the band and the coordinate lines along each level set do not cross themselves. Pre-registered experiments in two dimensions show how far the bounds are from the observed ranks, and suggest when each kind of chart is preferable; two choices in the last comparison were made after the experiments.

papers.title: CLFF: Automated Framework for Concurrent Learning Force Fields and Material Property Calculations
papers.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer an efficient paradigm for large-scale atomistic simulations with near first-principles accuracy. However, developing and deploying these potentials often involves intricate procedures that require substantial manual effort and domain expertise. In this work, we present CLFF, an open-source Python framework designed to automate concurrent learning workflows for MLIPs. CLFF integrates model training, MLIP-driven sampling, uncertainty-based candidate selection, quantum-mechanical labeling, and dataset augmentation into a unified workflow. The framework currently supports several modern graph-based MLIP architectures and is compatible with widely used computational chemistry and materials science tools. A distinguishing feature of CLFF is its ability to asynchronously distribute computational tasks across multiple heterogeneous remote computing resources, enabling users to aggregate fragmented hardware infrastructure within a single controllable workflow. In addition to concurrent learning, CLFF provides automated workflows for initial data generation and material property calculations, including phonon dispersion and potential energy surface scans. By minimizing manual intervention and enhancing reproducibility, CLFF offers a flexible platform for developing and deploying MLIPs in computational materials research.

authors.name: Sung Youb Kim
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: SKIA: Spatial-Knowledge Informed Attention for Robust Remote Photoplethysmography under Lower-Face Motion Artifacts
papers.abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) enables contactless physiological monitoring from facial videos, but facial motion, particularly mouth and jaw movements during cognitive and communicative tasks, can severely degrade signal reconstruction. We present SKIA, a lightweight, mask-guided framework that suppresses motion-prone lower-face regions while preserving physiological cues from the forehead and cheeks. Using the UBFC-rPPG benchmark, we first investigate static lower-face suppression in the classical CHROM pipeline. Static masking improves waveform Pearson correlation from 0.3507 to 0.4166 (p < 0.001) and reduces heart-rate mean absolute error (MAE) from 33.50 to 23.44 bpm. Building on this finding, we introduce SKIA-Net, a compact spatiotemporal architecture that combines raw facial frames, statically masked representations, and temporal motion differences to reconstruct blood volume pulse (BVP) waveforms. The full model achieves a Pearson correlation of 0.7522 and a heart-rate MAE of 3.73 bpm on UBFC-rPPG, outperforming single-stream variants. Ablation studies show that the static mask provides complementary information to raw appearance and that static anatomical priors outperform the tested dynamic optical-flow-based masking strategy. These results suggest that spatially informed, temporally stable masking can improve motion-robust rPPG estimation. Code: https://github.com/lee-vtruong/SKIA-rPPG

authors.name: Viet-Tham Huynh
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

papers.title: Pieri formula for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of flag manifolds of type $A$
papers.abstract: We prove a Pieri formula for the quantum product of an arbitrary opposite Schubert class with the opposite Schubert class associated to the cyclic permutation of the form $c[k,p]=(k-p+1,\ldots,k+1)$ in the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory ring of the (full) flag manifold $Fl_n = SL_n(\C)/B$. In this formula, the quantum product is expressed as a sum over $k$-Pieri chains in the quantum Bruhat graph on $S_n$. We give the coefficient of each $k$-Pieri chain in terms of the first components of its labels and the descents among labels with the same second component. By setting all equivariant parameters equal to $1$, the coefficient of a nonempty $k$-Pieri chain becomes the signed number of its $p$-markings.

authors.name: Khanh Nguyen Duc
authors.institution: Trường Đại học Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Nội

papers.title: CLIP-FMoE: Scalable CLIP via Fused Mixture-of-Experts with Enforced Specialization
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures have emerged as a promising approach for scaling deep learning models while maintaining computational efficiency. However, existing MoE adaptations for Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) models suffer from significant computational overhead during sequential training and degradation of zero-shot capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose CLIP-FMoE, a novel approach that integrates MoE architecture into CLIP fine-tuning. Our method uses Isolated Constrained Contrastive Learning, a pipeline that trains specialized experts on cluster-based data partitions to accelerate expert specialization. Additionally, we introduce a Fusion Gate mechanism to mitigate catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our approach achieves consistent improvements on downstream tasks while preserving zero-shot capabilities. Furthermore, our method demonstrates robust performance across varying context lengths, making it particularly suitable for diverse real-world applications.

authors.name: Huynh Dang Nguyen
authors.institution: Trường Đại học Tài nguyên và Môi trường TP. Hồ Chí Minh

papers.title: Monsky's nodal cubic and the arithmetic of Frobenius invariants
papers.abstract: We prove Monsky's conjecture on the colengths of the ideals $(x^q,y^q,z^q,h^j)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y,z]$, where $h=x^3+y^3+xyz$, $q=2^e$, and $0\le j\le q$. We derive Monsky's recursion by interchanging the values of sections of syzygy bundles on the two branches at the node of the cubic $h=0$. For the hypersurface $uv+h=0$, the Hilbert-Kunz and Frobenius splitting series are algebraic of degree two over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. For $uv+h(X_1)+\cdots+h(X_m)=0$, where the $X_i$ are disjoint triples of variables and $m\ge 2$, both series are transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. When $m=2$, we express the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity in terms of a period of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero. This gives an explicit seven-dimensional hypersurface over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with transcendental Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity and transcendental $F$-signature.

papers.title: Meddies-PII: A Multilingual Framework for Personally Identifiable Information Extraction in Clinical De-identification
papers.abstract: Multilingual PII extraction in clinical text is limited by scarce governed data and by synthetic corpora whose construction is thinly documented. We present a large multilingual dataset covering seventeen languages, including seven Southeast Asian languages, and nine PII labels. We also document a detailed generation pipeline and release the complete prompts, catalogues, checks and label maps. A compact 350M-parameter BIOES token classifier trained on the resource achieves the highest score on all fifteen public benchmarks, significantly ahead of the strongest of four public systems on fourteen of them, with a mean exact-match F1 of 0.827 against 0.672 for the strongest system. We also tested it, without adaptation, on multilingual benchmarks, including two human-annotated German and Spanish clinical-style corpora, where it is competitive with the best public systems once annotation conventions are aligned, and is best in four of ten MultiGraSCCo languages; the results show that performance transfers across public benchmarks. We also analyse the data and find almost no near-duplicates and no text overlap between training and any evaluation set. The dataset, benchmark, model, generation framework and evaluation code are planned for public release upon acceptance.

papers.title: Maximal sections of the cube
papers.abstract: We prove the folklore conjecture on maximal central sections of the cube in every dimension and codimension. The maximizing sections are exactly the products of diagonals of disjoint coordinate blocks whose sizes differ by at most one. This determines the sharp volume in the cases left open by Ball's 1989 bounds. In fixed dimensions, the logarithmic volume deficit controls both the direction and the displacement of an affine section linearly, with optimal exponent. We also obtain the sharp uniform bound on projection densities for independent real random variables with bounded densities.

papers.title: Filters as a localization of nets
papers.abstract: Based on different notions of subnet in the literature, we define categories of nets and investigate their categorical relationships. We show that the category of proper filters with filter-preserving functions is, up to equivalence, a localization of four of these categories.

papers.title: PseuDRAGON: Knowledge-Guided Local LLMs for Financial-Data Pseudonymization in Closed Networks
papers.abstract: Staff pseudonymizing financial data in closed networks must interpret abbreviated column names, identify personal information, and choose processing methods. Local language models can assist, but may give different labels for the same input. PseuDRAGON keeps confirmed judgments and corrections outside a fixed model and reuses them through exact-name lookup and learned rules. For expert review, the workflow searches institutional policy, national privacy law, then international sources. Across 92 columns from one institution, rules increase reuse under the same approval checks from 75 to 83 labels without reuse errors when all training judgments are available. With 25% of the training judgments, withholding non-PII rules for unseen names eliminated the extra PII misses in replay at the cost of lower reuse. Revising or withdrawing approvals rebuilds derived rules, and tests on synthetic records verify that selected methods produce the specified outputs. In three paired runs, the history-first baseline cut automated identification time by 83.0% on average versus no reuse.

authors.name: Seonho An
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: KyungTae Lim
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Optimal isotropic three-material conducting composites with an ideal conductor, in the plane and in space.Bounds and optimal structures
papers.abstract:
The paper describes an optimal isotropic three-dimensional, three-material conducting composite. One material is an ideal conductor, the volume fractions are prescribed, and the objective is to minimize the effective conductivity over all admissible layouts.
  We first derive a lower bound for the effective conductivity as a function of the material properties and volume fractions. The composite energy is bounded below by a constrained polyconvex envelope, where quadratic and cubic null Lagrangians are imposed through Lagrange multipliers. We further assume that the fields in optimal structures are positive semidefinite. Together with the use of the cubic null Lagrangian, this assumption makes the bound exact. The resulting bound determines the extremal conductivity and the set of associated support fields in optimal structures. Depending on the parameters, it has five regions with different analytic expressions.
  We then prove the bound attainability by constructing optimal structures that realize the bound in every region. They are spherical atoms: a core of the intermediate-conducting material, surrounded by a mantle of wrapped optimal planar structures. In the two extreme regions, a crust is added from the material whose prescribed volume fraction is excessive.

papers.title: CXL Coherence Writes Back What Surviving Hosts See, Leaving Flushes Only for Ordering
papers.abstract: Hosts that share memory over Compute Express Link (CXL) cache its lines, and a host that crashes loses the lines it has modified and not written back. Designs for such memory stop every host when one crashes, assume stored energy, or flush after each operation. We show that when a crashing host's clients die with it, the flushes a host crash requires are those that keep one line from reaching the memory device before a line it depends on, and not those that make a finished operation durable. The reason is a property that CXL requires of the fabric: a modified line is written back before another host accesses it. Whatever a surviving host has seen is then on the device, and our crash condition lets a crash drop operations that only the crashed host observed. We prove the claim for operations that take effect in a single store, and test it on small instances of models of three published designs, whose operations store several times. A lock table needs no flush to keep the locks of surviving hosts. A persistent hash index keeps every operation a survivor has observed, and in two workloads it writes fewer than half as many lines to the device as its published code does. An allocator's flush of each new reference is neither sufficient nor necessary for the survivors' safety: the allocator lacks ordering flushes, one of them when a reference changes hands.

papers.title: $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces
papers.abstract: We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.

papers.title: Infrared Relaxation Modes and the Emergence of Collective Order in Neural Dynamics
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic field theory of collective order formation in interacting nonlinear neural systems. Integrating out microscopic neural degrees of freedom yields an effective action whose quadratic kernel determines the ordering threshold, while higher-order connected responses govern nonlinear stabilization. Spectral decomposition reveals that relaxation rates and collective-mode overlaps control collective instability and memory dynamics. Enhanced infrared spectral weight lowers the critical coupling and generates long-time memory, revealing a common spectral origin of collective ordering and persistent dynamics. Controlled numerical constructions verify the spectral dependence of collective instability and response, while nonlinear mean-field scaling follows from the microscopic Landau expansion. Transformer Jacobian spectra further reveal learning-induced infrared organization and transient memory enhancement consistent with critical-like response. Our results establish a microscopic framework linking neural interactions, collective order, and long-time memory.

papers.title: The Hlawka-Schatten inequality: an exposition of recent progress
papers.abstract: We give an expository account of recent progress on a question of Audenaert and Kittaneh concerning a Hlawka-type inequality for Schatten norms of matrices. We review the classical Hornich-Hlawka inequality and explain the motivation behind understanding the so-called Hlawka-Schatten inequality. We present an elementary $2 \times 2$ construction showing that no finite constant satisfies the Hlawka-Schatten inequality for the trace norm, and explain Esa's proof that a dimension-independent constant exists for every $1 < p < \infty$. We also discuss the Hlawka-Schatten inequality for diagonal matrices and subsequent developments thereof on Prove2Me. Our aim is to make the mathematical ideas behind these AI-assisted results accessible, and to clarify their relationship with the available Lean formalizations.

papers.title: LEAF: Calibrated and Robust Wavelet Estimation of the Hurst Exponent
papers.abstract: Wavelet logscale regression for the Hurst exponent H of fractional Brownian motion (fBm) is sensitive to outliers and biased in finite samples. We introduce the Log-Energy with Adaptive Floor (LEAF) ordinate, which averages the logarithms of squared wavelet coefficients after adding a floor proportional to a pilot estimate of the level variance. If standardized coefficients share a common law across levels, a floor proportional to the true level variance preserves the population slope, and a consistent pilot preserves it asymptotically. We derive the asymptotic variance and influence function, and identify the variance-minimizing floor for median-pilot LEAF, whose influence grows only logarithmically. With outliers of ten increment standard deviations in up to 1% of observations, median-pilot LEAF reduces root mean squared error by a factor of 1.8 to 2.6 relative to calibrated log-energy. At H = 0.5 with 1% outliers, the error falls from 0.139 to 0.059. For small to moderate H, the main source of bias is the departure of expected wavelet energies from the ideal power law at fine scales. We estimate H from an estimating equation calibrated by simulation under fBm. Calibrating the mean logscale diagram alone delivers nearly all of the gain: it nearly eliminates bias in matched simulations and improves on the Abry--Veitch estimator most at small H. Simulations also show how scale-dependent tails can erode the gains of a robust pilot and how misspecification can undermine calibration.

papers.title: KernelMix: Bayesian kernel machine regression in Python
papers.abstract: Exposures measured together can have nonlinear associations with an outcome, and the association with one exposure may depend on another. Bayesian kernel machine regression represents these patterns through a flexible exposure-response function. We implement this approach in KernelMix, a Python package. To handle different outcome types, KernelMix combines the exposure function with continuous, binary, count and survival models, including selected extensions for clustered observations and censored event times. For fitted models, it returns posterior summaries, uncertainty intervals, joint predictions and sampling diagnostics. Fitting and prediction use NumPy and SciPy without requiring R. To assess the implementation, we compare selected Gaussian and probit posterior summaries and conditional calculations with installed R bkmr 0.2.2 and check additional model components against independent mathematical calculations. A daily ozone analysis illustrates how these components form an analysis workflow.

papers.title: AI Meets Turbulence Modeling: Balancing Causation, Correlation, and User Intent
papers.abstract: Turbulence states vary widely in modeling difficulty, requiring distinct paradigms; thus, no single AI or data-driven approach suits all flows. We propose an operational framework classifying data-driven turbulence modeling by balancing physical causation and statistical correlation via non-equilibrium flow memory and user intent. Using the Mori--Zwanzig projection formalism, we decompose unclosed turbulent stress into a local response ($\tau_{ij}^L$) and a spatio-temporally non-local memory integral ($\tau_{ij}^{NL}$). Near statistical equilibrium, rapid relaxation suppresses advective memory, letting local correlations capture physical causation via intrusive $\tau_{ij}^L$ constitutive relations in Reynolds-Averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) equations. Because the elliptic Poisson equation for fluctuating pressure couples stress evolution to eddy dimensionality beyond single-point velocity-gradient componentiality, local closures are not strictly valid even at equilibrium, yet remain acceptable engineering approximations. In non-equilibrium turbulence, modeling bifurcates by user intent. For predicting unseen geometries, large coherent structures sustain non-local memory ($\tau_{ij}^{NL}$), invalidating local total-stress closures and requiring first-principles causal scale resolution guided by Rules-Augmented AI (RAAI), with resolution set by a recent non-equilibrium theory. Conversely, for rapid design in a known, parameterized coherent flow class, a purely correlational strategy suffices: combining Non-Intrusive Reduced-Order Modeling (NIROM) with uncentered Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) across multi-realization ensembles yields zero-solver synthesis of stationary statistics and unsteady coherent evolution from governing dimensionless parameters. This framework aligns physical causation, statistical correlation, and user intent across flow regimes.

papers.title: Measuring GPU Memory Traffic on the NVIDIA GB10 Without C2C Telemetry
papers.abstract: The NVIDIA GB10, used in the DGX Spark and in desktop AI systems from several vendors, joins an Arm CPU die and a Blackwell GPU die with NVLink C2C. The GPU has no local memory, so every GPU access that misses in its L2 cache crosses C2C to the LPDDR5X attached to the CPU die. Yet the software on the systems we tested exposes no counter for this traffic. We show that five L2 sector counters of the GPU, sampled every 10 ms through NVIDIA's CUPTI sampling interface by a process that does not attach to the workload, measure GPU memory traffic live and separate copy engine traffic from the read misses and writes of GPU kernels. For large streaming transfers of known size, the counters agree within 0.28% on an Acer GN100 and within 0.005% on a DGX Spark, track the volume moved regardless of how it is split into copies, and exclude data reused in L2. The GPU's SMMU counter, a natural alternative, counts address translations rather than bytes. Applied to an unmodified server, the method shows Mistral 7B decode reading 13.47 GiB per token, the weights it uses plus its key value (KV) cache, at 83% of the memory bandwidth NVIDIA specifies. We release the method as an open source tool.

papers.title: eSPG: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Event Speckle Plethysmography
papers.abstract: Non-contact measurement of vital signs such as heart rate (HR) is valuable for patient monitoring and rescue operations. However, existing methods struggle with ambient illumination and motion, and have been demonstrated only at distances of tens of meters. Here we introduce event speckle plethysmography (eSPG), which illuminates a body part with a low-power (0.5-5 mW) laser and captures the resulting dynamic speckle pattern using an event camera. Event cameras, with their high dynamic range, temporal resolution, and sensitivity to intensity changes, are well-suited to capturing rapid speckle fluctuations that encode the physiological signal, even under challenging illumination and imaging conditions. We demonstrate HR estimation at 1 km with a mean absolute error of 5 beats per minute, and 90% of estimates satisfy an AAMI-defined HR estimation criterion. This distance exceeds previous remote plethysmography demonstrations by an order of magnitude and previous speckle plethysmography demonstrations by over three orders of magnitude. We also study and characterize robustness to motion and ambient illumination. Our theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate that resolving dynamic speckle fluctuations enables accurate heart rate estimation even at kilometer-scale distances, establishing a new direction toward robust, non-contact physiological monitoring.

authors.name: Pablo A. Valdes
authors.institution: The University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston

papers.title: Rollout Scheduling for Chaotic Neural ODEs: Coverage Gains, Computational Cost, and Predictive Accuracy
papers.abstract: Training Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs) on chaotic systems is difficult because small changes in model parameters can lead to rapidly growing differences in predictions. A rollout is a trajectory predicted by the model. Choosing its length from a single global Lyapunov time overlooks differences in local instability. We study rollout scheduling for training on one contiguous rollout per sampled state, asking whether adapting its length to local instability improves prediction. We find the schedule that uses the most trajectory data under an instability budget, a limit on how much instability any one rollout may accumulate. Under stated assumptions, we bound the resulting coverage gain and the coverage lost when the instability estimates are in error. Numerical checks illustrate the theory. Training experiments on Lorenz-63, Lorenz-96, and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky compare adaptive and constant schedules at the same instability budgets and maximum rollout lengths. The budgets are computed from the true system's finite-time Lyapunov exponents. Across the tested settings, adaptive schedules increase trajectory coverage at additional computational cost, without showing a consistent improvement in prediction accuracy. On Lorenz-63, limiting adaptive rollouts to the horizon used to estimate instability improves prediction at the larger budgets. On Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, most configurations provide useful short-time predictions, while all tested long rollouts eventually fail. These findings show why coverage, prediction accuracy, and long-time behavior need separate evaluation, and why instability estimates should be checked over the windows used in training.

authors.name: Xuping Xie
authors.institution: The University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston

papers.title: Contiguous relations for elliptic analogues of partial sums of very-well-poised ${}_8\psi_8$ series
papers.abstract: We introduce finite elliptic analogues of partial sums of a balanced very-well-poised ${}_8\psi_8$ series. By combining Abel's lemma on summation by parts with the Riemann theta relation, we establish two contiguous relations. Iterating the second relation gives two finite transformation formulas.

papers.title: Toward Open Room-Scale Scanning with Consumer LiDAR via Depth-Inertial Odometry
papers.abstract: Room scanning with consumer LiDAR today depends on ARKit, whose tracking and map update are a black box: an application receives depth and poses but cannot inspect how they were produced, so an error in a scan cannot be traced to its cause. This paper examines whether an open alternative, one whose every stage can be inspected, is feasible on the device. Mobile-LIO is a depth-inertial odometry pipeline that uses the phone's depth and inertial data and no ARKit poses. On seven ScanNet++ iPhone recordings it completed every scene with 0.2-2.0 m deviation from the ARKit-derived reference, where six open-source LiDAR-inertial estimators run as configured for dedicated scanners had at least 4.46 m in 41 of 42 runs (two of the six also failed a noise-free adapter check, and Mobile-LIO has a speed cap they lack; the comparison is not controlled and does not rone 15 Pro Max, a buildwith corrected phone code kept up with the sensor in 14 of 15 replay runs of three 7-13 s recordings; e estimator before thosecorrections. Laser-scanned meshes give the accuracy. Within 3 m, recorded depth differed from the m on three held-out scenes,maps fused with ARKit poses that the dataset scales and aligns to the mesh la a median 1.8-2.3 cm from 17 cm. Because thepipeline is open, the gap could be examined: in the scene with the largest error, noise-free renderefrom 1.97 m to 0.04 m, sorecorded depth, whose error reached 20-54 cm at 5-7 m, contributed alongside the estimator. An open de tracked on phone depth and kept up with the sensor in short phone replays, but it is not yet as accurate as ARKit-pose maps, whicheach only the coarsestUSIBD accuracy level (LOA10); its accuracy on the device was not measured.

papers.title: Note on the extendability problem for invariant quasimorphisms for mapping class groups
papers.abstract: In this note, we study the extendability problem of invariant quasimorphisms for short exact sequences related to mapping class groups of surfaces, possibly with one boundary component or one marked point. Using a recent result of Blatz, we prove that if the genus is at least two, then every homogeneous quasimorphism on the Torelli group that is invariant by the conjugation action by the mapping class group is uniquely extendable to the whole mapping class group. Contrastingly, for the surface with one marked point whose genus is at least three, we show the existence of a homogeneous Torelli-group-invariant quasimorphism on the Johnson kernel that is not extendable.

papers.title: Twisted K-Theory and Reduced Norms over Global and Higher Local Fields
papers.abstract: We prove the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture concerning reduced norms over both global and local fields. Furthermore, in both settings, we construct maps between truncated K-theory spectra that induce the reduced norms in degrees 1 and 2, and show that these maps are equivalences over local fields. Over global fields, we establish finiteness properties of their fibers and give a detailed description of their structure. We also extend the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture to two-dimensional local fields and three-dimensional local fields with characteristic sequences (0, 0, 0) and (0, 0, p), and prove it in these settings. Finally, we apply these results to noncommutative class field theory over number fields and obtain a description of the Artin map associated with a central simple algebra.

papers.title: VidRouteBench: A Benchmark for Budgeted Video-Generation Routing
papers.abstract:
Text-to-video generators differ by two orders of magnitude in price, and a cheap configuration of a strong model is often good enough for a prompt. Routing prompts across such arms (model x sampling configuration) should buy quality at fixed budget, but no dataset supports studying it: public video-preference sets contain only closed models, one configuration each.
  We release VidRouteBench: 16 arms from 7 open families spanning 121x in measured cost ($0.0025-$0.298 per clip), 27,110 clips (1,421 A800-hours) over 1,625 grouped prompts, a quality score frozen after calibration against human preferences (68.7% CV accuracy vs 66.2% for the best single scorer), per-clip scores on 9 identifiable quality dimensions, repeated seeds, an encrypted test split, and a sealed newest family for cold start. The evaluator compares a router against the best prompt-agnostic mixture of arms, not the best single arm. Per-prompt specialisation here is real and predictable (oracle gap 0.642, 47% reproducible across seeds, prompt-arm interaction F=4.47 at p=1.6e-63), unlike LLM-routing arms, where the same pipeline finds none.
  We then propose OPMU (one probe, many utilities): label a new arm on K probe prompts, predict its 9 dimensions once, and serve any scenario utility by scalarising afterwards. Over 215 utility directions OPMU Pareto-dominates the prompt-agnostic baseline for 94% of directions versus 90% for per-scenario routers, with no per-scenario retraining. Three baselines fail instructively: bag-of-words features lose almost all routing gain in the low-data regime (0.009 vs 0.168); crediting a new arm with its probe average is harmful (-3.32 recovery) although it is the strong baseline on RewardBench-style arms (0.786); Chebyshev scalarisation does not help, our cost-utility front being convex.

authors.name: Dayu Wang
authors.institution: Zhejiang University Medical College Affiliated Stomatological Hospital

papers.title: Geometric Polarization-Virial Theorems for Field-Induced Dipolar Interactions and Force Reversal
papers.abstract: Electric fields can turn attraction into repulsion between far-separated atoms, yet the complete angular mechanical structure governing this reversal has remained unknown. Here, we uncover an entropy-like geometric structure: the cubically weighted interaction free energy, r^3 F(r), is nondecreasing under physical dilation. This structure unifies two exact polarization-virial theorems for arbitrary stable quasistatic dipole assemblies and fully retarded dipole pairs under stated conditions. Consequently, the free energy has at most one zero and energetic cancellation precedes mechanical cancellation. A force zero retains strictly positive energy, whereas an energy zero retains an attractive force. The resulting analytical angular fine structure is resolved by a quantum harmonic oscillator pair, yielding the complete arbitrary-angle interaction energy and radial force that recover quantum-perturbative results. The conventional dipolar magic angle splits into strictly ordered energy- and force-zero angles; the latter uniquely bounds the radially repulsive sector and carries a positive energy barrier. Derived scaling laws and finite-sphere calculations provide experimentally testable signatures from microscopic dipoles to macroscopic polarizable bodies.

authors.name: Shuze Zhu
authors.institution: Zhejiang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Inner derivations and automorphism groups of vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type. We prove that the zero mode map $V_1\to\operatorname{Der}(V)$, $h\mapsto h_0$, is an isomorphism of Lie algebras. We prove surjectivity using traces on finite sums of weight spaces and Li's module construction, and injectivity using the vacuum character of Zhu's algebra. It follows that $\operatorname{Inn}(V)$ is the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ and has finite index in $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$. Moreover, $\operatorname{dim}\operatorname{Aut}(V)=\dim V_1$, so $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ is finite if and only if $V_1=0$.

papers.title: SAE-Audit: Clinical-Trial Prediction via Inference-Time Optimization of Black-Box LLMs Audited by Sparse Autoencoder Evidence
papers.abstract: Clinical trials are costly and often take years to complete, making early outcome prediction valuable for trial planning. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to forecast clinical-trial outcomes, yet their predictions remain unreliable and their rationales may not faithfully reflect the evidence underlying their answers. On tasks such as predicting whether a registered clinical trial will complete or terminate early, frontier LLMs perform only modestly above chance in our experiments. We introduce SAE-Audit, which optimizes a black-box LLM at inference time with evidence obtained from a deployable open model. A frozen sparse autoencoder (SAE) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is converted into a vocabulary of clinical concepts. Sparse probes fitted on past trials determine which concepts are associated with the outcome. For a new protocol, the concepts detected by the probe are written as evidence, each with the direction and strength of its association with the outcome, and the LLM being audited optimizes its answer in the light of this evidence. Without additional training, SAE-Audit raises balanced accuracy of deepseek-v4-flash by 9.6--12.0 points on five clinical-trial prediction tasks and raises GPT-5.6-terra by 8.0 points on trial completion, exceeding other agentic inference-time optimization methods by a large margin. As an auxiliary, SAE probes module within SAE-Audit is itself accurate and auditable, providing natural-language explanations directly derived from verified concept contributions and protocol evidence, without requiring additional LLMs at inference time. SAE-Audit provides verifiable, concept-level evidence for more accurate and auditable clinical-trial prediction. It can also be embedded into biomedical AI agents such as Biomni to optimize their performance.

authors.name: Junbo Shen
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

papers.title: A transitive $C^{1+\alpha}$ surface diffeomorphism with positive entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy
papers.abstract: Let $0<\alpha\le 1$. On a closed surface, every topologically transitive $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphism with positive topological entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy.

papers.title: Inverse spectra and Wilson traces of $SU(2)$ connections on finite graphs
papers.abstract: We study a fixed $SU(2)$ connection on a known finite labelled simple graph through its full Laplacian spectra with independently variable positive edge weights. This family is equivalent to all vertex-simple cycle traces. For connected graphs, it determines every vertex gauge class exactly for trees and graphs with a single cyclic block that is a cycle, a theta graph, or a subdivision of a simple three-vertex-connected cubic graph. For arbitrary graphs, we describe the full fibers, including degenerate connections, and give criteria for generic uniqueness and Wilson observability under restricted edge controls.

papers.title: Weighted Numerical Homological Regularities over Positively Graded Algebras
papers.abstract:
Let A be a noetherian positively graded algebra. We investigate several weighted numerical homological regularities: weighted CM-regularity, weighted Tor-regularity (Ext-regularity), and weighted Ex-regularity, defined in terms of the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of canonical complexes associated with graded A-modules. Introduced by Kirkman, Won, and Zhang, weighted regularities provide finite invariants even when their unweighted counterparts are infinite. Through parametrized degree reweightings, they unify classical homological invariants, including unweighted numerical regularities, sup, inf, depth, projective dimension, and local cohomology dimension. This framework clarifies the behavior of homological regularities under degree shifts and reveals intrinsic relationships among these invariants, particularly those involving the a-invariant.
  We establish several inequalities and equalities relating these weighted regularities to the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of derived Hom and derived tensor complexes. These results recover their unweighted counterparts and yield new relations involving the a-invariant for a fixed weight. Some of these results generalize the inequalities of Kirkman-Won-Zhang between weighted CM-regularity and Tor-regularity by allowing the weight to range over the entire plane R^2. We also give conditions under which these inequalities become equalities, thereby answering a question posed by Kirkman-Won-Zhang. We use weighted AS-regularity to study the Artin-Schelter regularity of A. Under mild conditions, we prove that the weighted AS-regularity of A vanishes if and only if A is an N-graded AS-regular algebra. This generalizes an unweighted result of the present authors and a weighted result of Kirkman, Won, and Zhang.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the Bryant Soliton via the Positive Mass Theorem
papers.abstract:
For all $n\ge 4$, we prove that every $n$-dimensional complete noncompact steady gradient Ricci soliton asymptotic to the cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ is, up to scaling, isometric to the Bryant soliton.
  Our proof combines the exponential Bryant asymptotics of Bamler-Lai with the positive mass theorem in all dimensions through a scalar curvature comparison.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Well-posedness and regularity of the integral invariant model from linear scalar transport equation" [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 564 (2026) 130904]
papers.abstract: We clarify the compactly supported terminal test space and the moving-domain Bochner spaces in the integral invariant formulation. We complete the existence proof by establishing strong measurability and the initial trace, and replace the stability argument by a compact-test density argument that retains the original stability constant. A short appendix shows that the integral invariant identity remains valid for all square-integrable terminal test functions that vanish almost everywhere outside the terminal domain, thereby admitting the zero extensions of the cell polynomials used in the SLDG/SLFV method. We also correct the velocity and divergence in the swirling-deformation example.

papers.title: Approximate controllability in Sobolev spaces of periodic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with bilinear controls
papers.abstract: We consider the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the torus $\T^d$ with a smooth real-valued potential and nonlinearity $\kappa|\psi|^{2p}\psi$, where the dimension $d\ge1$, the integer $p\ge1$, and the coefficient $\kappa\in\R$ are arbitrary. The controls act bilinearly through finitely many low Fourier modes. For every integer $s>d/2$, we prove approximate controllability in $H^s$ between any two nowhere vanishing states on the unit sphere in $L^2$ at any prescribed positive time. The proof combines small-time phase control, a transport approximation in $H^s$, and a construction of short uncontrolled trajectories connecting states with different winding vectors.

papers.title: Small-time global exact controllability of nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations on the circle with bilinear controls
papers.abstract:
We study nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations on the circle with nonlinearity $\kappa|\psi|^{2p}\psi$, a fixed smooth real potential $V$, and bilinear controls. Using only the three control potentials $\mathbf 1,\cos x,\sin x$, we prove global approximate controllability in $H^s$ on the unit sphere of $L^2$ for all integers $s,p\ge1$, every $\kappa\in\mathbb R$, and any prescribed positive time. The proof combines two ingredients: the approximate controllability between nowhere vanishing states from our companion paper, and a new mechanism that steers any nonzero initial state to a nowhere vanishing state in arbitrarily small time.
  When $V=0$ and the nonlinearity is defocusing or sufficiently weakly focusing, adding two explicit control potentials of finite regularity gives local exact controllability in $H^2$ near the constant state, via a moment problem and the inverse mapping theorem. Together, these results imply global exact controllability in $H^2$ on the unit sphere of $L^2$, at any prescribed positive time, with five control potentials. To~the best of our knowledge, this is the first global exact controllability result for a nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with finitely many bilinear controls.

papers.title: A cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values. For a diagonally constant index on a periodically extended skew Young diagram, it is a sum over semi-standard cyclic Young tableaux. It includes the cyclic multiple zeta values of Hirose, Murahara and Murakami as a special case. The first two main results are a cyclic analogue of the Maesaka--Seki--Watanabe formula for truncated sums and an {integral--series identity} under an admissibility condition. As an application, we give a proof of $4^n\zeta(\{1,3\}^n)=\zeta(\{4\}^n)$ by counting linear extensions of a poset. The third main result expresses a cyclic Schur multiple harmonic sum as a finite signed sum of Schur multiple harmonic sums with the same number of boxes and the same multiset of exponents.

authors.name: Hau-Yi Lin
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

papers.title: The Growth Path Is the Missing Half of Neural Networks
papers.abstract: An artificial neuron computes and learns, but it does not live: the units of a network are fixed when it is designed, and every one of them is kept and paid for whether it is used or not. We give each neuron a second pathway. Beside its Task Path, the usual computation and gradient learning, a dual-pathway neuron has a Growth Path: a nutrient flows from the outputs back through the network, every layer receives the same fixed budget, and each unit is fed in proportion to how much the units above it use it. A well-fed unit divides and a starving unit dies. This allocation is not a separate analysis or pruning step: it runs throughout training and reads only activations and weights. The task is still learned from labels with the ordinary loss, and the training procedure gains no phase, no schedule and no target size. Because the budget is conserved, the competition is zero-sum and a single number sets the size of the network. Switched on in a pretrained network that is deployed on a narrower domain, the Growth Path shrinks the network while it keeps learning. With Adam the network ends 1.0 to 1.2 points more accurate on the domain than the same network trained ordinarily, at 24% to 60% of its compute, and at 12% of the compute it is still ahead; a random choice of the same number of units gives no gain. Letting starving pretrained units sleep instead of die keeps 1.2 to 4.6 points more of the rarely used content. Over 800 changing tasks a network with the Growth Path holds its accuracy while ordinary networks decline. With plain SGD the gains are smaller: at deployment the method trades compute against rarely used content, and on one of the two continual-learning streams it only ties networks of equal size. The experiments are small (three-layer perceptrons on MNIST-like data); what they show is that a conserved, loss-free second pathway can decide by itself which units a network needs.

papers.title: Every Finite Incline Is Finitely Based
papers.abstract: We prove that every incline of finite additive height generates a Cross variety. In particular, every finite incline is finitely based. Moreover, we obtain a uniform bound on the number of variables needed to axiomatize subvarieties of decreasing Catalan semiring varieties, and give an effective construction of finite equational bases.

papers.title: $K$-Midranks: A robust clustering algorithm for heavy-tailed data with applications to spectroscopy and finance
papers.abstract: Clustering data with extreme observations and heavy tails can be challenging for methods that rely on distances between raw observations or specific distributional assumptions. We introduce $K$-midranks, a clustering method that replaces observations with coordinatewise ranks and partitions the transformed data using a procedure analogous to $K$-means. This transformation reduces the influence of extreme values while preserving the ordering of observations within each variable. We evaluate $K$-midranks against $K$-means, $K$-medoids, and mixture models based on Gaussian, Student's t, Cauchy, and generalized hyperbolic distributions through simulation studies, and provide some theoretical properties. $K$-midranks generally outperforms the competing methods on Cauchy-shifted data. In contrast, $K$-means and model-based methods perform better on Gaussian data and Student's t data with three degrees of freedom. We demonstrate the method's practical use in grouping samples based on Raman and LIBS spectra and clustering S\&P 500 stocks according to their returns. $K$-midranks achieves competitive performance with model-based methods in the spectroscopy applications and the best performance among the methods considered in the stock-return application. These findings suggest that $K$-midranks provides a useful alternative for clustering data with Cauchy-like heavy tails. An R package implementing the proposed method is available.

authors.name: Nathakhun Wiroonsri
authors.institution: King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi

papers.title: Ziv: A Language for Correctly Rounded Math Libraries
papers.abstract:
Developing performant, correctly rounded math libraries is challenging. Such implementations often rely on extended-precision arithmetic for correct rounding and precomputed constants for performance. Existing implementation languages, however, provide limited support for (i) high-level abstractions for such arithmetic and (ii) staged computation to combine precomputation and runtime computation in one program. As a result, existing implementations often miss abstraction opportunities and hard-code constants precomputed using separate programs. These practices make it difficult to write, understand, and modify these libraries.
  We present Ziv, a programming system for developing correctly rounded math libraries. It consists of a small language, a rich standard library, and a provably sound compiler targeting C. Ziv supports (i) high-level numerical abstractions via types and operations for extended-precision numbers, and (ii) staged computation via compile-time evaluation of expressions known to be input-independent. These features enable high-level code that unifies precomputation and runtime computation. We embed Ziv in Julia and evaluate it by reimplementing 19 functions from two state-of-the-art libraries targeting correct rounding; we achieve competitive performance with 2.63$\times$ reductions in lines of code. We also implement three new functions and automatically explore 824,256 variants, achieving 96.5$\times$ average speedup over an arbitrary-precision library.

authors.name: Lucas Yunkyu Lee
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Wonyeol Lee
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Bridging Blind Spots With Words: Decentralized Multi-View Spatial Reasoning via Language-Constrained Communication
papers.abstract: As multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) get increasingly used as collaborative partners across embodied robotics, AR/VR, and multi-user systems, spatial reasoning is now often distributed across agents with partial environment visibility, necessitating spatial reasoning integration. Prior work in language-mediated spatial integration is however strictly limited to simplified two-agent scenarios. To address this gap, we first formalize the general problem of decentralized multi-view spatial reasoning, where N agents observe distinct viewpoints, exchange budget-constrained natural language messages, and collaborate to enable a listener to answer spatial queries. We then introduce a novel multi-view spatial benchmark to isolate queries that demand non-trivial multi-view integration. Through an extensive empirical study, we discover that the penalty of restricting decentralized spatial reasoning to natural language with limited budget is far smaller than suggested by prior two-agent literature. Nevertheless, we observe that substantial headroom still remains for multi-agent spatial reasoning in this setting, as evidenced by a significant gap between current centralized performance and an oracle best-of-K ceiling. Moreover, we show that reinforcement learning with credit assignment substantially bolsters the decentralized model, effectively closing the gap with the centralized baseline.

authors.name: Soumyabrata Chaudhuri
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: The $T1$ theorem under Dini regularity
papers.abstract: We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calder\'on-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.

papers.title: Note on OpenAI's proof of the base of Lagrangian fibrations
papers.abstract: OpenAI proved that every Lagrangian fibration of a compact hyper-K\"ahler manifold has a base $\mathbb P^n$. This expository note summarizes the last section of their paper.

papers.title: Griffiths-Dwork Reduction For Smooth Hypersurfaces in Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We give an explicit Griffiths-Dwork pole-order reduction algorithm for a smooth hypersurface $Z$ in a Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$. Under two arithmetic conditions on $k,n$, and the degree of $Z$, the residue construction describes the Hodge filtration on the middle cohomology of the complement in terms of the Jacobian ring. We explicitly characterize the required cohomological vanishings. As applications, we compute group representations on the vanishing cohomology of two symmetric hyperplane sections of $\mathrm{Gr}(3,10)$ and deduce maximal Picard rank for their associated Debarre-Voisin fourfolds. We also compute a Picard-Fuchs equation for a pencil of symmetric Gushel-Mukai fivefolds.

papers.title: Sharp tails for arguments of Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: Let $t$ be uniform on $[T,2T]$, let $\chi$ be a Dirichlet character modulo $q$, and set $X=\Im\log L(1/2+it,\chi)$ and $Q=\sum_{p\le T,\,p\nmid q}1/p$. For fixed $K,\theta_0>0$, uniformly in $q\le T^{\theta_0}$, $\chi$, and $0\le V\le KQ$, each signed tail $\Pr\{\pm X>V\}$ has order $\sqrt Q\,(V+\sqrt Q)^{-1}\exp(-V^2/Q)$. In particular, for $S(t)=\pi^{-1}\arg\zeta(1/2+it)$ and $0\le V\le K\log\log T$, each tail $\Pr\{\pm S(t)>V\}$ has order $\sqrt{\log\log T}\,(V+\sqrt{\log\log T})^{-1}\exp(-\pi^2V^2/\log\log T)$. For $|v|\le KQ$, the probability that $X$ lies in a fixed-width interval centered at $v$ has order $Q^{-1/2}\exp(-v^2/Q)$ whenever the width is sufficiently large. The upper bound holds for every fixed positive width. We also obtain matching bounds of order $\exp(k^2Q)$ for the means of $\exp(\pm2kX)$ for fixed $k>0$. The proof begins with a one-sided polynomial bound for each sign, using Alp\"oge's zero-location theorem at the primitive inducing conductor. A weighted comparison with a sum over primes controls departures from the target interval, and a signed polynomial gives its lower bound.

papers.title: Sequential Selection against an Adaptive Opponent
papers.abstract: Selecting a strategy by testing it against an opponent is common in game-playing AI, red-teaming of language models, and safety evaluations of AI agents. In many of these settings, the opponent adapts to what it observes, so a strategy that keeps winning in practice may already have stopped working by the time it is used. Motivated by these settings, we study a player who tries strategies in practice games against an adaptive opponent, decides when to stop, and then either selects one strategy for the next game or abstains. The goal is to select a strategy that meets a target win probability while rarely selecting one that has already fallen below it. For a single strategy, we propose the Sequential Private Accumulated-excess Rule (SPAR), which accumulates evidence through a capped likelihood ratio and selects the strategy once this evidence reaches a privately drawn uniform threshold. We show that the stopping time must involve such private randomness. The number of games SPAR needs is inversely proportional to the error tolerance, and this rate is optimal even when the opponent happens not to adapt. To select among multiple strategies, we introduce Screen-then-SPAR, which screens candidates in stages before applying SPAR. The procedure adapts to the best strategy's unknown initial margin above the target and achieves the minimax rate up to logarithmic factors. The performance of Screen-then-SPAR is demonstrated through simulations and two real-data studies, one using recorded coding-agent attacks from MonitoringBench and the other using rock-paper-scissors matches between human players and an adaptive bot.

papers.title: A hyperbolic 7-manifold that fibers over the circle
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit orientable finite-volume hyperbolic $7$-manifold $M$ that fibers over the circle. The manifold is tessellated by $256$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic polytope $P^7$ and has $252$ cusps. The fiber is the interior of a compact aspherical $6$-manifold whose boundary consists of $256$ five-dimensional tori. The fibration comes from a Bestvina-Brady Morse function on the Davis complex. Bestvina-Brady theory shows that the kernel of the associated character is finitely presented. A perturbation argument over the integral Novikov ring shows that the infinite cyclic cover is finitely dominated. Farrell's fibering theorem, together with the vanishing of the Whitehead group, then gives the fibration.

papers.title: Several families of linear codes via weight functions of three-weight codes
papers.abstract: Recently, Huang et al. proposed a general framework for deriving new linear codes from a given code by applying weight functions to the set of codewords with a prescribed Hamming weight in [A structural theory of linear codes from weight functions: constructions, geometry and applications, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, DOI:10.1109/TIT.2026.3742840, 2026]. While this method was systematically developed for two-weight codes and yielded several families of projective two-weight codes, extending it to codes with more weights remains an interesting and challenging problem. In this paper, we generalize this construction to three-weight codes by employing a well-known family of ternary three-weight cyclic codes. By determining the weight distribution of every codimension-one subcode, as well as the distribution of fixed-weight codewords across these subcodes, we completely characterize the behavior of the weight-function construction on this family. As a result, we obtain three classes of linear codes with four nonzero weights and explicitly determine their parameters. Furthermore, the results show that these obtained codes are self-orthogonal and minimal.

papers.title: RAGA: Refreshable Animatable Gaussian Avatars from a Single Photo
papers.abstract: Avatars created from a single photo are fixed once made: regions the photo never showed, such as the back of a garment, are hallucinated and remain that way. We present Refreshable Animatable Gaussian Avatars (RAGA), a full-body Gaussian avatar that is created from a single image in about one second and can be refreshed whenever new images of the same person become available, without retraining or gradient-based optimization. RAGA maps each new observation into canonical UV space, accumulates it as visibility- and angle-weighted running sums, and re-decodes the fused map with the same decoder used for the photo. Although this decoder is trained only on single images, it makes use of the fused evidence. On 163 clips from five datasets, RAGA created from one photo outperforms LHM, LHM++ and IDOL, including on three datasets never used in training. Refreshing from later frames adds 0.49 dB PSNR overall and 0.68 dB on views turned at least 135{\deg} from the photo, where SSIM and LPIPS also improve. Given the same 16 images on all clips, LHM++ gains 0.15 dB, against 0.48 dB for RAGA. Creating an avatar takes 1.08 s and animating it 48.1 ms per frame on a laptop RTX 3080 GPU, with body fitting and matting included in creation and pose estimation included in animation. Code will be released on GitHub.
